children.text: Chapter 1
evaṃ mayā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: Thus have I heard.

children.text: ekasminsamaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ dvādaśabhirbhikṣusahasraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great community of monks, with twelve thousand monks.

children.text: tadyathāyuṣmatā ca jñānakauṇḍinyena ||
children.translated_text: That is, with the venerable <s>Jñānakauṇḍinya</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā cāśvajitā ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca bāṣpeṇa ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Bāṣpa</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca mahānāmnā ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Mahānāman</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca bhadrikeṇa ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Bhadrika</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca yaśodevena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Yaśodeva</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca vimalena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Vimala</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca subāhunā ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Subāhu</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca pūrṇena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca gavāṃpatinā ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Gavāṃpati</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā corubilvākāśyapena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca nadīkāśyapena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Nadīkāśyapa</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca gayākāśyapena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Gayākāśyapa</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca śāriputreṇa ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca mahāmaudgalyāyanena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca mahākāśyapena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca mahākātyāyanena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca kaphilena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Kaphila</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca kauṇḍinyena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca cunandena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Cunanda</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputreṇa ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā cāniruddhena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca nandikena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Nandika</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca kasphilena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Kasphila</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca subhūtinā ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca revatena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Revata</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca khadiravanikena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Khadiravanika</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā cāmogharājena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Amogharāja</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca mahāpāraṇikena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Mahāpāraṇika</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca bakkulena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Bakkula</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca nandena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Nanda</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca rāhulena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Rāhula</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā ca svāgatena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>,

children.text: āyuṣmatā cānandena ||
children.translated_text: and with the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.

children.text: evaṃpramukhairdvādaśabhir bhikṣusahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ dvātriṃśatā ca bodhisattvasahasraiḥ sarvairekajātipratibaddhaiḥ sarvabodhisattvapāramitānirjātaiḥ sarvabodhisattvābhijñatāvikrīḍitaiḥ sarvabodhisattvadhāraṇīpratibhānapratilabdhaiḥ sarvabodhisattvadhāraṇīpratilabdhaiḥ sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānasuparipūrṇaiḥ sarvabodhisattvapratisamyaggatiṃgataiḥ sarvabodhisattvasamādhivaśitāprāptaiḥ sarvabodhisattvavaśitāpratilabdhaiḥ sarvabodhisattvakṣāntyavakīrṇaiḥ sarvabodhisattvabhūmiparipūrṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with twelve thousand monks headed by these, and with thirty-two thousand bodhisattvas, all bound to only one more birth, all born from the bodhisattva perfections, all skilled in the play of the bodhisattva superknowledges, all having obtained bodhisattva dhāraṇī and eloquence, all having obtained bodhisattva dhāraṇī, all having perfectly fulfilled bodhisattva vows, all having gone to the complete true course of bodhisattvas, all having attained mastery over bodhisattva samādhis, all having obtained bodhisattva masteries, all suffused with bodhisattva patience, and all having fulfilled the bodhisattva stages.

children.text: tadyathā maitreyeṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ||
children.translated_text: That is, with <s>Maitreya</s>, the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

children.text: dharaṇīśvararājena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ||
children.translated_text: and with <s>Dharaṇīśvararāja</s>, the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

children.text: siṃhaketunā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ||
children.translated_text: and with <s>Siṃhaketu</s>, the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

children.text: siddhārthamatinā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ||
children.translated_text: and with <s>Siddhārthamati</s>, the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

children.text: praśāntacāritramatinā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ||
children.translated_text: and with <s>Praśāntacāritramati</s>, the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

children.text: pratisaṃvitprāptena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ||
children.translated_text: and with <s>Pratisaṃvitprāpta</s>, the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

children.text: nityodyuktena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ||
children.translated_text: and with <s>Nityodyukta</s>, the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

children.text: mahākaruṇācandriṇā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ||
children.translated_text: and with <s>Mahākaruṇācandrin</s>, the bodhisattva mahāsattva,

children.text: evaṃpramukhair dvātriṃśatā ca bodhisattvasahasraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with thirty-two thousand bodhisattvas headed by these.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīmupaniśritya viharati sma satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjitaśca tisṛṇāṃ pariṣadāṃ rājñāṃ rājakumārāṇāṃ rājamantriṇāṃ rājamahāmātrāṇāṃ rājapādamūlikānāṃ kṣatriyabrāhmaṇagṛhapatyamātyapārṣadyānāṃ paurajānapadānām anyatīrthikaśramaṇabrāhmaṇacarakaparivrājakānām ||
children.translated_text: Now at that time the Blessed One was dwelling near the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, honored, held in reverence, esteemed, and worshiped by the three assemblies: by kings, princes, royal ministers, great royal officers, those attached to the king's feet, kṣatriyas, brahmins, householders, counselors, council members, townspeople and country people, and by ascetics and brahmins of other sects, wandering religious mendicants, and itinerants.

children.text: lābhī ca bhagavān prabhūtānāṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyamāsvādanīyākalpikānāṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām ||
children.translated_text: And the Blessed One received abundant gains: chewable food, edible food, things to be tasted and suitable requisites, robes, alms bowls, beds and seats, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

children.text: lābhāgryayaśo'gryaprāptaśca bhagavān sarvatra cānupaliptaḥ padma iva jalena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One had attained the foremost gain and the foremost fame, yet everywhere he was unstained, like a lotus by water.

children.text: udāraśca bhagavataḥ kīrtiśabdaśloko loke 'bhyudgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavit paraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān pañcacakṣuḥsamanvāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: A lofty sound of renown, praise, and verse had arisen in the world for the Blessed One: he is an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, Blessed One, endowed with the five eyes.

children.text: sa imaṃ ca lokaṃ paraṃ ca lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ saśramaṇabrāhmaṇīn prajān sadevamānuṣān svayaṃ vijñāya sākṣātkṛtya upasaṃpadya viharati sma ||
children.translated_text: Having himself directly known, realized, and attained this world and the next world, with its gods, with its <s>Māra</s>, with its <s>Brahmā</s>, its beings with ascetics and brahmins, and its gods and humans, he dwelt there.

children.text: saddharmaṃ deśayati sma ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati sma ||
children.translated_text: He taught the true Dharma, good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good at the end, excellent in meaning and excellent in expression; he made manifest the spiritual life that is complete, full, purified, and entirely clear.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān rātryāṃ madhyame yāme buddhālaṃkāravyūhaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpanno 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: Now at that time, in the middle watch of the night, the Blessed One had entered a samādhi called the Array of the Buddha's Ornaments.

children.text: samanantarasamāpannasya ca bhagavata imaṃ buddhālaṃkāravyūhaṃ nāma samādhimatha tatkṣaṇameva bhagavata upariṣṭānmūrdhnaḥ saṃdhāvuṣṇīṣavivarāntarāt pūrvabuddhānusmṛtyasaṅgājñānālokālaṃkāraṃ nāma raśmiścacāra ||
children.translated_text: Immediately after the Blessed One had entered that samādhi called the Array of the Buddha's Ornaments, at that very instant a ray called the Ornament of the Light of Unobstructed Knowledge Remembering Former Buddhas issued from above the Blessed One, from the opening in the mass of his uṣṇīṣa at the crown of his head.

children.text: sā sarvā śuddhāvāsān devabhavanānyavabhāsya maheśvaradevaputrapramukhānaprameyān devaputrān saṃcodayāmāsa ||
children.translated_text: Having illuminated all the divine mansions of the Śuddhāvāsa gods, that ray stirred countless divine sons, headed by the divine son <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: tataśca tathāgataraśmijālānniścārya imāḥ saṃcodanāgāthā niścaranti sma ||
children.translated_text: Then, after the <s>Tathāgata</s> had sent forth a net of rays, these exhortatory verses issued forth:

children.text: jñānaprabhaṃ hatatamasaṃ prabhākaraṃ śubhraprabhaṃ śubhavimalāgratejasam
children.translated_text: Embrace the sage, the lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, whose radiance is knowledge, who has slain darkness, a maker of light, of pure radiance, possessed of supreme pure and stainless brilliance,

children.text: praśāntakāyaṃ śubhaśāntamānasaṃ muniṃ samāśliṣyata śākyasiṃham ||
children.translated_text: whose body is peaceful and whose mind is auspiciously tranquil.

children.text: jñānodadhiṃ śuddhamahānubhāvaṃ dharmeśvaraṃ sarvavidaṃ munīśam
children.translated_text: Take refuge in the ocean of knowledge, pure and of great majesty, the lord of dharma, the all-knowing lord of sages,

children.text: devātidevaṃ naradevapūjyaṃ dharme svayaṃbhuṃ vaśinaṃ śrayadhvam ||
children.translated_text: the god above gods, worshipped by men and gods, self-arisen in dharma, the master.

children.text: yo durdamaṃ cittamavartayadvaśe yo mārapāśairavamuktamānasaḥ
children.translated_text: He brought the hard-to-tame mind under control; his mind was released from the snares of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: yasyāpyavandhyāviha darśanaśravāstyayāntataḥ śāntavimokṣapāragaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For him, even the sight and hearing of him are not fruitless here; he has gone to the far shore of peaceful liberation.

children.text: ālokyabhūtaṃ tamatulyadharmaṃ tamonudaṃ sannayaveditāram
children.translated_text: Approach with devotion that Buddha, the light-made being, whose dharma is without equal, dispeller of darkness, knower of the true way,

children.text: śāntakriyaṃ buddhamameyabuddhiṃ bhaktyā samastā upasaṃkramadhvam ||
children.translated_text: peaceful in action and immeasurable in understanding, all of you together.

children.text: sa vaidyarājo 'mṛtabheṣajapradaḥ sa vādiśūraḥ kugaṇipratāpakaḥ
children.translated_text: He is the king of physicians, giver of the medicine of immortality; he is a heroic debater, subduer of false teachers.

children.text: sa dharmabandhuḥ paramārthakovidaḥ sa nāyako 'nuttaramārgadeśakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is the kinsman in dharma, skilled in the highest truth; he is the guide who teaches the unsurpassed path.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: samanantaraspṛṣṭāśca khalu punaste śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrāḥ tasyā buddhānusmṛtyasaṅgājñānālokāyā raśmyā ābhiścaivaṃrūpābhirgāthābhiḥ saṃcoditāḥ samantataḥ praśāntāḥ samādhervyutthāya tān buddhānubhāvenāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāgaṇanāsamatikrāntakalpātikrāntān buddhān bhagavanto 'nusmaranti sma ||
children.translated_text: And immediately, touched by that ray, the illumination of unobstructed knowledge born from recollection of the Buddha, and urged on by verses of this kind, those divine sons belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> realms became wholly pacified. Rising from samādhi, through the Buddha's power they recollected the Blessed Buddhas of immeasurable, countless, incalculable kalpas gone by.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ yāni buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhātparṣanmaṇḍalāni yāśca dharmadeśanāstā āsan tān sarvānanusmaranti sma ||
children.translated_text: They recollected all the arrays of qualities of the buddha-fields of those Blessed Buddhas, their assemblies, and the teachings of dharma that had taken place.

children.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ rātrau praśāntāyāmīśvaraśca nāma śuddhāvāsakāyiko devaputro maheśvaro nāma nandaśca sunandaśca candanaśca mahitaśca praśāntaśca praśāntavinīteśvaraścaite cānye ca saṃbahulāḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrā atikrāntātikrāntairvarṇaiḥ sarvāvantaṃ jetavanaṃ divyenāvabhāsenāvabhāsya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāman upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya ekānte tasthuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, in that peaceful night, the divine son of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> realm named <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Sunanda</s>, <s>Candana</s>, <s>Mahita</s>, <s>Praśānta</s>, and <s>Praśāntavinīteśvara</s>, along with these and many other divine sons belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> realms, illuminated all of <s>Jetavana</s> with divine radiance of colors surpassing all that had passed before. They approached the Blessed One, and having approached, bowed with their heads at the Blessed One's feet and stood to one side.

children.text: ekānte sthitāśca te śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrā bhagavantametadavocan asti bhagavan lalitavistaro nāma dharmaparyāyaḥ sūtrānto mahāvaipulyanicayo bodhisattvakuśalamūlasamudbhāvanaḥ tuṣitavarabhavanavikiraṇasaṃcintyāvakramaṇavikrīḍanagarbhasthānaviśeṣasaṃdarśano 'bhijātajanmabhūmiprabhāvasaṃdarśanaḥ sarvabālacaryāguṇaviśeṣasamatikramasarvalaukikaśilpasthānakarmasthānalipisaṃkhyāmudrāgaṇanāsidhanukalāpayuddhasālambhasarvasattvaprativiśiṣṭasaṃdarśanāntaḥpuraviṣayopabhogasaṃdarśanaḥ sarvabodhisattvacariniṣpandaniṣpattiphalādhigamaparikīrtano bodhisattvavikrīḍitaḥ sarvamāramaṇḍalavidhvaṃsanaḥ tathāgatabalavaiśāradyāṣṭādaśāveṇikasamuccayo 'pramāṇabuddhadharmanirdeśaḥ pūrvakairapi tathāgatairbhāṣitapūrvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Standing to one side, those divine sons belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> realms said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, there is a dharmaparyāya (teaching discourse), a sūtrānta called <s>Lalitavistara</s>, a great collection of vaipulya, which brings forth the roots of merit of bodhisattvas. It shows the scattering of radiance from the excellent palace of <s>Tuṣita</s>, the inconceivable descent and playful entry, the distinctive display of dwelling in the womb, and the display of the power of birth and native ground. It shows the surpassing of all special qualities of childish conduct, and the Bodhisattva's superiority over all beings in worldly arts, crafts, occupations, writing, numbers, seals, calculation, archery, martial skill, and wrestling, as well as the enjoyment of the inner palace. It proclaims the accomplishment, completion, and realization of the fruit of all bodhisattva practices; it is the Bodhisattva's sport, the destruction of every host of <s>Māra</s>, a compendium of the Tathāgata's powers, confidences, and eighteen special qualities, and an exposition of immeasurable Buddha-dharmas. It was formerly spoken by previous Tathāgatas as well."

children.text: tadyathā bhagavatā padmottareṇa ca dharmaketunā ca dīpaṃkareṇa ca guṇaketunā ca mahākareṇa ca ṛṣidevena ca śrītejasā ca satyaketunā ca vajrasaṃhatena ca sarvābhibhuvā ca hemavarṇena ca atyuccagāminā ca pravāhasāgareṇa ca puṣpaketunā ca vararūpeṇa ca sulocanena ca ṛṣiguptena ca jinavaktreṇa ca unnatena ca puṣpitena ca ūrṇatejasā ca puṣkareṇa ca suraśminā ca maṅgalena ca sudarśanena ca mahāsiṃhatejasā ca sthitabuddhidattena ca vasantagandhinā ca satyadharmavipulakīrtinā ca tiṣyeṇa ca puṣyeṇa ca lokasundareṇa ca vistīrṇabhedena ca ratnakīrtinā ca ugratejasā ca brahmatejasā ca sughoṣeṇa ca supuṣpeṇa ca sumanojñaghoṣeṇa ca suceṣṭarūpeṇa ca prahasitanetreṇa ca guṇarāśinā ca meghasvareṇa ca sundaravarṇena ca āyustejasā ca salīlagajagāminā ca lokābhilāṣitena ca jitaśatruṇā ca saṃpūjitena ca vipaśyinā ca śikhinā ca viśvabhuvā ca kakucchandena ca kanakamuninā ca kāśyapena ca tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitapūrvaḥ taṃ bhagavānapyetarhi saṃprakāśayet bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: "That is, it was formerly spoken by the Blessed Ones <s>Padmottara</s>, <s>Dharmaketu</s>, <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, <s>Guṇaketu</s>, <s>Mahākara</s>, <s>Ṛṣideva</s>, <s>Śrītejas</s>, <s>Satyaketu</s>, <s>Vajrasaṃhata</s>, <s>Sarvābhibhū</s>, <s>Hemavarṇa</s>, <s>Atyuccagāmin</s>, <s>Pravāhasāgara</s>, <s>Puṣpaketu</s>, <s>Vararūpa</s>, <s>Sulocana</s>, <s>Ṛṣigupta</s>, <s>Jinavaktra</s>, <s>Unnata</s>, <s>Puṣpita</s>, <s>Ūrṇatejas</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>, <s>Suraśmin</s>, <s>Maṅgala</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Mahāsiṃhatejas</s>, <s>Sthitabuddhidatta</s>, <s>Vasantagandhin</s>, <s>Satyadharmavipulakīrti</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Lokasundara</s>, <s>Vistīrṇabheda</s>, <s>Ratnakīrti</s>, <s>Ugratejas</s>, <s>Brahmatejas</s>, <s>Sughoṣa</s>, <s>Supuṣpa</s>, <s>Sumanojñaghoṣa</s>, <s>Suceṣṭarūpa</s>, <s>Prahasitanetra</s>, <s>Guṇarāśi</s>, <s>Meghasvara</s>, <s>Sundaravarṇa</s>, <s>Āyusteja</s>, <s>Salīlagajagāmin</s>, <s>Lokābhilāṣita</s>, <s>Jitaśatru</s>, <s>Saṃpūjita</s>, <s>Vipaśyin</s>, <s>Śikhin</s>, <s>Viśvabhū</s>, <s>Kakucchanda</s>, <s>Kanakamuni</s>, and by the Tathāgata, arhat, perfectly awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>. May the Blessed One now also make it manifest for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit and happiness of the great mass of people and of gods and humans."

children.text: asya ca mahāyānodbhāvanārthaṃ sarvaparapravādināṃ ca nigrahārthaṃ sarvabodhisattvānāṃ codbhāvanārthaṃ sarvamārāṇāṃ cābhibhavanārthaṃ sarvabodhisattvayānikānāṃ ca pudgalānāṃ vīryārambhasaṃjananārthaṃ saddharmasya cānuparigrahārthaṃ triratnavaṃśasyānuparigrahārthaṃ triratnavaṃśasyānupacchedanārthaṃ buddhakāryasya ca parisaṃdarśanārthamiti ||
children.translated_text: And this was for the proclaiming of the <s>mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), for the subduing of all advocates of rival doctrines, for the arousing of all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, for the overcoming of all <s>Māras</s>, for producing the undertaking of vigor in all persons who follow the <s>bodhisattvayāna</s> (bodhisattva vehicle), for the protection of the true Dharma, for the preservation of the lineage of the <s>triratna</s> (Three Jewels), for preventing the interruption of the lineage of the <s>triratna</s>, and for the display of the Buddha's work.

children.text: adhivāsayati sma bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena sadevakasya lokasyānukampāmupādāya ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted the request of those sons of gods by silence, out of compassion for the world together with its gods.

children.text: atha khalu devaputrā bhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanasaḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya divyaiścandanacūrṇairagurucūrṇair māndārapuṣpaiścābhyavakīrya tatraivāntardadhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those sons of gods, knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had accepted by silence, were pleased, elated, satisfied, delighted, and filled with joy and gladness; they bowed with their heads at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, scattered divine sandalwood powder, aloeswood powder, and <s>māndāra</s> flowers over him, and disappeared right there.

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāmeva rātryāmatyayena ca karīro maṇḍalamātravyūhastenopasaṃkrāmat ||
children.translated_text: Then, when that very night had passed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> approached that place, the <s>Karīra-maṇḍalamātravyūha</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavān prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdadbodhisattvagaṇapuraskṛtaḥ śrāvakasaṃghapuraskṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sat down on the prepared seat, with the assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> before him and the community of disciples before him.

children.text: niṣadya bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayati smeti hi bhikṣavo rātrau praśāntāyāmīśvaro nāma śuddhāvāsakāyiko devaputro maheśvaraśca nāma nandaśca sunandaśca candanaśca mahitaśca praśāntaśca vinīteśvaraścaite cānye ca saṃbahulāḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrāḥ pūrvavadyāvattatraivāntardadhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: After sitting down, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: "So it was, monks: when the night was quiet, the son of a god named <s>Īśvara</s>, belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> class, and <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Sunanda</s>, <s>Candana</s>, <s>Mahita</s>, <s>Praśānta</s>, and <s>Vinīteśvara</s>, and these and many other sons of gods belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> class, as before, up to 'disappeared right there.'"

children.text: atha khalu te bodhisattvāste ca mahāśrāvakā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocan tatsādhu bhagavan taṃ lalitavistaraṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ deśayatu ||
children.translated_text: Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and those great disciples, bowing with joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Good, <s>Bhagavān</s>; let him teach the Dharma discourse called the <s>Lalitavistara</s>."

children.text: tadbhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca etarhi cāgatānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām ||
children.translated_text: "It will be for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, and for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of a great body of people, of gods and human beings, and of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and great beings both present now and yet to come."

children.text: adhivāsayati sma bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ teṣāṃ ca mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena sadevamānuṣāsurasya lokasyānukampāmupādāya ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted the request of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and great beings and of those great disciples by silence, out of compassion for the world together with its gods, humans, and asuras.

children.text: tatredamucyate ||
children.translated_text: On this point the following is said:

children.text: rātryāmihāsyāṃ mama bhikṣavo 'dya sukhopaviṣṭasya niraṅgaṇasya
children.translated_text: "Here tonight, monks, while I was seated at ease, stainless,

children.text: praviṣṭamānasya śubhairvihārairekāgracittasya samāhitasya ||
children.translated_text: my mind entered into auspicious states, one-pointed and concentrated.

children.text: athāgaman devasutā maharddhayaḥ pratītavarṇa vimalaśriyojjvalāḥ
children.translated_text: Then sons of gods of great power came, confident in appearance and blazing with stainless splendor;

children.text: śriyāvabhāsyeha ca jetasāhvayaṃ vanaṃ mudā me 'ntikamabhyupāgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: illuminating here the grove called <s>Jeta</s> with their glory, they joyfully approached my presence.

children.text: maheśvaraścandana īśa nando praśāntacitto mahitaḥ sunandanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Candana</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, the tranquil-minded <s>Mahita</s>, and <s>Sunandana</s>,

children.text: śāntāhvayaścāpyuta devaputrastāstāśca bahvyo 'tha ca devakoṭyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also the son of a god called <s>Śānta</s>, and many, many crores of gods besides.

children.text: praṇamya pādau pratidakṣiṇaṃ ca kṛtvaiva māṃ tasthurihāgrato me
children.translated_text: Having bowed to my feet and made circumambulation to the right, they stood here before me;

children.text: pragṛhya caivāñjalimaṅgulībhiḥ sagauravā māmiha te yayācuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, holding their hands joined with their fingers, they respectfully entreated me here.

children.text: idaṃ mune rāganisūdanāḍhya vaipulyasūtraṃ hi mahānidānam
children.translated_text: 'O sage rich in the destruction of passion, this expansive sūtra is indeed the great source-narrative,

children.text: yadbhāṣitaṃ sarvatathāgataiḥ prāg lokasya sarvasya hitārthametat ||
children.translated_text: which was formerly spoken by all <s>Tathāgatas</s> for the benefit of the whole world.

children.text: tatsādhvidānīmapi bhāṣato muniḥ sa bodhisattvaughaparigrahecchayā
children.translated_text: Therefore, good sage, speak it now as well, wishing to gather in the hosts of <s>bodhisattvas</s>,

children.text: paraṃ mahāyānamidaṃ prabhāṣayan parapravādānnamuciṃ ca dharṣayan ||
children.translated_text: proclaiming this supreme <s>mahāyāna</s>, and assailing rival doctrines and <s>Namuci</s>.'

children.text: adhyeṣaṇāṃ devagaṇasya tūṣṇīmagṛhṇadevānadhivāsanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: I accepted in silence the request of the hosts of gods, and the gods received my consent.

children.text: sarve ca tuṣṭā muditā udagrāḥ puṣpāṇi cikṣepuravāptaharṣam ||
children.translated_text: And all, pleased, joyful, and elated, threw flowers, having gained delight.

children.text: tadbhikṣavo me śṛṇuteha sarve vaipulyasūtraṃ hi mahānidānam
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, all of you listen to me here: this expansive sūtra is indeed the great source-narrative,

children.text: yadbhāṣitaṃ sarvatathāgataiḥ prāg lokasya sarvasya hitārthamevam ||
children.translated_text: which was formerly spoken by all <s>Tathāgatas</s> for the benefit of the whole world."

sampūjyamānasya raśmyāyamaparamitaścyuto martyasya lokotpanno nacirādanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyatīti ||
children.translated_text: There, monks, what is the dharmaparyāya (teaching-discourse), the sūtrānta, the great vaipulya, called <s>Sulalitavistara</s>? Here, monks, it concerns the <s>bodhisattva</s>, dwelling in the excellent mansion of <s>Tuṣita</s>: honored by those worthy of honor, having received consecration, praised, lauded, described, and extolled by hundreds of thousands of gods, possessed of consecration, arisen from vows, a buddha in whom all the qualities of a Buddha had come together, whose eye of knowledge was very vast and pure, whose intellect was wide and heated bright with mindfulness, understanding, movement, and firmness; who had reached the supreme pāramitās of giving, morality, patience, energy, meditation, wisdom, and great skill in means; who was skilled in the brahmic courses of great loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity; who had become turned toward the vision of knowledge of the great superknowledges, unobstructed and without covering; who had reached the complete culmination of all the dharmas conducive to awakening: the establishments of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of miraculous power, faculties, powers, limbs of awakening, and the path; whose body was adorned with marks and minor signs born of immeasurable stores of merit; who acted in long continuity, did as he spoke, and uttered no false speech or deed; whose mind was straight, not crooked, not bent, and unobstructed; from whom all conceit, intoxication, pride, fear, and dejection had gone; whose mind was equal toward all beings; who had attended upon immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of crores of Buddhas; whose face had been gazed upon by many hundreds of thousands of myriads of crores of bodhisattvas; whose fame was rejoiced in by hosts of <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, world-guardians, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and rākṣasas; who was skilled in the knowledge that enters into the unobstructed discriminating insight explaining every division of words; who had obtained endless, limitless dhāraṇī, the vessel of recollection that retains what all Buddhas have spoken without distraction; who was the great caravan-leader brought forth by the great ship of dharma, by the jewels of dharma consisting of the establishments of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of power, faculties, powers, limbs of awakening, path, pāramitās, and skill in means, and by the accumulation of merit; whose intention went beyond the four floods; who had crushed the rival of pride; who had well subdued all opponents of other doctrines; who stood firmly at the head of battle, destroying the hosts of enemy afflictions, wielding the firm weapon of the excellent vajra of knowledge; who had arisen from the root of the mind of awakening, from the staff of great compassion, and from superior resolve; watered by the deep stream of energy, with skill in means as his pericarp, the limbs of awakening and meditations as his filaments, samādhi as his pollen, born well in the stainless lake of hosts of virtues, with broad petals pure as the moon, from which the overflow of intoxication and conceit had gone, spreading unimpeded through the ten directions with the fragrance of morality, learning, and serene faith: a great lotus-man in the world, mature in knowledge, unstained by the eight worldly dharmas, diffusing the fragrant scent of stores of merit and knowledge, a very pure hundred-petaled lotus opened by the rays of the sun of wisdom and knowledge; uttered by the supreme recitation of the four bases of miraculous power; with sharp claws and fangs that are the four noble truths; whose vision rested on the four brahmavihāras; whose head was well gathered by the four means of attraction; whose body arose gradually through awakening to the twelve-limbed dependent origination; a well-born lion of knowledge and non-ignorance, completely filled with the thirty-seven dharmas conducive to awakening, yawning open through the three gates of liberation; whose eyes were purified by calm and insight; dwelling in the mountain caves of meditations, liberations, concentrations, and attainments; a tree well grown in the grove of discipline of the four modes of deportment; whose strength had been cultivated by practice in the ten powers and fearlessnesses; from whom horripilation at fear of existence and non-existence had gone; whose valor was not contracted; who pacified the herds of deer-like hares who are the tīrthikas; who roared the great lion's roar, proclaiming the sound of selflessness; a lion among men, making dim the host of firefly-like tīrthikas by the rays of the brilliance of wisdom in the circle of liberation and meditation; dispelling the massed darkness and gloom of ignorance; with power and energy brought to heat, blazing with the splendor of merit among gods and humans; a great sun among men, free from the dark fortnight and filled with the bright fortnight, pleasant and lovely to see, with unobstructed faculty of sight; encircled by hundreds of thousands of lights of gods; possessing the circle of meditation, liberation, and knowledge; a moon among great men, with moonbeams that are the happiness of the limbs of awakening, awakening the water-lilies that are men awakened by the Buddha, surrounded by the four continents of assemblies; endowed with the seven jewels of the limbs of awakening; applying himself with an equal mind toward all beings; whose understanding was unobstructed; whose vows and austerity were the ten wholesome paths of action; whose intention was toward a well-accomplished, complete, and surpassing course; who, as the unobstructed king of dharma, set in motion the excellent, foremost wheel of the jewel of dharma; arisen in the family lineage of a wheel-turning king; filled with all the jewels of dharma of deep, hard-to-fathom dependent origination; not satiated with learning, whose knowledge had vast and extensive undertaking and did not overstep the boundary of morality; whose eyes were like the calyx of a great lotus; whose understanding was vast like the best ocean-bearing earth; whose mind was equal to earth, water, fire, and wind; whose firm strength was like <s>Meru</s>, unshaken, free from attachment and aversion; whose understanding was pure as the expanse of the sky, vast, unbearable, and expansive; whose superior resolve was very pure; whose gifts were well given; whose former yogic practice was well performed; who had well made his preparation, had given a pledge of truth, had sought out every root of good, had perfumed his dispositions, and was, as it were, the outlet of all roots of good; from whom the stream of all roots of good had been brought together over seven incalculable eons; who had given seven kinds of gifts; who had practiced the five bases of meritorious action; who had practiced threefold good conduct by body, fourfold by speech, and threefold by mind; who had undertaken and practiced the ten wholesome paths of action; who had practiced right application endowed with forty factors; who had set his vow as a right vow endowed with forty factors; who had entered into right superior resolve endowed with forty factors; who had fulfilled right liberation endowed with forty factors; who had made straight right faith endowed with forty factors; who had gone forth among forty hundreds of thousands of myriads of crores of Buddhas; who had given gifts among fifty-five hundreds of thousands of myriads of crores of Buddhas; who had performed service for three and a half hundred crores of pratyekabuddhas; who had set immeasurable incalculable beings upon the path to heaven and liberation; who desired to awaken to unsurpassed complete awakening; who was bound to one more birth; who, having passed away from here, was dwelling in the excellent mansion of <s>Tuṣita</s>; the highest son of gods named <s>Śvetaketu</s>, honored by all hosts of gods. This immeasurable one, having descended by a ray and been born in the mortal world, will before long awaken to unsurpassed complete awakening.

children.text: tasmin mahāvimāne sukhopaviṣṭasya dvātriṃśadbhūmisahasrapratisaṃsthite vitardiniryūhatoraṇagavākṣakūṭāgāraprāsādatalasamalaṃkṛte ucchritachatradhvajapaṭākaratnakiṅkiṇījālavitānavitate māndāravamahāmāndāravapuṣpasaṃstaraṇasaṃstṛte apsarasaḥkoṭīniyutaśatasahasrasaṃgītisaṃpracalite atimuktakacampakapāṭalakovidāramucilindamahāmucilindāśokanyagrodhatindukāsanakarṇikārakeśarasālaratnavṛkṣopaśobhite hemajālasaṃchanne mahatā pūrṇakumbhopaśobhite samatalavyūhopaśobhite jyotirmālikāsumanovāte devakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrābhimukhanayanāvalokitāloke mahāvipuladharmasaṃgītisarvakāmarativegakleśacchedane vyapagatākhilakrodhapratighamānamadadarpāpanayane prītiprasādaprāmodyottaptavipulasmṛtisaṃjanane sukhopaviṣṭasya tasmin mahādharmasāṃkathye pravṛtte tebhyaścaturaśītibhyas tūryasaṃgītisahasranirnāditebhyo bodhisattvasya pūrvaśubhakarmopacayenemāḥ saṃcodanāgāthā niścaranti sma ||
children.translated_text: As he sat comfortably in that great mansion, established on thirty-two thousand floors, adorned with balconies, projections, gateways, latticed windows, peaked halls, palaces, and terraces, stretched over with lofty parasols, banners, flags, jewel-bell nets, and canopies, spread with carpets of māndārava and great māndārava flowers, filled with the music of hundreds of thousands of millions and billions of apsarases, beautified by atimuktaka, campaka, pāṭala, kovidāra, mucilinda, great mucilinda, aśoka, nyagrodha, tinduka, āsana, karṇikāra, keśara, sāla, and jewel trees, covered with a golden net, beautified by great full jars and by an even arrangement of terraces, lit by garlands of lamps and wafted by pleasant breezes, its light seen by the eyes of hundreds of thousands of millions and billions of gods, cutting off the force of craving, sensual delight, and defilement by its great, abundant music of dharma, removing all anger, hostility, conceit, intoxication, and arrogance, and generating joy, faith, gladness, ardor, abundant mindfulness, and happiness, then, when that great conversation on dharma had begun, from those eighty-four thousand resounding musical ensembles, through the accumulation of the bodhisattva's former wholesome deeds, these exhortatory verses issued forth:

children.text: smara vipulapuṇyanicaya smṛtimatigatimanantaprajñāprabhākarin
children.translated_text: Remember your vast accumulation of merit, you who bear mindfulness, insight, progress, and rays of infinite wisdom.

children.text: atulabala vipulavikrama vyākaraṇaṃ dīpaṃkarasyāpi ||
children.translated_text: O you of incomparable strength and vast valor, remember even the prophecy of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>.

children.text: smara vipulanirmalamanas trimalamalaprahīṇaśāntamadadoṣam
children.translated_text: Remember your vast and stainless mind, your peace free from the three stains, from impurity, pride, and fault.

children.text: śubhavimalaśuddhacittā dāmacarī yādṛśā ti pure ||
children.translated_text: Remember what auspicious, stainless, purified states of mind and what practice of self-restraint were yours in the past.

children.text: smara kulakulīnā śamathaṃ śīlavrataṃ kṣamā damaṃ caiva
children.translated_text: Remember, noble through lineage after lineage, tranquility, moral discipline and vows, patience, and restraint,

children.text: vīryabaladhyānaprajñā niṣevitā kalpaniyutāni ||
children.translated_text: and the strength of energy, meditation, and wisdom that you cultivated for millions of kalpas.

children.text: smara smara anantakīrte sampūjitā ye ti buddhaniyutāni
children.translated_text: Remember, remember, you of endless fame, the countless buddhas whom you worshipped.

children.text: sarvān karuṇāyamānaḥ kālo 'yaṃ mā upekṣasva ||
children.translated_text: Have compassion for all. This is the time; do not let it pass by.

children.text: cyava cyava hi cyutividhijñā jaramaraṇakleśasūdanā virajā
children.translated_text: Depart, depart from there, knower of the way of descent, stainless destroyer of old age, death, and the afflictions.

children.text: samudīkṣante bahavo devāsuranāgayakṣagandharvā ||
children.translated_text: Many gods, asuras, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas are looking on.

children.text: kalpasahasra ramitvā tṛptirnāstyambhasīva samudre
children.translated_text: After enjoying yourself for thousands of kalpas, there is no satiety, as there is none for the ocean with water.

children.text: sādhu bhava prajñātṛpta tarpaya janatāṃ ciratṛṣārtām ||
children.translated_text: Good one, become satisfied by wisdom; satisfy the people who have long been tormented by thirst.

children.text: kiṃcāpyaninditayaśastvaṃ dharmaratirato na cāsi kāmarataḥ
children.translated_text: Although your fame is blameless and you are devoted to delight in dharma, not to delight in sensual pleasures,

children.text: atha ca punaramalanayanā anukampā sadevakaṃ lokam ||
children.translated_text: still, stainless-eyed one, have compassion for the world together with its gods.

children.text: kiṃcāpi devanayutāḥ śrutvā dharmaṃ na te vitṛpyante
children.translated_text: Although multitudes of gods do not become satisfied after hearing the dharma,

children.text: atha ca puna rakṣaṇagatānapāyasaṃsthānapekṣasva ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless look upon those who have gone for protection and those who are destined for the lower realms.

children.text: kiṃcāpi vimalacakṣo paśyasi buddhān daśādiśi loke
children.translated_text: Although, stainless-eyed one, you see buddhas in the world in the ten directions,

children.text: dharmaṃ śṛṇoṣi ca tatastaṃ dharmavaraṃ vibhaja loke ||
children.translated_text: and hear the dharma from them, nevertheless divide and distribute that excellent dharma in the world.

children.text: kiṃcāpi tuṣitabhavanaṃ tava puṇyaśriyābhiśobhate śrīmān
children.translated_text: Although the palace of <s>Tuṣita</s>, splendid one, shines with the glory of your merit,

children.text: atha ca puna karuṇamānasa pravarṣa jambudhvaje varṣam ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless, with a compassionate mind, rain down rain upon <s>Jambudhvaja</s>.

children.text: samatītya kāmadhātuṃ devā ye rūpadhātukāneke
children.translated_text: Passing beyond the realm of desire, the many gods who belong to the realm of form

children.text: sarve ty abhinandante spṛśeya siddhivrato bodhim ||
children.translated_text: all rejoice, saying, 'May he who is vowed to accomplishment touch awakening.'

children.text: nihatā ti mārakarmā jitāstvayānye kutīrthikā nāthā
children.translated_text: The deeds of <s>Māra</s> have been struck down, and the other false teachers have been conquered by you, protector.

children.text: kena sakalagata ti bodhī kālo 'yaṃ mā upekṣasva ||
children.translated_text: Since awakening has come within your complete reach, this is the time; do not let it pass by.

children.text: kleśāgninā pradīpte loke tvaṃ vīra meghavad vyāpya
children.translated_text: When the world is blazing with the fire of defilements, you, hero, spread out like a cloud.

children.text: abhivarṣāmṛtavarṣaṃ śamaya kleśānnaramarūṇām ||
children.translated_text: Rain down a rain of nectar and pacify the defilements of humans and gods.

children.text: tvaṃ vaidya dhātukuśala cirāturān satyavaidya satyavān
children.translated_text: You are the physician skilled in the elements, the true physician for those long afflicted, truthful one.

children.text: trivimokṣāgadayogairnirvāṇasukhe sthapaya śīghram ||
children.translated_text: By the medicines of the three liberations, quickly establish them in the happiness of nirvāṇa.

children.text: aśrutva siṃhanādaṃ kroṣṭukanādaṃ nadantyanutraṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Without having heard the lion's roar, the timid ones utter the cry of jackals.

children.text: nada buddhasiṃhanādaṃ trāsaya paratīrthikaśṛgālān ||
children.translated_text: Roar the lion's roar of a buddha and terrify the jackals who are followers of other teachers.

children.text: prajñāpradīpahasto balavīryabalodito dharaṇimaṇḍe
children.translated_text: With the lamp of wisdom in your hand, raised up by the power of strength and energy on the circle of the earth,

children.text: karatalavareṇa dharaṇīṃ parāhanitvā jinahi māram ||
children.translated_text: strike the earth with the best palm of your hand and conquer <s>Māra</s>, O victor.

children.text: samudīkṣante pālāścaturo ye tubhya dāsyate pātram
children.translated_text: The four guardians are looking on, who will give you the bowl.

children.text: śakrāśca brahma nayutā ye jātaṃ tvāṃ grahīṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: And countless <s>Śakras</s> and <s>Brahmās</s> will receive you when you are born.

children.text: vyavalokayābhiyaśā kularatnakuloditā kulakulīnā
children.translated_text: Look, illustrious one, at the noble family, arisen from a jewel among families, noble through lineage.

children.text: yatra sthitvā sumate darśeṣyasi bodhisattvacarim ||
children.translated_text: Standing there, wise one, you will display the bodhisattva's conduct.

children.text: yatraiva bhājane 'smin maṇiratnaṃ tiṣṭhate bhavati śrīmān
children.translated_text: In whatever vessel this jewel gem remains, splendid one,

children.text: maṇiratnaṃ vimalabuddhe pravarṣa jambudhvaje varṣam ||
children.translated_text: that jewel gem, stainless buddha, rains down rain upon <s>Jambudhvaja</s>.

children.text: evaṃ bahuprakārā saṃgītiravānuniścarā gāthā
children.translated_text: Thus, in many forms, verses issuing from the sounds of music

children.text: codenti karuṇāmanasaṃ ayaṃ sa kālo mā upekṣasva ||
children.translated_text: urged on the one whose mind was compassionate: 'This is the time; do not let it pass by.'

children.text: Chapter 3

iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattva evaṃ dharmakālasaṃcoditaḥ saṃstato mahāvimānānniṣkramya dharmoccayo nāma mahāprāsādo yatra niṣadya bodhisattvastuṣitebhyo devebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati sma taṃ bodhisattvo 'bhirohati sma abhiruhya ca sudharme siṃhāsane niṣīdati sma
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, the bodhisattva, so urged on by the time for dharma and praised, came out from the great mansion and ascended the great palace called <s>Dharmoccaya</s>, where the bodhisattva used to sit and teach dharma to the gods of <s>Tuṣita</s>; having ascended, he sat down on the lion throne in the hall <s>Sudharmā</s>.

children.text: atha ye devaputrā bodhisattvasya sabhāgāḥ samayānasamprasthitāste 'pi tameva prāsādamabhirohanti sma
children.translated_text: Then those divine sons who belonged to the bodhisattva's assembly and had set out together at the proper time also ascended that same palace.

children.text: ye ca daśadiksaṃnipatitā bodhisattvāḥ sabhāgacaritā bodhisattvasya devaputrāśca te 'pi taṃ prāsādamabhiruhya yathāpratyarheṣu siṃhāsaneṣu svakasvakeṣu niṣīdanti sma apagatāpsarogaṇā apagataprākṛtadevaputrāḥ samānādhyāśayaparivārā aṣṭaṣaṣṭikoṭisahasraparivārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the bodhisattvas assembled from the ten directions, whose conduct was like that of the Bodhisattva, and the divine sons also, mounted that palace and sat down, each on his own proper lion-throne. The hosts of apsarases and ordinary divine sons had withdrawn; they were attended by retinues of the same aspiration, each with a retinue of sixty-eight thousand koṭis.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo dvādaśabhirvarṣairbodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣimavakramiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, twelve years before the Bodhisattva would descend into his mother's womb, this occurred.

children.text: atha śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrā jambudvīpamāgatya divyaṃ varṇamantardhāpya brāhmaṇaveṣeṇa brāhmaṇān vedānadhyāpayanti sma
children.translated_text: Then divine sons belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> realm came to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, concealed their divine appearance, and, in the guise of brahmins, taught the brahmins the Vedas.

children.text: yasyaivarūpā garbhāvakrāntirbhavati sa dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati
children.translated_text: One for whom such a descent into the womb takes place is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man.

children.text: yaiḥ samanvāgatasya dve gatī bhavato na tṛtīyā
children.translated_text: For one endowed with these, there are two destinies, not a third.

children.text: sacedagāramadhyāvasati rājā bhavati cakravartī caturaṅgo vijitavān dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ
children.translated_text: If he dwells in a household, he becomes a king, a <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning king), possessed of the fourfold army, victorious, righteous, a king of dharma, endowed with the seven jewels.

children.text: tasyemāni sapta ratnāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: These are his seven jewels:

children.text: tadyathā cakraratnaṃ hastiratnaṃ aśvaratnaṃ strīratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnameva saptamam ||
children.translated_text: namely, the wheel-jewel, the elephant-jewel, the horse-jewel, the woman-jewel, the jewel-gem, the householder-jewel, and the counselor-jewel as the seventh.

children.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī cakraratnena samanvāgato bhavati iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya tadeva poṣadheyaṃ ca pañcadaśyāṃ śiraḥsnātasyopavāsoṣitasyopariprāsādatalagatasya stryāgāraparivṛtasya pūrvasyāṃ diśi divyaṃ cakraratnaṃ prādurbhavati
children.translated_text: In what manner is a <s>cakravartin</s> king endowed with the wheel-jewel? Here, for a consecrated kṣatriya king, on that fifteenth-day observance, after he has bathed his head, kept the fast, gone up to the upper terrace of the palace, and been surrounded by the women's quarters, a divine wheel-jewel appears in the eastern direction.

children.text: sahasrāraṃ sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ suvarṇavarṇakarmālaṃkṛtaṃ saptatālamuccaiḥ samantād dṛṣṭvāntaḥpuraṃ rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya taddivyaṃ cakraratnameva bhavati
children.translated_text: It has a thousand spokes, with rim and nave, adorned with golden-colored workmanship, seven palm trees high, visible all around; for the consecrated kṣatriya king, that is the divine wheel-jewel.

children.text: śrutaṃ khalu mayā yasya kila rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya tadeva poṣadheyaṃ pañcadaśyāṃ śiraḥsnātasyopavāsoṣitasyopariprāsādatalagatasya stryāgāraparivṛtasya pūrvasyāṃ diśi divyaṃ cakraratnaṃ prādurbhavati sa bhavati rājā cakravartī
children.translated_text: He thinks: I have heard that when such a divine wheel-jewel appears in the eastern direction for a consecrated kṣatriya king, on that fifteenth-day observance, after he has bathed his head, kept the fast, gone up to the upper terrace of the palace, and been surrounded by the women's quarters, he becomes a <s>cakravartin</s> king.

children.text: nūnamahaṃ rājā cakravartī yannvahaṃ divyaṃ cakraratnaṃ mīmāṃsayeyam
children.translated_text: Surely I am a <s>cakravartin</s> king. Therefore I should test the divine wheel-jewel.

children.text: atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikta ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā taddivyaṃ cakraratnaṃ prārthayedevaṃ cāvedayet pravartayasva bhaṭṭa divyaṃ cakraratnaṃ dharmeṇa mādharmeṇa
children.translated_text: Then the consecrated kṣatriya king, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, would address that divine wheel-jewel with his right hand and say: Set forth, lord divine wheel-jewel, by dharma, not by adharma.

children.text: atha taddivyaṃ cakraratnaṃ rājñā kṣatriyeṇa mūrdhābhiṣiktena pravartitaṃ samyageva ṛddhau vihāyasā pūrveṇa vrajati
children.translated_text: Then that divine wheel-jewel, set in motion by the consecrated kṣatriya king, proceeds eastward through the sky by its proper miraculous power.

children.text: anveti rājā cakravartī sārdhaṃ caturaṅgeṇa balakāyena
children.translated_text: The <s>cakravartin</s> king follows it together with his fourfold army.

children.text: yatra ca pṛthivīpradeśe taddivyaṃ cakraratnaṃ saṃtiṣṭhate tatra rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto vāsaṃ kalpayati sārdhaṃ caturaṅgeṇa balakāyena
children.translated_text: And wherever on the earth that divine wheel-jewel comes to rest, there the consecrated kṣatriya king makes his encampment together with his fourfold army.

children.text: atha ye te bhavanti pūrvasyāṃ diśi rājāno maṇḍalinaḥ te rūpyapātrīṃ vā suvarṇacūrṇaparipūrṇāmādāya svarṇapātrīṃ vā rūpyacūrṇaparipūrṇāmādāya rājānaṃ cakravartinaṃ pratyuttiṣṭhanti ehi deva svāgataṃ devāya idaṃ devasya rājyamṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Then the regional kings in the eastern direction take a silver bowl filled with gold dust or a golden bowl filled with silver dust and rise to meet the <s>cakravartin</s> king, saying: Come, lord; welcome to the lord. This kingdom of yours is prosperous, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, delightful, and crowded with many people.

children.text: adhyāvasatu deva svakaṃ vijitamanuprāptam
children.translated_text: May the lord dwell in his own conquered realm that he has now reached.

children.text: evamukte rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktastrātā tān rājño maṇḍalina etadavocat kārayantu bhavantaḥ svakāni rājyāni dharmeṇa
children.translated_text: When this has been said, the consecrated kṣatriya king, as protector, says this to those regional kings: Let your honors rule your own kingdoms by dharma.

children.text: hanta bhavanto mā prāṇinaṃ ghātayiṣyatha mādattādāsyatha mā kāmeṣu mithyā cariṣyatha mā mṛṣā vakṣyatha yāvanmā me vijite adharmamutpadyate mādharmacāriṇo rocetha
children.translated_text: Come now, gentlemen: do not kill living beings, do not take what has not been given, do not engage wrongly in sensual pleasures, do not speak falsely. Let no adharma arise in my conquered realm, and do not approve those who practice adharma.

children.text: evaṃ khalu rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ pūrvāṃ diśaṃ vijayati
children.translated_text: In this way, indeed, the consecrated kṣatriya king conquers the eastern direction.

children.text: pūrvāṃ diśaṃ vijitaḥ pūrvaṃ samudramavagāhya pūrvaṃ samudramavatarati
children.translated_text: Having conquered the eastern direction, he enters the eastern ocean and descends into the eastern ocean.

children.text: pūrvaṃ samudramavatīrya samyageva ṛddhyā vihāyasā dakṣiṇena vrajati
children.translated_text: Having descended into the eastern ocean, he proceeds southward through the sky by his proper miraculous power.

children.text: anveti rājā cakravartī sārdhaṃ caturaṅgeṇa balakāyena
children.translated_text: The <s>cakravartin</s> king follows it together with his fourfold army.

children.text: pūrvavadevaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ vijayati
children.translated_text: Just as before, in this way he conquers the southern direction.

children.text: yathā dakṣiṇāmevaṃ paścimāmuttarāṃ diśaṃ vijayati
children.translated_text: As he conquers the south, so too he conquers the western and northern directions.

children.text: uttarāṃ diśaṃ vijitya uttarasamudramavagāhate
children.translated_text: Having conquered the northern direction, he enters the northern ocean.

children.text: avagāhyottarāt samudrātpratyuttarati
children.translated_text: Having entered it, he emerges again from the northern ocean.

children.text: pratyuttīrya samyageva ṛddhyā vihāyasā rājadhānīmāgatyopari antaḥpuradvāre 'kṣatamevāsthāt
children.translated_text: After emerging, it returns to the royal capital through the sky by its proper miraculous power and comes to rest unharmed above the gate of the inner palace.

children.text: evaṃrūpeṇa rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaścakraratnena samanvāgato bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In this manner the consecrated kṣatriya king is endowed with the wheel-jewel.

children.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī hastiratnena samanvāgato bhavati iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pūrvavaddhastiratnamutpadyate
children.translated_text: In what manner is a <s>cakravartin</s> king endowed with the elephant-jewel? Here, for a consecrated kṣatriya king, the elephant-jewel arises as before.

children.text: sarvaśvetaṃ saptāṅgasupratiṣṭhitaṃ svarṇacūḍakaṃ svarṇadhvajaṃ svarṇālaṃkāraṃ hemajālapraticchannaṃ ṛddhimantaṃ vihāyasā gāminaṃ vikurvaṇādharmiṇaṃ yaduta bodhirnāma nāgarājā
children.translated_text: It is entirely white, well set in its seven limbs, with a golden crest, a golden banner, golden ornaments, covered with a golden net, possessed of miraculous power, able to go through the sky, and subject to transformations: namely, the nāgarāja named <s>Bodhi</s>.

children.text: yadā ca rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktastaddhastiratnaṃ mīmāṃsitukāmo bhavati atha sūryasyābhyudgamanavelāyāṃ taddhastiratnamabhiruhya imāmeva mahāpṛthivīṃ samudraparikhāṃ samudraparyantāṃ samantato 'nvāhiṇḍya rājadhānīmāgatya praśāsanaratiḥ pratyanubhavati
children.translated_text: And when the anointed kṣatriya king wishes to test that elephant-jewel, then, at the time of the sun's rising, he mounts that elephant-jewel, travels all around this very great earth, encircled by the ocean and bounded by the ocean, returns to the royal capital, and experiences the delight of ruling.

children.text: evaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī hastiratnena samanvāgato bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In such a manner the wheel-turning king is endowed with the elephant-jewel.

children.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī aśvaratnena samanvāgato bhavati atha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pūrvavadaśvaratnamutpadyate
children.translated_text: In what manner is the wheel-turning king endowed with the horse-jewel? Then, for the anointed kṣatriya king, as before, the horse-jewel arises.

children.text: sarvanīlaṃ kṛṣṇaśirasaṃ muñjakeśamādṛtavadanaṃ svarṇadhvajaṃ svarṇālaṃkāraṃ hemajālapraticchannaṃ ṛddhimantaṃ vihāyasā gāminaṃ vikurvaṇādharmiṇaṃ yaduta bālāhako nāmāśvarājam
children.translated_text: It is entirely blue, black-headed, with a muñja-like mane, with a pleasing face, with a golden banner, golden ornaments, covered with a golden net, possessed of miraculous power, able to go through the sky, and subject to transformations: namely, the horse-king named <s>Bālāhaka</s>.

children.text: yadā ca rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto 'śvaratnaṃ mīmāṃsitukāmo bhavati atha sūryasyābhyudgamanavelāyām aśvaratnamabhiruhya imāmeva mahāpṛthvīṃ samudraparikhāṃ samudraparyantāṃ samantato 'nvāhiṇḍya rājadhānīmāgatya praśāsanaratiḥ pratyanubhavati
children.translated_text: And when the anointed kṣatriya king wishes to test the horse-jewel, then, at the time of the sun's rising, he mounts the horse-jewel, travels all around this very great earth, encircled by the ocean and bounded by the ocean, returns to the royal capital, and experiences the delight of ruling.

children.text: evaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī aśvaratnena samanvāgato bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In such a manner the wheel-turning king is endowed with the horse-jewel.

children.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī maṇiratnena samanvāgato bhavati iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pūrvavanmaṇiratnamutpadyate śuddhanīlavaiḍūryamaṣṭāṃśaṃ suparikarmakṛtam
children.translated_text: In what manner is the wheel-turning king endowed with the jewel-jewel? Here, for the anointed kṣatriya king, as before, the jewel-jewel arises: a pure blue beryl, eight-sided, finely worked.

children.text: tasya khalu punarmaṇiratnasyābhayā sarvamantaḥpuramavabhāsyena sphuṭaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: By the radiance of that jewel-jewel, moreover, the whole inner palace becomes filled and suffused with light.

children.text: yadā ca rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktastaṃ maṇiratnaṃ mīmāṃsitukāmo bhavati atha rātryāmardharātrasamaye 'ndhakāratamisrāyāṃ taṃ maṇiratnaṃ dhvajāgre ucchrāpayitvā udyānabhūmiṃ niryāti subhūmidarśanāya
children.translated_text: And when the anointed kṣatriya king wishes to test that jewel-jewel, then at night, at midnight, amid deep darkness and gloom, he raises that jewel-jewel on the top of a banner and goes out to the park grounds in order to see the good ground.

children.text: tasya khalu punarmaṇiratnasyābhayā sarvāvantaṃ caturaṅgabalakāyamavabhāsena sphuṭībhavati sāmantena yojanam
children.translated_text: By the radiance of that jewel-jewel, moreover, the entire fourfold army becomes filled and suffused with light for a yojana all around.

children.text: ye khalu punastasya maṇiratnasya sāmantake manuṣyāḥ prativasanti te tenāvabhāsenāsphuṭa samānā anyonyaṃ saṃjānanti anyonyaṃ paśyanti anyonyamāhuḥ uttiṣṭha bhadramukhāḥ karmāntāni kārayata āpaṇāni prasārayata divā manyāmahe sūryamabhyudgatam
children.translated_text: And those people who live in the vicinity of that jewel-jewel, being illuminated by that light, recognize one another, see one another, and say to one another, 'Get up, good sirs; set the work going, open the shops. We think it is day and the sun has risen.'

children.text: evaṃrūpeṇa rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto maṇiratnena samanvāgato bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In such a manner the anointed kṣatriya king is endowed with the jewel-jewel.

children.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī strīratnena samanvāgato bhavati iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pūrvavatstrīratnamutpadyate
children.translated_text: In what manner is the wheel-turning king endowed with the woman-jewel? Here, for the anointed kṣatriya king, as before, the woman-jewel arises.

children.text: sadṛśī kṣatriyā nātidīrghā nātihrasvā nātisthūlā nātikṛśā nātigaurī nātikṛṣṇā abhirūpā prāsādikā darśanīyā
children.translated_text: She is a kṣatriya woman equal to him, neither too tall nor too short, neither too stout nor too thin, neither too fair nor too dark, beautiful, gracious, and lovely to behold.

children.text: tasyāḥ sarvaromakūpebhyaścandanagandhaṃ pravāti mukhāccotpalagandhaṃ pravāti
children.translated_text: From every pore of her body the fragrance of sandalwood wafts forth, and from her mouth the fragrance of blue lotus wafts forth.

children.text: kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśā
children.translated_text: Her touch is pleasant and soft like kācilindika cloth.

children.text: śītalakāle cāsyā uṣṇasaṃsparśāni gātrāṇi bhavanti uṣṇakāle ca śītasaṃsparśāni
children.translated_text: In the cold season her limbs are warm to the touch, and in the hot season they are cool to the touch.

children.text: sā rājānaṃ cakravartinaṃ muktvā nānyasmin manasāpi rāgaṃ karoti kiṃ punaḥ kāyena
children.translated_text: Apart from the wheel-turning king, she feels desire for no other man even in thought, how much less with her body.

children.text: evaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī strīratnena samanvāgato bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In such a manner the wheel-turning king is endowed with the woman-jewel.

children.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī gṛhapatiratnena samanvāgato bhavati iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pūrvavad gṛhapatiratnamutpadyate paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī divyacakṣuḥ
children.translated_text: In what manner is the wheel-turning king endowed with the householder-jewel? Here, for the anointed kṣatriya king, as before, the householder-jewel arises: learned, articulate, intelligent, and possessing the divine eye.

children.text: sa tena divyacakṣuṣā sāmantena yojanaṃ sasvāmikāni nidhānāni paśyati asvāmikāni nidhānāni paśyati
children.translated_text: With that divine eye he sees, for a yojana all around, treasures that have owners and treasures that have no owners.

children.text: sa yāni tāni bhavanti asvāmikāni tai rājñaścakravartino dhanena karaṇīyaṃ karoti
children.translated_text: With those treasures that are ownerless, he performs whatever financial business has to be done for the wheel-turning king.

children.text: evaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī gṛhapatiratnena samanvāgato bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In such a manner the wheel-turning king is endowed with the householder-jewel.

children.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī pariṇāyakaratnena samanvāgato bhavati iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pūrvavatpariṇāyakaratnamutpadyate paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī
children.translated_text: In what manner is the wheel-turning king endowed with the counselor-jewel? Here, for the anointed kṣatriya king, as before, the counselor-jewel arises: learned, articulate, and intelligent.

children.text: rājñaścakravartinaścintitamātreṇa udyojayitavyaṃ senāmudyojayati sma
children.translated_text: Merely when the wheel-turning king has thought of it, he mobilizes the army that is to be mobilized.

children.text: evaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī pariṇāyakaratnena samanvāgato bhavati
children.translated_text: In such a manner the wheel-turning king is endowed with the counselor-jewel.

children.text: ebhiḥ saptaratnaiḥ samanvāgato bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: He will be endowed with these seven jewels.

children.text: bhavati cāsya putrasahasraṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām
children.translated_text: And he will have a thousand sons, brave, heroic, handsome in their noble limbs, and crushers of opposing armies.

children.text: sa imāṃ mahāpṛthivīṃ sasāgaraparyantām akhilām akaṇṭakām adaṇḍenāśastreṇābhinirjityādhyāsayati
children.translated_text: Having conquered this great earth as far as the surrounding ocean, whole and free from thorns, without rod and without weapon, he will dwell upon it as ruler.

children.text: saced agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajiṣyati vāntachandarāgo netā ananyadevaḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: But if he goes forth from the household life into homelessness, he will be one who has cast away desire and passion, a guide dependent on no other deity, a teacher of gods and humans.

children.text: tathā anye 'pi devaputrā jambudvīpamāgatya pratyekabuddhebhya ārocayanti sma riñcata mārṣā buddhakṣetram
children.translated_text: Likewise, other divine sons came to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and announced to the pratyekabuddhas: "Depart, venerable sirs, from the Buddha-field.

children.text: ito dvādaśavatsare bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣimavakramiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Twelve years from now the <s>Bodhisattva</s> will enter his mother's womb."

children.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena rājagṛhe mahānagare golāṅgulaparivartane parvate mātaṅgo nāma pratyekabuddho viharati sma
children.translated_text: Now at that time, monks, in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on the mountain <s>Golāṅgulaparivartana</s>, there lived a pratyekabuddha named <s>Mātaṅga</s>.

children.text: sa taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā kardama iva śilāyāṃ prasthāya vihāyasā saptatālamātram atyudgamya ca tejodhātuṃ samāpadyolkeva parinirvāṇo 'yam
children.translated_text: Hearing that sound, he set out from the rock, like mud, rose up into the air to the height of seven palm trees, entered the fire element, and attained parinirvāṇa like a firebrand.

children.text: yattasya pittaśleṣmasnāyvasthimāṃsarudhiraṃ cāsīt tatsarvaṃ tejasā paryavadānamagacchat
children.translated_text: Whatever bile, phlegm, sinew, bone, flesh, and blood he had, all of it became purified by the fire.

children.text: śuddhaśarīrāṇyeva bhūmau prāpatan
children.translated_text: Only his pure bodily remains fell to the ground.

children.text: adyāpi ca tāni ṛṣipadānyeva saṃjñāyante ||
children.translated_text: Even today these are known as the footprints of the seers.

children.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena vārāṇasyāṃ ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve pañca pratyekabuddhaśatāni viharanti sma
children.translated_text: Now at that time, monks, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> in the <s>Mṛgadāva</s>, five hundred pratyekabuddhas were living.

children.text: te 'pi taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā vihāyasā saptatālamātramatyudgamya tejodhātuṃ samāpadyolkeva parinirvānti sma
children.translated_text: They too, hearing that sound, rose up into the air to the height of seven palm trees, entered the fire element, and attained parinirvāṇa like firebrands.

children.text: yatteṣāṃ pittaśleṣmamāṃsāsthisnāyurudhiraṃ cābhūt tatsarvaṃ tejasā paryavadānamagacchat
children.translated_text: Whatever bile, phlegm, flesh, bone, sinew, and blood they had, all of it became purified by the fire.

children.text: śuddhaśarīrāṇyeva bhūmau prāpatan
children.translated_text: Only their pure bodily remains fell to the ground.

children.text: asminnṛṣayaḥ patitā iti tasmātprabhṛti ṛṣipatanasaṃjñodapādi
children.translated_text: Because seers fell here, from that time onward the name <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, the Fall of the Seers, arose.

children.text: abhayadattāśca tasmin mṛgāḥ prativasanti iti tadagreṇa mṛgadāvasya mṛgadāva iti saṃjñodapādi ||
children.translated_text: And because deer who had been granted fearlessness dwell there, on that account the <s>Mṛgadāva</s> came to be called <s>Mṛgadāva</s>, the Deer Park.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvastuṣitavarabhavanasthitaścatvāri mahāvilokitāni vilokayati sma
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, dwelling in the excellent palace of <s>Tuṣita</s>, observed the four great observations.

children.text: katamāni catvāri tadyathā kālavilokitaṃ dvīpavilokitaṃ deśavilokitaṃ kulavilokitam ||
children.translated_text: What are the four? They are the observation of the time, the observation of the continent, the observation of the region, and the observation of the family.

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ kālavilokitaṃ vilokayati sma na bodhisattva ādipravṛtte loke sattvasaṃvartanīkālasamaye mātuḥ kukṣimavakrāmati atha tarhi yadā vyakto lokaḥ susthito bhavati jāti prajñāyate jarā prajñāyate vyādhi prajñāyate maraṇaṃ prajñāyate tadā bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣimavakrāmati ||
children.translated_text: For what reason, monks, did the <s>Bodhisattva</s> observe the observation of the time? A bodhisattva does not enter his mother's womb when the world is in its first emergence, at the time when beings are coming into formation. Rather, when the world is manifest and well established, when birth is discernible, old age is discernible, disease is discernible, and death is discernible, then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> enters his mother's womb.

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bodhisattvo dvīpavilokitaṃ vilokayati sma na bodhisattvāḥ pratyantadvīpā upapadyante na pūrvavidehe nāparagodānīye na cottarakurau
children.translated_text: For what reason did the <s>Bodhisattva</s> observe the observation of the continent? Bodhisattvas are not born on outlying continents, not in <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, not in <s>Aparagodānīya</s>, and not in <s>Uttarakuru</s>.

children.text: atha tarhi jambudvīpa evopapadyante ||
children.translated_text: Rather, they are born only in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bodhisattvo deśavilokitaṃ vilokayati sma na bodhisattvāḥ pratyantajanapadeṣūpapadyante yeṣu manuṣyā andhajātyā jaḍā eḍamūkajātīyā abhavyāḥ subhāṣitadurbhāṣitānāmarthaṃ jñātum
children.translated_text: For what reason, monks, did the <s>Bodhisattva</s> observe the observation of the region? Bodhisattvas are not born in border countries where people are blind from birth, dull, bleating or mute by nature, and incapable of knowing the meaning of what is well spoken and badly spoken.

children.text: atha tarhi bodhisattvā madhyameṣveva janapadeṣūpapadyante ||
children.translated_text: Rather, bodhisattvas are born only in the central countries.

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ kulavilokitaṃ vilokayati sma na bodhisattvā hīnakuleṣūpapadyante caṇḍālakuleṣu vā veṇukārakule vā rathakārakule vā puṣkasakule vā
children.translated_text: For what reason, monks, did the <s>Bodhisattva</s> observe the observation of the family? Bodhisattvas are not born in low families, whether in families of caṇḍālas, bamboo-workers, cartwrights, or pukkasas.

children.text: atha tarhi kuladvaye evopapadyante brāhmaṇakule kṣatriyakule ca
children.translated_text: Rather, they are born only in two kinds of family: in a brahmin family or in a kṣatriya family.

children.text: tatra yadā brāhmaṇaguruko loko bhavati tadā brāhmaṇakule upapadyante
children.translated_text: There, when the world esteems brahmins as foremost, they are born in a brahmin family.

children.text: yadā kṣatriyaguruko loko bhavati tadā kṣatriyakule upapadyante
children.translated_text: When the world esteems kṣatriyas as foremost, they are born in a kṣatriya family.

children.text: etarhi bhikṣavaḥ kṣatriyaguruko lokaḥ
children.translated_text: At present, monks, the world esteems kṣatriyas as foremost.

children.text: tasmādbodhisattvāḥ kṣatriyakule upapadyante
children.translated_text: Therefore bodhisattvas are born in a kṣatriya family.

children.text: tamarthaṃ ca sampratītya bodhisattvastuṣitavarabhavanasthaścatvāri mahāvilokitāni vilokayati sma ||
children.translated_text: Having considered that matter, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, dwelling in the excellent palace of <s>Tuṣita</s>, observed the four great observations.

children.text: evaṃ cāvalokya tūṣṇīmabhūt
children.translated_text: And having observed in this way, he remained silent.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavaste devaputrāḥ bodhisattvasyānyonyaṃ paripṛcchanti sma katamasmin kularatne kiyadrūpāyāṃ jananyāṃ bodhisattvaḥ pratiṣṭhateti
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, those divine sons asked one another concerning the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: "In what jewel of a family, and in what sort of mother, will the <s>Bodhisattva</s> be established?"

children.text: tatra kecidāhuḥ idaṃ vaidehīkulaṃ magadheṣu janapadeṣu ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ subhikṣaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Among them some said, "This <s>Vaidehī</s> family in the country of the <s>Magadhas</s> is prosperous, flourishing, secure, and well supplied with food.

children.text: idaṃ pratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhasthānam
children.translated_text: This is a suitable place in the womb for this <s>Bodhisattva</s>."

children.text: apare tvāhur na tatpratirūpam
children.translated_text: But others said, "That is not suitable.

children.text: tatkasmāt tathā hi tanna mātṛśuddhaṃ pitṛśuddhaṃ aplutaṃ cañcalamanavasthitaṃ parittapuṇyābhiṣyanditaṃ na vipulapuṇyābhiṣiktaṃ satkulapradeśopacāraṃ nodyānasarastaḍāgākīrṇaṃ karvaṭamiva pratyantavāsam
children.translated_text: Why? For it is not pure on the mother's side or pure on the father's side; it is unstable, fickle, unsettled, flowed over by little merit and not anointed with abundant merit, lacking the attendance of places of good family, not filled with parks, lakes, and ponds, and dwelling on the frontier like a market-town.

children.text: tena na tatpratirūpam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore that is not suitable."

children.text: apare tvāhur idaṃ punaḥ kauśalakulaṃ mahāvāhanaṃ ca mahāparivāraṃ ca mahādhanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Others said, "This <s>Kauśala</s> family, however, has many vehicles, a great retinue, and great wealth.

children.text: tatpratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti
children.translated_text: That is suitable for the establishment of this <s>Bodhisattva</s> in a womb."

children.text: apare 'pyāhuḥ tadapyapratirūpam
children.translated_text: Still others said, "That too is not suitable.

children.text: tatkasmāddhetoḥ tathā hi kauśalakulaṃ mātaṅgacyutyupapannaṃ na mātṛpitṛśuddham
children.translated_text: For what reason? For the <s>Kauśala</s> family has arisen from a fall into a mātaṅga birth and is not pure on the mother's and father's sides.

children.text: hīnādhimuktikaṃ na ca kuloditaṃ na cāparimitadhanaratnanidhisamutthitam
children.translated_text: It has inferior aspirations; it has not risen from noble lineage, nor has it arisen from immeasurable stores of wealth and jewels.

children.text: tena na tatpratirūpam ||
children.translated_text: For that reason it is not suitable.

children.text: apare tvāhuḥ idaṃ vaṃśarājakulaṃ ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca
children.translated_text: But others said, "This royal family of <s>Vaṃśa</s> is rich, flourishing, secure, and well supplied with food.

children.text: idaṃ pratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhasthānamiti
children.translated_text: This is a suitable womb-place for this Bodhisattva."

children.text: apara evamāhuḥ idamapyapratirūpam
children.translated_text: Others said, "This too is unsuitable.

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇam tathāhi vaṃśarājakulaṃ prākṛtaṃ ca caṇḍaṃ ca na cojjvalitatejasaṃ parapuruṣajanmāvṛtaṃ ca na mātṛpitṛsvatejaḥ karmābhinirvṛttaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Why? For the royal family of <s>Vaṃśa</s> is ordinary and fierce, and not radiant in splendor; it is obscured by birth from another man, and is not brought forth by the proper splendor of mother and father, but by karma.

children.text: ucchedavādī ca tatra rājā
children.translated_text: And the king there holds the doctrine of annihilation.

children.text: tena tadapyapratirūpam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore that too is unsuitable."

children.text: apare 'pyāhuḥ iyaṃ vaiśālī mahānagarī ṛddhā ca sphītā ca kṣemā ca subhikṣā ca ramaṇīyā cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyā ca vitardiniryūhatoraṇagavākṣaharmyakūṭāgāraprāsādatalasamalaṃkṛtā ca puṣpavāṭikāvanarājisaṃkusumitā ca amarabhavanapuraprākāśyā
children.translated_text: Others also said, "This great city <s>Vaiśālī</s> is rich, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, delightful, crowded with many people and men, adorned with terraces, gateways, arched portals, windows, mansions, peaked halls, palaces, and floors, full of flower gardens and groves in bloom, and shining like the city of the dwellings of the immortals.

children.text: sā pratirūpāsya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti
children.translated_text: It is suitable for this Bodhisattva's establishment in the womb."

children.text: apara āhuḥ sāpyapratirūpā
children.translated_text: Others said, "It too is unsuitable.

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇam tathā hi teṣāṃ nāsti parasparanyāyavāditā nāsti dharmācaraṇam noccamadhyavṛddhajyeṣṭhānupālitā
children.translated_text: Why? For among them there is no speaking according to mutual justice, no practice of dharma, and no observance of the high, the middle, the elders, and the seniors.

children.text: ekaika eva manyate ahaṃ rājā ahaṃ rājeti
children.translated_text: Each one thinks, 'I am king, I am king.'

children.text: na ca kasyacicchiṣyatvamabhyupagacchati na dharmatvam
children.translated_text: And no one accepts discipleship under anyone, nor the authority of dharma.

children.text: tena sāpyapratirūpā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it too is unsuitable."

children.text: apare tvevamāhuḥ idaṃ pradyotakulaṃ mahābalaṃ ca mahāvāhanaṃ ca paracamūśirasi vijayalabdhaṃ ca
children.translated_text: But others said, "This family of <s>Pradyota</s> has great strength and great forces, and has won victory at the head of an enemy army.

children.text: tatpratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti
children.translated_text: That is suitable for this Bodhisattva's establishment in the womb."

children.text: apare tvevamāhuḥ tadapyapratirūpam
children.translated_text: But others said, "That too is unsuitable.

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇam tathā hi te caṇḍāśca capalāśca raudrāśca paruṣāśca sāhasikāśca na ca karmadarśinaḥ
children.translated_text: Why? For they are fierce, fickle, cruel, harsh, and reckless, and they do not recognize karma.

children.text: tena tadapyapratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore that too is unsuitable for this Bodhisattva's establishment in the womb."

children.text: apara evamāhuḥ iyaṃ mathurā nagarī ṛddhā ca sphītā ca kṣemā ca subhikṣā cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyā ca
children.translated_text: Others said, "This city <s>Mathurā</s> is rich, flourishing, secure, well supplied with food, and crowded with many people and men.

children.text: rājñaḥ subāhoḥ kaṃsakulasya śūraseneśvarasya rājadhāniḥ
children.translated_text: It is the royal capital of King <s>Subāhu</s>, of the family of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, lord of <s>Śūrasena</s>.

children.text: sā pratirūpāsya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti
children.translated_text: It is suitable for this Bodhisattva's establishment in the womb."

children.text: apare tvāhuḥ sāpyapratirūpā
children.translated_text: But others said, "It too is unsuitable.

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇam tathāhi sa rājā mithyādṛṣṭikulavaṃśaprasūto dasyurājā
children.translated_text: Why? For that king was born in a family lineage of wrong view; he is a robber-king.
