children.translated_text: And the flocks of birds dwelling on the king of mountains, <s>Himavat</s>, such as patraguptas, parrots, mynas, cuckoos, geese, curlews, peacocks, cakravākas, kuṇālas, kalaviṅkas, jīvaṃjīvakas, and others, with variegated and beautiful wings and voices delightful and pleasant to hear, came to the excellent house of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>; standing on terraces, balconies, gateways, latticed windows, mansions, upper chambers, and palace roofs, they joyfully, filled with gladness and happiness, uttered their own particular calls.

children.text: iti dvitīyaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt ||
children.translated_text: This was the second preliminary omen that appeared.

children.text: ye ca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyārāmaramaṇīyeṣu vanaramaṇīyeṣu codyānaramaṇīyeṣu nānāpuṣpaphalavṛkṣā nānartukārikāḥ te sarve saṃpuṣpitāḥ saṃkusumitā abhūvan
children.translated_text: And all the various flower and fruit trees, bearing in different seasons, in the delightful parks, delightful woods, and delightful gardens of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, became fully blossomed and flowered.

children.text: idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt ||
children.translated_text: This third portent appeared.

children.text: yāśca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya puṣkariṇyo jalaparibhogyasthāḥ tāḥ sarvāḥ śakaṭacakrapramāṇairanekakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrapatraiḥ padmaiḥ saṃchāditā abhūvan
children.translated_text: And all the lotus ponds of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, places for enjoying water, became covered with lotuses as large as cartwheels, with many koṭis, niyutas, and hundreds of thousands of petals.

children.text: idaṃ caturthaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt ||
children.translated_text: This fourth portent appeared.

children.text: ye ca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhavare bhājanaviṣaye sarpistailamadhuphāṇitaśarkarādyānāṃ te paribhujyamānāḥ kṣayaṃ na gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: And in the excellent house of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, the supplies in the vessels, ghee, oil, honey, molasses, sugar, and the like, though being consumed, did not diminish.

children.text: paripūrṇā eva saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: They were seen to be completely full.

children.text: idaṃ pañcamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt ||
children.translated_text: This fifth portent appeared.

children.text: ye ca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhavarapradhāne mahatyantaḥpure bherīmṛdaṅgapaṇavatūṇavavīṇāveṇuvallakīsaṃpatāḍaprabhṛtayas tūryabhāṇḍāḥ te sarve svayamaghaṭṭitā eva manojñaśabdaṃ muñcanti sma
children.translated_text: And in the chief excellent house of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, in the great inner palace, all the musical instruments, bherīs, mṛdaṅgas, paṇavas, tūṇavas, vīṇās, flutes, vallakīs, cymbals, and the rest, emitted charming sounds by themselves, without being struck.

children.text: idaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt ||
children.translated_text: This sixth portent appeared.

children.text: yāni ca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhavarapradhāne suvarṇarūpyamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālādīnāṃ ratnānāṃ bhājanāni tāni sarvāṇi niravaśeṣaṃ vivṛtavimalaviśuddhaparipūrṇānyevaṃ virocante sma
children.translated_text: And in the chief excellent house of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, all the vessels of gold, silver, jewels, pearls, beryl, conch, stone, coral, and other treasures shone completely opened, spotless, pure, and full.

children.text: idaṃ saptamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt ||
children.translated_text: This seventh portent appeared.

children.text: vimalaviśuddhayā candrasūryajihmīkaraṇayā prabhayā kāyacittodbilyasaṃjananyā tadgṛhaṃ samantādavabhāsitamabhūt
children.translated_text: That house was illuminated all around by a spotless, pure radiance that dimmed the moon and sun and produced exhilaration in body and mind.

children.text: idamaṣṭamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt ||
children.translated_text: This eighth portent appeared.

children.text: māyā ca devī snātānuliptagātrā vividhābharaṇaviṣkambhitabhujā suślakṣṇasulīlavastravaradhāriṇī prītiprāmodyaprasādapratilabdhā sārdhaṃ daśabhiḥ strīsahasraiḥ parivṛtā puraskṛtā rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya saṃgītiprāsāde sukhopaviṣṭasyāntikamupasaṃkramya dakṣiṇe pārśve ratnajālapratyupte bhadrāsane niṣadya smitamukhī vyapagatabhṛkuṭikā prahasitavadanā rājānaṃ śuddhodanamābhirgāthābhirabhāṣat
children.translated_text: And Queen <s>Māyā</s>, her body bathed and anointed, her arms set off by many ornaments, wearing fine, graceful, excellent garments, and filled with joy, gladness, and serenity, surrounded and preceded by ten thousand women, approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> as he sat comfortably in the music palace. Sitting on his right side upon an auspicious seat inlaid with a jeweled lattice, smiling, free from frowning, and with a laughing face, she addressed King <s>Śuddhodana</s> with these verses:

children.text: sādho śṛṇuṣva mama pārthiva bhūmipālā yācāmi te nṛpatiradya varaṃ prayaccha
children.translated_text: "Good sir, listen to me, earthly lord, protector of the earth. I ask you, king; grant me a boon today.

children.text: abhiprāyu mahya yatha cittamanaḥpraharṣaṃ tanme śṛṇuṣva bhava prītamanā udagraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hear my intention, in accord with the delight of my heart and mind; be pleased and uplifted.

children.text: gṛhṇāmi deva vrataśīlavaropavāsaṃ aṣṭāṅgapoṣadhamahaṃ jagi maitracittā
children.translated_text: Lord, I undertake the excellent fast of vow and morality, the eightfold poṣadha, with a mind of loving-kindness toward the world.

children.text: prāṇeṣu hiṃsaviratā sada śuddhabhāvā premaṃ yathātmani pareṣu tathā karomi ||
children.translated_text: Abstaining from injury to living beings, always pure in disposition, I show love to others as to myself.

children.text: stainyādvivarjitamanā madalobhahīnā kāmeṣu mithya nṛpate na samācariṣye
children.translated_text: With a mind free from theft, without intoxication and greed, I shall not act wrongly with respect to sensual pleasures, O king.

children.text: satye sthitā apiśunā paruṣaprahīṇā saṃdhipralāpamaśubhaṃ na samācariṣye ||
children.translated_text: Standing in truth, not slanderous, having abandoned harsh speech, I shall not engage in unwholesome idle talk.

children.text: vyāpādadoṣakhilamohamadaprahīṇā sarvā abhidhya vigatā svadhanena tuṣṭā
children.translated_text: Having abandoned malice, fault, hardness, delusion, and pride, wholly free from covetousness, content with my own wealth,

children.text: samyakprayukta akuhānilayā anirṣyu karmā yathā daśa ime kuśalā cariṣye ||
children.translated_text: rightly disciplined, not dwelling in deceit, without envy, I shall practice these ten wholesome actions.

children.text: mā tvaṃ narendra mayi kāmatṛṣāṃ kuruṣva śīlavrateṣvabhiratāya susaṃvṛtāya
children.translated_text: Do not direct sensual craving toward me, king of men, when I delight in the vows of morality and am well restrained.

children.text: mā te apuṇya nṛpate bhavi dīrgharātramanumodayā hi mama śīlavratopavāsam ||
children.translated_text: Let no demerit be yours for a long time, O king; rather, rejoice in my morality, vow, and fast.

children.text: chando mameṣa nṛpate praviśādya śīghraṃ prāsādaharmyaśikhare sthita dhārtarāṣṭre
children.translated_text: This is my wish, O king: today let me quickly enter the palace mansion's upper pavilion, O sustainer of the realm.

children.text: sakhibhiḥ sadā parivṛtā sukha modayeyaṃ puṣpābhikīrṇaśayane mṛduke sugandhe ||
children.translated_text: Always surrounded by my friends, I would happily rejoice on a soft, fragrant bed strewn with flowers.

children.text: na ca kāñcukīya puruṣā na pi dārakāśca na ca istri prākṛta mamā purataḥ sthiheyā
children.translated_text: No chamberlain men, nor boys, nor ordinary women should stand before me.

children.text: no cāmanāpa mama rūpa na śabdagandhān nānyatra iṣṭamadhurā śṛṇuyā suśabdān ||
children.translated_text: Nor should any unpleasant form, sound, or smell come before me; I should hear only pleasing, sweet, beautiful sounds.

children.text: ye rodhabandhanagatāḥ parimuñca sarvān dravyāmbarāśca puruṣāndhaninaḥ kuruṣva
children.translated_text: Release all who are held in prisons and bonds; make men rich with goods and garments.

children.text: vastrānnapāna rathayugya tathāśvayānaṃ dada saptarātrikamidaṃ jagataḥ sukhārtham ||
children.translated_text: Give clothing, food, drink, chariots with teams, and horse mounts for seven nights, for the happiness of the world.

children.text: no co vivādakalahā na ca roṣavākyā cānyonyamaitramanaso hitasaumyacittā
children.translated_text: Let there be no disputes, quarrels, or angry words; let people have minds of mutual friendliness and hearts that are kind and gentle.

children.text: asmin pure puruṣa iṣṭika dārakāśca devāśca nandanagatā sahitā ramantām ||
children.translated_text: In this city, may men, women, and children, and the gods gone to <s>Nandana</s>, rejoice together.

children.text: na ca rājadaṇḍanabhaṭā na tathā kudaṇḍā notpīḍanā na pi ca tarjanatāḍanā vā
children.translated_text: Let there be no royal punitive soldiers, no improper punishments, no oppression, and no threatening or beating.

children.text: sarvān prasannamanaso hitamaitracitta vīkṣasva deva janatāṃ yatha ekaputram ||
children.translated_text: With a clear mind and a heart of kindness and benevolence, lord, look upon all the people as upon an only son."

children.text: śrutvaiva rāja vacanaṃ paramaṃ udagraṃ prāhāstu sarvamidameva yathā tavecchā
children.translated_text: As soon as the king heard her words, he was supremely uplifted and said, "Let all this be exactly according to your wish.

children.text: abhiprāyu tubhya manasā svanucintitāni yadyācase tava varaṃ tadahaṃ dadāmi ||
children.translated_text: Whatever intentions you have well considered in your mind, whatever boon you ask for, that I give you."

children.text: ājñāpyaḥ pārthivavaraḥ svakapāriṣadyāṃ prāsādaśreṣṭhaśikhare prakarotha ṛddhim
children.translated_text: Having given orders to his own retinue, the best of kings caused splendor to be prepared on the summit of the finest palace:

children.text: puṣpābhikīrṇaruciraṃ varadhūpagandhaṃ chatrāpatākasamalaṃkṛtatālapaṃktim ||
children.translated_text: beautiful with scattered flowers, fragrant with excellent incense, with rows of palm-columns adorned with parasols and banners.

children.text: viṃśatsahasra raṇaśoṇḍa vicitravarmāṃ nārācaśūlaśaraśaktigṛhītakhaṅgāḥ
children.translated_text: Twenty thousand warriors, fierce in battle, in variegated armor, holding swords, iron arrows, spears, arrows, and lances...

children.text: parivārayātha dhṛtarājyamanojñaghoṣaṃ devyā 'bhayārtha karuṇāsthita rakṣamāṇā ||
children.translated_text: Surround him with the pleasing sound of <s>Dhṛtarājya</s>; protecting him for the queen's fearlessness, stand established in compassion.

children.text: strībhistu sā parivṛtā yatha devakanyā snātānuliptapravarāmbarabhūṣitāṅgī
children.translated_text: Surrounded by those women, she was like a divine maiden, her body bathed, anointed, and adorned with excellent garments and ornaments.

children.text: tūryaiḥ sahasramanugītamanojñaghoṣaiḥ āruhya devyupaviveśa marutsnuṣeva ||
children.translated_text: With a thousand musical instruments following her with delightful sounds in song, the queen mounted it and sat down, as though she were a bride of the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: divyairmahārthasuvicitrasuratnapādaiḥ svāstīrṇapuṣpavividhaiḥ śayane manojñe
children.translated_text: On a lovely couch with divine, costly, variegated legs of excellent jewels, well spread and strewn with many kinds of flowers,

children.text: śayane sthitā vigalitā maṇiratnacūḍā yatha miśrakāvanagatā khalu devakanyā ||
children.translated_text: she remained upon the couch, her crest of jewels and gems loosened, just like a divine maiden who had gone into the <s>Miśraka</s> grove.

children.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaścatvāro mahārājānaḥ śakraśca devānāmindraḥ suyāmaśca devaputraḥ saṃtuṣitaśca sunirmitaśca paranirmitavaśavartī ca sārthavāhaśca māraputrabrahmā ca sahāṃpatirbrahmottaraśca purohitaḥ subrahmā ca purohitaḥ prabhāvyūhābhāsvaraśca maheśvaraśca śuddhāvāsakāyikā niṣṭhāgataścākaniṣṭhaśca etāni cānyāni cānekāni devaśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatya anyonyamevāhur ayuktametanmārṣā asmākaṃ syādakṛtajñatā ca yadvayamekākinamadvitīyaṃ bodhisattvamutsṛjema
children.translated_text: Then, monks, the Four Great Kings, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, the divine son <s>Suyāma</s>, <s>Saṃtuṣita</s>, <s>Sunirmita</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Sārthavāha</s>, the son of <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Brahmottara</s>, the priest <s>Subrahmā</s>, the priest <s>Prabhāvyūhābhāsvara</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, and the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>-bodied gods, <s>Niṣṭhāgata</s> and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, together with these and many other hundreds of thousands of gods, assembled and said to one another, "Sirs, it would be improper for us, and would be ingratitude, if we were to abandon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, alone and without a second."

children.text: ko 'smākaṃ mārṣā utsahate bodhisattvaṃ satatasamitam anubaddhum avakramaṇagarbhasthānajanmayauvanabhūmidārakakrīḍāntaḥpuranāṭakasaṃdarśanābhiniṣkramaṇaduṣkaracaryābodhimaṇḍopasaṃkramaṇamāradharṣaṇabodhyabhisaṃbodhanadharmacakrapravartanaṃ yāvanmahāparinirvāṇāddhitacittatayā snigdhacittatayā priyacittatayā maitracittatayā saumyacittatayā tasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata
children.translated_text: "Which of us, sirs, is able constantly and continually to accompany the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a mind for his welfare, with affectionate, loving, friendly, and gentle thought, from his descent, dwelling in the womb, birth, youth, stage of boyish play, displays of entertainments in the inner apartments, renunciation, difficult practice, approach to the seat of awakening, defeat of <s>Māra</s>, complete awakening to bodhi, turning of the wheel of <s>dharma</s> (teaching), all the way to the great parinirvāṇa?" At that time they spoke these verses:

children.text: ko votsaheta vararūpadharam anubandhayituṃ satataṃ prītamanāḥ
children.translated_text: Who would be able, with a joyful mind, always to follow the bearer of supreme beauty?

children.text: kaḥ puṇyateja yaśasā vacasā svayamātmanecchati vibaddhayitum ||
children.translated_text: Who, by merit, splendor, fame, speech, and his own self, desires to be bound to him?

children.text: yasyepsitaṃ tridaśadevapure divyaiḥ sukhairhi ramituṃ satatam
children.translated_text: He who desires always to delight in the city of the thirty-three gods, with divine pleasures,

children.text: paramāpsarobhiriha kāmaguṇaiḥ anubaddhitāṃ vimalacandramukham ||
children.translated_text: with the finest apsarases and the objects of desire here, should follow him whose face is like the stainless moon.

children.text: tatha miśrake vanavare rucire divyākare ramitu devapure
children.translated_text: So too, whoever desires to delight in the lovely excellent <s>Miśraka</s> grove, in the divine mine of jewels, in the city of the gods,

children.text: puṣpotkare kanakacūrṇanime anubandhatāṃ vimalatejadharam ||
children.translated_text: amid heaps of flowers and what appears like powdered gold, should follow the bearer of stainless splendor.

children.text: yasyepsitaṃ ramituḥ citrarathe tatha nandane suravadhūsahitaḥ
children.translated_text: He who desires to delight in <s>Citraratha</s>, and likewise in <s>Nandana</s>, together with the women of the gods,

children.text: māndāravaiḥ kusumapatracite anubandhatāmimu mahāpuruṣam ||
children.translated_text: amid flowers and petals of māndārava blossoms, should follow this great person.

children.text: yāmādhipatyamatha vā tuṣitairatha vāpi prārthayati ceśvaratām
children.translated_text: If one seeks lordship over the <s>Yāma</s> gods, or sovereignty among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods,

children.text: pūjāraho bhavitu sarvajage anubandhatāmimu anantayaśam ||
children.translated_text: or to become worthy of worship in the whole world, let him follow this one of endless fame.

children.text: yo icchati nirmitapure rucire vaśavartidevabhavane ramitum
children.translated_text: Whoever wishes to delight in the lovely city of the created gods, in the mansions of the gods who control others' creations,

children.text: manasaiva sarvamanubhoktikriyā anubandhatāmimu guṇāgradharam ||
children.translated_text: where every enjoyment is accomplished by mind alone, should follow this bearer of the foremost virtues.

children.text: māreśvaro na ca praduṣṭamanā sarvavidhaiśvaryapāragataḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Māra</s>, not ill-minded, having reached the far shore of every kind of sovereignty,

children.text: kāmeśvaro vaśitapāragato gacchatvasau hitakareṇa saha ||
children.translated_text: the lord of desires, having reached mastery's far shore, should go together with this benefactor.

children.text: tatha kāmadhātu samatikramituṃ mati yasya brahmapuramāvasitum
children.translated_text: Likewise, whoever has the intention to pass beyond the desire realm and to dwell in the city of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: caturapramāṇaprabhatejadharaḥ so 'dyānubaddhatu mahāpuruṣam ||
children.translated_text: bearing the splendid radiance of the four immeasurables, should today follow the great person.

children.text: atha vāpi yasya manujeṣu mati varacakravartiviṣaye vipule
children.translated_text: Or again, whoever has his mind set among humans on the vast realm of a supreme wheel-turning king,

children.text: ratnākaramabhayasaukhyadadam anubandhatāṃ vipulapuṇyadharam ||
children.translated_text: a treasury of jewels, giver of fearlessness and happiness, should follow the bearer of vast merit.

children.text: pṛthivīśvarastatha pi śreṣṭhisuto āḍhyo mahādhanu mahānicayaḥ
children.translated_text: So too, the lord of the earth, the merchant's son, wealthy, with great riches and a great store of treasure,

children.text: parivāravānnihataśatrugaṇo gacchatvasau hitakareṇa saha ||
children.translated_text: surrounded by retainers and with his hosts of enemies destroyed, should go together with this benefactor.

children.text: rūpaṃ ca bhogamapi ceśvaratā kīrtiryaśaśca balatā guṇavatī
children.translated_text: Beauty, enjoyment, sovereignty, renown, fame, strength, and virtuous excellence,

children.text: ādeyavākya bhavi grāhyaruto brahmeśvaraṃ samupayātu vidum ||
children.translated_text: speech that is accepted and a voice that is heeded: let one approach the wise one, lordly as <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: ye divya kāma tatha mānuṣakāṃ yo icchatī tribhavi sarvasukham
children.translated_text: Whoever desires divine pleasures, and human ones as well, and every happiness in the threefold existence,

children.text: dhyāne sukhaṃ ca pravivekasukhaṃ dharmeśvaraṃ samanubandhayatām ||
children.translated_text: the happiness of meditation and the happiness of seclusion, should follow the lord of <s>dharma</s> (teaching).

children.text: rāgaprahāṇu tatha doṣamapī yo icchate tatha kileśajaham
children.translated_text: Whoever desires the abandonment of passion and also of hatred, and the destruction of defilements,

children.text: śānta praśānta upaśāntamanā so dāntacittamanuyātu laghum ||
children.translated_text: peaceful, very peaceful, tranquil in mind, should quickly follow him whose mind is tamed.

children.text: śaikṣā aśaikṣa tatha pratyekajinā sarvajñajñānamanuprāpuritum
children.translated_text: Those who wish to attain the knowledge of a learner, of one beyond training, of a pratyekajina, and of the omniscient,

children.text: daśabhirbalairnaditu siṃha iva guṇasāgaraṃ samanuyātu vidum ||
children.translated_text: and to roar like a lion with the ten powers, should follow the wise ocean of virtues.

children.text: pithituṃ apāyapatha yeṣa matir vivṛtuṃ ca ṣaṅgatipathaṃ hyamṛtam
children.translated_text: Those whose intention is to close the path to the bad destinies and to open the deathless path of the six destinies,

children.text: aṣṭāṅgamārgagamanena gatim anubandhatāṃ gatipathāntakaram ||
children.translated_text: should, by traveling the eightfold path, follow the one who makes an end of the path of rebirth.

children.text: yo icchate sugata pūjayituṃ dharmaṃ ca teṣu śrutikāruṇike
children.translated_text: Whoever desires to worship the <s>Sugata</s>, and the <s>dharma</s> (teaching), merciful to those who hear it,

children.text: prāpto guṇānapi ca saṃghagatān guṇasāgaraṃ samanuyātu imam ||
children.translated_text: and also to obtain the virtues belonging to the <s>saṃgha</s> (community), should follow this ocean of virtues.

children.text: jātijarāmaraṇaduḥkhakṣaye saṃsārabandhana vimokṣayitum
children.translated_text: Whoever desires the destruction of the suffering of birth, old age, and death, and release from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence),

children.text: carituṃ viśuddhagamanāntasamaṃ so śuddhasattvamanubandhayatām ||
children.translated_text: and to practice the pure course equal to the final goal, should follow this pure being.

children.text: iṣṭo manāpa priyu sarvajage varalakṣaṇo varaguṇopacitaḥ
children.translated_text: Dear, pleasing, and beloved to the whole world, endowed with the finest marks and accumulated supreme virtues,

children.text: ātmā paraṃ ca tatha mocayituṃ priyadarśanaṃ samupayātu vidum ||
children.translated_text: whoever wishes to free himself and others as well should approach the wise one who is lovely to behold.

children.text: śīlaṃ samādhi tatha prajñamayī gambhīradurdaśaduropagamam
children.translated_text: Morality, concentration, and wisdom, profound, hard to see, and hard to approach,

children.text: yo icchate vidu vimukti labhe so vaidyarājamanuyātu laghum ||
children.translated_text: whoever desires to know and obtain liberation should quickly follow the king of physicians.

children.text: ete ca anya guṇa naikavidhā upapatti saukhya tatha nirvṛtiye
children.translated_text: And these many other kinds of virtues are for the happiness of rebirth and likewise for <s>nirvṛti</s> (release).

children.text: sarvairguṇebhi pratipūrṇa siddhaye siddhavrataṃ samanuyātu vidum ||
children.translated_text: For the accomplishment that is complete with all virtues, let the wise one follow the perfected vow.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: idaṃ khalu vacanaṃ śrutvā caturaśītisahasrāṇi cāturmahārājikānāṃ devānāṃ śatasahasraṃ trayatriṃśānāṃ śatasahasraṃ yāmānāṃ śatasahasraṃ tuṣitānāṃ śatasahasraṃ nirmāṇaratīnāṃ śatasahasraṃ paranirmitavaśavartīnāṃ devānāṃ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi mārakāyikānāṃ pūrvaśubhakarmaniryātānāṃ aṣṭaṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi brahmakāyikānāṃ bahūni śatasahasrāṇi yāvadakaniṣṭhānāṃ devānāṃ saṃnipatitānyabhūvan
children.translated_text: Having heard this statement, eighty-four thousand gods of the Four Great Kings, a hundred thousand <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, a hundred thousand <s>Yāma</s> gods, a hundred thousand <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, a hundred thousand <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, a hundred thousand <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, sixty thousand beings of <s>Māra</s>'s company, brought forth by former wholesome actions, sixty-eight thousand gods of the <s>Brahmā</s> host, and many hundreds of thousands of gods as far as <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> had assembled.

children.text: anye ca bhūyaḥ pūrvadakṣiṇapaścimottarebhyo digbhyo bahūni devaśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitānyabhūvan
children.translated_text: And still more, many hundreds of thousands of gods assembled from the eastern, southern, western, and northern directions.

children.text: tebhyo ye udāratamā devaputrāste tāṃ mahatīṃ devaparṣadaṃ gāthābhirabhyabhāṣantaḥ
children.translated_text: The most exalted divine sons among them addressed that great divine assembly with verses:

children.text: hanta śṛṇotha vacanaṃ amareśvarāho asmin vidhānamati yādṛśatatvabhūtā
children.translated_text: Come, listen to this word, O lords of the immortals; in this matter the intention is just as it truly is.

children.text: tyaktārthikāmarati dhyānasukhaṃ praṇītam anubandhayāma imamuttamaśuddhasattvam ||
children.translated_text: Let us abandon delight in wealth and sensual pleasure, and even the excellent bliss of meditation, and follow this supreme pure being.

children.text: okrāntapāda tatha garbhasthitaṃ mahātmaṃ pūjārahaṃ atiśayamabhipūjayāmaḥ
children.translated_text: When the great-souled one has descended and is thus abiding in the womb, let us worship, in surpassing measure, the one worthy of worship.

children.text: puṇyaiḥ surakṣitamṛṣiṃ parirakṣisanto yasyāvatāra labhate na manaḥ praduṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: Wishing to guard the seer who is protected by merit, we shall guard him, for a defiled mind gains no access to his descent.

children.text: saṃgītitūryaracitaiśca suvādyakaiśca varṇāguṇāṃ kathayato guṇasāgarasya
children.translated_text: With well-played instruments and music arranged in concert, proclaiming the colors and virtues of the ocean of virtues,

children.text: kurvāma devamanujāna praharṣaṇīyaṃ yaṃ śrutva bodhivaracitta jane janeryā ||
children.translated_text: let us make something gladdening for gods and humans, hearing which the excellent thought of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) may arise among people.

children.text: puṣpābhikīrṇa nṛpateśca karoma gehaṃ kālāgurūttamasudhūpitasaumyagandham
children.translated_text: Let us make the king's house strewn with flowers, gently fragrant, and well fumigated with the finest black aloe.

children.text: yaṃ ghrātva devamanujāśca bhavantyudagrā vigatajvarāśca sukhinaśca bhavantyarogāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Smelling that, gods and humans become uplifted, free from fever, happy, and without illness.

children.text: māndāravaiśca kusumaistatha pārijātaiścandraiḥ sucandra tatha sthālavirocamānaiḥ
children.translated_text: With <s>māndārava</s> blossoms, with <s>pārijāta</s> flowers, and with shining flowers called <s>candra</s>, <s>sucandra</s>, and <s>sthāla</s>,

children.text: puṣpābhikīrṇa kapilāhvaya taṃ karoma pūjārtha pūrvaśubhakarmasamudgatasya ||
children.translated_text: let us make that place called <s>Kapila</s> strewn with flowers for the worship of the one arisen from former wholesome action.

children.text: yāvacca garbhi vasate trimalairalipto yāvajjarāmaraṇa cāntakaraḥ prasūtaḥ
children.translated_text: As long as he dwells in the womb, unstained by the three impurities, until he is born as the one who will end old age and death,

children.text: tāvatprasannamanaso anubandhayāma eṣā matirmatidharasya karoma pūjām ||
children.translated_text: for so long let us follow with serene minds. This is our thought; let us perform worship for the bearer of wisdom.

children.text: lābhā sulabdha vipulāḥ suramānuṣāṇāṃ drakṣyanti jānu imu saptapadāṃ kramantam
children.translated_text: Great and well gained are the gains of gods and humans: they will see this one, newly born, walking seven steps,

children.text: śakraiśca brahmaṇakaraiḥ parigṛhyamānaṃ gandhodakaiḥ snapiyamāni suśuddhasattvam ||
children.translated_text: the supremely pure being held by the hands of <s>Śakras</s> and <s>Brahmās</s> and bathed with scented waters.

children.text: yāvacca loki anuvartanatāṃ karoti antaḥpure vasati kāmakileśaghātī
children.translated_text: As long as he acts in conformity with the world and dwells in the women's quarters, though he is the destroyer of the defilements of desire,

children.text: yāvacca niṣkramati rājyamapāsya sarvaṃ tāvatprasannamanaso anubandhayāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and as long as he goes forth, casting away the entire kingdom, for so long let us follow with serene minds.

children.text: yāvadupaiti mahimaṇḍi tṛṇāṃ gṛhītvā yāvacca bodhi spṛśate vinihatya māram
children.translated_text: Until he approaches the great circle of earth, taking up grass, and until he touches <s>bodhi</s> after defeating <s>Māra</s>,

children.text: adhyeṣṭu brāhmaṇayutebhi pravarti cakraṃ tāvatkaroma vipulāṃ sugatasya pūjām ||
children.translated_text: and, entreated by <s>Brahmā</s> together with multitudes, turns the wheel, until then let us perform abundant worship for the <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: yada buddhakāryu kṛtu bheṣyati trisahasre sattvāna koṭinayutā amṛte vinītā
children.translated_text: When he will have done the work of a Buddha in the three-thousandfold world, and crores and nayutas of beings have been guided to immortality,

children.text: nirvāṇamārgamupayāsyati śītibhāvaṃ tāvanmahāśayamṛṣiṃ na jahāma sarve ||
children.translated_text: and when he will approach the path of <s>nirvāṇa</s> and cool peace, until then we all shall not abandon the great-hearted seer.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ kāmadhātvīśvarāṇāṃ devakanyānāṃ bodhisattvasya rūpakāyapariniṣpattiṃ dṛṣṭvā etadabhavat kīdṛśī tvasau kanyā bhaviṣyati yā imaṃ varapravaraśuddhasattvaṃ dhārayiṣyati
children.translated_text: Then, monks, when the divine maidens belonging to the lords of the desire realm saw the perfection of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s bodily form, this occurred to them: "What kind of woman will she be who will bear this excellent, supreme, pure being?"

children.text: tāḥ kautūhalajātā varapravarapuṣpadhūpadīpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaraparigṛhītā divyamanomayātmabhāvapratilabdhāḥ puṇyavipākādhisthānādhisthitāḥ tasmin kṣaṇe 'marapurabhavanādantarhitāḥ kapilāhvaye mahāpuravare udyānaśatasahasraparimaṇḍite rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhe dhṛtarāṣṭre mahāprāsāde amarabhavanaprakāśe vigalitāmbaradhāriṇyaḥ śubhavimalatejapratimaṇḍitā divyābharaṇastambhitabhujāḥ śayanavaragatāṃ māyādevīmekāṅgulikayopadarśayantyo gaganatalagatāḥ parasparaṃ gāthābhirabhyabhāṣanta
children.translated_text: Filled with curiosity, holding the finest flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, garlands, unguents, powders, and garments, having obtained divine mind-made bodies and being sustained by the support of the ripening of merit, at that moment they vanished from the palace of the city of the immortals. In the excellent great city called <s>Kapila</s>, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of parks, in the house of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, in the great palace <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, shining like the abode of the immortals, wearing loosened garments, adorned with pure stainless radiance, their arms weighted with divine ornaments, they stood in the sky, pointed out with one finger <s>Māyādevī</s> lying on the excellent couch, and addressed one another with verses.

children.text: amarapuragatāna apsarāṇāṃ rūpa manorama dṛṣṭva bodhisattve
children.translated_text: Having seen the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s form, delightful to the apsarases who dwell in the city of the immortals,

children.text: matiriyamabhavattadā hi tāsāṃ pramada nu kīdṛśa bodhisattvamātā ||
children.translated_text: this thought then arose among them: "What kind of lovely woman is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother?"

children.text: tāśca sahitapuṣpamālyahastā upagami veśma nṛpasya jātakāṅkṣā
children.translated_text: And they, all together, with flowers and garlands in their hands, eager for the birth, approached the king's house.

children.text: puṣpa tatha vilepanāṃ gṛhītvā daśanakhaañjalibhirnamasyamānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Taking flowers and unguents, they bowed with joined palms, their ten nails together.

children.text: vigalitavasanāḥ salīlarūpāḥ karatala dakṣiṇi aṅgulīṃ praṇamya
children.translated_text: Their garments slipping, graceful in form, they bent the finger of the right hand with the palm,

children.text: śayanagata vidarśi māyadevīṃ sādhu nirīkṣatha rūpa mānuṣīṇām ||
children.translated_text: and pointed out <s>Māyādevī</s> lying on the couch: "Look well at the beauty of human women."

children.text: vayamiha abhimanyayāma anye paramamanorama surūpa apsarāṇām
children.translated_text: Here we suppose ourselves, the apsarases, to have supremely charming and beautiful forms, better than others;

children.text: ima nṛpativadhūṃ nirīkṣamāṇā jihma vipaśyatha divya ātmabhāvām ||
children.translated_text: but as you gaze at this bride of the king, see how crookedly we view our own divine bodies.

children.text: ratiriva sadṛśī guṇānvitā ca jananiriyaṃ pravarāgrapudgalasya
children.translated_text: She is like <s>Rati</s> herself and endowed with virtues; this is the mother of the foremost and highest person.

children.text: maṇiratana yathā subhājanastha tatha iva bhājana devi devadeve ||
children.translated_text: Just as a jewel-gem rests in a fine vessel, so this goddess is the vessel for the god of gods.

children.text: karacaraṇatalebhi yāvadūrdhvaṃ aṅga mahorama divya ātirekāḥ
children.translated_text: From the palms of her hands and the soles of her feet upward, her limbs were very delightful, divine, and surpassing.

children.text: prekṣatu nayanānna cāsti tṛptiṃ bhūya praharṣati citta mānasaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: One does not find satisfaction in looking at her with the eyes; again and again the heart and mind are filled with joy.

children.text: śaśiriva gagane virājate 'syā vadanu varaṃ ca virāja gātrabhāsā
children.translated_text: Her excellent face shines like the moon in the sky, and it gleams with the radiance of her body.

children.text: raviriva vimalā śaśīva dīptā tatha prabha niścarate 'sya ātmabhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Like the sun, spotless, and shining like the moon, such radiance issues from her own body.

children.text: kanakamiva sujātajātarūpā varṇa virocati deviye tathaiva
children.translated_text: Her complexion shines just like well-formed refined gold, O divine lady.

children.text: bhramaravaranikāśa kuntalānī mṛdukasugandhaśravāsya mūrdhajāni ||
children.translated_text: Her locks resemble the finest black bees; the hair of her head is soft and sweetly fragrant.

children.text: kamaladalanibhe tathāsya netre daśanaviśuddha nabheva jyotiṣāṇi
children.translated_text: Her eyes are like lotus petals, and her pure teeth are like the lights in the sky.

children.text: cāpa iva tanūdarī viśālā pārśva samudgata māṃsi nāsti saṃdhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Slender-bellied like a bow, broad at the sides, her flesh rises smoothly, and no joints are seen.

children.text: gajabhujasadṛśe 'sya ūrujaṅghe jānu sujātvanupūrvamudgatāsya
children.translated_text: Her thighs and shanks are like an elephant's trunk; her knees are well formed and rise in proper order.

children.text: karatalacaraṇā samā suraktā vyaktamiyaṃ khalu devakanya nānyā ||
children.translated_text: Her palms and feet are even and deeply red; clearly she is a divine maiden and no other.

children.text: eva bahuvidhaṃ nirīkṣya devīṃ kusuma kṣipitva pradakṣiṇaṃ ca kṛtvā
children.translated_text: Having looked upon the queen in many ways, scattered flowers, and circumambulated her,

children.text: supiya yaśavatī jinasya mātā punarapi devapuraṃ gatā kṣaṇena ||
children.translated_text: the beloved, renowned mother of the <s>Jina</s> again went to the city of the gods in an instant.

children.text: atha caturi caturdiśāsu pālāḥ śakra suyāma tathaiva nirmitāśca
children.translated_text: Then the four guardians in the four directions, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Suyāma</s>, and the <s>Nirmita</s> gods as well,

children.text: devagaṇa kumbhāṇḍa rākṣasāśca asura mahoraga kinnarāśca vocan ||
children.translated_text: the hosts of gods, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s>, said:

children.text: gacchata purato narottamasya puruṣavarasya karotha rakṣaguptim
children.translated_text: "Go before the best of men, the supreme person, and provide protection and guarding.

children.text: mā kuruta jage manaḥpradoṣaṃ mā ca karota viheṭha mānuṣāṇām ||
children.translated_text: Do not produce mental hostility in the world, and do not cause harm to human beings.

children.text: yatra gṛhavarasmi māyadevī tatra samagra sapāriṣadya sarve
children.translated_text: Where <s>Māyādevī</s> is in the excellent house, there all of you, together with your retinues,

children.text: asidhanuśaraśaktikhaṅgahastā gaganatalasmi sthitā nirīkṣayātha ||
children.translated_text: holding swords, bows, arrows, spears, and blades in your hands, should stand in the sky and keep watch."

children.text: jñātva cyavanakāla devaputrā upagami māyasakāśa hṛṣṭacittā
children.translated_text: Knowing the time of descent, the divine sons approached <s>Māyā</s>, their minds joyful,

children.text: puṣpa tatha vilepanāṃ gṛhītvā daśanakhaañjalibhirnamasyamānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: carrying flowers and unguents, and bowing with their ten-nailed joined palms.

children.text: cyava cyava hi narendra śuddhasattvā ayu samayo bhavato 'dya vādisiṃha
children.translated_text: "Descend, descend, lord of men, pure being; today is your time, lion among speakers.

children.text: kṛpakaruṇa janitva sarvaloke asmi adhyeṣama dharmadānahetoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having generated pity and compassion for the whole world, we invite you here for the sake of the gift of the <s>dharma</s> (teaching)."

children.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvasya cyavanakālasamaye pūrvasyā diśo bahūni bodhisattvaśatasahasrāṇi sarva ekajātipratibaddhāstuṣitavarabhavanavāsino yena bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāman bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe
children.translated_text: Then, monks, at the time of the Bodhisattva's descent, many hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas from the eastern direction, all bound to one more birth and dwelling in the excellent palace of <s>Tuṣita</s>, approached the Bodhisattva in order to perform worship for him.

children.text: evaṃ daśabhyo digbhya ekaikasyā diśo bahūni bodhisattvaśatasahasrāṇi sarva ekajātipratibaddhāstuṣitavarabhavanavāsino yena bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāman bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe
children.translated_text: In the same way, from the ten directions, from each direction, many hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas, all bound to one more birth and dwelling in the excellent palace of <s>Tuṣita</s>, approached the Bodhisattva in order to perform worship for him.

children.text: cāturmahārājakāyikebhyo devebhyaścaturaśītyapsaraḥśatasahasrāṇyevaṃ trayatriṃśato yāmebhyastuṣitebhyo nirmāṇaratibhyaḥ paranirmitavaśavartibhyo devebhyaścaturaśītyapsaraḥśatasahasrāṇi nānātūryasaṃgītivāditena yena bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāman bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods came eighty-four hundred thousand apsarases; likewise, from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, and <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods came eighty-four hundred thousand apsarases, with varied instruments, songs, and music, approaching the Bodhisattva in order to perform worship for him.

children.text: atha khalu bodhisattvaḥ śrīgarbhasiṃhāsane sarvapuṇyasamudgate sarvadevanāgasaṃdarśane mahākūṭāgāre niṣadya sārdhaṃ bodhisattvairdevanāgayakṣakoṭiniyutaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtastuṣitavarabhavanāt pracalati sma
children.translated_text: Then the Bodhisattva, seated on the lion-throne called <s>Śrīgarbha</s>, arisen from all merit and visible to all gods and nāgas, in a great palace pavilion, surrounded and honored by bodhisattvas and by hundreds of thousands of koṭis and niyutas of gods, nāgas, and yakṣas, set forth from the excellent palace of <s>Tuṣita</s>.

children.text: pracalatā ca bhikṣavo bodhisattvena tathārūpā kāyāt prabhā muktābhūd yayā prabhayā ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturevaṃ vipulavistīrṇo mahatodāreṇa supracalitapūrveṇa divyaprabhāsamatikrāntenāvabhāsena parisphuṭo 'bhūt
children.translated_text: And, monks, as the Bodhisattva set forth, such a radiance was released from his body that this three-thousand-great-thousand world-system, so vast and extensive, was pervaded by a great and sublime light, never before arisen and surpassing divine radiance.

children.text: yā api tā lokāntarikā aghā aghasphuṭā andhakārāstamisrā yatremau candrasūryāvevaṃ maharddhikāvevaṃ mahānubhāvāvevaṃ maheśākhyau ābhayā ābhāṃ varṇena varṇaṃ tejasā tejo nābhitapato nābhivirocataḥ tatra ye sattvā upapannāste svakānapi bāhuprasāritānna paśyanti
children.translated_text: Even those intermediate worlds, empty, unfilled, dark, and gloomy, where these moon and sun, though so mighty, so powerful, and so majestic, do not warm or illumine anything with their rays, color, light, or brilliance, and where the beings born there do not see even their own outstretched arms,

children.text: tathāpi tasmin samaye mahata udārasyāvabhāsasya prādurbhāvo 'bhūt
children.translated_text: even there, at that time, a great and sublime radiance appeared.

children.text: ye ca tatra sattvā upapannāste tenaivāvabhāsena sphuṭāḥ samānā anyonyaṃ samyak paśyanti sma
children.translated_text: And the beings born there, being pervaded by that very radiance, saw one another clearly.

children.text: anyonyaṃ saṃjānante sma
children.translated_text: They recognized one another.

children.text: evaṃ cāhur anye 'pi kila bhoḥ sattvā ihopapannāḥ kila bho iti ||
children.translated_text: And they said, "Indeed, friends, there are also other beings born here; indeed, friends."

children.text: ayaṃ ca trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāram aṣṭādaśamahānimittamabhūt
children.translated_text: And this three-thousand-great-thousand world-system displayed six kinds of movement and eighteen great portents.

children.text: akampat prākampat samprākampat
children.translated_text: It shook, shook strongly, and shook all around.

children.text: avedhat prāvedhat saṃprāvedhat
children.translated_text: It quivered, quivered strongly, and quivered all around.

children.text: acalat prācalat saṃprācalat
children.translated_text: It moved, moved strongly, and moved all around.

children.text: akṣubhyat prākṣubhyat samprākṣubhyat
children.translated_text: It was agitated, strongly agitated, and agitated all around.

children.text: araṇat prāraṇat saṃprāraṇat
children.translated_text: It resounded, resounded strongly, and resounded all around.

children.text: agarjat prāgarjat saṃprāgarjat
children.translated_text: It thundered, thundered strongly, and thundered all around.

children.text: ante 'vanamati sma madhye unnamati sma
children.translated_text: It sank down at the edges and rose up in the middle.

children.text: madhye 'vanamati sma ante unnamati sma
children.translated_text: It sank down in the middle and rose up at the edges.

children.text: pūrvasyāṃ diśyavanamati sma paścimāyāṃ diśyunnamati sma
children.translated_text: It sank down in the eastern direction and rose up in the western direction.

children.text: paścimāyāṃ diśyavanamati sma pūrvasyāṃ diśyunnamati sma
children.translated_text: It sank down in the western direction and rose up in the eastern direction.

children.text: dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśyavanamati sma uttarasyāṃ diśyunnamati sma
children.translated_text: It sank down in the southern direction and rose up in the northern direction.

children.text: uttarasyāṃ diśyavanamati sma dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśyunnamati sma
children.translated_text: It bent down toward the northern direction and rose up toward the southern direction.

children.text: tasmin samaye harṣaṇīyās toṣaṇīyāḥ premaṇīyāḥ prasādanīyā avalokanīyāḥ prahlādanīyā nirvarṇanīyā asecanīyā apratikūlā anuttrāsakarāḥ śabdāḥ śrūyante sma
children.translated_text: At that time sounds were heard that were gladdening, satisfying, lovable, inspiring confidence, worth beholding, delight-giving, worth gazing upon, inexhaustible, not disagreeable, and causing no terror.

children.text: na ca kasyacit sattvasya tasmin kṣaṇe viheṭhā vā trāso vā bhayaṃ vā stambhitatvaṃ vābhūt
children.translated_text: And at that moment no being had any injury, alarm, fear, or paralysis.

children.text: na ca bhūyaḥ sūryācandramasorna brahmaśakralokapālānāṃ tasmin kṣaṇe prabhā prajñāyate sma
children.translated_text: Nor, moreover, was the radiance of the sun and moon, or of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, and the world-protectors, perceived at that moment.

children.text: sarvanarakatiryagyoniyamalokopapannāśca sattvāstasmin kṣaṇe vigataduḥkhā abhūvan sarvasukhasamarpitāḥ
children.translated_text: And all beings born in the hells, in animal wombs, and in the world of <s>Yama</s> became free from suffering at that moment and were endowed with every happiness.

children.text: na ca kasyacit sattvasya rāgo bādhate sma dveṣo vā moho vā īrṣyā vā mātsaryaṃ vā māno vā mrakṣo vā mado vā krodho vā vyāpādo vā paridāho vā
children.translated_text: No being was then troubled by passion, hatred, delusion, envy, stinginess, pride, hypocrisy, intoxication, anger, malice, or burning anguish.

children.text: sarvasattvāstasmin kṣaṇe maitracittā hitacittāḥ parasparaṃ mātāpitṛsaṅgino 'bhūvan
children.translated_text: At that moment all beings became friendly-minded, benevolent, and attached to one another like mothers and fathers.

children.text: aghaṭṭitāni ca divyamānuṣyakāṇi tūryakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi manojñaghoṣamutsṛjanti sma
children.translated_text: And hundreds of thousands of crores and niyutas of divine and human instruments, without being struck, gave forth a charming sound.

children.text: devakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi pāṇibhiraṃsaiḥ śirobhistaṃ mahāvimānaṃ vahanti sma
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of crores and niyutas of gods carried that great celestial palace with their hands, shoulders, and heads.

children.text: tāni cāpsaraḥśatasahasrāṇi svāṃ svāṃ saṃgītiṃ samprayujya purataḥ pṛṣṭhato vāmadakṣiṇena ca sthitvā bodhisattvaṃ saṃgītirutasvareṇābhistuvanti sma
children.translated_text: And those hundreds of thousands of apsarases, each beginning her own song and standing in front, behind, to the left, and to the right, praised the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with the sound of musical song.

children.text: pūrvakarmaśubhasaṃcitasya te dīrgharātrakuśaloditasya te
children.translated_text: For you, whose former wholesome karma has been accumulated, for you, whose goodness has arisen through the long night,

children.text: satyadharmanayaśodhitasya te pūja adya vipulā pravartate ||
children.translated_text: for you, purified by the rule of true <s>dharma</s>, vast worship proceeds today.

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo dānu dattu priyaputradhītarā
children.translated_text: In former times, for many crores of kalpas, beloved sons and daughters were given by you as gifts.

children.text: tasya dānacaritasya tatphalaṃ yena divya kusumāḥ pravarṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the fruit of that practice of giving, divine flowers have been showered down.

children.text: ātmamāṃsa tulayitva te vibho so 'bhidattu priyapakṣikāraṇāt
children.translated_text: Having weighed out your own flesh, O lord, you gave it away for the sake of a beloved bird.

children.text: tasya dānacaritasya tatphalaṃ pretaloki labhi pānabhojanam ||
children.translated_text: As the fruit of that practice of giving, beings in the preta-world obtained drink and food.

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo śīla rakṣitamakhaṇḍanavratam
children.translated_text: In former times, for many crores of kalpas, you guarded morality, an unbroken vow.

children.text: tasya śīlacaritasya tatphalaṃ yena akṣaṇa apāya śodhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the fruit of that practice of morality, inopportune states and bad destinies have been purified.

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo kṣānti bhāvita nidānabodhaye
children.translated_text: In former times, for many crores of kalpas, you cultivated patience for the sake of the foundation of <s>bodhi</s>.

children.text: tasya kṣānticaritasya tatphalaṃ maitracitta bhuta devamānuṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the fruit of that practice of patience, gods and humans became friendly-minded.

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo vīryu bhāvitamalīnamuttamam
children.translated_text: In former times, for many crores of kalpas, you cultivated stainless, supreme energy.

children.text: tasya vīryacaritasya tatphalaṃ yena kāyu yatha meru śobhate ||
children.translated_text: As the fruit of that practice of energy, your body shines like <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo dhyāna dhyāyita kileśadhyeṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: In former times, for many crores of kalpas, you meditated in meditation for the subduing of defilements.

children.text: tasya dhyānacaritasya tatphalaṃ yena kleśa jagato na bādhate ||
children.translated_text: As the fruit of that practice of meditation, the defilements of the world do not trouble you.

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo prajña bhāvita kileśachedanī
children.translated_text: In former times, for many crores of kalpas, you cultivated wisdom that cuts off defilements.

children.text: tasya prajñacaritasya tatphalaṃ yena ābha paramā virocate ||
children.translated_text: As the fruit of that practice of wisdom, the highest radiance shines forth.

children.text: maitravarmita kileśasūdanā sarvasattvakaruṇāya udgatā
children.translated_text: Armored in friendliness, destroyer of defilements, arisen out of compassion for all beings,

children.text: modiprāpta paramā upekṣakā brahmabhūta sugatā namo 'stu te ||
children.translated_text: attained to joy, supreme in equanimity, become <s>Brahmā</s>-like: homage to you, <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: prajña ulkaprabha tejasodgatā sarvadoṣatamamohaśodhakā
children.translated_text: Your wisdom has risen with torch-like radiance and splendor, purifying the darkness of all faults and delusion.

children.text: cakṣubhūta trisahasrināyakā mārgadeśika mune namo 'stu te ||
children.translated_text: Become an eye, leader of the three-thousandfold world, guide of the path, sage: homage to you.

children.text: ṛddhipādavarabhijñakovidā satyadarśi paramārthi śikṣitā
children.translated_text: Skilled in the excellent bases of miraculous power and in higher knowledge, seer of truth, trained in the supreme reality,

children.text: tīrṇa tārayasi anyaprāṇino dāśabhūta sugatā namo 'stu te ||
children.translated_text: having crossed over, you cause other living beings to cross; become a helper, <s>Sugata</s>: homage to you.

children.text: sarvopāyavarabhijñakovidā darśayasi cyutimacyuticyutim
children.translated_text: Skilled in all excellent means and higher knowledge, you show passing away, non-passing-away, and passing away.

children.text: lokadharmabhavanābhivartase no ca loki kvaci opalipyase ||
children.translated_text: You move within the sphere of worldly dharmas, yet nowhere in the world are you stained.

children.text: lābha teṣa paramā acintiyā yeṣu darśana śravaṃ ca eṣyase
children.translated_text: Supreme and inconceivable are the gains of those among whom the sight and hearing of you will come.

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ śṛṇuya yo tidharmatāṃ śraddha prīti vipulā janeṣyase ||
children.translated_text: How much more for one who hears that true nature of things: you will generate abundant faith and joy.

children.text: jihma sarva tuṣitālayo bhuto jambudvīpi puri yo udāgataḥ
children.translated_text: The whole abode of <s>Tuṣita</s> has bowed down; he who has arisen in a city in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>

children.text: prāṇikoṭinayutā acintiyāṃ bodhayiṣyasi prasupta kleśato ||
children.translated_text: will awaken inconceivable crores and niyutas of living beings from the sleep of defilements.

children.text: ṛddha sphīta puramadya bheṣyatī devakoṭinayutaiḥ samākulam
children.translated_text: Today the city will become flourishing and prosperous, crowded with crores and niyutas of gods,

children.text: apsarobhi turiyairnināditaṃ rājagehi madhuraṃ śruṇiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: resounding with apsarases and instruments; the royal house will hear a sweet sound.

children.text: puṇyatejabharitā śubhakarmaṇā nāri sā paramarūpaupetā
children.translated_text: That woman, filled with the radiance of merit through wholesome karma and endowed with supreme beauty,

children.text: yasya putra ayameva samṛddhaḥ tisraloki abhibhāti śīriye ||
children.translated_text: whose son is this very prosperous one, outshines the three worlds in splendor.

children.text: no bhuyo puravarasmi dehināṃ lobhadoṣakalahā vivādakā
children.translated_text: No longer in the best of cities, among embodied beings, will there be quarrels and disputes born of greed and hatred.

children.text: sarva maitramanasaḥ sagauravā bhāvino naravarasya tejasā ||
children.translated_text: All will be friendly-minded and respectful through the splendor of the future best of men.

children.text: rājavaṃśa nṛpateḥ pravardhate cakravartikularājasaṃbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: The royal lineage of the king will increase, born from the family of wheel-turning kings.

children.text: bheṣyate kapilasāhvayaṃ puraṃ ratnakoṣabharitaṃ susamṛddham ||
children.translated_text: The city called <s>Kapila</s> will become filled with treasuries of jewels and very prosperous.

children.text: yakṣarākṣasakumbhāṇḍaguhyakā devadānavagaṇāḥ saindrakāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>guhyakas</s>, gods, and hosts of <s>dānavas</s> together with <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: ye sthitā naravarasya rakṣakāḥ teṣu mokṣa nacireṇa bheṣyate ||
children.translated_text: who stand as protectors of the best of men, will soon have liberation among them.

children.text: puṇyupārjitu stavitva nāyakaṃ premagauravamupasthapisva nā
children.translated_text: Having accumulated merit by praising the Leader, let us establish love and reverence.

children.text: sarva bodhi pariṇāmayāmahe kṣipra bhoma yatha tvaṃ narottama ||
children.translated_text: We dedicate all to <s>bodhi</s>; may we quickly become as you are, best of men.

children.text: Chapter 6

iti hi bhikṣavaḥ śiśirakālavinirgate vaiśākhamāse viśākhānakṣatrānugate ṛtupravare vasantakālasamaye taruvarapatrākīrṇe varapravarapuṣpasaṃkusumite śītoṣṇatamorajovigate mṛduśādvale susaṃsthite tribhuvanajyeṣṭho lokamahito vyavalokya ṛtukālasamaye pañcadaśyāṃ pūrṇamāsyāṃ poṣadhagṛhītāyā mātuḥ puṣyanakṣatrayogena bodhisattvastuṣitavarabhavanāccyutvā smṛtaḥ samprajānan pāṇḍuro gajapoto bhūtvā ṣaḍdanta indragopakaśirāḥ suvarṇarājīdantaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgo 'hīnendriyo jananyā dakṣiṇāyāṃ kukṣāvavakrāmat
children.translated_text: Thus, monks: when the cold season had passed, in the month of Vaiśākha, under the asterism Viśākhā, in the excellent season, at springtime, when the best trees were covered with leaves, blossoming with the finest flowers, when cold, heat, darkness, and dust had departed, and the soft grass was well established, the eldest of the three worlds, honored by the world, considered the season and time. On the fifteenth day, at the full moon, when his mother had taken the poṣadha observance, with the conjunction of the asterism Puṣya, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> fell from the excellent palace of <s>Tuṣita</s>; mindful and clearly aware, he became a pale young elephant, six-tusked, with veins like indragopaka insects, with tusks streaked with gold, with all limbs and secondary limbs complete and no faculty deficient, and entered his mother's right side.

children.text: avakrāntaśca sa dakṣiṇāvacaro 'bhūnna jātu vāmāvacaraḥ
children.translated_text: And having entered, he remained on the right side; never at all did he go to the left side.

children.text: māyādevī sukhaśayanaprasuptā imaṃ svapnamapaśyat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māyādevī</s>, asleep on a pleasant couch, saw this dream:

children.text: himarajatanibhaśca ṣaḍviṣāṇaḥ sucaraṇa cārubhujaḥ suraktaśīrṣaḥ
children.translated_text: "One like snow and silver, six-tusked, with good feet, lovely arms, and a deep-red head,

children.text: udaramupagato gajapradhāno lalitagatirdṛḍhavajragātrasaṃdhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the foremost elephant, graceful in gait, with firm joints and a body like adamant, entered my belly.

children.text: na ca mama sukha jātu evarūpaṃ dṛṣṭamapi śrutaṃ nāpi cānubhūtam
children.translated_text: And never have I seen, heard, or experienced such happiness as this.

children.text: kāyasukhacittasaukhyabhāvā yathariva dhyānasamāhitā abhūvam ||
children.translated_text: Because of bodily pleasure and mental joy, I became as though absorbed in meditation."

children.text: atha khalu māyādevī ābharaṇavigalitavasanā prahlāditakāyacittā prītiprāmodyaprasādapratilabdhā śayanavaratalādutthāya nārīgaṇaparivṛtā puraskṛtā prāsādavaraśikharādavatīrya yenāśokavanikā tenopajagāma
children.translated_text: Then <s>Māyādevī</s>, her ornaments and garments loosened, her body and mind gladdened, having obtained joy, delight, and serenity, rose from the surface of her excellent couch and, surrounded and preceded by a company of women, descended from the summit of the excellent palace and went to the aśoka grove.

children.text: sā aśokavanikāyāṃ sukhopaviṣṭā rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya dūtaṃ preṣayati sma āgacchatu devo devī te draṣṭukāmeti ||
children.translated_text: Seated comfortably in the aśoka grove, she sent a messenger to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: "Let the lord come; your queen wishes to see you."

children.text: atha sa rājā śuddhodanastadvacanaṃ śrutvā praharṣitamanā ākampitaśarīro bhadrāsanādutthāya amātyanaigamapārṣadyabandhujanaparivṛto yenāśokavanikā tenopasaṃkrāmad upasaṃkrāntaśca na śaknoti sma aśokavanikāṃ praveṣṭum
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, hearing that message, delighted in mind and trembling in body, rose from his fine seat and, surrounded by ministers, townsmen, courtiers, and kinsmen, approached the aśoka grove; but when he had approached, he was not able to enter the aśoka grove.

children.text: gurutaramivātmānaṃ manyate sma
children.translated_text: He felt his own body to be, as it were, very heavy.

children.text: aśokavanikādvāre sthito muhūrtaṃ saṃcintya tasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Standing at the gate of the aśoka grove, after reflecting for a moment, at that time he spoke this verse:

children.text: na smari raṇaśauṇḍi mūrdhasaṃsthasya mahyam eva guru śarīraṃ manyamī yādṛśo 'dya
children.translated_text: "I do not remember, even when I was a battle champion with a crest on my head, ever feeling my body so heavy as I do today.

children.text: svakulagṛhamadya na prabhomi praveṣṭuṃ kimiha mama bhave 'ṅgo kānva pṛccheya cāham ||
children.translated_text: Today I am unable to enter my own family house. What has happened here to my limbs? Whom should I ask?"

children.text: atha khalu śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrā gaganatalagatā ardhakāyamabhinirmāya rājānaṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣanta ||
children.translated_text: Then divine sons belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> class, standing in the sky and manifesting half their bodies, addressed the king with a verse:

children.text: vratatapaguṇayuktastisralokeṣu pūjyo maitrakaruṇalābhī puṇyajñānābhiṣiktaḥ
children.translated_text: "Endowed with the qualities of vows and austerities, honored in the three worlds, rich in loving-kindness and compassion, consecrated by merit and knowledge,

children.text: tuṣitapuri cyavitvā bodhisattvo mahātmā nṛpati tava sutatvaṃ māyakukṣaupapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the great-souled <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having fallen from the city of <s>Tuṣita</s>, has come into <s>Māyā</s>'s womb as your son, O king."

children.text: daśanakha tada kṛtvā svaṃ śiraṃ kampayanto nṛpatiranupraviṣṭaścitrikārānuyuktaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, placing his ten nails together and shaking his head, entered, intent on showing reverence.

children.text: māya tada nirīkṣya mānadarpopanītāṃ vadahi kurumi kiṃ te kiṃ prayogo bhaṇāhi ||
children.translated_text: Then, looking at <s>Māyā</s>, who was endowed with dignity and majesty, he said, "Tell me: what should I do for you? What is your purpose? Speak."

children.text: devyāha ||
children.translated_text: The queen said:

children.text: himarajatanikāśaścandrasūryātirekaḥ sucaraṇa suvibhaktaḥ ṣaḍviṣāṇo mahātmā
children.translated_text: "One resembling snow and silver, surpassing the moon and sun, with good feet, well proportioned, six-tusked, great-souled,

children.text: gajavaru dṛḍhasaṃdhirvajrakalpaḥ surūpaḥ udari mama praviṣṭastasya hetuṃ śruṇuṣva ||
children.translated_text: a noble elephant with firm joints, adamant-like and beautiful in form, has entered my belly. Hear the reason for it.

children.text: vitimira trisahasrāṃ paśyamī bhrājamānāṃ devanayuta devā ye stuvantī sayānā
children.translated_text: I see the three-thousandfold world free of darkness and shining; gods by the tens of thousands praise me as I lie here.

children.text: na ca mama khiladoṣo naiva roṣo na moho dhyānasukhasamaṅgī jānamī śāntacittā ||
children.translated_text: There is no hardness of heart in me, no anger and no delusion; joined with the happiness of meditation, I know myself to be of peaceful mind.

children.text: sādhu nṛpati śīghraṃ brāhmaṇānānayāsmin vedasupinapāṭhā ye gṛheṣū vidhijñāḥ
children.translated_text: Good, O king: quickly bring here those brāhmaṇas in the houses who are learned in the Vedas, readers of dreams, and knowers of ritual procedure.

children.text: supinu mama hi yemaṃ vyākarī tattvayuktaṃ kimida mama bhaveyā śreyu pāpaṃ kulasya ||
children.translated_text: Let them interpret this dream of mine in accordance with truth: whether from this there will be good or evil for the family."

children.text: vacanamimu śruṇitvā pārthivastatkṣaṇena brāhmaṇa kṛtavedānānayacchāstrapāṭhān
children.translated_text: Having heard this statement, the king immediately brought brāhmaṇas who had mastered the Vedas and recited the śāstras.

children.text: māya purata sthitvā brāhmaṇānāmavocat supina mayi ha dṛṣṭastasya hetuṃ śṛṇotha ||
children.translated_text: Standing before <s>Māyā</s>, he said to the brāhmaṇas, "A dream has been seen by me; hear the reason for it."

children.text: brāhmaṇā āhuḥ brūhi devi tvayā kīdṛśaṃ svapnaṃ dṛṣṭam
children.translated_text: The brāhmaṇas said, "Tell us, queen, what kind of dream did you see?

children.text: śrutvā jñāsyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: After hearing it, we shall know."

children.text: devyāha ||
children.translated_text: The queen said:

children.text: himarajatanikāśaścandrasūryātirekaḥ sucaraṇa suvibhaktaḥ ṣaḍviṣāṇo mahātmā
children.translated_text: "One resembling snow and silver, surpassing the moon and sun, with good feet, well proportioned, six-tusked, great-souled,

children.text: gajavaru dṛḍhasaṃdhirvajrakalpaḥ surūpaḥ udari mama praviṣṭastasya hetuṃ śṛṇotha ||
children.translated_text: a noble elephant with firm joints, adamant-like and beautiful in form, has entered my belly. Hear the reason for it."

children.text: vacanamimu śruṇitvā brāhmaṇā evamāhuḥ prīti vipula cintyā nāsti pāpaṃ kulasya
children.translated_text: Having heard this statement, the brāhmaṇas said thus: "Let there be great joy and thoughtfulness; there is no evil for the family.

children.text: putra tava janesī lakṣaṇairbhūṣitāṅgaṃ rājakulakulīnaṃ cakravarti mahātmaṃ ||
children.translated_text: You will give birth to a son whose limbs are adorned with the marks, noble in a royal lineage, a great-souled wheel-turning monarch.

children.text: sa ca pura vijahitvā kāmarājyaṃ ca gehaṃ pravrajita nirapekṣaḥ sarvalokānukampī
children.translated_text: And if he abandons the city, the kingdom of sensual pleasures, and the house, and goes forth without attachment, compassionate toward all the world,

children.text: buddho bhavati eṣo dakṣiṇīyastriloke amṛtarasavareṇā tarpayet sarvalokam ||
children.translated_text: he will become a Buddha, worthy of offerings in the three worlds; with the excellent taste of immortality he will satisfy the whole world."

children.text: vyākaritva giraṃ saumyāṃ bhuktvā pārthivabhojanam
children.translated_text: Having made this gentle prediction and eaten the royal food,

children.text: ācchādanāni codgṛhya prakrāntā brāhmaṇāstataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the brāhmaṇas took garments and then departed.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo rājā śuddhodano brāhmaṇebhyo lakṣaṇanaimittikavaipañcakebhyaḥ svapnādhyāyīpāṭhakebhyaḥ pratiśrutya hṛṣṭastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātastān brāhmaṇān prabhūtena khādanīyabhojanīyāsvādanīyena saṃtarpya saṃpravāryācchādanāni ca dattvā visarjayati sma
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having made a promise to the brahmins who knew bodily marks, omens, the fivefold sciences, dreams, and recitations, was delighted, satisfied, elated, pleased, glad, and filled with joy and happiness. He satisfied and fully served those brahmins with abundant foods to be chewed, eaten, and savored, gave them garments, and dismissed them.

children.text: tasyāṃ velāyāṃ kapilavastuni mahānagare caturṣu nagaradvāreṣu sarvanagaracatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu ca dānaṃ dāpayati sma annamannārthikebhyaḥ pānaṃ pānārthikebhyaḥ vastrāṇi vastrārthikebhyaḥ yānāni yānārthikebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: At that time, in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, he had gifts distributed at the four city gates and at all the city's squares and crossroads: food to those who needed food, drink to those who needed drink, garments to those who needed garments, and vehicles to those who needed vehicles.

children.text: evaṃ gandhamālyavilepanaśayyopāśrayaṃ prājīvikaṃ prājīvikārthibhyo yāvadeva bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe ||
children.translated_text: In the same way he gave perfumes, garlands, unguents, beds, lodging, and provisions for livelihood to those who sought provisions for livelihood, solely as an act of worship for the Bodhisattva.

children.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyaitadabhavat katamasmin gṛhe māyādevī sukham anupakliṣṭā viharediti
children.translated_text: Then, monks, this occurred to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: "In what house will <s>Māyādevī</s> dwell happily and without distress?"

children.text: atha tatkṣaṇameva catvāro mahārājāno rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, at that very moment, the four great kings approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said this:

children.text: alpotsuko deva bhava sukhaṃ tiṣṭha upekṣako
children.translated_text: "Be free from anxiety, O lord; remain happily at ease and calmly observant.

children.text: vayaṃ hi bodhisattvasya veśma vai māpayāmahe ||
children.translated_text: For we will have a dwelling built for the Bodhisattva."

children.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāha ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said this:

children.text: hīnā vimānā pālānāṃ trayatriṃśānamuttamāḥ
children.translated_text: "Inferior are the palaces of the guardians; those of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods are supreme.

children.text: vaijayantasamaṃ veśma bodhisattvasya dāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: I give the Bodhisattva a dwelling equal to <s>Vaijayanta</s>."

children.text: atha khalu suyāmo devaputro rājānaṃ śuddhodanamusaṃkramyaivamāha ||
children.translated_text: Then the devaputra <s>Suyāma</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said this:

children.text: madīyaṃ bhavanaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitāḥ śakrakoṭayaḥ
children.translated_text: "Having seen my palace, millions of <s>Śakras</s> are astonished.

children.text: suyāmabhavanaṃ śrīmadbodhisattvasya dāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: I give the splendid palace of <s>Suyāma</s> to the Bodhisattva."

children.text: atha khalu saṃtuṣito devaputro rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāha ||
children.translated_text: Then the devaputra <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said this:

children.text: yatraiva uṣitaḥ pūrvaṃ tuṣiteṣu mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: "That very place where the greatly renowned one formerly dwelt among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods,

children.text: tadeva bhavanaṃ ramyaṃ bodhisattvasya dāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: that delightful palace I give to the Bodhisattva."

children.text: atha khalu sunirmito devaputro rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāha ||
children.translated_text: Then the devaputra <s>Sunirmita</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said this:

children.text: manomayamahaṃ śrīmadvaśma tadratanāmayam
children.translated_text: "I will bring a splendid mind-made dwelling, one made of jewels,

children.text: bodhisattvasya pūjārthamupaneṣyāmi pārthiva ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of worshiping the Bodhisattva, O earthly king."

children.text: atha khalu paranirmitavaśavartī devaputro rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāha ||
children.translated_text: Then the devaputra <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said this:

children.text: yāvantaḥ kāmadhātusthā vimānāḥ śobhanāḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: "As many beautiful palaces as there are anywhere in the realm of desire,

children.text: bhābhiste madvimānasya bhavantyabhihataprabhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: their radiances are overpowered by the radiances of my palace.

children.text: tat prayacchāmyahaṃ śrīmadveśma ratnamayaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: Therefore I offer that splendid, auspicious, jewel-made dwelling;

children.text: bodhisattvasya pūjārthamānayiṣyāmi pārthiva ||
children.translated_text: I will bring it for the sake of worshiping the Bodhisattva, O earthly king.

children.text: divyaiḥ puṣpaiḥ samākīrṇaṃ divyagandhopavāsitam
children.translated_text: Strewn with divine flowers and perfumed with divine fragrances,

children.text: upanāmayiṣye vipulaṃ yatra devī vasiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: I will present a vast one in which the queen will dwell."

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ sarvaiḥ kāmāvacarair deveśvarairbodhisattvasya pūjārthaṃ kapilāhvaye mahāpuravare svakasvakāni gṛhāṇi māpitānyabhūvan
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, for the sake of worshiping the Bodhisattva, all the lordly gods of the desire realm had their own houses built in the excellent great city called <s>Kapila</s>.

children.text: rājñā cāpi śuddhodanena manuṣyātikrāntaṃ divyāsaṃprāptaṃ gṛhataraṃ pratisaṃskāritamabhūt
children.translated_text: And King <s>Śuddhodana</s> too had a very great house prepared, one surpassing the human yet not reaching the divine.

children.text: tatra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāvyūhasya samādheranubhāvena sarveṣu teṣu gṛheṣu māyādevīmupadarśayati sma
children.translated_text: There, through the power of the <s>Mahāvyūha</s> samādhi, the Bodhisattva, the great being, caused <s>Māyādevī</s> to appear in all those houses.

children.text: abhyantaragataśca bodhisattvo māyādevyāḥ kukṣau dakṣiṇe pārśve paryaṅkamābhujya niṣaṇṇo 'bhūt
children.translated_text: And the Bodhisattva, having entered within, was seated cross-legged in the womb of <s>Māyādevī</s>, on her right side.

children.text: sarve ca te deveśvarā ekaikamevaṃ saṃjānīte sma mamaiva gṛhe bodhisattvamātā prativasati nānyatreti ||
children.translated_text: And each of those lordly gods thought in just this way: "The mother of the Bodhisattva is dwelling in my house alone, and nowhere else."

children.text: tatredamucyate ||
children.translated_text: On this, the following is said:

children.text: mahāvyūhāya sthitaḥ samādhiye acintiyā nirmita nirmiṇitvā
children.translated_text: Established in the <s>Mahāvyūha</s> samādhi, having created inconceivable magical manifestations,

children.text: sarveṣa devānabhiprāya pūritā nṛpasya pūrṇaśca tadā manorathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he fulfilled the wishes of all the gods, and at that time the king's desire too was fulfilled.

children.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ devaparṣadi keṣāṃciddevaputrāṇāmetadabhavad ye 'pi tāvaccāturmahārājakāyikā devāste 'pi tāvanmanuṣyāśrayagatatvena nirvidyāpakramanti
children.translated_text: Then, in that assembly of gods, this occurred to certain devaputras: "Even those gods who belong to the retinue of the four great kings withdraw in disgust from being in a human abode.

children.text: kaḥ punarvādo ye tadanye udāratamā devāḥ trāyatriṃśā vā yāmā vā tuṣitā vā
children.translated_text: How much more, then, those other more exalted gods, whether <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, or <s>Tuṣita</s>?

children.text: tatkathaṃ hi nāma sarvalokābhyudgato bodhisattvaḥ śucirnirāmagandhaḥ sattvaratnaḥ saṃtuṣitāddevanikāyāccyutvā durgandhe manuṣyāśraye daśamāsān mātuḥ kukṣau sthita iti ||
children.translated_text: How, then, has the Bodhisattva, risen above the whole world, pure, without the smell of raw flesh, a jewel among beings, fallen from the divine host of <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> and remained for ten months in the foul-smelling human abode, in his mother's womb?"

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānando buddhānubhāvena bhagavantametadavocat āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvajjugupsanīyaśca mātṛgrāmastathāgatenokto yāvadrāgacaritaśca
children.translated_text: Then venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, through the Buddha's power, said this to the Blessed One: "It is astonishing, Blessed One, how repulsive womankind has been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be, and how much it is characterized by passion.

children.text: idaṃ tu bhagavan āścaryataram
children.translated_text: But this, Blessed One, is still more astonishing.

children.text: kathaṃ hi nāma sarvalokābhyudgato bhagavān pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūta eva tuṣitāddevanikāyāccyavitvā manuṣyāśraye durgandhe māturdakṣiṇe pārśve kukṣāvupapanna iti
children.translated_text: How indeed did the Blessed One, formerly while still a Bodhisattva, risen above the whole world, fall from the divine host of <s>Tuṣita</s> and take birth in the foul-smelling human abode, in his mother's womb, on her right side?

children.text: nāhaṃ bhagavan idamutsahe evaṃ vaktuṃ yathaiva pūrve bhagavatā vyākṛtamiti
children.translated_text: Blessed One, I am not able to state this in the very way it was previously explained by the Blessed One."

children.text: bhagavānāha icchasi tvamānanda ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ draṣṭuṃ yo mātuḥ kukṣigatasya bodhisattvasya paribhogo 'bhūt
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Do you wish, <s>Ānanda</s>, to see the jeweled array, the Bodhisattva's enjoyment, which was the enjoyment of the Bodhisattva while he was in his mother's womb?"

children.text: ānanda āha ayamasya bhagavan kālaḥ ayaṃ sugata samayaḥ yattathāgatastaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogamupadarśayed yaṃ dṛṣṭvā prītiṃ vetsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> said, "Blessed One, this is the time for it; <s>Sugata</s>, this is the occasion when the <s>Tathāgata</s> should show that bodhisattva-paribhoga (Bodhisattva accoutrement). Seeing it, we shall feel joy."

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstathārūpanimittamakarot yad brahmā sahāpatiḥ sārdhamaṣṭaṣaṣṭibrahmaśatasahasrair brahmaloke 'ntarhito bhagavataḥ purataḥ pratyasthāt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One made such a sign that <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, together with sixty-eight hundred thousand <s>Brahmās</s>, disappeared from the <s>Brahmā</s> world and stood before the Blessed One.

children.text: sa bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ tripradakṣiṇīkṛtyaikānte 'sthāt prāñjalībhūto bhagavantaṃ namasyan
children.translated_text: He bowed with his head to the Blessed One's feet, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the Blessed One.

children.text: tatra khalu bhagavān jānanneva brahmāṇaṃ sahāpatimāmantrayate sma gṛhītastvayā brahman sa bodhisattvaparibhogo daśamāsiko yo mama pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūtasya mātuḥ kukṣigatasyābhūt
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One, knowing already, addressed <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>: "<s>Brahmā</s>, did you take that bodhisattva-paribhoga of ten months, which formerly belonged to me when I was a Bodhisattva in my mother's womb?"

children.text: brahmā āha evametadbhagavan evametat sugata
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> said, "So it is, Blessed One; so it is, <s>Sugata</s>."

children.text: bhagavānāha kva sa idānīṃ brahman upadarśaya tam
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Where is it now, <s>Brahmā</s>? Show it."

children.text: brahmā cāha brahmaloke sa bhagavan
children.translated_text: And <s>Brahmā</s> said, "Blessed One, it is in the <s>Brahmā</s> world."

children.text: bhagavānāha tena hi tvaṃ brahman upadarśaya taṃ daśamāsikaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ jñāsyanti kiyatsaṃskṛtamiti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Then, <s>Brahmā</s>, show that bodhisattva-paribhoga of ten months. They will understand how far conditioned things extend."

children.text: atha khalu brahmā sahāpatistān brāhmaṇānetadavocat tiṣṭhatu tāvadbhavanto yāvadvayaṃ ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogamānayiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> said this to those brahmins: "Let the gentlemen wait for a while, until we bring the jewel-array, the bodhisattva-paribhoga."

children.text: atha khalu brahmā sahāpatirbhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivanditvā bhagavataḥ purato 'ntarhitastatkṣaṇameva brahmaloke pratyasthāt ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, having bowed with his head to the Blessed One's feet, disappeared from before the Blessed One and in that very instant stood in the <s>Brahmā</s> world.

children.text: atha khalu brahmā sahāpatiḥ subrahmāṇaṃ devaputrametadavocat gaccha tvaṃ mārṣā ito brahmalokamupādāya yāvattrāyatriṃśadbhavanaṃ śabdamudīraya ghoṣamanuśrāvaya
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> said this to <s>Subrahmā</s> the divine son: "Go, good sir, and from here, beginning with the <s>Brahmā</s> world and extending as far as the palace of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, raise a sound and make an announcement:

children.text: ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ vayaṃ tathāgatasyāntikamupanāmayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: 'We shall bring the jewel-array, the bodhisattva-paribhoga, into the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: yo yuṣmākaṃ draṣṭukāmaḥ sa śīghramāgacchatviti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever among you wishes to see it should come quickly.'"

children.text: atha khalu brahmā sahāpatiścaturaśītyā devakoṭyā nayutaśatasahasraḥ sārdhaṃ taṃ ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ parigṛhya mahati brāhme vimāne triyojanaśatike pratiṣṭhāpyānekair daivakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraiḥ samantato 'nuparivārya jambūdvīpamavatārayati sma ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, together with eighty-four koṭis of gods and hundreds of thousands of nayutas, took that jewel-array, the bodhisattva-paribhoga, set it upon a great <s>Brahmā</s> aerial palace three hundred yojanas wide, surrounded it on all sides with many hundreds of thousands of koṭis and nayutas of gods, and caused it to descend to <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena kāmāvacarāṇāṃ devānāṃ mahāsaṃnipāto 'bhūt bhagavatsakāśe gantum
children.translated_text: At that time there was a great assembly of the gods of the desire realm, wishing to go into the Blessed One's presence.

children.text: sa khalu punā ratnavyūho bodhisattvaparibhogo divyairvastrairdivyairmālyair divyairgandhairdivyaiḥ puṣpairdivyairvādyairdivyaiśca paribhogairabhisaṃskṛto 'bhūt
children.translated_text: That jewel-array, the bodhisattva-paribhoga, was adorned with divine garments, divine garlands, divine perfumes, divine flowers, divine instruments, and divine enjoyments.

children.text: tāvanmaheśākhyaiśca devaiḥ parivṛto 'bhūd yacchakro devānāmindraḥ sumerau sthitvā dūrata eva mukhe tālacchatrakaṃ dattvā śīrṣavyavalokanenānuvilokayati sma unmeṣadhyāyikayā vā
children.translated_text: It was surrounded by gods of such great majesty that <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, standing on <s>Sumeru</s>, looked at it from afar, placing a palm-leaf parasol before his face and peering upward with his head, or gazing with unblinking attention,

children.text: na ca śaknoti sma draṣṭum
children.translated_text: but he was not able to see it.

children.text: tatkasmāt maheśākhyā hi devā brāhmaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Why was that? Because, O brahmins, the gods were of great majesty.

children.text: itarāstrāyatriṃśā yāmāstuṣitā nirmāṇaratayaḥ paranirmitavaśavartinaḥ
children.translated_text: The others were the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, the <s>Yāmas</s>, the <s>Tuṣitas</s>, the <s>Nirmāṇaratis</s>, and the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartins</s>.
