children.text: kaḥ punarvādaḥ śakro devānāmindraḥ
children.translated_text: How much more, then, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods?

children.text: mohaṃ te vai yānti sma ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, they fell into bewilderment.

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstaṃ divyaṃ vādyanirghoṣamantardhāpayati sma
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One caused that divine sound of instruments to disappear.

children.text: tatkasmāt yatsahaśravaṇādeva jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyā unmādamāpatsyanta iti ||
children.translated_text: Why was that? Because, from hearing it alone, the people of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> would have fallen into madness.

children.text: atha khalu catvāro mahārājānaḥ śakraṃ devānāmindramupasaṃkramyaivamāhuḥ kathaṃ devānāmindra kariṣyāmo na labhāmahe ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ draṣṭum
children.translated_text: Then the four great kings approached <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and said this: "Lord of the gods, what shall we do? We do not get to see the jewel-array, the bodhisattva-paribhoga."

children.text: sa tānavocat kimahaṃ mārṣāḥ kariṣyāmi ahamapi na labhe draṣṭum
children.translated_text: He said to them, "Good sirs, what can I do? I too do not get to see it.

children.text: api tu khalu punarmārṣā bhagavatsamīpamupanītaṃ drakṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: But, good sirs, when it has been brought near to the Blessed One, we shall see it."

children.text: te tadā āhus tena hi devānāmindra tathā kuru yathāsya kṣipraṃ darśanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: They then said, "Then, lord of the gods, act in such a way that its sight may occur quickly."

children.text: śakra āha āgamayata mārṣā muhūrtaṃ yāvadatikrāntātikrāntatamā devaputrā bhagavantaṃ pratisaṃmodayante sma
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said, "Wait, good sirs, for a moment, until the divine sons who are higher and higher have greeted the Blessed One.

children.text: tadekānte sthitvā śīrṣonmiñjitakayā bhagavantamanuvilokayanti sma ||
children.translated_text: Standing to one side, they look toward the Blessed One with heads raised."

children.text: atha khalu brahmā sahāpatiḥ sārdhaṃ taiścaturaśītyā devakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraistaṃ ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ gṛhītvā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāmayati sma
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, together with those eighty-four koṭis of gods and hundreds of thousands of nayutas, took that jewel-array, the bodhisattva-paribhoga, and approached the place where the Blessed One was.

children.text: sa khalu puna ratnavyūho bodhisattvaparibhogo 'bhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaścaturasraścatuṣṭhūṇaḥ
children.translated_text: That jewel-array, the bodhisattva-paribhoga, was beautiful, pleasing, handsome, square, and four-pillared.

children.text: upariṣṭācca kūṭāgārasamalaṃkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Above, it was adorned with a peaked pavilion.

children.text: evaṃpramāṇaḥ tadyathāpi nāma ṣaṇmāsajāto dāraka uccaistvena
children.translated_text: Its measure was as follows: in height it was like a child born six months earlier.

children.text: tasya khalu punaḥ kūṭāgārasya madhye paryaṅkaḥ prajñaptaḥ tadyathāpi nāma ṣaṇmāsajātasya dārakasya bhittīphalakaḥ
children.translated_text: In the middle of that peaked pavilion a couch was set out, like the bed-plank of a child born six months earlier.

children.text: sa khalu puna ratnavyūho bodhisattvaparibhoga evaṃ varṇasaṃsthāno yasya na kaścit sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sadṛśo 'sti ākṛtyā vā varṇena vā
children.translated_text: Now that jewel-array, the furnishing of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, was of such color and form that in the world with its gods, with <s>Māra</s>, and with <s>Brahmā</s>, there was no one equal to it in shape or in color.

children.text: devāḥ khalvapi taṃ dṛṣṭvā āścaryaprāptā abhuvan
children.translated_text: Indeed, when the gods saw it, they were filled with wonder.

children.text: cakṣūṃṣi teṣāṃ vibhramanti sma
children.translated_text: Their eyes reeled.

children.text: sa ca tathāgatasyāntika upanīto 'tīva bhāsate tapati virocate sma
children.translated_text: And when it was brought into the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, it shone, glowed, and blazed exceedingly.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma dvinirdhāntaṃ suvarṇaṃ kuśalena karmakāreṇa supariniṣṭhitamapagatakācadoṣam evaṃ tasmin samaye sa kūṭāgāro virājate sma
children.translated_text: Just as twice-refined gold, well finished by a skilled artisan and freed from the fault of dross, gleams, so at that time that pavilion shone forth.

children.text: tasmin khalu punarbodhisattvaparibhoge paryaṅkaḥ prajñapto yasya sadevake loke nāsti kaścit sadṛśo varṇena vā saṃsthānena vā anyatra kambugrīvāyā bodhisattvasya
children.translated_text: In that furnishing of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> a couch had been prepared, and in the world with its gods there was no one equal to it in color or in form, apart from the conch-necked <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: yat khalu mahābrahmaṇā cīvaraṃ prāvṛtamabhūt tattasya bodhisattvaparyaṅkasyāgrato na bhāsate sma tadyathāpi nāma vātavṛṣṭyābhihataḥ kṛṣṇakambalaḥ
children.translated_text: The robe that <s>Mahābrahmā</s> had worn did not shine before that couch of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, just as, for example, a black blanket beaten by wind and rain does not shine.

children.text: sa khalu punaḥ kūṭāgāra uragasāracandanamayo yasyaikasuvarṇadharaṇī sāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ mūlyaṃ kṣamate tathāvidhenoragasāracandanena sa kūṭāgāraḥ samantād anupaliptaḥ
children.translated_text: Now that pavilion was made of uragasāra sandalwood; a single golden portion of it was worth a thousand-world realm, and with such uragasāra sandalwood that pavilion was covered all around.

children.text: tādṛśa eva dvitīyaḥ kūṭāgāraḥ kṛto yastasmin prathame kūṭāgāre 'bhyantarataḥ asakto 'baddhasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: A second pavilion of the same kind was made, which stood inside that first pavilion, unattached and unfastened.

children.text: tādṛśa eva tṛtīyo 'pi kūṭāgāro yastasmin dvitīye kūṭāgāre 'bhyantare 'sakto 'baddhasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: A third pavilion of the same kind was also made, which stood inside that second pavilion, unattached and unfastened.

children.text: sa ca paryaṅkastasmin gandhamaye tṛtīye kūṭāgāre vyavasthitaḥ saṃpraticchannaḥ
children.translated_text: And the couch was set and enclosed within that fragrant third pavilion.

children.text: tasya khalu punaruragasāracandanasyaivaṃrūpo varṇaḥ tadyathāpi nāma abhijātasya nīlavaiḍūryasya
children.translated_text: That uragasāra sandalwood had a color like that of fine blue vaiḍūrya.

children.text: tasya khalu punargandhakūṭāgārasyopari samantādyāvanti kāniciddivyātikrāntāni puṣpāṇi santi tāni sarvāṇi tasmin kūṭāgāre bodhisattvasya pūrvakuśalamūlavipākenānuprāptānyeva jāyante sma
children.translated_text: On top of that fragrant pavilion, all the flowers that exist as surpassingly divine flowers arose upon that pavilion, obtained by the ripening of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s former roots of merit.

children.text: sa khalu puna ratnavyūho bodhisattvaparibhogo dṛḍhasāro 'bhedyo vajropamaḥ sparśena ca kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśaḥ
children.translated_text: That jewel-array, the furnishing of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, had a firm core, was unbreakable, and was like adamant; to the touch it had the pleasant softness of kācilindika cloth.

children.text: tasmin khalu puna ratnavyūhe bodhisattvaparibhoge ye kecit kāmāvacarāṇāṃ devānāṃ bhavanavyūhāste sarve tasmin saṃdṛśyante sma ||
children.translated_text: In that jewel-array, the furnishing of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, all the palace arrays of the <s>kāmāvacara</s> gods of the sense-sphere were visible.

children.text: yāmeva ca rātriṃ bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣimavakrāntastāmeva rātrimadha āpaskandhamupādāya aṣṭaṣaṣṭiyojanaśatasahasrāṇi mahāpṛthivīṃ bhittvā yāvad brahmalokaṃ padmamabhyudgatamabhūt
children.translated_text: On the very night when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> entered his mother's womb, on that same night, beginning from below at the mass of water, a lotus rose up, piercing the great earth for sixty-eight hundred thousand yojanas, as far as the <s>Brahmā</s> world.

children.text: na ca kaścittaṃ padmaṃ paśyati sma anyatra sārathinarottamād daśaśatasāhasrikācca mahābrahmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: No one saw that lotus except <s>Sārathinarottama</s> and <s>Mahābrahmā</s> of the ten hundred-thousandfold world.

children.text: yacceha trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātāvojo vā maṇḍo vā raso vā tatsarvaṃ tasmin mahāpadme madhubinduḥ saṃtiṣṭhate sma ||
children.translated_text: And whatever vigor, essence, or sap there was here in the three-thousand great-thousand world-system, all of it remained in that great lotus as a drop of honey.

children.text: tamenaṃ mahābrahmā śubhe vaiḍūryabhājane prakṣipya bodhisattvasyopanāmayati sma
children.translated_text: <s>Mahābrahmā</s> placed that drop in a pure vaiḍūrya vessel and presented it to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: taṃ bodhisattvaḥ parigṛhya bhuṅkte sma mahābrahmaṇo 'nukampāmupādāya
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> took it and ate it, out of compassion for <s>Mahābrahmā</s>.

children.text: nāsti sa kaścit sattvaḥ sattvanikāye yasya sa ojobinduḥ paribhuktaḥ samyak sukhena pariṇamedanyatra caramabhavikādbodhisattvāt sarvabodhisattvabhūmiparipūrṇāt
children.translated_text: There is no being among the classes of beings for whom that drop of essence, if eaten, would digest properly and with ease, apart from a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence who has fulfilled all the bodhisattva grounds.

children.text: kasya ca karmaṇo vipākena sa ojobindurbodhisattvasyopatiṣṭhate sma dīrgharātraṃ khalvapi bodhisattvena pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā glānebhyaḥ sattvebhyo bhaiṣajyaṃ dattam āśatparāṇāṃ sattvānāmāśāḥ paripūritāḥ śaraṇāgatāśca na parityaktāḥ nityaṃ cāgrapuṣpamagraphalamagrarasaṃ tathāgatebhyastathāgatacaityebhyas tathāgataśrāvakasaṃghebhyo mātāpitṛbhyaśca dattvā paścādātmanā paribhuktam
children.translated_text: Through the ripening of what karma did that drop of essence attend upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? For a long time in the past, while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was practicing the bodhisattva conduct, he had given medicine to sick beings, fulfilled the hopes of beings intent upon hope, and not abandoned those who had come for refuge; and he had always first given the finest flowers, the finest fruits, and the finest flavors to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, to the caityas of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, to the community of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s disciples, and to his mother and father, and only afterward consumed them himself.

children.text: tasya karmaṇo vipākena mahābrahmā bodhisattvasya taṃ madhubindumupanāmayati sma ||
children.translated_text: Through the ripening of that karma, <s>Mahābrahmā</s> presented that drop of honey to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: tasmin khalu punaḥ kūṭāgāre yāni kānicit santyatikrāntātikrāntāni māyāguṇaratikrīḍāsamavasṛtasthānāni tāni sarvāṇi tasmin prādurbhāvāni saṃdṛśyante sma bodhisattvasya pūrvakarmavipākena ||
children.translated_text: Now in that pavilion, whatever places there were that were most surpassingly filled with the delights and play of magical powers, all of them appeared there as manifestations, visible through the ripening of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s former karma.

children.text: tasmin khalu puna ratnavyūhe bodhisattvaparibhoge śatasahasravyūhaṃ nāma vāsoyugaṃ prādurbhūtam
children.translated_text: In that jewel-array, the furnishing of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a pair of garments named Hundred-Thousand Array appeared.

children.text: na sa kaścitsattvaḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyate yasya tatprādurbhavedanyatra caramabhavikād bodhisattvāt
children.translated_text: There is no being among the classes of beings for whom that would appear, apart from a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence.

children.text: na ca te kecana udārodārā rūpaśabdagandharasasparśā ye tasmin kūṭāgāre na saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: And there were no especially noble forms, sounds, smells, tastes, or tangible objects that were not visible in that pavilion.

children.text: sacetkūṭāgāraparibhoga evaṃ suparibhoga evaṃ supariniṣpannaḥ sāntarabahirevaṃ supariniṣṭhita evaṃ mṛdukaśca
children.translated_text: If the pavilion's furnishing was thus a fine furnishing, thus well perfected, thus well finished inside and outside, and thus soft...

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśo nidarśanamātreṇa na tu tasyopamā saṃvidyate
children.translated_text: As, for example, the pleasant touch of kācilindika cloth is only a mere illustration; no real comparison for it is found.

children.text: dharmatā khalveṣā bodhisattvasya pūrvakeṇa ca praṇidhānena iyaṃ cetanā ṛddhāvavaśyaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena manuṣyaloka upapattavyamabhiniṣkramya cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya dharmacakraṃ pravartayitavyam
children.translated_text: Indeed this is the nature of things: by the former vow of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and by this intention in his miraculous power, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> Mahāsattva must be reborn in the human world, must go forth, must awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening, and must turn the wheel of Dharma.

children.text: yasyā mātuḥ kukṣāvupapattirbhavati tasyā dakṣiṇe kukṣāvādita eva ratnavyūhakūṭāgāro 'bhinirvartate
children.translated_text: In the womb of whatever mother his rebirth takes place, from the very beginning a jewel-arrayed pavilion comes into being on the right side of her womb.

children.text: paścādbodhisattvastuṣitebhyaścyuttvā tasmin kūṭāgāre paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇaḥ sambhavati
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having fallen from <s>Tuṣita</s>, appears in that pavilion seated cross-legged.

children.text: na hi caramabhavikasya bodhisattvasya kalalārbudaghanapeśībhāvaṃ kāyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate sma
children.translated_text: For the body of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence did not abide in the states of kalala, arbuda, ghana, or peśī, the successive embryonic masses.

children.text: atha tarhi sarvāṅgapratyaṅgalakṣaṇasampannaḥ saṃniṣaṇṇa eva prādurbhavati
children.translated_text: Rather, complete with all major and minor limbs and with the marks, he appears seated just so.

children.text: svapnāntaragatā ca bodhisattvamātā māyādevī mahānāgakuñjaramavakrāntaṃ saṃjānīte sma ||
children.translated_text: And in a dream the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother, <s>Māyādevī</s>, recognized a great royal elephant descending.

children.text: tasya khalu punastathā niṣaṇṇasya śakro devānāmindraścatvāraśca mahārājāno 'ṣṭāviṃśatiśca mahāyakṣasenāpatayo guhyakādhipatiśca nāma yakṣakulaṃ yato vajrapāṇerutpattiste bodhisattvaṃ mātuḥ kukṣigataṃ viditvā satataṃ samitamanubaddhā bhavanti sma
children.translated_text: And while he was seated thus, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, the Four Great Kings, the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals, and the yakṣa clan named <s>Guhyakādhipati</s>, from which <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> arose, knowing that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was in his mother's womb, constantly and continually attended him.

children.text: santi khalu punaścatasro bodhisattvaparicārakā devatāḥ utkhalī ca nāma samutkhalī ca nāma dhvajavatī ca nāma prabhāvatī ca nāma
children.translated_text: Moreover, there are four attendant deities of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: <s>Utkhalī</s>, <s>Samutkhalī</s>, <s>Dhvajavatī</s>, and <s>Prabhāvatī</s>.

children.text: tā api bodhisattvaṃ mātuḥ kukṣigataṃ viditvā satataṃ samitaṃ rakṣanti sma
children.translated_text: They too, knowing that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was in his mother's womb, constantly and continually guarded him.

children.text: śakro 'pi devānāmindraḥ sārdhaṃ pañcamātrairdevaputraśatairbodhisattvaṃ mātuḥ kukṣigataṃ jñātvā satataṃ samitamanubadhnāti sma ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, also, together with about five hundred divine sons, knowing that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was in his mother's womb, constantly and continually attended him.

children.text: bodhisattvasya khalu punarmātuḥ kukṣigatasya kāyastathāvidho 'bhūt tadyathāpi nāma parvatamūrdhani rātrāvandhakāratamisrāyāṃ mahānagniskandho yojanādapi dṛśyate sma yāvat pañcabhyo yojanebhyo dṛśyate sma
children.translated_text: Moreover, the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> while in his mother's womb was of such a kind: as, for example, on a mountaintop in the darkness and gloom of night, a great mass of fire is seen from even a yojana away, indeed is seen from as far as five yojanas away,

children.text: evameva bodhisattvasya mātuḥ kukṣigatasyātmabhāvo 'bhinirvṛtto 'bhūt prabhāsvaro 'bhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ
children.translated_text: just so the bodily form of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> while in his mother's womb had come into being radiant, beautiful, pleasing, and lovely to see.

children.text: sa tasmin kūṭāgāre paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇo 'tīva śobhate sma
children.translated_text: Seated cross-legged in that pavilion, he shone exceedingly.

children.text: vaiḍūryapratyuptamivābhijātaṃ jātarūpam
children.translated_text: He was like native gold inlaid with lapis lazuli.

children.text: bodhisattvasya mātā ca nidhyāya sthitā paśyati sma kukṣigataṃ bodhisattvam
children.translated_text: And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother, standing and gazing, saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> within her womb.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma mahato 'bhrakūṭādvidyuto niḥsṛtya mahāntamavabhāsaṃ saṃjanayanti evameva bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigataḥ śriyā tejasā varṇena ca taṃ prathamaṃ ratnakūṭāgāramavabhāsayati sma
children.translated_text: As, for example, lightning issuing from a great mass of clouds produces a great illumination, just so the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while in his mother's womb, illumined that first jewel pavilion with his glory, splendor, and color.

children.text: avabhāsya dvitīyaṃ gandhakūṭāgāramavabhāsayati sma
children.translated_text: Having illumined it, he illumined the second fragrant pavilion.

children.text: dvitīyaṃ gandhakūṭāgāramavabhāsya tṛtīyaṃ ratnakūṭāgāramavabhāsayati sma
children.translated_text: Having illumined the second fragrant pavilion, he illumined the third jewel pavilion.

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ ratnakūṭāgāramavabhāsya sarvāvantaṃ māturātmabhāvamavabhāsayati sma
children.translated_text: Having illumined the third jewel pavilion, he illumined the whole extent of his mother's bodily form.

children.text: tamavabhāsya yatra cāsane niṣaṇṇo bhavati sma tadavabhāsayati sma
children.translated_text: Having illumined that, he illumined the seat on which he was sitting.

children.text: tadavabhāsya sarvaṃ gṛhamavabhāsayati sma
children.translated_text: Having illumined that, he illumined the whole house.

children.text: sarvaṃ gṛhamavabhāsya gṛhasyopariṣṭānniḥsṛtya pūrvāṃ diśamavabhāsayati sma
children.translated_text: Having illumined the whole house, he emerged above the house and illumined the eastern direction.

children.text: evaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ paścimāṃ uttarāmadha ūrdhvaṃ samantāddaśadiśaḥ krośamātramekaikasyāṃ diśi mātuḥ kukṣigato bodhisattvaḥ śriyā tejasā varṇena cāvabhāsayati sma ||
children.translated_text: In this way he illumined the southern, western, and northern directions, below, above, and all around, the ten directions, for about a krośa in each direction, while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was in his mother's womb, by his glory, splendor, and color.

children.text: āgacchanti sma khalu punarbhikṣavaścatvāro mahārājāno 'ṣṭāviṃśacca mahāyakṣasenāpatayaḥ sārdhaṃ pañcamātrayakṣaśataiḥ pūrvāhṇakālasamaye bodhisattvasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca
children.translated_text: Moreover, monks, the Four Great Kings and the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals came, together with about five hundred yakṣas, in the forenoon, to see, venerate, attend upon, and hear the Dharma from the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: tadā bodhisattvastānāgatān viditvā dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇim abhyutkṣipya ekāṅgulikayā āsanānyupadarśayati sma
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, knowing that they had come, raised his right hand and with one finger pointed out seats.

children.text: niṣīdanti sma te lokapālādayo yathāprajñapteṣvāsaneṣu
children.translated_text: Those beginning with the guardians of the world sat down on the seats arranged according to their rank.

children.text: paśyanti sma bodhisattvaṃ mātuḥ kukṣigataṃ jātarūpamiva vigrahaṃ hastaṃ cālayantaṃ vicālayantam utkṣipantaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayantam
children.translated_text: They saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his mother's womb, like an image of gold, moving his hand, waving it, raising it, and setting it down.

children.text: te prītiprāmodyaprasādapratilabdhā bodhisattvaṃ namaskurvanti sma
children.translated_text: Having obtained joy, gladness, and serene faith, they bowed to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: niṣaṇṇāṃśca tān viditvā bodhisattvo dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati sma samādāpayati sma samuttejayati sma saṃpraharṣayati sma
children.translated_text: And knowing that they were seated, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> instructed them with a dharmic discourse, caused them to accept it, roused them, and gladdened them.

children.text: yadā ca prakramitukāmā bhavanti tadā bodhisattvasteṣāṃ cetasaiva vicintitaṃ vijñāya dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇimutkṣipya saṃcārayati sma
children.translated_text: And when they wished to depart, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, knowing by mind alone the thought in their minds, raised his right hand and moved it.

children.text: saṃcārya vicārayati sma
children.translated_text: Having moved it, he waved it about.

children.text: mātaraṃ ca na bādhate sma
children.translated_text: And he did not trouble his mother.

children.text: tadā teṣāṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāmevaṃ bhavati sma visarjitāḥ sma vayaṃ bodhisattveneti
children.translated_text: Then it occurred to those four Great Kings: "We have been dismissed by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>."

children.text: te bodhisattvaṃ bodhisattvamātaraṃ ca tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya prakrāmanti sma
children.translated_text: Having circumambulated the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother three times, they departed.

children.text: ayaṃ heturayaṃ pratyayo yadbodhisattvo rātryāṃ praśāntāyāṃ dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ saṃcārya vicārayati sma
children.translated_text: This was the cause, this the condition: when the night had become quiet, the Bodhisattva moved his right hand and turned it about.

children.text: vicārya punarapi smṛtaḥ samprajānaṃstaṃ pāṇiṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati sma
children.translated_text: Having turned it about, again mindful and clearly aware, he set that hand back in place.

children.text: punaraparaṃ yadā bodhisattvasya keciddarśanāyāgacchanti sma striyo vā puruṣo vā dārako vā dārikā vā tān bodhisattvaḥ pūrvatarameva pratisaṃmodayate sma paścādbodhisattvasya mātā ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, whenever some people came to see the Bodhisattva, whether women or a man, a boy or a girl, the Bodhisattva greeted them first, and afterward the Bodhisattva's mother did so.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigataḥ san sattvān pratisaṃmodanakuśalo bhavati smeti
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, while the Bodhisattva was in his mother's womb, he was skilled in greeting beings.

children.text: na ca kaściddevo vā nāgo vā yakṣo vā manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā yaḥ śaknoti sma bodhisattvaṃ pūrvataraṃ pratisaṃmoditum
children.translated_text: And there was no god, <s>nāga</s>, <s>yakṣa</s>, human being, or non-human being who was able to greet the Bodhisattva first.

children.text: atha tarhi bodhisattva eva tāvat pūrvataraṃ pratisaṃmodate sma paścādbodhisattvamātā ||
children.translated_text: Rather, the Bodhisattva himself first greeted them, and afterward the Bodhisattva's mother did so.

children.text: nirgate khalu punaḥ pūrvāhṇakālasamaye madhyāhnakālasamaye pratyupasthite atha khalu śakro devānāmindro niṣkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when the morning period had passed and the midday period had arrived, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, set out.

children.text: abhiniṣkrāntāśca trāyatriṃśaddevaputrā bodhisattvasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya
children.translated_text: And the divine sons of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, having set out, came to see the Bodhisattva, to venerate him, to attend upon him,

children.text: dharmaśravaṇāya cāgacchanti sma
children.translated_text: and to hear the Dharma.

children.text: tāṃśca bodhisattvo dūrata evāgacchato dṛṣṭvā dakṣiṇaṃ suvarṇavarṇaṃ bāhuṃ prasārya śakraṃ devānāmindraṃ devāṃśca trāyatriṃśān pratisaṃmodate sma
children.translated_text: Seeing them coming from afar, the Bodhisattva stretched out his right, golden-colored arm and greeted <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.

children.text: ekāṅgulikayā cāsanānyupadarśayati sma
children.translated_text: And with one finger he indicated the seats.

children.text: na ca śaknoti sma bhikṣavaḥ śakro devānāmindro bodhisattvasyājñāṃ pratiroddhum
children.translated_text: And, monks, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, was not able to resist the Bodhisattva's command.

children.text: niṣīdati sma śakro devānāmindrastadanye ca devaputrā yathāprajñapteṣvāsaneṣu
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and the other divine sons sat down on the seats that had been prepared.

children.text: tān bodhisattvo niṣaṇṇān viditvā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati sma samādāpayati sma samuttejayati sma saṃpraharṣayati sma
children.translated_text: Knowing that they were seated, the Bodhisattva instructed them with a Dharma discourse, caused them to accept it, roused them, and gladdened them.

children.text: yena ca bodhisattvaḥ pāṇiṃ saṃcārayati sma tanmukhā bodhisattvamātā bhavati sma
children.translated_text: And in whatever direction the Bodhisattva moved his hand, the Bodhisattva's mother faced that way.

children.text: tatasteṣāmevaṃ bhavati sma asmābhiḥ sārdhaṃ bodhisattvaḥ saṃmodate sma
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to them: "The Bodhisattva is conversing with us."

children.text: ekaikaścaivaṃ saṃjānīte sma mayaiva sārdhaṃ bodhisattvaḥ saṃlapati māmeva pratisaṃmodate sma iti ||
children.translated_text: And each one thought, "The Bodhisattva is speaking with me alone; he is greeting only me."

children.text: tasmin khalu punaḥ kūṭāgāre śakrasya devānāmindrasya trāyatriṃśānāṃ devānāṃ ca pratibhāsaḥ saṃdṛśyate sma
children.translated_text: In that peaked pavilion there appeared the reflection of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.

children.text: na khalu punaranyatraivaṃ pariśuddho bodhisattvaparibhogo bhavati yathā mātuḥ kukṣigatasya bodhisattvasya
children.translated_text: Indeed, nowhere else was the bodhisattva-paribhoga (Bodhisattva accoutrement) so pure as that of the Bodhisattva while he was in his mother's womb.

children.text: yadā ca bhikṣavaḥ śakro devānāmindrastadanye ca devaputrāḥ prakramitukāmā bhavanti sma tadā bodhisattvasteṣāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇimutkṣipya saṃcārayanti sma
children.translated_text: And when, monks, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and the other divine sons wished to depart, then the Bodhisattva, knowing by his own mind the thought arising in their minds, raised and moved his right hand.

children.text: saṃcārya vicārya punarapi smṛtaḥ samprajānan pratiṣṭhāpayati sma
children.translated_text: Having moved it and turned it about, again mindful and clearly aware, he set it back in place.

children.text: mātaraṃ ca na bādhate sma
children.translated_text: And he did not trouble his mother.

children.text: tadā śakrasya devānāmindrasyānyeṣāṃ ca trāyatriṃśānāṃ devānāmevaṃ bhavati sma visarjitā vayaṃ bodhisattveneti
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and to the other <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods: "We have been dismissed by the Bodhisattva."

children.text: te bodhisattvaṃ bodhisattvamātaraṃ ca tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya prakrāmanti sma ||
children.translated_text: Having circumambulated the Bodhisattva and the Bodhisattva's mother three times, they departed.

children.text: nirgate ca khalu punarbhikṣavo madhyāhnakālasamaye sāyāhnakālasamaye pratyupasthite atha khalu brahmā sahāpatiranekairbrahmakāyikair devaputraśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtastaṃ divyamojobindumādāya yena bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmati sma bodhisattvaṃ draṣṭuṃ vandituṃ paryupāsituṃ dharmaṃ ca śrotum
children.translated_text: And when, monks, the midday period had passed and the evening period had arrived, then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, surrounded and attended by many hundreds of thousands of divine sons of the <s>Brahmā</s> host, took that divine drop of essence and approached the place where the Bodhisattva was, in order to see the Bodhisattva, venerate him, attend upon him, and hear the Dharma.

children.text: samanvāharati sma bhikṣavaḥ bodhisattvo brahmāṇaṃ sahāpatimāgacchantaṃ saparivāram
children.translated_text: Monks, the Bodhisattva attended to <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> as he was coming with his retinue.

children.text: punareva ca bodhisattvo dakṣiṇaṃ suvarṇavarṇapāṇimutkṣipya brahmāṇaṃ sahāpatiṃ brahmakāyikāṃśca devaputrān pratisaṃmodate sma
children.translated_text: And again the Bodhisattva raised his right, golden-colored hand and greeted <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> and the divine sons of the <s>Brahmā</s> host.

children.text: ekāṅgulikayā cāsanānyupadarśayati sma
children.translated_text: And with one finger he indicated the seats.

children.text: na ca śaktirasti bhikṣavo brahmaṇaḥ sahāpaterbodhisattvasyājñāṃ pratiroddhum
children.translated_text: And, monks, <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> had no power to resist the Bodhisattva's command.

children.text: niṣīdati sma bhikṣavo brahmā sahāpatistadanye ca brahmakāyikā devaputrā yathāprajñapteṣvāsaneṣu
children.translated_text: Monks, <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> and the other divine sons of the <s>Brahmā</s> host sat down on the seats that had been prepared.

children.text: tān bodhisattvo niṣaṇṇān viditvā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati sma samādāpayati sma samuttejayati sma saṃpraharṣayati sma
children.translated_text: Knowing that they were seated, the Bodhisattva instructed them with a Dharma discourse, caused them to accept it, roused them, and gladdened them.

children.text: yena ca bodhisattvaḥ pāṇiṃ saṃcārayati sma tanmukhaiva māyādevī bhavati sma
children.translated_text: And in whatever direction the Bodhisattva moved his hand, <s>Māyādevī</s> faced that way.

children.text: tatasteṣāmekaikasyaivaṃ bhavati sma mayā sārdhaṃ bodhisattvaḥ saṃlapati māmeva pratisaṃmodate sma iti
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to each one of them: "The Bodhisattva is speaking with me; he is greeting only me."

children.text: yadā ca brahmā sahāpatistadanye ca brahmakāyikā devaputrā gantukāmā bhavanti sma tadā bodhisattvasteṣāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya dakṣiṇaṃ suvarṇavarṇaṃ bāhumutkṣipya saṃcārayati sma
children.translated_text: And when <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> and the other divine sons of the <s>Brahmā</s> host wished to go, then the Bodhisattva, knowing by his own mind the thought arising in their minds, raised and moved his right, golden-colored arm.

children.text: saṃcārya vicārayati sma
children.translated_text: Having moved it, he turned it about.

children.text: saṃcārya vicārya avasādatākāreṇa pāṇiṃ saṃcārayati sma
children.translated_text: Having moved it about and considered it, he moved his hand in a gesture indicating withdrawal.

children.text: mātaraṃ ca na bādhate sma
children.translated_text: And he did not trouble his mother.

children.text: tato brahmaṇaḥ sahāpatestadanyeṣāṃ ca brahmakāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāmevaṃ bhavati sma visarjitā vayaṃ bodhisattveneti
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> and those other divine sons belonging to the <s>Brahmā</s> host thought, "We have been dismissed by the Bodhisattva."

children.text: te bodhisattvaṃ bodhisattvamātaraṃ ca tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya punareva prakrāmanti sma
children.translated_text: They circumambulated the Bodhisattva and the Bodhisattva's mother three times, and then departed again.

children.text: bodhisattvaśca smṛtaḥ samprajānan pāṇiṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati sma ||
children.translated_text: And the Bodhisattva, mindful and fully aware, set his hand back in place.

children.text: āgacchanti sma khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ pūrvadakṣiṇapaścimottarābhyo digbhyo 'dhastādupariṣṭāt santāddaśabhyo digbhyo bahūni bodhisattvaśatasahasrāṇi bodhisattvasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca dharmasaṃgītisaṃgāyanāya ca
children.translated_text: Again, monks, from the east, south, west, and north, from below and above, and from all ten directions, many hundreds of thousands of Bodhisattvas came to see the Bodhisattva, to venerate him, to attend upon him, to hear the <s>dharma</s> (teaching), and to chant the collection of the <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: teṣāmāgatāgatānāṃ bodhisattvaḥ kāyāt prabhāmutsṛjya prabhāvyūhāni siṃhāsanānyabhinirmimīte sma
children.translated_text: For each of them as they arrived, the Bodhisattva emitted radiance from his body and fashioned lion-thrones made of arrays of light.

children.text: abhinirmāya tān bodhisattvāṃsteṣvāsaneṣu niṣīdayati sma
children.translated_text: After fashioning them, he seated those Bodhisattvas on those seats.

children.text: niṣaṇṇāṃścainān viditvā paripṛcchati sma paripraśnayati sma yadutāsyaiva bodhisattvasya mahāyānasya vistaravibhāgatāmupādāya
children.translated_text: And knowing that they were seated, he questioned and examined them concerning the extensive divisions of this very Bodhisattva's <s>Mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle).

children.text: na ca tān kaścidanyaḥ paśyati sma anyatra sabhāgebhyo devaputrebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: No one else saw them, except for divine sons of a corresponding class.

children.text: ayaṃ bhikṣavo heturayaṃ pratyayo yena bodhisattvaḥ praśāntāyāṃ rātryāṃ kāyāt prabhāmutsṛjati sma ||
children.translated_text: This, monks, is the cause and this is the condition by which the Bodhisattva emitted radiance from his body in the stillness of the night.

children.text: na khalu punarbhikṣavo māyādevī bodhisattvakukṣigate gurukāyatāṃ saṃjānīte sma anyatra laghutāmeva mṛdutāmeva saukhyatāmeva
children.translated_text: Moreover, monks, while the Bodhisattva was in her womb, <s>Māyādevī</s> did not feel heaviness in her body, but only lightness, only softness, only ease.

children.text: na codaragatāni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavati sma
children.translated_text: Nor did she experience the pains that occur within the belly.

children.text: na ca rāgaparidāhena vā dveṣaparidāhena vā mohaparidāhena vā paridahyate sma
children.translated_text: She was not burned by the fever of passion, or by the fever of hatred, or by the fever of delusion.

children.text: na ca kāmavitarkaṃ vā vyāpādavitarkaṃ vā vihiṃsāvitarkaṃ vā vitarkayati sma
children.translated_text: Nor did she think thoughts of sensual desire, thoughts of malice, or thoughts of harming.

children.text: na ca śītaṃ na coṣṇaṃ vā jighatsāṃ vā pipāsāṃ vā tamo vā rajo vā kleśaṃ vā saṃjānīte sma paśyati vā
children.translated_text: She did not feel or perceive cold, heat, hunger, thirst, darkness, dust, or affliction.

children.text: na cāsyā amanāpā rūpaśabdagandharasasparśā vā ābhāsamāgacchanti sma
children.translated_text: Nor did disagreeable forms, sounds, smells, tastes, or touches come into her awareness.

children.text: na ca pāpakān svapnān paśyati sma
children.translated_text: Nor did she see evil dreams.

children.text: na cāsyāḥ strīmāyā na śāṭhyaṃ nerṣyā na strīkleśā bādhante sma
children.translated_text: Nor did feminine guile, deceit, jealousy, or the afflictions associated with women trouble her.

children.text: pañcaśikṣāpadasamādattā khalu punaḥ śīlavatī daśakuśalakarmapathe pratiṣṭhitā tasmin samaye bodhisattvamātā bhavati sma
children.translated_text: At that time the Bodhisattva's mother was virtuous, having undertaken the five training rules and established in the ten paths of wholesome action.

children.text: na ca bodhisattvamātuḥ kvacit puruṣe rāgacittamutpadyate sma nāpi kasyacitpuruṣasya bodhisattvasya māturantike
children.translated_text: Nowhere did a mind of passion toward any man arise in the Bodhisattva's mother, nor did such a mind arise in any man in the presence of the Bodhisattva's mother.

children.text: ye ca kecitkapilāhvaye mahāpuravare anyeṣu vā janapadeṣu devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍabhūtāviṣṭāḥ strīpuruṣadārakadārikā vā te sarve bodhisattvamātuḥ sahadarśanādeva svasthāḥ smṛtipratilabdhā bhavanti sma
children.translated_text: And whoever in the great noble city called <s>Kapilāhvaya</s>, or in other districts, whether women, men, boys, or girls, were possessed by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, or bhūtas, all of them became well and regained mindfulness merely by seeing the Bodhisattva's mother.

children.text: te cāmanuṣyāḥ kṣiprameva prakrāmanti sma
children.translated_text: And those nonhuman beings quickly departed.

children.text: ye ca kecinnānārogaspṛṣṭāḥ sattvā bhavanti sma vātapittaśleṣmasaṃnipātajai rogaiḥ pīḍyante sma cakṣurogeṇa vā śrotrarogeṇa vā ghrāṇarogeṇa vā jihvārogeṇa vā oṣṭharogeṇa vā dantarogeṇa kaṇṭharogeṇa vā galagaṇḍarogeṇa vā uragaṇḍakuṣṭhakilāsaśoṣonmādāpasmārajvaragalagaṇḍapiṭakavisarpavicarcikādyai rogaiḥ sampīḍyante sma teṣāṃ bodhisattvamātā dakṣiṇapāṇiṃ mūrdhni pratiṣṭhāpayati sma
children.translated_text: And whatever beings were afflicted by various diseases, tormented by illnesses arising from wind, bile, phlegm, or their combination, or oppressed by eye disease, ear disease, nose disease, tongue disease, lip disease, tooth disease, throat disease, goiter, swellings, leprosy, white leprosy, wasting, madness, epilepsy, fever, pustules, erysipelas, eczema, and similar diseases, the Bodhisattva's mother placed her right hand on their heads.

children.text: te sahapratiṣṭhāpite pāṇau vigatavyādhayo bhūtvā svakasvakāni gṛhāṇi gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: As soon as her hand had been placed there, they became free from illness and went to their own homes.

children.text: antato māyādevī tṛṇagulmakamapi dharaṇitalādabhyutkṣipya glānebhyaḥ sattvebhyo 'nuprayacchati sma
children.translated_text: Even if <s>Māyādevī</s> lifted up a blade of grass or a shrub from the surface of the earth and gave it to sick beings,

children.text: te sahapratilambhādaroganirvikārā bhavanti sma
children.translated_text: they became free from disease and without disorder as soon as they received it.

children.text: yadā ca māyādevī svaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvaṃ pratyavekṣate sma tadā paśyati sma bodhisattvaṃ kukṣigataṃ tadyathāpi nāma supariśuddha ādarśamaṇḍale mukhamaṇḍalaṃ dṛśyate
children.translated_text: And when <s>Māyādevī</s> looked toward her own right side, then she saw the Bodhisattva dwelling in her womb, just as the disk of one's face is seen in a perfectly clean mirror-disc.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punastuṣṭā udagrā āttamanāḥ pramuditā prītisaumanasyajātā bhavati sma ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, she became satisfied, elated, delighted, glad, and filled with joy and happiness.

children.text: bodhisattvasya khalu punarbhikṣavo mātuḥ kukṣigatasyādhiṣṭhitaṃ satataṃ samitaṃ rātriṃdivaṃ divyāni tūryāṇi abhinirmāya pranadanti sma
children.translated_text: Moreover, monks, through the power of the Bodhisattva while he was dwelling in his mother's womb, divine instruments, having been manifested, constantly and continuously resounded night and day.

children.text: divyāni ca puṣpāṇi abhipravarṣanti sma
children.translated_text: And divine flowers rained down in abundance.

children.text: kālena devā varṣanti sma
children.translated_text: At the proper time the gods sent rain.

children.text: kālena vāyavo vānti sma
children.translated_text: At the proper time the winds blew.

children.text: kālena ṛtavo nakṣatrāṇi ca parivartante sma
children.translated_text: At the proper time the seasons and constellations turned in their courses.

children.text: kṣemaṃ ca rājyaṃ subhikṣaṃ ca sumanākulam anubhavati sma
children.translated_text: The kingdom experienced security, abundant food, and a population full of goodwill.

children.text: sarve ca kapilāhvaye mahāpuravare śākyā anye ca sattvāḥ khādanti sma pibanti sma krīḍanti sma pravicārayanti sma dānāni ca dadanti sma puṇyāni ca kurvanti sma kaumodyāmiva cāturmāsyāmekāntare krīḍāsukhavihārairviharanti sma
children.translated_text: And all the <s>Śākyas</s> and other beings in the great noble city called <s>Kapilāhvaya</s> ate, drank, played, wandered about, gave gifts, and performed meritorious deeds; as at the <s>Kaumudī</s> festival or during the <s>Cāturmāsya</s>, they dwelt continually in the pleasures and comforts of play.

children.text: rājāpi śuddhodanaḥ samprāptabrahmacaryoparatarāṣṭrakāryo 'pi supariśuddhastapovanagata iva dharmamevānuvartate sma ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Śuddhodana</s> too, although he had attained brahmacarya and had withdrawn from affairs of state, was completely purified; as if gone to a grove of ascetic practice, he followed only the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: evaṃrūpeṇa bhikṣava ṛddhiprātihāryeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigato 'sthāt
children.translated_text: With such a miracle of magical power, monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> remained in his mother's womb.

children.text: tatra khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma drakṣyasi tvamānanda ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ yatra bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigato vyāhārṣīt
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "<s>Ānanda</s>, you shall see the jewel-array, the furnishing of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, where the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while in his mother's womb, spoke."

children.text: āha paśyeyaṃ bhagavan paśyeyaṃ sugata
children.translated_text: He said, "I would see it, Blessed One; I would see it, <s>Sugata</s>."

children.text: darśayati sma tathāgata āyuṣmata ānandasya śakrasya devānāmindrasya caturṇāṃ ca lokapālānāṃ tadanyeṣāṃ ca devamanuṣyāṇām
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> showed it to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, to the four <s>Lokapālas</s>, and to the other gods and humans.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca te tuṣṭā abhūvan udagrā āttamanasaḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātāḥ
children.translated_text: Having seen it, they became satisfied, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness.

children.text: sa ca brahmā sahāpatiḥ punareva brahmaloke samāropya pratiṣṭhāpayati sma caityārtham ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> again carried it up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s> and established it there as an object of worship, a caitya.

children.text: tatra khalu bhagavān punarapi bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma iti hi bhikṣavo daśamāsakukṣigatena bodhisattvena ṣaṭtriṃśannayutāni devamanuṣyāṇāṃ triṣu yāneṣu paripācitānyabhūvan
children.translated_text: There the Blessed One again addressed the monks: "Thus indeed, monks, while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was in the womb for ten months, thirty-six nayutas of gods and humans were brought to maturity in the three vehicles.

children.text: yatredamucyate yat ||
children.translated_text: About this the following is said:

children.text: bodhisattva agrasattva mātukukṣisaṃsthitaḥ prakampitā ca ṣaḍvikāra medinī sakānanā
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the foremost being, was established in his mother's womb, and the earth with its forests shook in six ways.

children.text: suvarṇavarṇa ābha mukta sarvāpāya śodhitā praharṣitāśca devasaṃgha dharmagañju bheṣyate ||
children.translated_text: A golden-colored radiance was released; all bad destinies were purified; and the hosts of gods rejoiced, for he would become a treasury of <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: suṃsaṃsthito mahāvimānu naikaratnacitrito yatra vīru āruhitva tiṣṭhate vināyakaḥ
children.translated_text: Well established was a great palace, adorned with many jewels, where the hero, the guide, having ascended, stood.

children.text: gandhottamena candanena pūrito virocate yasyaikakarṣu trisahasramūlyaratnapūrito ||
children.translated_text: Filled with the finest fragrance and sandalwood, it shone; a single karṣa of it was filled with jewels worth three thousand.

children.text: mahāsahasralokadhātu heṣvi bhindiyitvanā udāgato guṇākarasya padmaojabinduko
children.translated_text: Having pierced the great-thousand world-systems, the lotus-drop of essence of the mine of virtues arose.

children.text: so saptarātra puṇyateja brahmaloki udgato gṛhītva brahma ojabindu bodhisattva nāmayī ||
children.translated_text: For seven nights that drop, through the brilliance of merit, rose to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>; <s>Brahmā</s> took the drop of essence and offered it to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: na asti sarvasattvakāyi bhuktu yo jareya taṃ anyatra bhūri bodhisattva brahmakalpasaṃnibhe
children.translated_text: There is no body of any being that could digest it after eating it, apart from the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s>, comparable to a <s>Brahmā</s> kalpa.

children.text: anekakalpa puṇyateja ojabindu saṃsthito bhujitva sattva kāyacitta jñānaśuddha gacchiṣu ||
children.translated_text: That drop of essence, established through the brilliance of merit for many kalpas, when eaten, made the bodies, minds, and knowledge of beings become pure.

children.text: śakra brahma lokapāla pūjanāya nāyakaṃ trīṇi kāla āgamitva bodhisattvamantikam
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the <s>Lokapālas</s>, to worship the leader, came three times to the side of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: vandayitva pūjayitva dharma śṛṇute varaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ karitva sarva gacchiṣū yathāgatā ||
children.translated_text: Having bowed and worshiped, they listened to the excellent <s>Dharma</s>; having circumambulated, all went away just as they had come.

children.text: bodhisattva dharmakāma enti lokadhātuṣu prabhāviyūha āsaneṣu te niṣaṇṇa dṛśyiṣu
children.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who desired the <s>Dharma</s> came in the world-systems; they were seen seated on seats of splendid array.

children.text: parasparaṃ ca śrutva dharma yānaśreṣṭhamuttamaṃ prayānti sarvi hṛṣṭacitta varṇamāla bhāṣato ||
children.translated_text: Having heard from one another the <s>Dharma</s> of the supreme and highest vehicle, all departed with joyful minds, uttering garlands of praise.

children.text: ye ca iṣṭidārakāsu duḥkhitā tadā abhūt bhūtaspṛṣṭa kṣiptacitta nagna pāṃśumrakṣitā
children.translated_text: And those who at that time were suffering among beloved children, touched by spirits, deranged in mind, naked, and smeared with dust,

children.text: te ca sarva dṛṣṭva māya bhonti labdhacetanā smṛtīmatīgatīupeta gehi gehi gacchiṣu ||
children.translated_text: all of them, having seen <s>Māyā</s>, recovered consciousness, became endowed with mindfulness and right course, and went each to their homes.

children.text: vātato va pittato va śleṣmasaṃnipātakaiḥ ye ca cakṣuroga śrotraroga kāyacittapīḍitā
children.translated_text: Those afflicted by wind, or bile, or phlegm, or their combination, and those afflicted by eye disease, ear disease, or pain of body and mind,

children.text: naikarūpa naikajāti vyādhibhiśca ye hatā sthāpite sma māya mūrdhni pāṇi bhonti nirjarā ||
children.translated_text: and those struck by diseases of many forms and many kinds, when <s>Māyā</s> placed her hand upon their heads, became free from decay and sickness.

children.text: athāpi vā tṛṇasya tūli bhūmito gṛhītvanā dadāti māya āturāṇa sarvi bhonti nirjarā
children.translated_text: Or again, taking a tuft of grass from the ground, <s>Māyā</s> gave it to the sick, and all became free from sickness.

children.text: saukhyaprāpti nirvikāra gehi gehi gacchiṣu bhaiṣajyabhūti vaidyarāji kukṣisaṃpratiṣṭhite ||
children.translated_text: Having attained ease and being without disorder, they went each to their homes, when the medicine-being, the king of physicians, was established in the womb.

children.text: yasmi kāli māyadevi svātanuṃ nirīkṣate adṛśāti bodhisattva kukṣiye pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: At the time when <s>Māyādevī</s> looked at her own body, she saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in her womb.

children.text: yathaiva candra antarīkṣa tārakai parīvṛtaṃ tathaiva nāthu bodhisattvalakṣaṇairalaṃkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Just as the moon in the sky is surrounded by stars, so the Lord was adorned with the marks of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: no ca tasya rāga doṣa naiva moha bādhate kāmachandu naiva tasya īrṣi naiva hiṃsitā
children.translated_text: Neither passion nor hatred, nor delusion, troubled her; neither sensual desire, nor envy, nor harmfulness was in her.

children.text: tuṣṭacitta hṛṣṭacitta prīti saumanasthitā kṣudhāpipāsa śīta uṣṇa naiva tasya bādhate ||
children.translated_text: She was content in mind, joyful in mind, established in gladness and happiness; hunger, thirst, cold, and heat did not trouble her.

children.text: aghaṭṭitāśca nityakāla divyatūrya vādiṣu pravarṣayanti divyapuṣpa gandhaśreṣṭha śobhanā
children.translated_text: At all times, without being struck, divine instruments sounded; beautiful heavenly flowers and the finest fragrances rained down.

children.text: deva paśyi mānuṣāśca mānuṣā amānuṣāṃ no viheṭhi no vihiṃsi tatra te parasyaram ||
children.translated_text: Gods saw humans, and humans saw non-humans; there they did not harass or harm one another.

children.text: ramanti sattva krīḍayanti annapānudenti ca ānandaśabda ghoṣayanti hṛṣṭatuṣṭamānasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beings delighted and played; they gave food and drink; with joyful and satisfied minds they made sounds of rejoicing.

children.text: kṣamā rajoanākulā ca kāli deva varṣate tṛṇāśca puṣpa oṣadhīya tasmi kāli rohiṣu ||
children.translated_text: At that time, when the gods rained, the earth was patient and untroubled by dust; grasses, flowers, and herbs grew then.

children.text: rājagehi saptarātra ratnavarṣa varṣito yato daridrasattva gṛhya dāna denti bhuñjate
children.translated_text: In the royal palace, for seven nights a rain of jewels rained down; poor beings took it, gave gifts, and enjoyed it.

children.text: nāsti sattva yo daridra yo ca āsi duḥkhito bherumūrdhni nandaneva eva sattva nandiṣu ||
children.translated_text: There was no being who was poor or who was distressed; beings rejoiced as if in <s>Nandana</s> on the summit of <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: so ca rāju śākiyāna poṣadhī upoṣito rājyakāryu no karoti dharmameva gocarī
children.translated_text: That king of the <s>Śākyas</s> observed the <s>poṣadha</s>; he did not conduct affairs of state, but had only the <s>Dharma</s> as his sphere.

children.text: tapovanaṃ ca so praviṣṭa māyādevī pṛcchate kīdṛśenti kāyi saukhya agrasattva dhārati ||
children.translated_text: And he entered the ascetic grove and asked <s>Māyādevī</s>, "What kind of bodily ease is there as you bear the foremost being?"

children.text: Chapter 7
iti hi bhikṣavo daśamāseṣu nigateṣu bodhisattvasya janmakālasamaye pratyupasthite rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhodyāne dvātriṃśatpūrvanimittāni prādurabhūvan
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, when ten months had passed and the time for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s birth had arrived, thirty-two preliminary omens appeared in the household garden of King <s>Suddhodana</s>.

children.text: katamāni dvātriṃśat sarvapuṣpāṇi suṅgībhūtāni na puṣpanti sma
children.translated_text: What were the thirty-two? All the flowers had become buds, but they did not bloom.

children.text: puṣkariṇīṣu cotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkāṇyabhyudgatāni kuḍmalībhūtāni na puṣpanti sma
children.translated_text: And in the lotus ponds blue lotuses, lotuses, water lilies, and white lotuses had risen up and become buds, but they did not bloom.

children.text: tadā ca puṣpaphalavṛkṣā dharaṇītalādabhyudgamya kṣārakajātā na phalanti sma
children.translated_text: At that time flowering and fruiting trees sprang up from the surface of the earth, became young shoots, but did not bear fruit.

children.text: aṣṭau ca ratnavṛkṣāḥ prādurabhūvan
children.translated_text: And eight jewel trees appeared.

children.text: viṃśati ca ratnanidhānaśatasahasrāṇyutplutya vyavasthitāni dṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: And twenty hundred-thousand deposits of jewels sprang up and were seen standing forth.

children.text: antaḥpure ca ratnāṅkurāḥ prādurabhūvan
children.translated_text: And jewel sprouts appeared in the inner apartments.

children.text: sugandhitailaparivāsitāśca gandhodakaśītoṣṇāḥ prasravanti sma
children.translated_text: Streams of scented water, cool and warm and perfumed with fragrant oil, flowed forth.

children.text: himavatparvatapārśvācca siṃhapotakā āgatyāgatyābhinadantaḥ kapilāhvayapuravaraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya dvāramūleṣvavatiṣṭhante sma na kaṃcitsattvaṃ viheṭhayanti sma
children.translated_text: And from the side of Mount <s>Himavat</s>, lion cubs came again and again, roaring; after circumambulating the excellent city called <s>Kapila</s>, they stood at the bases of the gates and did not harm any being.

children.text: pañcaśatāni pāṇḍarāṇāṃ hastiśāvakānāmāgatya rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyāgrakaraiścaraṇāvabhilikhanti sma
children.translated_text: Five hundred white elephant calves came and stroked King <s>Suddhodana</s>'s feet with the tips of their trunks.

children.text: mekhalībaddhakāśca devadārakā rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyāntaḥpure utsaṅgenotsaṅgamanuparivartamānāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: Divine boys wearing girdles were seen in King <s>Suddhodana</s>'s inner palace, passing from lap to lap.

children.text: gaganatalagatārdhakāyā nāgakanyā nānāpūjopakaraṇaparigṛhītā adhyālambamānāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: Nāga maidens, their upper bodies in the sky and holding various implements of worship, were seen leaning down.

children.text: daśa ca nāgakanyāsahasrāṇi mayūrāṅgahastakaparigṛhītā gaganatale 'vasthitāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: Ten thousand nāga maidens, holding peacock-feather fans in their hands, were seen standing in the sky.

children.text: daśa ca pūrṇakumbhasahasrāṇi kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ pradakṣiṇīkurvanti saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: Ten thousand full jars were seen circumambulating the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>.

children.text: daśa ca devakanyāsahasrāṇi gandhodakabhṛṅgāraparigṛhītā mūrdhni dhārayantyo 'vasthitāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: Ten thousand divine maidens, holding pitchers of scented water and carrying them on their heads, were seen standing there.

children.text: daśa ca devakanyāsahasrāṇi chatradhvajapatākāparigṛhītā avasthitāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: Ten thousand divine maidens, holding parasols, banners, and standards, were seen standing there.

children.text: bahūni cāpsaraḥśatasahasrāṇi śaṅkhabherīmṛdaṅgapaṇavaiḥ ghaṇṭāvasaktaiḥ pratīkṣamāṇānyavasthitāni saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: Many hundreds of thousands of apsarases, with conches, kettledrums, mrdangas, and panavas hung with bells, were seen standing in attendance.

children.text: sarve vāyavaścāvasthitā na vānti sma
children.translated_text: All the winds came to rest and did not blow.

children.text: sarvanadī ca prasravaṇāni ca na vahanti sma
children.translated_text: All the rivers and springs did not flow.

children.text: candrasūryavimānāni nakṣatrajyotirgaṇāśca na vahanti sma
children.translated_text: The moon- and sun-palaces and the hosts of stars and lights did not move.

children.text: puṣyaṃ ca nakṣatrayuktamabhūt
children.translated_text: And the asterism <s>Puṣya</s> was in conjunction.

children.text: ratnajālaparisphuṭaṃ ca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhaṃ saṃsthitamabhūt
children.translated_text: King <s>Suddhodana</s>'s house was covered with a net of jewels.

children.text: vaiśvānaraśca na jvalati sma
children.translated_text: The fire <s>Vaiśvānara</s> did not blaze.

children.text: kūṭāgāraprāsādatoraṇadvārakataleṣu ca maṇiratnānyabhipralambamānāni ca saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: On the pinnacled pavilions, palaces, gateways, doorways, and lintels, jewels and precious stones were seen hanging down.

children.text: dūṣyagañjāśca viviratnagañjāśca prāvṛtāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: Heaps of cloth and heaps of various jewels were seen laid open.

children.text: kākolūkagṛdhravṛkaśṛgālaśabdāścāntarhitā abhūvan
children.translated_text: The sounds of crows, owls, vultures, wolves, and jackals disappeared.

children.text: sujātajātaśabdāśca śrūyante sma
children.translated_text: Auspicious sounds, born of noble beings, were heard.

children.text: sarvajanapadakarmāntāśca samucchinnā abhūvan
children.translated_text: All work activities in the districts ceased.

children.text: utkūlanikūlāśca pṛthivīpradeśāḥ samāḥ samavasthitāḥ sarvavīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakarathyāntarāpaṇamukhāni ca pāṇitalamṛṣṭānīva puṣpābhikīrṇāni virocante sma
children.translated_text: High and low places of the earth became even and level, and all streets, squares, crossroads, roads, lanes, and shop-fronts shone, strewn with flowers as though wiped smooth by the palm of a hand.

children.text: sarvāśca gurviṇyaḥ samyaksukhena prasūyante sma
children.translated_text: And all pregnant women gave birth properly and happily.

children.text: sarvaśālavanadevatāśca patreṣvardhakāyānabhinirmāya namyamānāḥ sthitāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma
children.translated_text: All the deities of the sala groves, manifesting half of their bodies among the leaves, were seen standing bowed down.

children.text: imāni dvātriṃśatpūrvanimittāni prādurabhūvan ||
children.translated_text: These thirty-two preliminary omens appeared.

children.text: atha khalu māyādevī bodhisattvasya janmakālasamayaṃ jñātvā bodhisattvasyaiva tejo'nubhāvena rātryāṃ prathame yāme rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramya gāthābhirabhyabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Mayadevi</s>, knowing that the time of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s birth had come, through the very splendor and power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, approached King <s>Suddhodana</s> in the first watch of the night and addressed him in verses:

children.text: deva śṛṇu hi mahyaṃ bhāṣato yaṃ mataṃ me aciraciracireṇā jāta udyānabuddhiḥ
children.translated_text: "Lord, listen to me as I speak of what I think: very soon the wish for the garden has arisen in me.

children.text: yadi ca tava na roṣo naiva doṣo na mohaḥ kṣipramahu vrajeyā krīḍaudyānabhūmim ||
children.translated_text: If there is no anger, no fault, and no delusion in you, I would quickly go to the pleasure-garden ground.

children.text: tvamiha tapasi khinno dharmacittaprayukto ahu ca cirapraviṣṭā śuddhasattvaṃ dharentī
children.translated_text: You here are wearied by austerity and intent on the thought of dharma; and I, long pregnant, am bearing a pure being.

children.text: drumavara pratibuddhāḥ phullitā śālavṛkṣāḥ yukta bhaviya devā gantumudyānabhūmim ||
children.translated_text: The best trees have awakened; the sala trees are in blossom. It would be fitting, lord, to go to the garden ground.

children.text: ṛtupravara vasanto yoṣitāṃ maṇḍanīyo bhramaravaravighuṣṭāḥ kokilabarhigītāḥ
children.translated_text: The excellent season is spring, an adornment for women, resounding with excellent bees and with the songs of cuckoos and peacocks.

children.text: śuciruciravicitrā bhrāmyate puṣpareṇuḥ sādhu dadahi ājñāṃ gacchamo mā vilambaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Pure, lovely, variegated flower-pollen is swirling about. Kindly give the command; let us go, do not delay."

children.text: vacanamimu śruṇitvā deviye pārthivendraḥ tuṣṭo muditacittaḥ pāriṣadyānavocat
children.translated_text: Having heard this speech of the queen, the lord of the earth, pleased and glad at heart, spoke to his attendants:

children.text: hayagajarathaṃ paṅktyā vāhanā yojayadhvaṃ pravaraguṇasamṛddhāṃ lumbinīṃ maṇḍayadhvam ||
children.translated_text: "Yoke the horses, elephants, and chariots in rows as vehicles; adorn <s>Lumbini</s>, endowed with excellent qualities.

children.text: nīlagirinikāśāṃ meghavarṇānubaddhāṃ viṃśati ca sahasrān yojayadhvaṃ gajānām
children.translated_text: Yoke twenty thousand elephants, resembling blue mountains and covered with cloud-colored trappings,

children.text: maṇikanakavicitrāṃ hemajālopagūḍhāṃ ghaṇṭarucirapārśvān ṣaḍviṣāṇāṃ gajendrān ||
children.translated_text: lordly six-tusked elephants, variegated with jewels and gold, enclosed in nets of gold, their flanks lovely with bells.

children.text: himarajatanikāśāṃ muñjakeśāṃ sukeśāṃ viṃśati ca sahasrān yojayadhvaṃ hayānām
children.translated_text: Yoke twenty thousand horses, resembling snow and silver, with manes like muñja grass, fine-maned,

children.text: kanakaracitapārśvā kiṅkiṇījālalambā pavanajavitavegā vāhanā pārthivasya ||
children.translated_text: the king's mounts, with sides fashioned in gold, hanging with nets of little bells, swift with the speed of the wind."

children.text: naragaṇa raṇaśauṇḍān śūra saṃgrāmakāmān asidhanuśaraśaktipāśakhaḍgāgrahastān
children.translated_text: Appoint companies of men, battle-seasoned heroes eager for combat, with swords, bows, arrows, spears, nooses, and sword-points in their hands,

children.text: viṃśati ca sahasrān yojayadhvaṃ suśīghraṃ māya saparivārāṃ rakṣathā apramattā ||
children.translated_text: twenty thousand in number, very quickly; guard <s>Māyā</s> and her retinue without negligence.

children.text: maṇikanakaniṣiktāṃ lumbinīṃ kārayadhvaṃ vividhavasanaratnaiḥ sarvavṛkṣāṃ pravethā
children.translated_text: Have <s>Lumbinī</s> made bright with jewels and gold; adorn all the trees with various garments and jewels.

children.text: vividhakusumacitraṃ nandanaṃ vā surāṇāṃ vadatha ca mama śīghraṃ sarvametaṃ vidhāya ||
children.translated_text: Make it variegated with many kinds of flowers, like the gods' <s>Nandana</s> grove; and when all this has been done, tell me quickly.

children.text: vacanamimu niśamyā pāriṣadyaiḥ kṣaṇena vāhana kṛta sajjā lumbinī maṇḍitā sā
children.translated_text: Having heard this command, the attendants in an instant made the vehicles ready, and that <s>Lumbinī</s> was adorned.

children.text: pāriṣadya āha ||
children.translated_text: The attendants said:

children.text: jaya jaya hi narendrā āyu pālehi dīrghaṃ sarva kṛtu yathoktaṃ kāru deva pratīkṣa ||
children.translated_text: Victory, victory, O king! Preserve your life for a long time. Everything has been done as ordered; graciously wait, O lord.

children.text: so ca naravarendro hṛṣṭacitto bhavitvā gṛhavaramanuviṣṭo iṣṭikānevamāha
children.translated_text: Then that best of kings, delighted in heart, entered the excellent house and spoke thus to his beloved women:

children.text: yasya ahu manāpo yā ca me prītikāmā sā mi kuruta ājñāṃ maṇḍayitvātmabhāvam ||
children.translated_text: Whichever of you is dear to me and desires my pleasure, let her carry out my command after adorning herself.

children.text: varasurabhisugandhāṃ bhāvaraṅgāṃ vicitrāṃ vasana mṛdumanojñāṃ prāvṛṇothā udagrāḥ
children.translated_text: Put on excellent, sweetly fragrant perfumes, varied and colored with pleasing dyes, and soft, charming garments; be exultant.

children.text: urasi vigalitānāṃ muktahārā bhavethā ābharaṇavibhūṣāṃ darśayethādya sarvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let pearl necklaces hang down upon your breasts; today display every ornament and adornment.

children.text: tuṇapaṇavamṛdaṅgāṃ vīṇaveṇūmukuṇḍāṃ tūryaśatasahasrān yojayadhvaṃ manojñāṃ
children.translated_text: Set in place pleasant tūṇas, paṇavas, mṛdaṅgas, vīṇās, flutes, and mukuṇḍas, hundreds of thousands of musical instruments.

children.text: bhūya kuruta harṣaṃ devakanyāna yūyaṃ śrutva madhuraghoṣaṃ devatāpi spṛheyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Make still greater joy, you women like divine maidens; hearing the sweet sound, even the deities will long for it.

children.text: ekarathavaresmiṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ māyadevī mā ca puruṣa istrī anya tatrāruheyā
children.translated_text: Let <s>Māyādevī</s> alone sit in this excellent chariot, and let no other man or woman mount there.

children.text: nāri vividhavarmā taṃ rathaṃ vāhayantāṃ mā ca pratikūlaṃ mā manāpaṃ śruṇeṣyā ||
children.translated_text: Let women in various armor and attire drive that chariot, and let her hear nothing adverse or unpleasant.

children.text: hayagajarathapattīṃ sainyaśrīmadvicitrāṃ dvāri sthita nṛpasyā śrūyate uccaghoṣāḥ
children.translated_text: At the king's gate loud cries were heard from a splendid, varied army of horses, elephants, chariots, and infantry.

children.text: kṣubhitajalanidhirvā śrūyate eva śabdo * * * * ||
children.translated_text: A sound was heard just like that of a stirred ocean ... [lacuna].

children.text: māya yada gṛhāto nirgatā dvāramūlaṃ ghaṇṭa śatasahasrā tāḍitā maṅgalārtham ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Māyā</s> came out from the house to the doorway, hundreds of thousands of bells were struck for auspiciousness.

children.text: so ca ratha vicitro maṇḍitaḥ pārthivena api ca marusahasrairdivyasiṃhāsanebhiḥ
children.translated_text: That splendid chariot had been adorned by the king, and also by thousands of <s>Maruts</s> with divine thrones;

children.text: caturi ratanavṛkṣā patrapuṣpopapetā abhinaditamanojñāṃ haṃsakrauñcān mayūrān ||
children.translated_text: it had four jewel trees furnished with leaves and flowers, and was delightful with the cries of geese, cranes, and peacocks.

children.text: chatradhvajapatākāścocchritā vaijayantyaḥ kiṅkiṇivarajālaiśchāditaṃ divyavastraiḥ
children.translated_text: Umbrellas, banners, flags, and pennants were raised; it was covered with nets of tinkling bells and with heavenly fabrics.

children.text: maruvadhu gaganesmiṃ taṃ rathaṃ prekṣayante divyamadhuraghoṣaṃ śrāvayantyaḥ stuvanti ||
children.translated_text: The wives of the <s>Maruts</s> gazed at that chariot in the sky, uttering divine, sweet sounds and praising it.

children.text: upaviśati yadā sā māya siṃhāsanāgre pracalita trisahasrā medinī ṣaḍvikāram
children.translated_text: When <s>Māyā</s> sat at the front of the lion throne, the three-thousandfold earth shook in six ways.

children.text: puṣpa maru kṣipiṃsū ambarāṃ bhrāmayiṃsū adya jagati śreṣṭho jāyate lumbinīye ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maruts</s> scattered flowers and whirled them through the sky, saying, 'Today the best one in the world will be born in <s>Lumbinī</s>.'

children.text: caturi jagatipālāstaṃ rathaṃ vāhayante tridaśapatirapīndro mārgaśuddhiṃ karoti
children.translated_text: The four world-protectors drove that chariot, and <s>Indra</s>, lord of the Thirty-three, made the road pure.

children.text: brahma puratu gacchī durjanāṃ vārayanto amaraśatasahasrāḥ prāñjalīkā namante ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> went in front, warding off wicked people, and hundreds of thousands of immortals bowed with joined palms.

children.text: nṛpati muditacitto vīkṣate tāṃ viyūhāṃ tasya bhavati evaṃ vyakta yaṃ devadevo
children.translated_text: The king, joyful in heart, looked upon that array, and this thought arose in him: 'Clearly this one is the god of gods.

children.text: yasya caturi pālā brahma sendrāśca devāḥ kuruta vipulapūjāṃ vyakta yaṃ śuddhabhāvī ||
children.translated_text: He for whom the four protectors, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the gods together with <s>Indra</s> perform vast worship is clearly pure in nature.'

children.text: nāsti tribhavi sattvo yaḥ sahetpūjametāṃ deva atha ca nāgāḥ śakra brahmā ca pālāḥ
children.translated_text: There is no being in the three realms who could endure this worship from the gods, nāgas, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the protectors.

children.text: mūrdha tada phaleyā jīvitaṃ cāsya naśyet ayu puna atidevaḥ sarvapūjāṃ sahāti ||
children.translated_text: His head would split apart then, and his life would perish; but this super-divine one endures every worship.

children.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo māyādevī caturaśītyā hayarathasahasraiḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitaiḥ parivṛtā caturaśītyā gajarathasahasraiḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitaiḥ caturaśītyā ca pattisahasraiḥ śūrairvīrairvarāṅgarūpibhiḥ susaṃnaddhadṛḍhavarmakavacitairanuparigṛhītā ṣaṣṭyā ca śākyakanyāsahasraiḥ puraskṛtā catvāriṃśatā ca sahasrai rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya jñātikulaprasūtaiḥ śākyaiḥ vṛddhadaharamadhyamaiḥ saṃrakṣitā ṣaṣṭyā ca sahasrai rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyāntaḥpureṇa gītavādyasamyaktūryatāḍāvacarasaṃgītisaṃpravāditena parivṛtā caturaśītyā ca devakanyāsahasraiḥ parivṛtā caturaśītyā ca nāgakanyāsahasraiḥ caturaśītyā ca gandharvakanyāsahasraiḥ caturaśītyā ca kinnarakanyāsahasraiḥ caturaśītyā cāsurakanyāsahasraiḥ nānāvyūhālaṃkārālaṃkṛtābhiḥ nānāgītavādyavarṇabhāṣiṇībhir anugamyamānā niryāti sma
children.translated_text: Then, monks, <s>Māyādevī</s> set out surrounded by eighty-four thousand horse-chariots adorned with every ornament, by eighty-four thousand elephant-chariots adorned with every ornament, and by eighty-four thousand foot soldiers, heroic, brave, handsome in their finest form, well armed and clad in firm armor. She was preceded by sixty thousand <s>Śākya</s> maidens, guarded by forty thousand <s>Śākyas</s> born from the kinsmen's line of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, elders, youths, and middle-aged men, surrounded by sixty thousand women of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s inner palace with songs, instruments, full orchestral music, and beating drums sounding forth, surrounded by eighty-four thousand deva maidens, by eighty-four thousand nāga maidens, by eighty-four thousand gandharva maidens, by eighty-four thousand kinnara maidens, and by eighty-four thousand asura maidens, all adorned with many kinds of arrays and ornaments, speaking in many kinds of song, music, and praise.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca lumbinīvanaṃ gandhodakasiktaṃ divyapuṣpābhikīrṇīkṛtamabhūt
children.translated_text: The whole <s>Lumbinī</s> grove was sprinkled with scented water and strewn with divine flowers.

children.text: sarvavṛkṣāśca tasmin vanavare akālapatrapuṣpaphalāni dadanti sma
children.translated_text: And all the trees in that excellent grove gave leaves, flowers, and fruits out of season.

children.text: devaiśca tathā tadvanaṃ samalaṃkṛtamabhūt tadyathāpi nāma miśrakāvanaṃ devānāṃ samalaṃkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The gods too had adorned that grove, just as the gods' <s>Miśrakāvana</s> grove is adorned.

children.text: atha khalu māyādevī lumbinīvanamanupraviśya tasmādrathavarādavatīrya naramarukanyāparivṛtā vṛkṣeṇa vṛkṣaṃ paryaṭantī vanādvanaṃ caṅkramyamāṇā drumād drumaṃ nirīkṣamāṇā anupūrveṇa yenāsau plakṣo mahādrumaratnavarapravaraḥ suvibhaktaśākhaḥ samapatramañjarīdharo divyamānuṣyanānāpuṣpasaṃpuṣpito varapravarasurabhigandhinānāgandhinānāraṅgavastrābhipralambito vividhamaṇivicitraprabhojjvalitaḥ sarvaratnamūladaṇḍaśākhāpatrasamalaṃkṛtaḥ suvibhaktavistīrṇaśākhaḥ karatalanibhe bhūmibhāge suvibhaktavistīrṇanīlatṛṇamayūragrīvāsaṃnibhe kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśe dharaṇītale saṃsthitaḥ pūrvajinajanetryābhinivāsitaḥ devasaṃgītyanugītaḥ śubhavimalaviśuddhaḥ śuddhāvāsadevaśatasahasraiḥ praśāntacittair abhinatajaṭāmakuṭāvalambitāvanatamūrdhabhir abhinandyamānastaṃ plakṣavṛkṣamupajagāma ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Māyādevī</s>, having entered the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove and descended from that excellent chariot, surrounded by daughters of men and gods, wandered from tree to tree, walked from grove to grove, and looked from tree to tree. In due order she approached that plakṣa tree, the foremost and best jewel among great trees: its branches were well divided; it bore even leaves and flower-clusters; it was in bloom with many divine and human flowers; it was hung with various fragrances, many perfumes, many colors, and cloths; it shone with the splendor of varied jewels; its roots, trunk, branches, and leaves were adorned with every jewel; its wide branches were beautifully arranged; it stood on a patch of earth like the palm of a hand, on ground covered with widely spread blue grass resembling a peacock's neck and soft to the touch like kācilindika cloth; it had been inhabited by the mothers of former Jinas, sung of by divine choirs, auspicious, stainless, and pure; and it was being joyfully honored by hundreds of thousands of <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> gods, whose minds were peaceful and whose heads were bent low, their braided crowns and diadems hanging down. She approached that plakṣa tree.

children.text: atha sa plakṣavṛkṣo bodhisattvasya tejo'nubhāvenāvanamya praṇamati sma
children.translated_text: Then, through the power and majesty of the Bodhisattva, that plakṣa tree bent down and bowed.

children.text: atha māyādevī gaganatalagateva vidyut dṛṣṭiṃ dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ prasārya plakṣaśākhāṃ gṛhītvā salīlaṃ gaganatalaṃ prekṣamāṇā vijṛmbhamānā sthitābhūt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Māyādevī</s>, like lightning in the vault of the sky, extended her right arm, grasped a branch of the plakṣa tree, and stood gracefully, looking up into the sky and stretching herself.

children.text: atha tasmin samaye ṣaṣṭyapsaraḥśatasahasrāṇi kāmāvacaradevebhya upasaṃkramya māyādevyā upasthāne paricaryāṃ kurvanti sma ||
children.translated_text: At that time sixty hundreds of thousands of apsarases came from the gods of the desire realm and performed service and attendance for <s>Māyādevī</s>.

children.text: evaṃrūpeṇa khalu puna ṛddhiprātihāryeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigato 'sthāt
children.translated_text: Endowed with such a display of supernormal power and miracle, the Bodhisattva remained in his mother's womb.

children.text: sa paripūrṇānāṃ daśānāṃ māsānāmatyayena māturdakṣiṇapārśvānniṣkramati sma smṛtaḥ samprajānannanupalipto garbhamalairyathā nānyaḥ kaściducyate 'nyeṣāṃ garbhamala iti ||
children.translated_text: When ten full months had passed, he emerged from his mother's right side, mindful, fully aware, and unstained by the impurities of the womb, unlike anyone else in whom what is called womb-impurity is found.

children.text: tasmin khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samaye śakro devānāmindro brahmā ca sahāpatiḥ purataḥ sthitāvabhūtām yau bodhisattvaṃ paramagauravajātau divyakāśikavastrāntaritaṃ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgaiḥ smṛtau saṃprajñau pratigṛhṇāte sma ||
children.translated_text: At that time, monks, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> stood before him; filled with supreme reverence, they received the Bodhisattva, wrapped in divine Kāśika cloth, mindful and fully aware in every limb and part.

children.text: yasmiṃśca kūṭāgāre bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigato 'sthāt taṃ brahmā sahāpatirbrahmakāyikāśca devaputrā abhyutkṣipya brahmalokaṃ caityārthaṃ pūjārthaṃ copanāmayāmāsuḥ
children.translated_text: And the peaked pavilion in which the Bodhisattva had remained in his mother's womb was lifted up by <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> and the divine sons of the <s>Brahmā</s> host, and they brought it to the <s>Brahmā</s> world as an object of veneration and worship.

children.text: aparigṛhītaḥ khalu punarbodhisattvaḥ kenacinmanuṣyabhūtena atha tarhi bodhisattvaṃ devatāḥ prathamataraṃ pratigṛhṇanti sma ||
children.translated_text: The Bodhisattva was not taken hold of by any human being; rather, deities were the very first to receive him.

children.text: atha bodhisattvo jātamātraḥ pṛthivyāmavatarati sma
children.translated_text: Then the Bodhisattva, just born, descended upon the earth.

children.text: samanantarāvatīrṇasya ca bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya mahāpṛthivīṃ bhittvā mahāpadmaṃ prādurabhūt
children.translated_text: Immediately after the Bodhisattva, the great being, had descended, a great lotus appeared, breaking through the great earth.

children.text: nandopanandau ca nāgarājānau gaganatale 'rdhakāyau sthitvā śītoṣṇe dve vāridhāre 'bhinirbhittvā bodhisattvaṃ snāpayataḥ sma
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, the nāga kings, stood in the sky with half their bodies visible, brought forth two streams of water, one cool and one warm, and bathed the Bodhisattva.

children.text: śakrabrahmalokapālāḥ pūrvaṃgamāścānye ca bahavo devaputrāḥ śatasahasrā ye bodhisattvaṃ jātamātraṃ nānāgandhodakamuktakusumaiḥ snāpayantyabhyavakiranti sma
children.translated_text: Led by <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the world-protectors, many other hundreds of thousands of divine sons bathed and sprinkled the newborn Bodhisattva with waters scented by many perfumes and with scattered flowers.

children.text: antarikṣe ca dve cāmare ratnacchatraṃ ca prādurbhūtam
children.translated_text: In the sky two yak-tail fans and a jeweled parasol appeared.

children.text: sa tasmin mahāpadme sthitvā caturdiśamavalokayati sma
children.translated_text: Standing on that great lotus, he looked toward the four directions.

children.text: caturdiśamavalokya siṃhāvalokitaṃ mahāpuruṣāvalokitaṃ vyavalokayati sma ||
children.translated_text: Having looked toward the four directions, he gazed with the gaze of a lion, the gaze of a great man.

children.text: tasmin khalu punaḥ samaye bodhisattvaḥ pūrvakuśalamūlavipākajenāpratihatena divyacakṣuprādurbhūtena divyena cakṣuṣā sarvāvantaṃ trisāhasraṃ mahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ sanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṃ sadevamānuṣaṃ paśyati sma
children.translated_text: At that time, with the unobstructed divine eye that had arisen from the ripening of former roots of merit, the Bodhisattva saw with his divine eye the whole three-thousand great-thousand world-system, with its cities, market-towns, provinces, kingdoms, and capitals, together with gods and humans.

children.text: sarvasattvānāṃ ca cittacaritaṃ ca prajānāti sma
children.translated_text: And he knew the mental dispositions of all beings.

children.text: jñātvā ca vyavalokayati sma asti tvasau kaścitsattvo yo mayā sadṛśaḥ śīlena vā samādhinā vā prajñayā vā kuśalamūlacaryayā vā
children.translated_text: Having known them, he looked about and thought, "Is there any being who is equal to me in morality, or in concentration, or in wisdom, or in the practice of roots of merit?"

children.text: yadā ca bodhisattvaḥ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau na kaṃcitsattvamātmatulyaṃ paśyati sma atha tasminsamaye bodhisattvaḥ siṃha iva vigatabhayabhairavo 'saṃtrastaḥ astambhī sucintitaṃ smṛtvā cintayitvā sarvasattvānāṃ cittacaritāni jñātvā aparigṛhīto bodhisattvaḥ pūrvāṃ diśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrāntaḥ pūrvaṃgamo bhaviṣyāmi sarveṣāṃ kuśalamūlānāṃ dharmāṇām
children.translated_text: And when the Bodhisattva saw no being equal to himself in the three-thousand great-thousand world-system, then at that time the Bodhisattva, like a lion, free from fear and terror, unafraid and unwavering, having remembered what was well considered, having reflected, and having known the mental dispositions of all beings, unsupported, faced the eastern direction and took seven steps, saying, "I shall be foremost among all dharmas that are roots of merit."

children.text: tasya prakramata uparyantarīkṣe 'parigṛhītaṃ divyaśvetavipulachatraṃ cāmaraśubhe gacchantamanugacchanti sma yatra yatra ca bodhisattvaḥ padamutkṣipati sma tatra tatra padmāni prādurbhavanti sma
children.translated_text: As he stepped forward, a broad divine white parasol, unsupported in the upper air, and beautiful yak-tail fans moved along and followed him; and wherever the Bodhisattva lifted his foot, lotuses appeared there.

children.text: dakṣiṇāṃ diśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrāntaḥ dakṣiṇīyo bhaviṣyāmi devamanuṣyāṇām
children.translated_text: Facing the southern direction, he advanced seven steps, saying, "I shall be worthy of offerings from gods and humans."

children.text: paścimāṃ diśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Facing the western direction, he advanced seven steps.

children.text: saptame sthitvā siṃha ivāhlādanātmikāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate sma ahaṃ loke jyeṣṭho 'haṃ loke śreṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: Standing on the seventh step, he spoke a gladdening utterance like a lion: "I am the eldest in the world; I am the best in the world.

children.text: iyaṃ me paścimā jātiḥ
children.translated_text: This is my last birth.

children.text: kariṣyāmi jātijarāmaraṇaduḥkhasyāntam
