children.translated_text: I shall bring an end to the suffering of birth, old age, and death."

children.text: uttarāṃ diśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrāntaḥ anuttaro bhaviṣyāmi sarvasattvānām
children.translated_text: Facing the northern direction, he advanced seven steps, saying, "I shall be unsurpassed among all beings."

children.text: adhastāddiśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrāntaḥ nihaniṣyāmi māraṃ ca mārasenāṃ ca
children.translated_text: Facing the direction below, he advanced seven steps, saying, "I shall strike down <s>Māra</s> and the army of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: sarvanairayikāṇāṃ ca nirayāgnipratighātāya saha dharmameghavṛṣṭiṃ varṣiṣyāmi yena te sukhasamarpitā bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: And for all beings in the hells, to ward off the fire of hell, I shall pour down a rain from a cloud of <s>dharma</s> (teaching), by which they will be endowed with happiness."

children.text: upariṣṭāddiśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrānta ūrdhvaṃ cāvalokayati sma ullokanīyo bhaviṣyāmi sarvasattvānām
children.translated_text: Facing the direction above, he advanced seven steps and looked upward, saying, "I shall be looked up to by all beings."

children.text: samanantarabhāṣitā ceyaṃ bodhisattvena vāk
children.translated_text: Immediately after this utterance had been spoken by the Bodhisattva,

children.text: atha tasmin samaye ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuḥ svareṇābhivijñāpto 'bhūt
children.translated_text: then, at that time, this three-thousand-great-thousand world-system was made aware by the sound.

children.text: iyaṃ bodhisattvasya karmavipākajā abhijñādharmatā ||
children.translated_text: This is the supernormal, dharmic nature born from the karmic result of the Bodhisattva.

children.text: yadā bodhisattvaścaramabhavika upajāyate yadā cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate tadā asyemānyevaṃrūpāṇi ṛddhiprātihāryāṇi bhavanti tasmin khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samaye saṃhṛṣitaromakūpajātāḥ sarvasattvā abhūvan
children.translated_text: When a Bodhisattva in his final existence is born, and when he awakens to unsurpassed complete awakening, such miracles and displays of power occur for him. At that time, monks, all beings had the pores of their skin thrilled with joy.

children.text: mahataśca pṛthivīcālasya loke prādurbhāvo 'bhūt bhairavasya romaharṣaṇasya
children.translated_text: And a great earthquake appeared in the world, terrifying and hair-raising.

children.text: aghaṭṭitāni ca divyamānuṣyakāni tūryāṇi saṃpravāditāni
children.translated_text: Divine and human musical instruments sounded without being struck.

children.text: sarvartukālikāśca vṛkṣāstasmin samaye trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau saṃkusumitāḥ phalitāśca
children.translated_text: And trees bearing in every season blossomed and bore fruit at that time throughout the three-thousand-great-thousand world-system.

children.text: viśuddhācca gaganatalānmeghaśabdaḥ śrūyate sma
children.translated_text: From the pure surface of the sky the sound of clouds was heard.

children.text: apagatameghācca gaganācchanaiḥ sūkṣmasūkṣmo devaḥ pravarṣati sma
children.translated_text: And from a cloudless sky a fine, very fine divine rain fell gently.

children.text: nānāvarṣadivyakusumavastrābharaṇagandhacūrṇavyāmiśrāḥ paramasukhasaṃsparśāśca saumyāḥ sugandhavātāḥ pravāyanti sma
children.translated_text: Gentle fragrant winds blew, pleasant with the touch of supreme happiness and mingled with showers of various heavenly flowers, garments, ornaments, perfumes, and powders.

children.text: vyapagatatamorajodhūmanīhārāśca sarvadiśaḥ suprasannā virājante sma
children.translated_text: All directions, freed from darkness, dust, smoke, and mist, shone bright, clear, and serene.

children.text: upariṣṭāccāntarikṣādadṛśyā gambhīrā mahābrahmaghoṣāḥ saṃśrūyante sma
children.translated_text: From above, in the sky, unseen, deep, great voices of <s>Brahmā</s> were heard.

children.text: sarvacandrasūryaśakrabrahmalokapālaprabhāścābhibhūtā abhūvan
children.translated_text: The radiances of all moons, suns, <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and world-protectors were surpassed.

children.text: paramasukhasaṃsparśayā ca sarvasattvakāyacittasukhasaṃjananyā lokottarayā anekaśatasahasravarṇaprabhayā sarvatrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuḥ parisphuṭo 'bhūt
children.translated_text: The whole three-thousand-great-thousand world-system was pervaded by a supramundane radiance of many hundreds of thousands of colors, whose touch was supreme happiness and which produced happiness in the bodies and minds of all beings.

children.text: samantarajātasya khalu punarbodhisattvasyaikāntasukhasamarpitāḥ sarvasattvā babhūvuḥ
children.translated_text: And just after the Bodhisattva was born, all beings became completely endowed with happiness.

children.text: sarvarāgadveṣamohadarpārativiṣād abhayalobherṣyāmātsaryavigatāḥ sarvākuśalakriyāprativiratā vyādhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ vyādhaya upaśāntāḥ
children.translated_text: They were freed from all passion, hatred, delusion, pride, discontent, despondency, fear, greed, envy, and stinginess; they abstained from all unwholesome actions, and the illnesses of sick beings were calmed.

children.text: kṣutpipāsitānāṃ sattvānāṃ kṣutpipāsā prasrabdhābhūt
children.translated_text: For beings afflicted by hunger and thirst, hunger and thirst subsided.

children.text: madyamadamattānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ madāpagamaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ
children.translated_text: For beings intoxicated and maddened by liquor, the disappearance of intoxication came about.

children.text: unmattaiśca smṛtiḥ pratilabdhā
children.translated_text: Those who were insane recovered their mindfulness.

children.text: cakṣurvikalaiśca sattvaiścakṣuḥ pratilabdhaṃ śrotravikalaiśca sattvaiḥ śrotram
children.translated_text: Beings lacking sight obtained sight, and beings lacking hearing obtained hearing.

children.text: aṅgapratyaṅgavikalendriyāścāvikalendriyāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ
children.translated_text: Those whose limbs, minor limbs, or faculties were impaired became unimpaired in their faculties.

children.text: daridraiśca dhanāni pratilabdhāni
children.translated_text: The poor obtained wealth.

children.text: bandhanabaddhāśca bandhanebhyo vimuktāḥ
children.translated_text: Those bound in fetters were released from their fetters.

children.text: āvīcim ādiṃ kṛtvā sarvanairayikāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvakāraṇād duḥkhaṃ tasminsamaye prasrabdham
children.translated_text: Beginning with <s>Avīci</s>, at that time all suffering from every kind of torment subsided for all beings in the hells.

children.text: tiryagyonikānām anyonyabhakṣaṇādi duḥkham yamalokikānāṃ sattvānāṃ kṣutpipāsādiduḥkhaṃ vyupaśāntamabhūt ||
children.translated_text: For beings born as animals, suffering such as mutual devouring, and for beings in <s>Yama</s>'s realm, suffering such as hunger and thirst, became pacified.

children.text: yadā ca bodhisattvo jātamātraḥ sapta padāni prakrānto 'bhūd asaṃkhyeyākalpakoṭinayutaśatasahasraiḥ sucaritacaraṇair mahāvīryamahāsthāmadharmatāpratilambhena tasmin samaye daśadiglokadhātusthitā buddhā bhagavantastaṃ pṛthvīpradeśaṃ vajramayam adhitiṣṭhanti sma
children.translated_text: And when the Bodhisattva, just born, had advanced seven steps, then, because through incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis and nayutas of kalpas he had practiced good conduct and had attained the nature of great vigor and great strength, the blessed Buddhas dwelling in the world-systems of the ten directions empowered that spot of earth to be diamond-like.

children.text: yena mahāpṛthivī tasmin pradeśe nāvatīryata tāvanmahābalavegasamanvāgato hi bhikṣavo jātamātro bodhisattvaḥ sapta padāni prakrānto 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Therefore the great earth did not sink down in that place; for so endowed with great power and force, monks, was the Bodhisattva just after birth when he advanced seven steps.

children.text: sarvalokāntarikāśca tasmin samaye mahatāvabhāsena sphuṭā abhūvan
children.translated_text: At that time all the spaces between worlds were pervaded by a great light.

children.text: mahāṃśca tasmin samaye gītaśabdo 'bhūnnṛtyaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: And at that time there was a great sound of song and a sound of dancing.

children.text: aprameyāśca tasmin samaye puṣpacūrṇagandhamālyaratnābharaṇavastrameghā abhipravarṣanti sma
children.translated_text: At that time immeasurable clouds of flowers, powders, perfumes, garlands, jewels, ornaments, and garments rained down.

children.text: paramasukhasamarpitāśca sarvasattvā abhūvan
children.translated_text: And all beings were endowed with supreme happiness.

children.text: saṃkṣepādacintyā sā kriyābhūd yadā bodhisattvo loke prādurabhūt sarvalokābhyudgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In brief, inconceivable was that event when the Bodhisattva appeared in the world, risen above all the world.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānandaḥ utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat sarvasattvānāṃ bhagavaṃstathāgata āścaryabhūto 'bhūd bodhisattvabhūta evādbhutadharmasamanvāgataśca
children.translated_text: Then venerable <s>Ānanda</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, set his right knee on the ground, bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, for all beings the Tathāgata was wondrous, and even while he was a bodhisattva he was endowed with marvelous qualities.

children.text: kaḥ punarvāda evaṃ hyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: How much more so, then, now that he has awakened to unsurpassed, complete awakening?

children.text: eṣo 'haṃ bhagavaṃścatuṣpañcakṛtvo 'pi daśakṛtvo 'pi yāvatpañcāśatkṛtvo 'pi śatakṛtvo 'pi yāvadanekaśatasahasraśo 'pyahaṃ bhagavan buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, Blessed One, four or five times, ten times, up to fifty times, a hundred times, and even many hundreds of thousands of times, Blessed One, I go for refuge to the Buddha, the Blessed One."

children.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandametadavocat bhaviṣyanti khalu punarānanda anāgate 'dhvani kecidbhikṣavo 'bhāvitakāyā abhāvitacittā abhāvitaśīlā abhāvitaprajñā bālā apaṇḍitā ābhimānikā uddhatā unnatā asaṃvṛtā vikṣiptacittāḥ kāṅkṣāparīttā vicikitsābahulā aśraddhāḥ śramaṇamalāḥ śramaṇapratirūpakāḥ
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Ānanda, in a future time there will be certain monks whose bodies are undeveloped, whose minds are undeveloped, whose morality is undeveloped, whose wisdom is undeveloped: fools, unwise men, conceited, excited, haughty, unrestrained, distracted in mind, meager in aspiration, full of uncertainty, faithless, stains upon ascetics, mere semblances of ascetics.

children.text: te na śraddhāsyanti imāmevaṃrūpāṃ bodhisattvasya garbhāvakrāntipariśuddhim
children.translated_text: They will not believe in this kind of purity of the bodhisattva's descent into the womb.

children.text: te 'nyonyamekānte saṃnipātyaivaṃ vakṣyanti paśyata bho yūyam etad apūjyamānaṃ bodhisattvasya kila mātuḥ kukṣigatasyoccāraprasrāvamaṇḍoparimiśrasya īdṛśī vibhūtirāsīt
children.translated_text: Having gathered together in private with one another, they will say, 'Look, sirs, at this thing unworthy of reverence: supposedly, while the bodhisattva was in his mother's womb, mixed with a mass of excrement and urine, such magnificence belonged to him!

children.text: sa ca kila abhiniṣkrāman māturdakṣiṇāyāḥ kukṣer anupalipto garbhamalenābhūditi
children.translated_text: And supposedly, when he came forth from his mother's right side, he was unstained by the impurity of the womb.'

children.text: kathametadyojyate na punaste mohapuruṣā evaṃ jñāsyanti na sukṛtakarmaṇāṃ sattvānāmuccāraprasrāvamaṇḍe kāyaḥ sambhavatīti
children.translated_text: How can this be made sense of? But those deluded men will not know this: the body of beings whose actions are meritorious does not arise in a mass of excrement and urine.

children.text: bhadrikā khalvapi tathārūpāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ garbhāvakrāntirbhavati
children.translated_text: Indeed, the descent into the womb of beings of such a kind is excellent.

children.text: garbhāvasthitaśca sattvānukampayā hi bodhisattvo manuṣyaloke upapadyate na devabhūta eva dharmacakraṃ pravartayati
children.translated_text: And while dwelling in the womb, the bodhisattva is born in the human world out of compassion for beings; he does not turn the wheel of Dharma while being a deva.

children.text: tatkasmāt mā khalvānanda sattvāḥ kausīdyamāpatsyante
children.translated_text: Why is that? So that beings, Ānanda, may not fall into laziness.

children.text: devabhūtaḥ sa bhagavān tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vayaṃ tu manuṣyamātrāḥ
children.translated_text: They might say, 'That Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the completely awakened Buddha, was a divine being, but we are merely human.

children.text: na vayaṃ samarthāstatsthānaṃ paripūrayitumiti kausīdyamāpadyeran
children.translated_text: We are not capable of fulfilling that state,' and so they would fall into laziness.

children.text: na khalu punasteṣāṃ mohapuruṣāṇāṃ dharmastainyakānāmevaṃ bhaviṣyati acintyo hi sa sattvo nāsāvasmābhiḥ prāmāṇikaḥ kartavya iti
children.translated_text: Moreover, those deluded men, thieves of the Dharma, will not think, 'That being is inconceivable; he should not be made subject to our measure.'

children.text: api tu khalvānanda buddharddhiprātihāryamapi te tasmin kāle nāvakalpayiṣyanti kimaṅga punarbodhisattvabhūtasya tathāgatasya bodhisattvaprātihāryāṇi
children.translated_text: Rather, Ānanda, at that time they will not accept even the miraculous display of the Buddha's supernormal power, much less the bodhisattva-miracles of the Tathāgata when he was a bodhisattva.

children.text: paśya ānanda kiyantaṃ te mohapuruṣā bahvapuṇyābhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskariṣyanti ye buddhadharmān pratikṣepsyanti lābhasatkāraślokābhibhūtā uccāralagnā lābhasatkārābhibhūtā itarajātīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: See, Ānanda, how great an accumulation of demerit those deluded men will produce: those who, overwhelmed by gain, honor, and fame, stuck to filth, overwhelmed by gain and honor, and of an inferior sort, will reject the Buddha's dharmas.

children.text: ānanda āha mā maivaṃrūpā bhagavan anāgate 'dhvani bhikṣavo bhaviṣyanti ya imāmevaṃ bhadrikāṃ sūtrāntāṃ pratikṣepsyanti pratipakṣaṃ pakṣanti ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> said, "May there not, Blessed One, be such monks in a future time, who will reject this excellent discourse and take the opposing side."

children.text: bhagavānāha evaṃrūpāśca te ānanda sūtrāntāṃ pratikṣepsyanti prativakṣyanti cānekaprakārān cānyān pāpakānabhisaṃskārānabhisaṃskariṣyanti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Such men, Ānanda, will reject this discourse, will speak against it, and will produce many other kinds of evil actions.

children.text: anarthikāśca te śrāmaṇyena bhaviṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: And they will have no concern for the ascetic life."

children.text: ānanda āha kā punarbhagavan teṣāṃ tathārūpāṇāmasatpuruṣāṇāṃ gatirbhaviṣyati ko 'bhisaṃparāyaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> said, "Blessed One, what will be the destiny of such bad men? What will be their future lot?"

children.text: bhagavānāha yā gatir buddhabodhim antardhāyāpyatītānāgatapratyutpannāṃśca buddhān bhagavato 'tyākhyāya tāṃ te gatiṃ gamiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "They will go to the destiny of those who, having caused the Buddha's awakening to disappear and having denied the blessed Buddhas of the past, future, and present, go to that destiny."

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānandaḥ saṃharṣitaromakūpajāto namo buddhāya ityuktvā bhagavantametadavocan mūrcchā me bhagavan kāyasyābhūdimaṃ teṣāmasatpuruṣāṇāṃ samudācāraṃ śrutvā ||
children.translated_text: Then venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, the pores of his hair bristling, said, "Homage to the Buddha," and said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, my body fainted when I heard of the conduct of those bad men."

children.text: bhagavānāha na teṣāmānanda samācāro bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Ānanda, they will not have proper conduct.

children.text: viṣamasamudācārāḥ khalu punaste sattvā bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: Rather, those beings will be of perverse conduct.

children.text: te tena viṣamena samudācāreṇāvīcau mahānarake prapatiṣyanti
children.translated_text: By that perverse conduct they will fall into the great Avīci hell.

children.text: tatkasya hetor ye kecidānanda bhikṣavo vā bhikṣuṇyo vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā imānevaṃrūpān sūtrāntān śrutvā nādhimokṣyanti na śraddhāsyanti na prativetsyanti te cyutāḥ samānā avīcau mahānarake prapatiṣyanti
children.translated_text: Why is that? Ānanda, whatever monks or nuns, laymen or laywomen, having heard discourses of this kind, do not accept them, do not believe them, and do not understand them, when they die they will fall into the great Avīci hell.

children.text: mā ānanda tathāgatāprāmāṇikaṃ akārṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Ānanda, do not make the Tathāgata something to be measured.

children.text: tatkasmāddhetor aprameyo hyānanda tathāgato gambhīro vipulo duravagāhaḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For, Ānanda, the Tathāgata is immeasurable, profound, vast, and difficult to fathom.

children.text: yeṣāṃ keṣāṃcidānanda imānevaṃrūpān sūtrāntāñchrutvopapatsyate prītiprāmodyaṃ prasādalābhāstaiḥ sattvaiḥ sulabdhāḥ
children.translated_text: Ānanda, whatever beings, having heard discourses of this kind, obtain joy and gladness and the gain of serene faith, those beings have obtained them well."

children.text: amoghaṃ ca teṣāṃ jīvitam amoghaṃ ca teṣāṃ mānuṣyaṃ sucaritacaraṇāśca te ādattaṃ ca taiḥ sāraṃ muktāśca te tribhyo 'pāyebhyaḥ bhaviṣyanti ca te putrāstathāgatasya pariprāptaṃ ca taiḥ sarvakāryam amoghaśca teṣāṃ śraddhāpratilambhaḥ suvibhaktaṃ ca tai rāṣṭrapiṇḍaṃ prasannāśca te 'grasattvaiḥ saṃchinnāstairmārapāśāḥ nistīrṇaśca taiḥ saṃsārāṭavīkāntāraḥ samuddhṛtaśca taiḥ śokaśalyo 'nuprāptaṃ ca taiḥ prāmodyavastu sugṛhītāni ca taiḥ śaraṇagamanāni dakṣiṇīyāśca te pūjārhāḥ durlabhaprādurbhāvāśca te loke dakṣiṇīyāśca te dhārayitavyāḥ
children.translated_text: Their life is not fruitless, and their human birth is not fruitless; they have practiced good conduct, taken up the essence, and been freed from the three bad destinies. They will be sons of the tathāgata; every task has been accomplished by them; their obtaining of faith is not fruitless; the alms of the realm has been well apportioned by them; they are pleasing to the foremost beings; Māra's snares have been cut by them; the wilderness and difficult passage of saṃsāra has been crossed by them; the dart of sorrow has been pulled out by them; they have reached the ground of gladness; their goings for refuge have been well taken; they are worthy of gifts and deserving of worship; their appearance in the world is hard to find, and they should be borne in mind as worthy recipients of gifts.

children.text: tatkasya hetos tathā hi te sarvaloke imamevaṃ sarvalokavipratyanīkaṃ tathāgatadharmaṃ śraddadhanti
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because in the whole world they put faith in this tathāgata-dharma, which is opposed to the whole world.

children.text: na te ānanda sattvā avarakeṇa kuśalamūlena samanvāgatā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Those beings, <s>Ānanda</s>, are not endowed with a meager root of merit.

children.text: te cānanda sattvā mamaikajātipratibaddhāni mitrāṇi bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: And those beings, <s>Ānanda</s>, will be friends of mine, bound to me in this one birth.

children.text: tatkasmāddhetoḥ kaścidānanda śravaṇādeva priyo bhavati manāpaśca na tu darśanena
children.translated_text: Why is that? Someone, <s>Ānanda</s>, becomes dear and agreeable merely through hearing, but not through seeing.

children.text: kaścidānanda darśanenāpi priyo bhavati manāpaśca na tu khalu punaḥ śravaṇena
children.translated_text: Someone, <s>Ānanda</s>, becomes dear and agreeable also through seeing, but not, again, through hearing.

children.text: kaścidānanda darśanenāpi śravaṇenāpi priyo bhavati manāpaśca
children.translated_text: Someone, <s>Ānanda</s>, becomes dear and agreeable both through seeing and through hearing.

children.text: teṣāṃ keṣāṃcidānanda ahaṃ darśanena vā śravaṇena vā priyo manāpo bhaveyaṃ niṣṭhāṃ tvaṃ tatra gacchethāḥ na tāni mamaikajātipratibaddhāni mitrāṇi
children.translated_text: For whichever of them, <s>Ānanda</s>, I should become dear and agreeable through seeing or through hearing, you should come to this settled conclusion: they are my friends bound to me in this one birth.

children.text: dṛṣṭāste tathāgatena mocayitavyāste tathāgatena te samaguṇapratyaṃśās te tathāgataguṇapratyaṃśās te tathāgatena kartavyā upāsakāḥ te tathāgataṃ śaraṇaṃ gatā upāttāste tathāgatena
children.translated_text: They have been seen by the tathāgata; they are to be liberated by the tathāgata; they have a share in equal qualities, a share in the qualities of the tathāgata. They are to be made lay followers by the tathāgata; they have gone to the tathāgata for refuge and have been taken up by the tathāgata.

children.text: mamāntikāt khalvapyānanda pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāmeva tāvaccarato ye kecidbhayārditāḥ sattvā āgatya abhayaṃ pratiyācante sma tebhyo 'haṃ sattvebhyo 'bhayaṃ dattavān kimaṅga punaretarhyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: Even formerly, <s>Ānanda</s>, when I was still practicing the bodhisattva's course, whatever beings came to my presence, afflicted by fear and begging for fearlessness, I gave fearlessness to those beings. How much more so now, when I have awakened to unsurpassed complete and perfect awakening?

children.text: śraddhāyāmānanda yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ
children.translated_text: Effort, <s>Ānanda</s>, should be made in faith.

children.text: idaṃ tathāgato vijñāpayati
children.translated_text: This is what the tathāgata makes known.

children.text: yadānanda tathāgatena yuṣmākaṃ karaṇīyaṃ kṛtaṃ tattathāgatena śodhito mānaśalyaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever, <s>Ānanda</s>, had to be done for you by the tathāgata has been done; the dart of pride has been purified away by the tathāgata.

children.text: śravaṇenāpyānanda mitrasya nanu yojanaśatāntaramapi gacchanti gatvā ca sukhitā bhavanti adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ mitraṃ dṛṣṭvā
children.translated_text: Even on hearing of a friend, <s>Ānanda</s>, do people not travel a distance of a hundred yojanas and, having gone, become happy on seeing a friend whom they had never seen before?

children.text: kaḥ punarvādo ye māṃ niśritya kuśalamūlānyavaropayanti
children.translated_text: What need is there to speak of those who, relying on me, plant roots of merit?

children.text: jñāsyantyānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ pūrvaṃ mitrāṇyete sattvāstathāgatānām asmākamapyete mitrāṇi bhavantīti
children.translated_text: The tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened ones, will know, <s>Ānanda</s>: 'These beings were formerly friends of the tathāgatas; they are friends of ours as well.'

children.text: tatkasmāt khalu punarānanda mitraṃ mitrasya priyaṃ ca manāpaṃ ca bhavati tasyāpi tadapi priyameva bhavati mitrasya yatpriyaṃ mitram tadapi priyameva bhavati manāpaṃ ca
children.translated_text: For what reason, then, <s>Ānanda</s>, is a friend dear and agreeable to a friend? Whatever is dear to that friend is dear to him as well; the dear friend is himself dear and agreeable too.

children.text: tasmāttarhyānanda ārocayāmi ca prativedayāmi ca
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, I announce and declare this to you.

children.text: śraddhāmātrakamutpādayatha
children.translated_text: Produce even a mere measure of faith.

children.text: anuparindiṣyāmo vayamanāgatānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmantike te 'smākamapi mitrāṇīti viditvā yathābhiprāyaṃ paripūrayiṣyanti
children.translated_text: We shall entrust you to the future tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened ones; and knowing, 'They are friends of ours as well,' they will fulfill your intention accordingly.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma ānanda kasyacideva puruṣasyaikaputrako bhavet suvayāḥ pradakṣiṇagrāhī
children.translated_text: It is like this, <s>Ānanda</s>: suppose a certain man had an only son, well grown and receptive to guidance.

children.text: sa ca puruṣo bahumitro bhavet
children.translated_text: And that man had many friends.

children.text: sa tasmin pitari kālagate na hi vihanyeta pitṛmitrasuparigṛhītaḥ
children.translated_text: When that father had died, the son would not be ruined, because he was well looked after by his father's friends.

children.text: evameva ānanda ye kecinmama śraddhāsyanti tānahamupādadāmi
children.translated_text: In just the same way, <s>Ānanda</s>, whoever will have faith in me, I take them up.

children.text: mitrāṇīva mama tāni
children.translated_text: They are like friends of mine.

children.text: te mama śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: They have gone to me for refuge.

children.text: bahumitraśca tathāgataḥ
children.translated_text: And the tathāgata has many friends.

children.text: tāni ca tathāgatasya mitrāṇi bhūtavādīni na mṛṣāvādīni
children.translated_text: Those friends of the tathāgata are speakers of truth, not speakers of falsehood.

children.text: anuparindāmyahaṃ bhūtavādinām
children.translated_text: I entrust them to the speakers of truth.

children.text: yāni tathāgatasya mitrāṇyanāgatāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: The friends of the tathāgata are the future tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened ones.

children.text: śraddhāyāmānanda yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ
children.translated_text: Effort, <s>Ānanda</s>, should be made in faith.

children.text: atrāhaṃ yuṣmān vijñāpayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Here I make this known to you.

children.text: iti hi jāte bodhisattve gaganatalagatānyapsaraḥkoṭinayutaśatasahasrāṇi divyaiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanavastrābharaṇair māyādevīmabhyavakiranti sma
children.translated_text: Thus, when the Bodhisattva was born, hundreds of thousands of tens of millions of apsarases moving in the vault of the sky showered <s>Māyādevī</s> with divine flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, garments, and ornaments.

children.text: tatredamucyate ||
children.translated_text: There this is said:

children.text: śubhavimalaviśuddhahemaprabhā candrasūryaprabhā ṣaṣṭi daśasahasra devāpsarā mañjughoṣasvarāḥ
children.translated_text: Apsarases of the gods, sixty times ten thousand, with voices of lovely sound, shining with the radiance of auspicious, stainless, purified gold, with the radiance of moon and sun,

children.text: tasmi kṣaṇi upetya tāṃ lumbinīṃ māyadevyabruvan mā khu jani viṣādu tuṣṭā bhavopasthāyikāṣte vayam ||
children.translated_text: at that moment came to <s>Lumbinī</s> and said to <s>Māyādevī</s>: 'Do not give rise to distress; be joyful. We are your attendants.

children.text: bhaṇahi kiṃ karaṇīyu kiṃ kurmahe kena kāryaṃ ca te vayaṃ tava susamarthopasthāyikā premabhāvasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Tell us what is to be done. What shall we do, and what task is there for us? We are fully capable attendants for you, standing in an attitude of love.

children.text: api ca bhava udagra harṣānvitā mā ca khedaṃ janehi jarāmaraṇavighāti vaidyottamaṃ adya devī janeṣī laghum ||
children.translated_text: And be exalted, filled with joy; do not give rise to weariness. Today, O queen, you will quickly give birth to the supreme physician who destroys old age and death.'

children.text: yatha druma pariphulla saṃpuṣpitā śālavṛkṣā ime yatha ca marusahasra pārśve sthitā bhrāmayanto bhujān
children.translated_text: Just as these trees, the <s>śāla</s> trees, are fully opened and covered with flowers, and just as thousands of <s>Maruts</s> stand beside him, waving their arms,

children.text: yatha ca cali sasāgarā medinī ṣaḍvikārā iyaṃ divi divi ca vighuṣṭa lokottaraṃ tvaṃ janeṣī sutam ||
children.translated_text: and just as this ocean-girt earth shook in six ways, and in the heavens it was proclaimed again and again, 'You have borne a son who is beyond the world,'

children.text: yatha ca prabha viśuddha vibhrājate svarṇavarṇa śubhā tūryaśata manojñā cāghaṭṭitā ghuṣyayante 'mbare
children.translated_text: and just as a pure radiance shines forth, golden-colored and auspicious, while hundreds of lovely instruments sound in the sky without being struck,

children.text: yatha ca śatasahasra śuddhā śubhā vītarāgāḥ surā namiṣu muditacittā adyo jane sarvaloke hitam ||
children.translated_text: and just as hundreds of thousands of pure, auspicious, passionless gods bow with joyful minds, saying, 'Today you have borne one who benefits the whole world,'

children.text: śakramapi ca brahmapālāpi cānyā ca yā devatā tuṣṭamuditacittā pārśve sthitā nāmayanto bhujām
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> too, and <s>Brahmā</s> with the protectors, and whatever other deities there are, stood at his side with pleased and joyful minds, bending their arms in homage.

children.text: so ca puruṣasiṃha śuddhavrato bhittva kukṣinirdhāvito kanakagirinikāśa śuddhavrato niṣkramī nāyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That lion among men, pure in vow, broke forth from the womb; the leader, pure in vow and like a golden mountain, came out.

children.text: śakramapi ca brahma tau pāṇibhiḥ saṃpratīcchā muniṃ kṣetra śatasahasra saṃkampitā ābha muktā śubhā
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> received the sage in their hands; hundreds of thousands of fields shook, and a pure radiance was released.

children.text: api ca triṣu apāyi sattvā sukhī nāsti duḥkhaṃ puna amaraśatasahasra puṣpāṃ kṣipī bhrāmayantyambarān ||
children.translated_text: And beings in the three bad destinies became happy; suffering was no more. Hundreds of thousands of immortals threw flowers and whirled them through the sky.

children.text: vīryabalaupeta vajrātmikā medinī saṃsthitā 'bhuttadā padmu ruciracitru abhyudgato yatra cakrāṅgacitrebhiḥ padbhyāṃ sthito 'pi nāyakaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the earth, endowed with the strength of vigor and diamond-like in nature, stood firm; a lovely, variegated lotus rose up where the leader stood with feet marked by wheel-signs.

children.text: sapta pada kramitva brahmasvaro muñci ghoṣottamaṃ jaramaraṇavighāti vaidyottamo bheṣyi sattvottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having taken seven steps, he uttered an excellent cry in a <s>Brahmā</s>-like voice: 'I shall be the supreme healer, destroyer of old age and death, the best of beings.'

children.text: gaganatala sthihitva brahmottamo śakradevottamaḥ śuciruciraprasannagandhodakairvisnapī nāyakam
children.translated_text: Standing in the expanse of the sky, the best <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, best of gods, bathed the leader with clean, lovely, clear, scented waters.

children.text: api ca uragarājā śītoṣṇa dve vāridhāre śubhe vyamuñcatāntarīkṣe sthitāḥ amara śatasahasra gandhodakairvisnapī nāyakam ||
children.translated_text: And the nāga kings, standing in the air, released two auspicious streams of water, cool and warm; hundreds of thousands of immortals bathed the leader with scented waters.

children.text: lokapālāśca saṃbhrānta saṃdhārayantī karaiḥ śobhanaiḥ
children.translated_text: The world-protectors, hastening in awe, held him with their beautiful hands.

children.text: trisahasrā iyaṃ bhūmiḥ kampate sacarācarā ||
children.translated_text: This three-thousandfold earth, with its moving and unmoving beings, trembled.

children.text: prabhā ca rucirā muktā apāyāśca viśodhitāḥ
children.translated_text: A lovely radiance was released, and the bad destinies were purified.

children.text: kleśaduḥkhāśca te śāntā jāte lokavināyake ||
children.translated_text: Their afflictions and sufferings became pacified when the guide of the world was born.

children.text: kṣipanti marutaḥ puṣpaṃ jāte 'sminnaranāyake
children.translated_text: The <s>Maruts</s> scattered flowers at the birth of this leader of men.

children.text: krama sapta padāṃ vīraḥ kramate balavīryavān ||
children.translated_text: The hero, possessed of strength and vigor, strode seven steps.

children.text: pādau nikṣipate yatra bhūmau padmavarāḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: Wherever he placed his feet upon the earth, excellent and auspicious lotuses

children.text: abhyudgacchaṃstato mahyāṃ sarvaratnavibhūṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: sprang up there from the ground, adorned with every jewel.

children.text: yadā sapta padāṃ gatvā brahmasvaramudāhari
children.translated_text: When, after going seven steps, he uttered a <s>Brahmā</s>-like voice,

children.text: jarāmaraṇavighāti bhiṣagvara ivodgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he arose like the foremost physician, the destroyer of old age and death.

children.text: vyavalokayitvā ca viśārado diśaḥ tato girāṃ muñcati arthayuktām
children.translated_text: And after looking over the directions with confidence, he then uttered a speech full of meaning:

children.text: jyeṣṭho 'haṃ sarvalokasya śraṣṭho loke vināyakaḥ iyaṃ ca jātirmama paścimā iti ||
children.translated_text: 'I am the eldest of all the world; I am the best in the world, the guide. This birth of mine is the last.'

children.text: hāsyaṃ ca muktaṃ naranāyakena salokapālairmarubhiśca sendraiḥ
children.translated_text: A smile was released by the leader of men, together with the world-protectors, the <s>Maruts</s>, and <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: prasannacittairvaragandhavāribhiḥ saṃskārito lokahitārthakārī ||
children.translated_text: With serene minds they consecrated the doer of the world's welfare with excellent scented waters.

children.text: api coragendraiḥ sahitaiḥ samagraiḥ gandhogradhārāvisaraiḥ snapiṃsu
children.translated_text: And the great nāgas also, united and assembled, bathed him with streams and outpourings of fragrance.

children.text: anye 'pi devā nayutā sthitāḥ 'ntarīkṣe snapiṃsu gandhāgrajine svayaṃbhum ||
children.translated_text: Other gods too, countless in number and standing in the sky, bathed the self-born foremost <s>Jina</s> with fine perfumes.

children.text: śvetaṃ ca vipulaṃ chatraṃ cāmarāṃśca śubhāmbarān
children.translated_text: A broad white parasol, yak-tail fans, and beautiful garments

children.text: antarīkṣe gatā devāḥ snāpayanti nararṣabham ||
children.translated_text: were offered from the sky by the gods as they bathed the bull among men.

children.text: pañcakulikaśatāni prasūyante sma
children.translated_text: Five hundred children of noble families were born.

children.text: puruṣa tvaritu gatva śuddhodanamabravīt harṣito vṛddhi vipula jātu devā suto bhūṣito lakṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: A man went quickly and said to <s>Śuddhodana</s>, delighted: 'Great prosperity, O lord! A son has been born, adorned with marks.

children.text: mahakularatanasya vṛddhibhūtā vyakto asau cakravartīśvaraḥ na ca bhavi pratiśatru jambudhvaje ekachatro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: He is the increase of the jewel of a great family. Clearly he will be a lord, a wheel-turning king; he will have no rival in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and will rule under one parasol.'

children.text: dvitiyu puruṣu gatva rājñi śuddhodane śleṣayitvā krame vṛddhi vipula deva jātā nṛpe śākiyānāṃ kule
children.translated_text: A second man went to King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and, approaching in due order, said: 'Great prosperity, O lord! A child has been born, O king, in the family of the <s>Śākyas</s>.

children.text: pañcaviṃśatisahasra jātāḥ sutāḥ śākiyānāṃ gṛhe sarvi balaupeta nagnāḥ samā duṣpradharṣā paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Twenty-five thousand sons have been born in the houses of the <s>Śākyas</s>, all endowed with strength, equal in form, and hard for others to overpower.

children.text: aparu puruṣa āha devā śruṇā nandaśabdaṃ mamā chandakapramukhāni ceṭīsutā jāta aṣṭau śatā
children.translated_text: Another man said: 'Listen, O lord, to my glad announcement: eight hundred sons of maidservants, headed by <s>Chandaka</s>, have been born.

children.text: api ca daśasahasra jātā hayāḥ kaṇṭhakasya sakhā turagavarapradhāna hemaprabhā mañjukeśā varāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And ten thousand horses have been born, companions of <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, chiefs among excellent steeds, golden in radiance, with lovely manes.

children.text: viṃśati ca sahasra paryantakāḥ koṭṭarājāstathā nṛpati kramatalebhi cānvākramī sādhu devā jayā
children.translated_text: And twenty thousand attendants, and likewise the Koṭṭa chiefs, came in order to the king's feet, saying, 'Good, O lord, victory!'

children.text: ājñā khalu dadāhi gacchāma kiṃ vā karomo nṛpā tvamiha vaśitu prāptu bhṛtyā vayaṃ bhaṭṭa devā jayā ||
children.translated_text: 'Give your command: shall we go, or what shall we do, O king? We servants have come here under your power, master. O lord, victory!'

children.text: viṃśati ca sahasra nāgottamā hemajālojjvalā tvaritamupagamiṃsu rājño gṛhaṃ garjamānā nabhe
children.translated_text: And twenty thousand finest elephants, shining with golden nets, quickly approached the king's house, roaring in the sky.

children.text: kṛṣṇaśabala vatsa gopāmukhā jāta ṣaṣṭiśatā iyamapi suti devadevottame vṛddhi rājño gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: Six hundred maidens headed by <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Śabalā</s>, <s>Vatsā</s>, and <s>Gopā</s> have been born; this too, O best of gods, is prosperity in the king's house.

children.text: api ca nṛpati gaccha prekṣa svayaṃ sarvameva prabho puṇyateja prabho naramarutasahasra ye harṣitā dṛṣṭva jāte guṇāṃ
children.translated_text: And go yourself, O king, and see everything, O lord; O lord of meritorious splendor, thousands of men and <s>Maruts</s> are delighted, having seen the virtues at his birth.

children.text: bodhivara aśoka saṃprasthitāḥ kṣipra bhomā jināḥ ||
children.translated_text: The excellent <s>Bodhi</s> tree and the <s>Aśoka</s> have appeared; quickly, O lord, behold the <s>Jina</s>.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo jāte bodhisattve tatkṣaṇaṃ dānanisargaḥ punaruttari pravartate sma
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, when the Bodhisattva was born, at that very moment the outpouring of gifts proceeded still further.

children.text: pañca ca kulikāśatāni prasūyante sma daśa ca kanyāsahasrāṇi yaśovatīpramukhāni
children.translated_text: And five hundred kulikās were born, and ten thousand maidens headed by <s>Yaśovatī</s>.

children.text: aṣṭau dāsīśatāni aṣṭau dāsaśatāni chandakapramukhāni
children.translated_text: There were eight hundred female servants and eight hundred male servants headed by <s>Chandaka</s>.

children.text: daśa vaḍavāsahasrāṇi daśa kiśorasahasrāṇi kaṇṭhakapramukhāni
children.translated_text: There were ten thousand mares and ten thousand colts headed by <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>.

children.text: pañca kareṇusahasrāṇi pañca piṅgasahasrāṇi prasūyante sma
children.translated_text: Five thousand female elephants and five thousand tawny elephants were born.

children.text: tāni sarvāṇi rājñā śuddhodanena pustavaropitāni kumārasya krīḍārthaṃ dattānyabhūvan ||
children.translated_text: All these were entered in the records by King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and given to the prince for his play.

children.text: caturṇāṃ ca dvīpakoṭīśatasahasrāṇāṃ madhye pṛthivīpradeśe aśvatthayaṣṭiḥ prādurabhūdantardvīpe ca candanavanaṃ prādurbabhūva bodhisattvasya paribhogārthaṃ bodhisattvasyaivānubhāvena
children.translated_text: In a region of earth amid hundreds of thousands of crores of four-continent worlds, an aśvattha staff appeared; and in the intermediate island a sandalwood forest appeared for the Bodhisattva's use, by the Bodhisattva's own power.

children.text: pañca codyānaśatāni samantānnagarasya prādurbabhūvurbodhisattvasya paribhogāya
children.translated_text: Five hundred parks appeared all around the city for the Bodhisattva's enjoyment.

children.text: pañca ca nidhānasahasrāṇi dharaṇītalādutplutya mukhaṃ darśayanti sma
children.translated_text: And five thousand treasures, springing up from beneath the earth, showed their openings.

children.text: iti hi ye kecidrājñaḥ śuddhodanasyārthābhipretā abhūvan te sarve samṛddhābhipretā abhūvan saṃsiddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, whatever aims were desired by King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, all those desired aims were fulfilled, prosperously accomplished.

children.text: tato rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyaitadabhūt kimahaṃ kumārasya nāmadheyaṃ kariṣyāmīti
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'What name shall I give the prince?'

children.text: tato 'syaitadabhūd asya hi jātamātreṇa mama sarvārthāḥ saṃsiddhāḥ
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to him: 'For as soon as he was born, all my aims were accomplished.

children.text: yannvahamasya sarvārthasiddha iti nāma kuryām
children.translated_text: Therefore I should give him the name <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>.'

children.text: tato rājā bodhisattvaṃ mahatā satkāreṇa satkṛtya sarvārthasiddho 'yaṃ kumāro nāmnā bhavatu iti nāmāsyākārṣīt ||
children.translated_text: Then the king, honoring the Bodhisattva with great honor, gave him the name, saying, 'Let this prince be named <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>.'

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo jāte bodhisattve mātuḥ kukṣipārśvamakṣatamanupahatamabhavadyathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścāt
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, when the Bodhisattva was born, the side of his mother's womb was uncut and unharmed, the same afterward as it had been before.

children.text: tritaviṣyandāmbukūpāḥ prādurabhūvan api ca sugandhatailapuṣkariṇyaḥ
children.translated_text: Three wells of flowing water appeared, and also lotus ponds of fragrant oil.

children.text: pañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyagandhaparivāsitatailaparigṛhītāni bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma
children.translated_text: Five thousand apsarases, carrying divine oil perfumed with fragrance, approached the Bodhisattva's mother and, upon the good birth, asked her whether her body was unwearied.

children.text: pañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyānulepanaparigṛhītāni bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma
children.translated_text: Five thousand apsarases, carrying divine ointments, approached the Bodhisattva's mother and, upon the good birth, asked her whether her body was unwearied.

children.text: pañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyagandhodakaparipūrṇaghaṭāparigṛhītāni bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma
children.translated_text: Five thousand apsarases, carrying jars filled with divine scented water, approached the Bodhisattva's mother and, upon the good birth, asked her whether her body was unwearied.

children.text: pañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyānulepanaparigṛhītāni bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma
children.translated_text: Five thousand apsarases, carrying divine ointments, approached the Bodhisattva's mother and, upon the good birth, asked her whether her body was unwearied.

children.text: pañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyadārakācīvaraparigṛhītāni bodhisatvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma
children.translated_text: Five thousand apsarases, carrying divine garments for a child, approached the Bodhisattva's mother and, upon the good birth, asked her whether her body was unwearied.

children.text: pañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyadārakābharaṇaparigṛhītāni bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma
children.translated_text: Five thousand apsarases, carrying divine ornaments for a child, approached the Bodhisattva's mother and, upon the good birth, asked her whether her body was unwearied.

children.text: pañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyatūryasaṃgītisaṃprabhaṇitena bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma
children.translated_text: Five thousand apsarases, with divine instrumental music resounding, approached the Bodhisattva's mother and, upon the good birth, asked her whether her body was unwearied.

children.text: yāvantaśceha jambudvīpe bāhyāḥ pañcābhijñā ṛṣayaste sarve gaganatalenāgatya rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya purataḥ sthitvā jayavṛddhiśabdamanuśrāvayanti sma ||
children.translated_text: And all the outside seers with the five superknowledges who were here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> came through the sky, stood before King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, and made heard the cry of victory and increase.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo jātamātro bodhisattvaḥ saptarātraḥ lumbinīvane divyamānuṣyakaistūryatālāvacaraiḥ satkriyate sma gurukriyate sma mānyate sma pūjyate sma khādyabhojyasvādanīyāni viśrāṇyante sma
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, for seven nights after his birth the newborn Bodhisattva was honored, revered, respected, and worshiped in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove with divine and human instruments, cymbals, and performances, and foods, meals, and delicacies were distributed.

children.text: sarvaśākyagaṇāśca saṃnipātyānandaśabdamudīrayanti sma dānāni ca dadanti sma puṇyāni ca kurvanti sma
children.translated_text: All the <s>Śākya</s> community assembled and uttered cries of joy, gave gifts, and performed meritorious deeds.

children.text: dvātriṃśacca brāhmaṇaśatasahasrāṇi dine dine saṃtarpyante sma
children.translated_text: And thirty-two hundred thousand Brahmins were satisfied day after day.

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca yenārthena tebhyastaddīyate sma
children.translated_text: Whatever each of them needed was given to them.

children.text: śakraśca devānāmindro brahmā ca tasyāṃ brāhmaṇaparṣadi māṇavakarūpamabhinirmāyāgrāsane niṣadyemāṃ maṅgalyāṃ gāthāmabhyabhāṣatām ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and <s>Brahmā</s>, having manifested the form of young Brahmins in that assembly of Brahmins, sat down on the foremost seat and spoke these auspicious verses:

children.text: apāyāśca yathā śāntā sukhī sarvaṃ yathā jagat
children.translated_text: Just as the lower realms are at peace, and just as the whole world is happy,

children.text: dhruvaṃ sukhāvaho jātaḥ sukhe sthāpayitā jagat ||
children.translated_text: surely one who brings happiness has been born, one who will establish the world in happiness.

children.text: yathā vitimirā cābhā ravicandrasuraprabhāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as light free from darkness, and the splendors of the sun, moon, and gods,

children.text: abhibhūtā na bhāsante dhruvaṃ puṇyaprabhodbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are overcome and do not shine, surely he has arisen from the radiance of merit.

children.text: paśyantyanayanā yadvacchrotrahīnāḥ śruṇanti ca
children.translated_text: As the eyeless see and those without hearing also hear,

children.text: unmattakāḥ smṛtīmanto bhavitā lokacetiyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the mad become mindful, he will be an object of veneration for the world.

children.text: na bādhante yathā kleśā jātaṃ maitrajanaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Just as the afflictions do not torment and the world is born as a kindly people,

children.text: niḥsaṃśayaṃ brahmakoṭīnāṃ bhavitā pūjanārahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: without doubt he will be worthy of worship by crores of <s>Brahmās</s>.

children.text: yathā saṃpuṣpitāḥ śālā medinī ca samā sthitā
children.translated_text: Just as the śāla trees are in full bloom and the earth stands level,

children.text: dhruvaṃ sarvajagatpūjyaḥ sarvajño 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: surely this one will become omniscient, worshiped by the whole world.

children.text: yathā nirākulo loko mahāpadmo yathodbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as the world is undisturbed, and just as a great lotus has arisen,

children.text: niḥsaṃśayaṃ mahātejā lokanātho bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: without doubt the greatly radiant one will become lord of the world.

children.text: yathā ca mṛdukā vātā divyagandhopavāsitāḥ
children.translated_text: And just as gentle winds, perfumed with heavenly fragrance,

children.text: śamenti vyādhiṃ sattvānāṃ vaidyarājo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: pacify the sickness of beings, he will become the king of physicians.

children.text: vītarāgā yathā ceme rūpadhātau marucchatāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as these passionless hosts of gods in the realm of form,

children.text: kṛtāñjaliṃ namasyante dakṣiṇīyo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: bowing with joined hands, pay homage, he will be one worthy of offerings.

children.text: yathā ca manujā devān devāḥ paśyanti mānuṣān
children.translated_text: And just as humans see gods and gods see humans,

children.text: heṭhayanti na cānyonyaṃ sārthavāho bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and they do not injure one another, he will be a caravan leader.

children.text: yathā ca jvalanaḥ śāntaḥ sarvā nadyaśca visthitāḥ
children.translated_text: And just as fire is quieted and all the rivers stand still,

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ ca kampate bhūmiḥ bhavitā tattvadarśakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the earth trembles slightly, he will be a seer of reality.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ saptarātrajātasya bodhisattvasya mātā māyādevī kālamakarot
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, when the Bodhisattva was seven nights old, his mother <s>Māyādevī</s> died.

children.text: sā kālagatā trāyatriṃśati deveṣūpapadyata
children.translated_text: When she had died, she was reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.

children.text: syāt khalu punarbhikṣavo yuṣmākamevaṃ bodhisattvāparādhena māyādevī kālagateti na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam
children.translated_text: Now, monks, it might occur to you: "Did <s>Māyādevī</s> die because of some offense against the Bodhisattva?" It should certainly not be seen in that way.

children.text: tatkasmāddhetor etat paramaṃ hi tasyā āyuṣpramāṇamabhūt
children.translated_text: Why? For that was the full measure of her life.

children.text: atītānāmapi bhikṣavo bodhisattvānāṃ saptarātrajātānāṃ janetryaḥ kālamakurvanta
children.translated_text: Monks, the mothers of Bodhisattvas of the past too died when their sons were seven nights old.

children.text: tatkasmāddhetoḥ vivṛddhasya hi bodhisattvasya paripūrṇendriyasyābhiniṣkrāmato māturhṛdayaṃ sphuṭet ||
children.translated_text: Why? For if the Bodhisattva, grown up and fully developed in his faculties, were to go forth, his mother's heart would burst.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ saptame divase yādṛśenaiva vyūhena māyādevī kapilavastuno mahānagarādudyānabhūmimabhiniṣkrāntābhūt tataḥ koṭīśatasahasraguṇottareṇa mahāvyūhena bodhisattvaḥ kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ prāvikṣat
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, on the seventh day, with a great display hundreds of thousands of crores of times superior to the very display with which <s>Māyādevī</s> had gone out from the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> to the parkland, the Bodhisattva entered the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>.

children.text: tasya ca praviśataḥ pañca pūrṇakumbhasahasrāṇi gandhodakaparipūrṇāni purato nīyante sma
children.translated_text: As he entered, five thousand full jars filled with scented water were carried before him.

children.text: evaṃ pañcakanyāsahasrāṇi mayūrahastakaparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: Likewise, five thousand maidens holding peacock-feather fans went before him.

children.text: pañca ca kanyāsahasrāṇi tālavṛkṣakaparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: And five thousand maidens holding palm-tree emblems went before him.

children.text: pañca sa kanyāsahasrāṇi gandhodakabhṛṅgāraparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma mārgamavasiñcanti sma
children.translated_text: And five thousand maidens holding pitchers of scented water went before him, sprinkling the road.

children.text: pañca ca kanyāsahasrāṇi vicitrapaṭalakaparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: And five thousand maidens holding variegated cloths went before him.

children.text: pañca ca kanyāsahasrāṇi navavicitrapralambanamālāparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: And five thousand maidens holding fresh, variegated hanging garlands went before him.

children.text: pañca ca kanyāsahasrāṇi ratnabhadrālaṃkāraparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma mārgaṃ śodhayanti sma
children.translated_text: And five thousand maidens holding auspicious jeweled ornaments went before him, clearing the road.

children.text: pañca ca kanyāsahasrāṇi bhadrāsanaparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: And five thousand maidens holding excellent seats went before him.

children.text: pañca ca brāhmaṇasahasrāṇi ghaṇṭāparigṛhītāni māṅgalyaśabdaṃ śrāvayantaḥ purato gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: And five thousand brahmins holding bells went before him, causing auspicious sounds to be heard.

children.text: viṃśatināgasahasrāṇi sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitāni purato gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: Twenty thousand elephants, adorned with every ornament, went before him.

children.text: viṃśatihayasahasrāṇi suvarṇālaṃkārasaṃchannāni sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitāni purato gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: Twenty thousand horses, covered with golden ornaments and adorned with every ornament, went before him.

children.text: aśītirathasahasrāṇi ucchritachatradhvajapatākākiṅkiṇījālasamalaṃkṛtāni bodhisattvasya pṛṣṭhato 'nugacchanti sma
children.translated_text: Eighty thousand chariots, adorned with raised parasols, banners, flags, and networks of little bells, followed behind the Bodhisattva.

children.text: catvāriṃśatpadātisahasrāṇi śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ saṃnaddhadṛḍhavarmakavacānāṃ bodhisattvaṃ gacchantamanugacchanti sma
children.translated_text: Forty thousand infantrymen, brave, heroic, handsome in their limbs, and equipped with firm armor and cuirasses, followed the Bodhisattva as he went.

children.text: gaganatalagatāni cāprameyāsaṃkhyeyānyabhijñātāni kāmāvacarāṇāṃ rūpāvacaradevaputrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi nānāprakāram anekavyūhair bodhisattvasya pūjāṃ kurvanto 'nugacchanti sma
children.translated_text: And, moving in the expanse of the sky, immeasurable, incalculable, well-known hundreds of thousands of crores and nayutas of divine sons from the desire realm and the form realm followed him, making offerings to the Bodhisattva with various kinds of manifold displays.

children.text: yasmiṃśca varapravararathe bodhisattvaḥ samabhirūḍho 'bhūt sa kāmāvacarairdevair anekairmahāvyūhaiḥ samalaṃkṛto 'bhūt
children.translated_text: And the excellent, most excellent jewel chariot on which the Bodhisattva had mounted was adorned by the desire-realm gods with many great displays.

children.text: viṃśati ca devakanyāsahasrāṇi sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitāni ratnasūtraparigṛhītāni taṃ rathaṃ vahanti sma
children.translated_text: And twenty thousand divine maidens, adorned with every ornament and holding jeweled cords, drew that chariot.

children.text: dvayoścāpsarasormadhye ekā mānuṣī kanyā dvayormānuṣīkanyayormadhye ekāpsarā
children.translated_text: Between two apsarases there was one human maiden, and between two human maidens there was one apsaras.

children.text: na cāpsaraso mānuṣīṇāmāmagandhaṃ jighranti sma
children.translated_text: The apsarases did not smell the raw odor of the human women.

children.text: na ca mānuṣā apsarasāṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā pramādamāpadyante sma yadidaṃ bodhisattvasya tejo'nubhāvena ||
children.translated_text: Nor did the humans, seeing the beauty of the apsarases, fall into heedlessness; this was because of the power of the Bodhisattva's splendor.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ kapilāhvaye puravare sarvārthasiddhāya pañcamātraiḥ śākyaśataiḥ pañcagṛhaśatāni nirmāpitānyabhūvan bodhisattvamuddiśya
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, in the excellent city called <s>Kapila</s>, about five hundred <s>Śākyas</s> had five hundred houses built for <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, for the sake of the Bodhisattva.

children.text: te bodhisattvaṃ nagaraṃ praviśantaṃ svasvagṛhadvāramūle sthitvā kṛtāñjalipuṭā abhinatakāyāḥ sagauravā evamāhur iha bhoḥ sarvārthasiddha praviśa
children.translated_text: Standing at the thresholds of their own houses, their hands joined in reverence, their bodies bowed, and full of respect, they addressed the Bodhisattva as he entered the city, saying, "Enter here, sir <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>.

children.text: iha bho devātideva praviśa
children.translated_text: Enter here, sir, god above gods.

children.text: iha bhoḥ śuddhasattva praviśa
children.translated_text: Enter here, sir, pure being.

children.text: iha bhoḥ sārathivara praviśa
children.translated_text: Enter here, sir, best of charioteers.

children.text: iha bhoḥ prītiprāmodyakara praviśa
children.translated_text: Enter here, sir, maker of joy and gladness.

children.text: iha bho aninditayaśaḥ praviśa
children.translated_text: Enter here, sir, you of blameless fame.

children.text: iha bhoḥ samantacakṣu praviśa
children.translated_text: Enter here, sir, all-seeing one.

children.text: iha bho asamasama praviśa
children.translated_text: Enter here, sir, incomparable one.

children.text: iha bho asadṛśaguṇatejodhara lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasvalaṃkṛtakāya praviśeti
children.translated_text: Enter here, sir, bearer of incomparable qualities and splendor, whose body is well adorned with the marks and secondary signs."

children.text: tataścopādāya kumārasyeha sarvārthasiddhaḥ sarvārthasiddha iti saṃjñāmagamat ||
children.translated_text: From then on, the prince came to be known by the designation "<s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>" here.

children.text: tatra rājā śuddhodanasteṣāṃ sarveṣāmanuvartanārthaṃ bodhisattvaṃ sarvagṛheṣu praveśya caturṇāṃ māsānāmatyayādbodhisattvaṃ svagṛhe praveśayati sma
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, in order to comply with all of them, had the Bodhisattva enter every house; and after four months had passed, he brought the Bodhisattva into his own house.

children.text: tatra ca nānāratnavyūho nāma mahāprāsādastaṃ bodhisattvaḥ samārūḍho 'bhūt
children.translated_text: There the Bodhisattva had mounted a great palace named <s>Nānāratnavyūha</s>, the Array of Many Jewels.

children.text: tatra te vṛddhavṛddhāḥ śākyāḥ saṃnipatyaivaṃ mataṃ cārayanti sma kā nu khalu samarthā bodhisattvaṃ gopāyituṃ kelayituṃ mamāyituṃ hitacittatayā maitracittatayā guṇacittatayā saumyacittatayā ceti
children.translated_text: There the aged and very aged <s>Śākyas</s> assembled and circulated this opinion: "Who indeed is capable of protecting the Bodhisattva, amusing him, cherishing him, and attending him with a mind of welfare, a mind of friendliness, a mind attentive to his qualities, and a gentle mind?"

children.text: tatra pañcamātrāṇi śākyavadhūśatāni
children.translated_text: There were about five hundred young <s>Śākya</s> women.

children.text: ekaikā evamāhur ahaṃ kumāramupasthāsya iti
children.translated_text: Each one said, "I will attend the prince."

children.text: tatra mahallakamahallikāḥ śākyā evamāhuḥ sarvā etā vadhūkā navā dahrāstaruṇyaḥ rūpayauvanamadamattāḥ
children.translated_text: There the elder <s>Śākyas</s> said, "All these young women are newly married, tender, and youthful, intoxicated by the pride of beauty and youth.

children.text: naitāḥ samarthā bodhisattvaṃ kālena kālamupasthāpayitum
children.translated_text: They are not capable of attending the Bodhisattva properly from time to time.

children.text: atha ca punariyaṃ mahāprajāpatī gautamī kumārasya mātṛsvasā
children.translated_text: But this <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> is the prince's maternal aunt.

children.text: eṣā samarthā kumāraṃ samyaksukhena saṃvardhayitum rājānaṃ ca śuddhodanamabhidhārayitum
children.translated_text: She is capable of raising the prince in complete comfort and of sustaining King <s>Śuddhodana</s>."

children.text: iti hi te sarve samagrā bhūtvā mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīmutsāhayanti sma
children.translated_text: Thus all of them, being united, encouraged <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>.

children.text: iti hi mahāprajāpatī gautamī kumāraṃ saṃvardhayati sma
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> raised the prince.

children.text: tatra bodhisattvasyārthe dvātriṃśaddhātryaḥ saṃsthāpitā abhuvan aṣṭāvaṅgadhātryaḥ aṣṭau kṣīradhātryaḥ aṣṭau maladhātryaḥ aṣṭau krīḍādhātryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the Bodhisattva's sake thirty-two nurses were appointed: eight nurses for his limbs, eight milk nurses, eight nurses for cleaning him, and eight play nurses.

children.text: tato rājā śuddhodanaḥ sarvaṃ śākyagaṇaṃ saṃnipātyaivaṃ mīmāṃsate sma kiṃ nu khalvayaṃ kumāro rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartī āhosvid abhiniṣkramiṣyati pravrajyāyai
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having assembled the whole group of <s>Śākyas</s>, reflected thus: "Will this prince become a king, a cakravartin, or will he go forth into renunciation?"

children.text: tena ca samayena himavataḥ parvatarājasya pārśve asito nāma maharṣiḥ prativasati sma pañcābhijñaḥ sārdhaṃ naradattena bhāgineyena
children.translated_text: At that time, beside the king of mountains, the <s>Himavat</s>, there lived a great seer named <s>Asita</s>, possessed of the five superknowledges, together with his nephew <s>Naradatta</s>.

children.text: sa bodhisattvasya jātamātrasya bahūnyāścaryādbhutaprātihāryāṇyadrākṣīt
children.translated_text: He saw many marvelous, wondrous miracles belonging to the Bodhisattva, just born.

children.text: gaganatalagatāṃśca devaputrān buddhaśabdamanuśrāvayato 'mbarāṇi ca bhrāmayata itastataḥ pramuditān bhramato 'drākṣīt
children.translated_text: He saw divine sons moving in the expanse of the sky, making the word "Buddha" be heard, waving garments, and wandering here and there in delight.

children.text: tasyaitadabhūd yannvahaṃ vyavalokayeyamiti
children.translated_text: It occurred to him, "Let me look into this."

children.text: sa divyena cakṣuṣā sarvaṃ jambudvīpamanuvilokayannadrākṣīt kapilāhvaye mahāpuravare rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhe kumāraṃ jātaṃ śatapuṇyatejastejitaṃ sarvalokamahitaṃ dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtagātram
children.translated_text: Surveying all <s>Jambudvīpa</s> with his divine eye, he saw that in the excellent great city called <s>Kapila</s>, in the house of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, a prince had been born, radiant with the splendor of a hundred merits, honored by the whole world, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarnaradattaṃ māṇavakamāmantrayate sma yat khalu māṇavaka jānīyā jambudvīpe mahāratnamutpannam
children.translated_text: Having seen this, he addressed the young brahmin <s>Naradatta</s>: "Young man, know that a great jewel has arisen in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.

children.text: kapilavastuni mahānagare rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhe kumāro jātaḥ śatapuṇyatejastejitaḥ sarvalokamahito dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgataḥ
children.translated_text: In the great city <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the house of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, a prince has been born, radiant with the splendor of a hundred merits, honored by the whole world, and endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great person.

children.text: sacetso 'gāramadhyāvasiṣyati rājā bhaviṣyati caturaṅgaścakravartī vijitavān dhārmiko dharmarājo jānapadasthāmavīryaprāptaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ
children.translated_text: If he remains living in the household, he will become a king, a cakravartin with a fourfold army, victorious, righteous, a king of dharma, possessing the steadfast strength and vigor of the people, and endowed with the seven jewels.

children.text: tasyemāni sapta ratnāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: These will be his seven jewels:

children.text: tadyathā cakraratnaṃ hastiratnaṃ aśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnam
children.translated_text: namely, the jewel of the wheel, the jewel of the elephant, the jewel of the horse, the jewel of the gem, the jewel of the woman, the jewel of the householder, and the jewel of the counselor.

children.text: evaṃ saptaratnasampūrṇaśca
children.translated_text: Thus he will be complete with the seven jewels.

children.text: asya putrasahasraṃ bhaviṣyati śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām
children.translated_text: He will have a thousand sons, brave, heroic, handsome in their limbs, and crushers of enemy armies.

children.text: sa imaṃ mahāpṛthivīmaṇḍalaṃ samudraparikhamadaṇḍenāśastreṇa svena dharmeṇa balenābhibhūyābhinirjitya rājyaṃ kariṣyatyaiśvaryādhipatyena
children.translated_text: Having overcome and conquered this circle of the great earth, bounded by the ocean, without rod or sword, by his own dharma and power, he will rule with lordship and sovereignty.

children.text: sacetpunaragārādanagārikāṃ pravrajiṣyati tathāgato bhaviṣyati arhan samyaksaṃbuddho netā ananyaneyaḥ śāstā loke saṃbuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: But if he goes forth from home into homelessness, he will become a Tathāgata, an arhat, a fully awakened Buddha, a leader not led by another, a teacher in the world, awakened.

children.text: tadetarhyupasaṃkramiṣyāvastad draṣṭumiti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore let us now go there to see him."

children.text: atha khalvasito maharṣiḥ sārdhaṃ naradattena bhāgineyena rājahaṃsa iva gaganatalādabhyudgamya samutplutya yena kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ tenopasaṃkrāmat
children.translated_text: Then the great seer <s>Asita</s>, together with his nephew <s>Naradatta</s>, rose up and leapt from the expanse of the sky like a royal swan, and approached the great city <s>Kapilavastu</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya ṛddhiṃ pratisaṃhṛtya padbhyāmeva kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ praviśya yena rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmat
children.translated_text: Having approached, he withdrew his miraculous power, entered the great city <s>Kapilavastu</s> on foot, and went to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s residence.

children.text: upasaṃkramya rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhadvāre 'sthāt ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he stood at the doorway of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s house.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo 'sito maharṣiḥ paśyati sma rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhadvāre 'nekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, the great seer <s>Asita</s> saw many hundreds of thousands of beings gathered at the doorway of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s house.

children.text: atha khalvasito maharṣirdauvārikamupasaṃkramyaivamāha gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya nivedaya dvāre ṛṣirvyavasthita iti
children.translated_text: Then the great seer <s>Asita</s> approached the doorkeeper and said, "Go, sir, inform King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'A seer is standing at the door.'"

children.text: parameti dauvāriko 'sitasya maharṣeḥ pratiśrutya yena rājā śuddhodanastenopasaṃkrāmat
children.translated_text: "Very well," the doorkeeper replied to the great seer <s>Asita</s>, and he went to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya kṛtāñjalipuṭo rājānaṃ śuddhodanamevamāha yat khalu deva jānīyā ṛṣirjīrṇo vṛddho mahallako dvāre sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having approached, with his hands joined in reverence, he said to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, "Your Majesty should know: an aged seer, old, elderly, advanced in years, is standing at the door.

children.text: evaṃ ca vadati rājānamahaṃ draṣṭukāma iti
children.translated_text: And he says, 'I wish to see the king.'"

children.text: atha rājā śuddhodano 'sitasya maharṣerāsanaṃ prajñāpya taṃ puruṣamevamāha praviśatu ṛṣiriti
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had a seat prepared for the great seer <s>Asita</s> and said to that man, "Let the seer enter."

children.text: atha sa puruṣo rājakulānniṣkramyāsitaṃ maharṣimevamāha praviśeti ||
children.translated_text: Then that man, having gone out from the royal residence, said this to the great seer <s>Asita</s>: "Enter."

children.text: atha khalvasito maharṣiryena rājā śuddhodanastenopasaṃkrāmat
children.translated_text: Then the great seer <s>Asita</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purataḥ sthitvā rājānaṃ śuddhodanamevamāha jaya jaya mahārāja ciramāyuḥ pālaya dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayeti ||
children.translated_text: Approaching him and standing before him, he said this to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: "Victory, victory, great king. May you guard long life; rule the kingdom according to <s>dharma</s>."

children.text: atha sa rājā śuddhodano 'sitasya maharṣerarghapādyamarcanaṃ ca kṛtvā sādhu suṣṭhu ca parigṛhya āsanenopanimantrayate sma
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having performed the offering of arghya, water for the feet, and worship for the great seer <s>Asita</s>, received him properly and well, and invited him to a seat.

children.text: sukhopaviṣṭaṃ cainaṃ jñātvā sagauravaḥ supratīta evamāha na smarāmyahaṃ tava ṛṣe darśanam
children.translated_text: Knowing that he was comfortably seated, the king, respectfully and with great pleasure, said this: "I do not remember having seen you, O seer.

children.text: tatkenārthenehābhyāgato 'si kiṃ prayojanam
children.translated_text: For what purpose have you come here? What is the reason?"

children.text: evamukte 'sito maharṣī rājānaṃ śuddhodanametadavocat putraste mahārāja jātastamahaṃ draṣṭukāma ihāgata iti ||
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the great seer <s>Asita</s> said this to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: "A son has been born to you, great king. Desiring to see him, I have come here."

children.text: rājā āha svapiti maharṣe kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: The king said, "The prince is sleeping, great seer.

children.text: muhūrtamāgamaya yāvadutthāsyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Wait a moment, until he wakes."

children.text: ṛṣiravocan na mahārāja tādṛśā mahāpuruṣāściraṃ svapanti
children.translated_text: The seer said, "Great king, such great persons do not sleep long.

children.text: jāgaraśīlāstādṛśāḥ satpuruṣā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Such good beings are wakeful by nature."

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo 'sitasya maharṣeranukampayā jāgaraṇanimittamakarot
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, out of compassion for the great seer <s>Asita</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> made the sign of waking.

children.text: atha khalu rājā śuddhodanaḥ sarvārthasiddhaṃ kumāramubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ sādhu ca suṣṭhu cānuparigṛhya asitasya maharṣerantikamupanāmayati sma ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, carefully and properly supporting the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> with both hands, brought him near the great seer <s>Asita</s>.

children.text: iti hi asito maharṣirbodhisattvamavalokya dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgatamaśītyanuvyañjanasuvicitragātraṃ śakrabrahmalokapālātirekavapuṣaṃ dinakaraśatasahasrātirekatejasaṃ sarvāṅgasundaraṃ dṛṣṭvā codānamudānayati sma āścaryapudgalo batāyaṃ loke prādurbhūta mahāścaryapudgalo batāyaṃ loke prādurbhūta ityutthāyāsanātkṛtāñjalipuṭo bodhisattvasya caraṇayoḥ praṇipatya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ca bodhisattvamaṅkena parigṛhya nidhyāyannavasthito 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, the great seer <s>Asita</s>, beholding the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, saw him endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great person, his body beautifully adorned with the eighty secondary signs, his form surpassing <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the guardians of the world, his radiance surpassing a hundred thousand suns, beautiful in every limb. Then he uttered an inspired exclamation: "Ah, a marvelous person has appeared in the world! Ah, a greatly marvelous person has appeared in the world!" Rising from his seat, with joined palms, he bowed at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet, circumambulated the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, took him onto his lap, and remained there contemplating him.

children.text: so 'drākṣīdbodhisattvasya dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni yaiḥ samanvāgatasya puruṣapudgalasya dve gatī bhavato nānyā
children.translated_text: He saw the thirty-two marks of a great person on the <s>Bodhisattva</s>; when a human person is endowed with these, there are two destinies for him, and no other.

children.text: sacedagāramadhyāvasati rājā bhavati caturaṅgaścakravartī pūrvavadyāvadevaiśvaryādhipatyena
children.translated_text: If he dwells in the midst of a household, he becomes a king, a fourfold wheel-turning monarch, as described before, up to sovereign lordship.

children.text: sacetpunaragārādanagārikāṃ pravrajati tathāgato bhaviṣyati vighuṣṭaśabdaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: But if he goes forth from home into homelessness, he will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, one whose renown is proclaimed, a perfectly awakened <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>.

children.text: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā prārodīdaśrūṇi ca pravartayan gambhīraṃ ca niśvasati sma ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, he began to weep, shed tears, and sighed deeply.

children.text: adrākṣīdrājā śuddhodano 'sitaṃ maharṣiṃ rudantamaśrūṇi ca pravartayamānaṃ gambhīraṃ ca niśvasantam
children.translated_text: King <s>Śuddhodana</s> saw the great seer <s>Asita</s> weeping, shedding tears, and sighing deeply.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca saṃharṣitaromakūpajātastvaritatvaritaṃ dīnamanā asitaṃ maharṣimetadavocat kimidamṛṣe rodasi aśrūṇi ca pravartayasi gambhīraṃ ca niśvasasi mā khalu kumārasya kācidvipratipattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this, with the hairs of his body standing on end, very hastily and distressed in mind, he said this to the great seer <s>Asita</s>: "What is this, O seer? Why do you weep, shed tears, and sigh deeply? Surely there is no misfortune for the prince?"

children.text: evamukte 'sito maharṣī rājānaṃ śuddhodanamevamāha nāhaṃ mahārāja kumārasyārthena rodimi nāpyasya kācidvipratipattiḥ
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the great seer <s>Asita</s> said this to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: "Great king, I am not weeping on account of the prince, nor is there any misfortune for him.

children.text: kiṃtvātmānamahaṃ rodimi
children.translated_text: Rather, I am weeping for myself.

children.text: tatkasmāddhetor ahaṃ ca mahārāja jīrṇo vṛddho mahallakaḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? Great king, I am aged, old, and advanced in years,

children.text: ayaṃ ca sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro 'vaśyamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyati
children.translated_text: while this prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> will certainly fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: abhisaṃbudhya cānuttaraṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayiṣyati apravartitaṃ śramaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā māreṇa vā anyena vā punaḥ kenacilloke sahadharmeṇa
children.translated_text: Having fully awakened, he will set rolling the unsurpassed wheel of <s>dharma</s>, which has not been set rolling by any ascetic, brahmin, god, <s>Māra</s>, or anyone else in the world in accordance with true <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: sadevakasya lokasya hitāya sukhāya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇam
children.translated_text: For the welfare and happiness of the world with its gods, he will teach the <s>dharma</s>, good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good at the end.

children.text: svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ sattvānāṃ saṃprakāśayiṣyati
children.translated_text: He will reveal to beings the holy life, good in meaning and good in expression, entire, complete, pure, and spotless.

children.text: asmāttaṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā jātidharmāṇaḥ sattvā jātyā parimokṣante
children.translated_text: Having heard that <s>dharma</s> from him, beings subject to birth will be freed from birth.

children.text: evaṃ jarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ parimokṣante
children.translated_text: In the same way they will be freed from old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and distress.

children.text: rāgadveṣamohāgnisaṃtaptānāṃ sattvānāṃ saddharmajalavarṣeṇa prahlādanaṃ kariṣyati
children.translated_text: For beings scorched by the fires of passion, hatred, and delusion, he will bring refreshment with the rainfall of the water of the true <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: nānākudṛṣṭigrahaṇapraskandhānāṃ sattvānāṃ kupathaprayātānāmṛjumārgeṇa nirvāṇapathamupaneṣyati
children.translated_text: Beings who have rushed into grasping various false views and have gone along a wrong path he will lead by the straight path to the path of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: saṃsārapañjaracārakāvaruddhānāṃ kleśabandhanabaddhānāṃ bandhananirmokṣaṃ kariṣyati
children.translated_text: For beings confined in the cage and prison of <s>saṃsāra</s>, bound by the bonds of the afflictions, he will bring release from bondage.

children.text: ajñānatamastimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanayanānāṃ sattvānāṃ prajñācakṣurutpādayiṣyati
children.translated_text: For beings whose eyes are covered by the veil of the blinding darkness of ignorance, he will produce the eye of wisdom.

children.text: kleśaśalyaviddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ śalyoddharaṇaṃ kariṣyati
children.translated_text: For beings pierced by the thorn of the afflictions, he will extract the thorn.

children.text: tadyathā mahārāja audumbarapuṣpaṃ kadācitkarhicilloke utpadyate evameva mahārāja kadācitkarhicidbahubhiḥ kalpakoṭinayutairbuddhā bhagavanto loke utpadyante
children.translated_text: Just as, great king, the flower of the udumbara appears in the world only once in a long while, so too, great king, only once in a long while, after many crores and nayutas of kalpas, do blessed Buddhas appear in the world.

children.text: so 'yaṃ kumāro 'vaśyamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate
children.translated_text: This prince will certainly fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening."

children.text: abhisaṃbudhya ca sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi saṃsārasāgarāt pāramuttārayiṣyati amṛte ca pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyati
children.translated_text: And, having awakened to perfect enlightenment, he will carry hundreds of thousands of nayutas of crores of beings across from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> to the far shore, and he will establish them in <s>amṛta</s> (the deathless).

children.text: vayaṃ ca taṃ buddharatnaṃ na drakṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: And we shall not see that jewel of a Buddha.

children.text: ityeva tadahaṃ mahārāja rodimi paridīnamanā dīrghaṃ ca niśvasāmi yadahamimaṃ nārogye 'pi rādhayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: It is for just this reason, great king, that I weep, downcast in mind, and sigh deeply: I shall not be able to attend upon this one, even if I am in health.

children.text: yathā hyasmākaṃ mahārāja mantravedaśāstreṣvāgacchati nārhati sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro 'gāram adhyāvasitum
children.translated_text: For, great king, just as it is stated in our texts of mantra, Veda, and śāstra, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> is not fit to dwell in a household.

children.text: tatkasya hetos tathā hi mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? For, great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> is endowed with the thirty-two <s>mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇas</s> (marks of a great man).

children.text: katamairdvātriṃśatā tadyathā
children.translated_text: Which thirty-two? They are as follows:

children.text: uṣṇīṣaśīrṣo mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has a head with an <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance).

children.text: anena mahārāja prathamena mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇena samanvāgataḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: By this, great king, the first mark of a great man, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> is endowed.

children.text: bhinnāñjanamayūrakalāpābhinīlavallitapradakṣiṇāvartakeśaḥ
children.translated_text: His hair curls to the right in dark-blue locks, like split collyrium and peacock plumes.

children.text: samavipulalalāṭaḥ
