children.translated_text: His forehead is even and broad.

children.text: ūrṇā mahārāja sarvārthasiddhasya kumārasya bhruvormadhye jātā himarajataprakāśā
children.translated_text: Great king, an <s>ūrṇā</s> hair has arisen between Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>'s brows, bright like snow and silver.

children.text: gopakṣmanetraḥ
children.translated_text: His eyes have lashes like a cow's.

children.text: abhinīlanetraḥ
children.translated_text: His eyes are deep blue.

children.text: samacatvāriṃśaddantaḥ
children.translated_text: He has a full and even forty teeth.

children.text: aviraladantaḥ
children.translated_text: His teeth are without gaps.

children.text: śukladantaḥ
children.translated_text: His teeth are white.

children.text: brahmasvaro mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: rasarasāgravān
children.translated_text: He possesses the foremost excellence of taste.

children.text: prabhūtatanujihvaḥ
children.translated_text: His tongue is large and slender.

children.text: siṃhahanuḥ
children.translated_text: His jaw is like a lion's.

children.text: susaṃvṛttaskandhaḥ
children.translated_text: His shoulders are well rounded.

children.text: saptotsadaḥ
children.translated_text: He has the seven raised parts of the body.

children.text: citāntarāṃsaḥ
children.translated_text: The hollow between his shoulders is filled in.

children.text: sūkṣmasuvarṇavarṇacchaviḥ
children.translated_text: His skin has a fine, golden-colored complexion.

children.text: sthito 'navanatapralambabāhuḥ
children.translated_text: When standing upright, his arms hang down long without his bending.

children.text: siṃhapūrvārdhakāyaḥ
children.translated_text: The front half of his body is like a lion's.

children.text: nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalo mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has the proportions of a banyan tree, his height and arm-span being equal.

children.text: ekaikaromā
children.translated_text: He has one hair in each pore.

children.text: ūrdhvāgrābhipradakṣiṇāvartaromāḥ
children.translated_text: The hairs of his body have their tips upward and curl to the right.

children.text: kośopagatabastiguhyaḥ
children.translated_text: His male organ is enclosed in a sheath.

children.text: suvivartitoruḥ
children.translated_text: His thighs are well rounded.

children.text: eṇeyamṛgarājajaṅghaḥ
children.translated_text: His calves are like those of the king of the eṇeya deer.

children.text: dīrghāṅguliḥ
children.translated_text: His fingers are long.

children.text: āyatapārṣṇipādaḥ
children.translated_text: His feet have long heels.

children.text: utsaṅgapādaḥ
children.translated_text: His feet have raised insteps.

children.text: mṛdutaruṇahastapādaḥ
children.translated_text: His hands and feet are soft and tender.

children.text: jālāṅgulihastapādaḥ
children.translated_text: His hands and feet have webbed fingers and toes.

children.text: dīrghāṅguliradhaḥkramatalayormahārāja sarvārthasiddhasya kumārasya cakre jāte ci arciṣmatī prabhāsvare site sahasrāre sanemike sanābhike
children.translated_text: Great king, on the soles of Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>'s downward-stepping feet, wheels have appeared, flaming, radiant, white, thousand-spoked, with rims and hubs.

children.text: supratiṣṭhitasamapādo mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has well-planted, even feet.

children.text: anena mahārāja dvātriṃśattamena mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇena samanvāgataḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: By this, great king, the thirty-second mark of a great man, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> is endowed.

children.text: na ca mahārāja cakravartināmevaṃvidhāni lakṣaṇāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: And, great king, universal monarchs do not have marks of this kind.

children.text: bodhisattvānāṃ ca tādṛśāni lakṣaṇāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Bodhisattvas have marks of such a kind.

children.text: saṃvidyante khalu punarmahārāja sarvārthasiddhasya kumārasya kāye 'śītyanuvyañjanāni yaiḥ samanvāgataḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro nārhatyagāramadhyāvasitum
children.translated_text: Moreover, great king, there are eighty secondary signs on the body of Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>; endowed with them, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> is not fit to dwell in a household.

children.text: avaśyamabhiniṣkramiṣyati pravrajyāyai
children.translated_text: He will inevitably go forth into <s>pravrajyā</s> (renunciation).

children.text: katamāni ca mahārāja tānyaśītyanuvyañjanāni tadyathā tuṅganakhaśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: And what, great king, are those eighty secondary signs? They are as follows: great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has raised nails.

children.text: tāmranakhaśca snigdhanakhaśca vṛttāṅguliśca anupūrvacitrāṅguliśca gūḍhaśiraśca gūḍhagulphaśca ghanasaṃdhiśca aviṣamasamapādaśca āyatapārṣṇiśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has copper-colored nails, glossy nails, rounded fingers, beautifully graduated fingers, hidden veins, hidden ankles, firm joints, even and symmetrical feet, and long heels.

children.text: snigdhapāṇilekhaśca tulyapāṇilekhaśca gambhīrapāṇilekhaśca ajihmapāṇilekhaśca anupūrvapāṇilekhaśca bimboṣṭhaśca noccavacanaśabdaśca mṛdutaruṇatāmrajihvaśca gajagarjitābhistanitameghasvaramadhuramañjughoṣaśca paripūrṇavyañjanaśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has glossy palm-lines, matching palm-lines, deep palm-lines, straight palm-lines, regularly ordered palm-lines, lips like the bimba fruit, a voice that is neither too high nor too low, a soft, tender, copper-colored tongue, a sweet and charming tone like the roar of an elephant and the thunder of a cloud, and complete secondary characteristics.

children.text: pralambabāhuśca śucigātravastusampannaśca mṛdugātraśca viśālagātraśca adīnagātraśca anupūrvonnatagātraśca susamāhitagātraśca suvibhaktagātraśca pṛthuvipulasuparipūrṇajānumaṇḍalaśca vṛttagātraśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has long-hanging arms, a pure bodily constitution, a soft body, a broad body, a body not shrunken, a body gradually and well developed, a well-composed body, a well-proportioned body, broad, wide, and perfectly full kneecaps, and rounded limbs.

children.text: suparimṛṣṭagātraśca ajihmavṛṣabhagātraśca anupūrvagātraśca gambhīranābhiśca ajihmanābhiśca anupūrvanābhiśca śucyācāraśca ṛṣabhavat samantaprāsādikaśca paramasuviśuddhavitimirālokasamantaprabhaśca nāgavilambitagatiśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has a very smooth body, a straight and bull-like body, a body regular in form, a deep navel, a straight navel, a regular navel, pure conduct, a presence pleasing on every side like a bull, an all-around radiance of supremely pure light free from darkness, and a gait stately like an elephant's.

children.text: siṃhavikrāntagatiśca ṛṣabhavikrāntagatiśca haṃsavikrāntagatiśca abhipradakṣiṇāvartagatiśca vṛttakukṣiśca mṛṣṭakukṣiśca ajihmakukṣiśca cāpodaraśca vyapagatachandadoṣanīlakālakāduṣṭaśarīraśca vṛttadaṃṣṭraśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has the stride of a lion, the stride of a bull, the stride of a haṃsa bird, a gait turning auspiciously to the right, a rounded belly, a smooth belly, a straight belly, a bow-shaped abdomen, a body free from ugly blue, black, and dark blemishes, and rounded canine teeth.

children.text: tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭraśca anupūrvadaṃṣṭraśca tuṅganāsaśca śucinayanaśca vimalanayanaśca prahasitanayanaśca āyatanayanaśca viśālanayanaśca nīlakuvalayadalasadṛśanayanaśca sahitabhrūśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Great king, Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has sharp canine teeth, regular canine teeth, a high nose, pure eyes, stainless eyes, smiling eyes, long eyes, wide eyes, eyes like the petals of a blue lotus, and connected eyebrows.

children.text: citrabhrūśca asitabhrūśca saṃgatabhrūśca anupūrvabhrūśca pīnagaṇḍaśca aviṣamagaṇḍaśca vyapagatagaṇḍadoṣaśca anupahatakruṣṭaśca suviditendriyaśca suparipūrṇendriyaśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: O great king, prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has variegated eyebrows, dark eyebrows, connected eyebrows, evenly ordered eyebrows, full cheeks, even cheeks, cheeks free from defects, an unspoiled resonant voice, clearly manifest faculties, and completely full faculties.

children.text: saṃgatamukhalalāṭaśca paripūrṇottamāṅgaśca asitakeśaśca sahitakeśaśca susaṃgatakeśaśca surabhikeśaśca aparuṣakeśaśca anākulakeśaśca anupūrvakeśaśca sukuñcitakeśaśca śrīvatsasvastikanandyāvartavardhamānasaṃsthānakeśaśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: O great king, prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has a well-joined mouth and forehead, a perfectly full head, black hair, coherent hair, well-arranged hair, fragrant hair, hair that is not harsh, hair that is not tangled, hair in regular order, well-curled hair, and hair shaped in the forms of the śrīvatsa, svastika, nandyāvarta, and vardhamāna.

children.text: imāni tāni mahārāja sarvārthasiddhasya kumārasyāśītyanuvyañjanāni yaiḥ samanvāgataḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro nārhatyagāramadhyāvasitum
children.translated_text: These, O great king, are the eighty secondary marks of prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>. Endowed with them, prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> is not fit to dwell in the midst of a household.

children.text: avaśyamabhiniṣkramiṣyati pravrajyāyai ||
children.translated_text: He will certainly go forth into renunciation.

children.text: atha khalu rājā śuddhodano 'sitasya maharṣeḥ sakāśātkumārasyedaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā saṃtuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāta utthāyāsanādbodhisattvasya caraṇayoḥ praṇipatyemāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having heard this prediction about the prince from the great seer <s>Asita</s>, was satisfied, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness. Rising from his seat, he bowed at the feet of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and spoke this verse:

children.text: vanditastvaṃ suraiḥ sendraiḥ ṛṣibhiścāsi pūjitaḥ
children.translated_text: You have been honored by the gods together with <s>Indra</s>, and you are worshiped by the seers;

children.text: vaidya sarvasya lokasya vande 'hamapi tvāṃ vibho ||
children.translated_text: O physician of the whole world, I too bow to you, mighty lord.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo rājā śuddhodano 'sitaṃ maharṣiṃ sārdhaṃ naradattena bhāgineyenānurūpeṇa bhaktena saṃtarpayati sma
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> satisfied the great seer <s>Asita</s>, together with his nephew <s>Naradatta</s>, with suitable food.

children.text: saṃtarpyābhicchādya pradakṣiṇamakarot
children.translated_text: After satisfying him and covering him with gifts, he circumambulated him.

children.text: atha khalvasito maharṣistata evarddhyā vihāyasā prākramat yena svāśramastenopāsaṃkrāmat ||
children.translated_text: Then the great seer <s>Asita</s>, by that very supernormal power, set out through the air and approached his own hermitage.

children.text: atha khalu dvayaṃ saṃkramya tatra khalvasito maharṣirnaradattaṃ māṇavakametadavocad yadā tvaṃ naradatta śṛṇuyā buddho loke utpanna iti tadā tvaṃ gatvā tasya śāsane pravrajeḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after some time had passed, the great seer <s>Asita</s> said this to the young brahmin <s>Naradatta</s>: "When you hear, <s>Naradatta</s>, that a Buddha has arisen in the world, then go and go forth in his teaching.

children.text: tatte bhaviṣyati dīrgharātramarthāya hitāya sukhāyeti ||
children.translated_text: That will be for your welfare, benefit, and happiness for a long time."

children.text: tatredamucyate ||
children.translated_text: On this point the following is said:

children.text: dṛṣṭvā devagaṇānnabhastalagatān buddhaśravodgāriṇo devarṣīrasito 'drikandaragataḥ prītiṃ parāṃ prāptavān
children.translated_text: Seeing the hosts of gods moving in the sky and proclaiming the fame of the Buddha, the divine seer <s>Asita</s>, dwelling in a mountain cave, attained supreme joy.

children.text: buddho nāma padaṃ kimetadiha bho harṣāvahaṃ prāṇināṃ prahlāda mama kāya eti sukhitaṃ śāntaṃ ca cittaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: "What, friends, is this word 'Buddha' here, bringing joy to living beings? Delight comes over my body; my mind is happy and supremely calm.

children.text: kiṃ devo tvasuro 'thavāpi sa bhaved garuḍo 'thavā kinnaraḥ buddho nāma kimetadaśrutapadaṃ prītikaraṃ modanam
children.translated_text: Is he a god, or perhaps an asura? Might he be <s>Garuḍa</s> or a kinnara? What is this unheard word 'Buddha,' delight-giving and gladdening?"

children.text: divyā cakṣuṣa prekṣate daśa diśaḥ śailān mahīṃ sāgarān bhūyaḥ paśyati cādbhutaṃ bahuvidhaṃ bhūmau girau sāgare ||
children.translated_text: With his divine eye he looks upon the ten directions, the mountains, the earth, and the oceans; again he sees many kinds of wonders on the earth, on the mountains, and in the sea.

children.text: ābheyaṃ pravirājate surucirā prahlādayantī tanuṃ jātāścaiva yathā hi śailaśikhare snigdhāḥ pravālāṅkurāḥ
children.translated_text: This beautiful radiance shines forth, delighting the body; and just as tender coral shoots are born on a mountain peak,

children.text: vṛkṣāścaiva yathā supuṣpabharitā nānāphalairmaṇḍitāḥ suvyaktaṃ tribhave bhaviṣyati laghu ratnodbhavaḥ śobhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and just as trees are filled with abundant blossoms and adorned with many fruits, so it is clear that in the three worlds there will soon be the arising of a splendid jewel.

children.text: bhūmirbhāti yathā ca pāṇisadṛśā sarvā samā nirmalā devāścaiva yathā prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ khe bhrāmayantyambarān
children.translated_text: Just as the earth shines, all level and spotless like the palm of a hand, and just as the gods, joyful in mind, wave their garments in the sky,

children.text: yadvat sāgaranāgarājanilaye ratnāḥ plavante 'dbhutāḥ suvyaktaṃ jinaratna jambunilaye dharmākarasyodbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and just as marvelous jewels float in the abode of the ocean's nāga kings, so it is clear that the Jina-jewel, the source of Dharma, has arisen in the abode of <s>Jambu</s>.

children.text: yadvacchānta apāya duḥkhavigatāḥ sattvāśca saukhyānvitāḥ yadvaddevagaṇā nabhastalagatā gacchanti harṣānvitāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as the beings in the lower states are pacified, freed from suffering, and endowed with happiness, and just as the hosts of gods in the sky move about filled with joy,

children.text: yatha ca snigdharavaṃ manojña śṛṇuyā divyāna saṃgītināṃ ratanasyā iva prādurbhāvu tribhave yasyā nimittā ime ||
children.translated_text: and just as one hears the sweet and pleasing sound of divine musicians, so these are signs of the manifestation of that jewel in the three worlds.

children.text: asitaḥ prekṣati jambusāhvayamidaṃ divyena vai cakṣuṣā so 'drākṣīt kapilāhvaye puravare śuddhodanasyālaye
children.translated_text: <s>Asita</s> looks with his divine eye upon this place called <s>Jambu</s>. In the excellent city called <s>Kapila</s>, in the residence of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, he saw

children.text: jāto lakṣaṇapuṇyatejabharito nārāyaṇasthāmavān dṛṣṭvā cāttamanā udagramanasaḥ sthāmāsya saṃvardhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one born filled with the marks, merit, and splendor, possessing the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. Seeing him, <s>Asita</s> became glad and exultant in mind, and his own strength increased.

children.text: udyuktastvarito 'tivismitamanā cāsau svaśiṣyānvitaḥ āgatvā kapilāhvayaṃ puravaraṃ dvāri sthito bhūpateḥ
children.translated_text: Eager, hurrying, and exceedingly amazed, he came with his disciples to the excellent city called <s>Kapila</s> and stood at the king's gate.

children.text: anubaddhā bahuprāṇikoṭinayutā dṛṣṭvā ṛṣirjīrṇakaḥ avacī sārathi rājña vedaya laghuṃ dvāre ṛṣistiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Followed by many crores and nayutas of living beings, the aged seer, seeing the gatekeeper, said to the charioteer, "Quickly inform the king: a seer is standing at the gate."

children.text: śrutvā cāśu praviśya rājabhavanaṃ rājñastamākhyātavān dvāre deva tapasvi tiṣṭhati mahān jīrṇo ṛṣirjarjaraḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this, he quickly entered the royal palace and reported to the king, "Lord, at the gate there stands a great ascetic, an aged and decrepit seer.

children.text: so cāpī abhinandate ṛṣivaraḥ prāveṣṭu rājño gṛhaṃ ājñā dīyatu tāva pārthivavarā demi praveśaṃ tesā ||
children.translated_text: And that best of seers wishes to enter the king's house. Let the command be given, O best of rulers, so that I may grant him entry."

children.text: sthāpyā cāsanamasya cāha nṛpatiḥ gaccha praveśaṃ dada asitaḥ sārathivākya śrutva muditaḥ prītyā sukhenānvitaḥ
children.translated_text: "Set out a seat for him," said the king. "Go and grant him entry." Hearing the charioteer's words, <s>Asita</s> was glad, filled with joy and happiness.

children.text: śītaṃ vāri yathābhikāṅkṣi tṛṣito bhuktvādito cāśanaṃ tadvatsukhyabhinandito ṛṣivaraḥ taṃ draṣṭu sattvottamam ||
children.translated_text: As a thirsty man rejoices in cool water as he desires, or a hungry man in food to eat, so the best of seers rejoiced happily at seeing that highest of beings.

children.text: jaya bhoḥ pārthiva ityuvāca mudito cāyuṃ ciraṃ pālaya vṛddhiṃ kṛtva niṣaṇṇa dāntamanasaḥ śāntendriyaḥ sūrataḥ
children.translated_text: "Victory, O king," he said joyfully, "and may you long preserve your life." Having uttered a blessing for prosperity, he sat down, controlled in mind, tranquil in his faculties, and gentle.

children.text: rājā vai abhivādya taṃ sunibhṛtaṃ provāca kiṃ kāraṇaṃ āgāmastava pārthivendra nilaye tad brūhi śīghraṃ mune ||
children.translated_text: The king, having respectfully greeted him, said very quietly, "What is the reason for your coming to the lord of kings' palace? Tell it quickly, sage."

children.text: putraste vararūpa pāramigato jāto mahātejavān dvātriṃśadvaralakṣaṇaiḥ kavacito nārāyaṇasthāmavān
children.translated_text: "Your son, of excellent beauty, has been born having gone beyond the farther shore, greatly radiant, armored with the thirty-two excellent marks, and possessing the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: taṃ draṣṭuṃ hi mamepsitaṃ narapate sarvārthasiddhaṃ śiśum ityarthaṃ samupāgato 'smi nṛpate nāstyanyakāryaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: I wish to see that child, <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, lord of men. For this purpose I have come, king; I have no other business."

children.text: sādhu svāgatu yācase kilamitaḥ prīto 'smi te darśanāt eṣo 'sau śayitaḥ kumāra varado draṣṭuṃ na śakyo 'dhunā
children.translated_text: "Good, welcome. Since you ask this of me, I am pleased by the sight of you. Here is that prince, the boon-giver, asleep; just now he cannot be seen.

children.text: sādhū tāva mūhūrtamāgama ihā yad drakṣyase nirmalaṃ candraṃ vā yatha pūrṇamāsi vimalaṃ tārāgaṇairmaṇḍitam ||
children.translated_text: Wait here a moment, good sir, and then you will see the stainless one, like the spotless moon on the full-moon night, encircled by the hosts of stars."

children.text: yada cāsau pratibuddha sārathivaraḥ paripūrṇacandraprabhaḥ tada rājā pratigṛhya vahnivapuṣaṃ sūryātirekaprabham
children.translated_text: And when that best guide awoke, shining like the full moon, the king took up the fire-bodied one, whose radiance surpassed the sun,

children.text: hantā paśya ṛṣe nṛdevamahitaṃ hemāgrabimbopamam asito dṛṣṭva ca tasya tau sucaraṇau cakrāṅkitau śobhanau ||
children.translated_text: and said, "Come, see, seer, this one honored by gods and kings, like a disk of finest gold." <s>Asita</s>, seeing his two beautiful feet marked with wheels,

children.text: pratyutthāya tataḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo caraṇāni so vandate aṅke gṛhya mahātmaśāstrakuśalo nidhyāyato prekṣate
children.translated_text: rose up, joined his hands in reverence, and bowed to his feet. Taking him on his lap, skilled in the great treatises, he gazed at him in contemplation.

children.text: so 'paśyadvaralakṣaṇaiḥ kavacitaṃ nārāyaṇasthāmavaṃ śīrṣaṃ kampya sa vedaśāstrakuśalo dve tasya paśyadgatī ||
children.translated_text: He saw him armored with the excellent marks and possessing the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; shaking his head, skilled in Veda and śāstra, he saw his two destinies.

children.text: rājā vā bhavi cakravarti balavān buddho va lokottamaḥ bāṣpaṃ tyakta sudīnakāyamanaso gambhīra niśvasya ca
children.translated_text: "He will become either a powerful cakravartin king or a supreme, world-transcending Buddha." Then he shed tears, his body and mind deeply saddened, and sighed profoundly.

children.text: udvignaśca babhūva pārthivavaraḥ kiṃ brāhmaṇo roditī mā vighnaṃ khalu paśyate 'yamasitaḥ sarvārthasiddhasya me ||
children.translated_text: The excellent king became anxious: "Why is the brahmin weeping? Surely this <s>Asita</s> does not see some obstacle for my <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>?"

children.text: bhūtaṃ vyāhara kiṃ tu rodiṣi ṛṣe śreyo 'tha kiṃ pāpakaṃ pāpaṃ nāsti na cāntarāyamiha bhoḥ sarvārthasiddhasya te
children.translated_text: "Tell the truth. Why are you weeping, seer? Is it for good, or is there something bad?" "There is no evil here, sir, and no obstacle for your <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>.

children.text: ātmānaṃ bahu śocamī narapate jīrṇo 'smi yajjarjaraḥ yadayaṃ bheṣyati buddha lokamahito dharmaṃ yadā vakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: I grieve much for myself, king, for I am old and decrepit. When this one will become the Buddha, honored by the world, and when he will teach the dharma,

children.text: na drakṣe ahu labdhaprītimanaso ityartha rodāmyahaṃ yasyā kāyi bhavanti lakṣaṇavarā dvātriṃśati nirmalā
children.translated_text: I shall not see him, though my mind would have gained joy. For that reason I weep. He in whose body the thirty-two stainless excellent marks are found

children.text: dve tasyā gatayo na anya tṛtiyā jānīṣva evaṃ nṛpa rājā vā bhavi cakravarti balavān buddho 'tha lokottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has two destinies and no other third one. Know this, king: he will become either a powerful cakravartin king or a supreme Buddha.

children.text: nāyaṃ kāmaguṇebhirarthiku punaḥ buddho ayaṃ bheṣyati śrutvā vyākaraṇaṃ ṛṣeḥ sa nṛpatiḥ prītiṃ sukhaṃ labdhavān
children.translated_text: This one will not seek the objects of sensual pleasure; this one will become the Buddha." Hearing the seer's prophecy, the king obtained joy and happiness.

children.text: pratyutthāya tataḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo caraṇāvasau vandate devaistvaṃ svabhipūjitaḥ subalavān ṛṣibhiśca saṃvarṇitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he rose up, joined his hands in reverence, and bowed to his feet: "You are worshiped by the gods, mighty one, and praised by the seers.

children.text: vande tvāṃ varasārthavāha tribhave sarve jage pūjitaṃ asitaḥ prāha ca bhāgineya muditaḥ saṃśrūyatāṃ bhāṣato
children.translated_text: I bow to you, excellent caravan-leader, worshiped in the three worlds and in the whole world." And <s>Asita</s>, delighted, said to his sister's son, "Listen as I speak.

children.text: buddhā bodhi yadā śṛṇoṣi jagato varteti cakraṃ hyayaṃ śīghraṃ pravraja śāsane 'sya munaye tatprāpsyase nirvṛtim ||
children.translated_text: When you hear of the Buddha's awakening and that he turns the wheel for the world, quickly go forth in this sage's teaching; by that you will attain nirvṛti."

children.text: vanditvā caraṇau hyasau munivaraḥ kṛtvā ca prādakṣiṇaṃ lābhā te nṛpate sulabdha vipulā yasyedṛśaste sutaḥ
children.translated_text: Having bowed to his feet and circumambulated him, that best of sages said, "Your gains are gains indeed, king, abundantly and well gained, since such a son is yours.

children.text: eṣo loka sadevakaṃ samanujaṃ dharmeṇa tarpeṣyati niṣkrāmaṃ kapilāhvayādṛṣivaro 'raṇye sthitaḥ svāśrame ||
children.translated_text: He will satisfy the world, together with gods and humans, by the dharma." Departing from the place called <s>Kapila</s>, the excellent seer stayed in his own hermitage in the forest.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo jātamātrasya bodhisattvasya maheśvaro devaputraḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikān devaputrānāmantryaivamāha yo 'sau mārṣā asaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrasukṛtakarmadānaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñopāyaśrattacaraṇavratatapaḥsucaritacaraṇaḥ mahāmaitrīmahākaruṇāmahāmuditāsamanvāgata upekṣāsamudgatacittaḥ sarvasattvahitasukhodyato dṛḍhavīryakavacasusaṃnāhasaṃnaddhaḥ pūrvajinakṛtakuśalamūloditaḥ śatapuṇyalakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtaḥ sukṛtaniścayaparākramaḥ paracakrapramathanaḥ suvimalaśuddhāśayasampannaḥ sucaritacaraṇo mahājñānaketudhvajaḥ mārabalāntakaraṇaḥ trisāhasramahāsāhasrasārthavāhaḥ devamanuṣyapūjitamahāyajñayaṣṭaḥ susamṛddhapuṇyanicayaniḥsaraṇābhiprāyo jātijarāmaraṇāntakaraḥ sujātajātaḥ ikṣvākurājakulasambhūto jagadvibodhayitā bodhisattvo mahāsattvo manuṣyaloka upapannaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, when the Bodhisattva had only just been born, the divine son <s>Maheśvara</s> addressed the divine sons belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> class and said this: "Sirs, that one who, through innumerable hundreds of thousands of crores and nayutas of aeons, practiced meritorious deeds, giving, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, wisdom, skillful means, faith-filled conduct, vows, austerities, and good conduct; who is endowed with great loving-kindness, great compassion, and great sympathetic joy; whose mind has arisen into equanimity; who is intent on the welfare and happiness of all beings; who is well armed and clad in the firm armor of vigor; who has arisen from roots of merit made by former <s>Jinas</s>; who is adorned with the marks produced by a hundred merits; whose valor is assured by good deeds; who crushes hostile forces; who is endowed with a very pure and clean intention; who practices good conduct; who is the banner and standard of great knowledge; who will bring <s>Māra</s>'s army to an end; who is the caravan-leader of the great trichiliocosm; who is a great object of offering worshiped by gods and humans; whose intention is toward release through a well-accumulated store of merit; who will put an end to birth, old age, and death; who is well born, born in the royal lineage of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>; who will awaken the world, the Bodhisattva, the great being, has appeared in the human world.

children.text: na cirādasāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate
children.translated_text: Before long he will awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: hanta gacchāmastamabhivandituṃ mānayituṃ pūjayitum abhistotum anyeṣāṃ ca mānābhibhūtānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ mānamadadarpacchedanārtham
children.translated_text: Come, let us go to bow to him, honor him, worship him, and praise him, and also for the sake of cutting down the arrogance, intoxication, and pride of other divine sons overcome by pride.

children.text: te 'smānabhivandamānān dṛṣṭvā te 'pi bodhisattvaṃ vandiṣyanti mānayiṣyanti pūjayiṣyanti ca
children.translated_text: When they see us bowing to him, they too will bow to the Bodhisattva, honor him, and worship him.

children.text: tatteṣāṃ bhaviṣyati dīrgharātramarthāya hitāya sukhāya yāvadamṛtādhigamāya
children.translated_text: That will be for their welfare, benefit, and happiness through the long night, up to the attainment of the deathless.

children.text: rājñaśca śuddhodanasya jayavṛddhiranuśrāvitā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And the victorious increase of King <s>Śuddhodana</s> will be proclaimed.

children.text: tattvavyākaraṇena ca bodhisattvaṃ vyākṛtya punarapyāgamiṣyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: "And, having prophesied the <s>Bodhisattva</s> by a true prediction, we shall return again."

children.text: atha khalu maheśvaro devaputro dvādaśabhirdevaputraśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ sarvakapilavastumahānagaramavabhāsena sphurayitvā yena rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmat
children.translated_text: Then the divine son <s>Maheśvara</s>, surrounded and preceded by twelve hundred thousand divine sons, filled the entire great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> with his radiance and approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s residence.

children.text: upasaṃkramya dauvārike nivedya rājñābhyanujñāto rājakulaṃ praviśya bodhisattvasya pādau śirasābhivandyaikāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā anekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bodhisattvamaṅke samāropya rājānaṃ śuddhodanamāśvāsayati sma tuṣṭo mahārāja bhava paramaprītaśca
children.translated_text: Having approached, he announced himself to the gatekeepers; permitted by the king, he entered the royal household, bowed with his head to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, circumambulated the <s>Bodhisattva</s> many hundreds of thousands of times, placed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> on his lap, and reassured King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: "Be content, great king, and supremely delighted.

children.text: tatkasmāddhetor yathā mahārāja bodhisattvasya lakṣaṇairanuvyañjanaiśca kāyaḥ samalaṃkṛto yathā ca kumāro 'bhibhavati sadevamānuṣāsuralokaṃ varṇena tejasā ca yaśasā lakṣmyā ca niḥsaṃśayaṃ mahārāja bodhisattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate ||
children.translated_text: Why is that? Great king, because the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body is adorned with marks and secondary signs, and because the prince surpasses the world with its gods, humans, and asuras in beauty, splendor, fame, and majesty. Without doubt, great king, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening."

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo maheśvaro devaputraḥ sārdhaṃ śuddhāvāsakāyikairdevaputrair bodhisattvasya mahatpūjopasthānaṃ kṛtvā bodhisattvaṃ tattvavyākaraṇena vyākṛtya punarapi svabhavanaṃ prākrāmat ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, the divine son <s>Maheśvara</s>, together with the divine sons belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> realm, performed great worship and attendance for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, prophesied the <s>Bodhisattva</s> by a true prediction, and returned again to his own abode.

children.text: tatredamucyate ||
children.translated_text: On this point the following is said:

children.text: jātasya tasya guṇasāgarasāgarasya jñātvā sureśvaramarud bruvate udagraḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing that he had been born, an ocean of an ocean of virtues, the lord of the gods spoke joyfully to the <s>Maruts</s>:

children.text: yasyā sudurlabhaśravo bahukalpakoṭyā hantetha taṃ vrajama pūjayituṃ munīndram ||
children.translated_text: "Come now, let us go to worship that lord of sages, whose hearing is very hard to obtain even in many crores of kalpas."

children.text: paripūrṇadvādaśasahasra marudviśuddhā maṇiratnacūḍasamalaṃkṛta iryavantaḥ
children.translated_text: Twelve thousand purified <s>Maruts</s> in full, adorned with crests of jewel-gems and moving gracefully,

children.text: kapilāhvayaṃ puravaraṃ samupetya śīghraṃ dvāri sthitā narapateḥ suvilambacūḍāḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly came to the excellent city called <s>Kapila</s> and stood at the king's gate with beautifully hanging crests.

children.text: te dvārapālamavadan sumanojñaghoṣāḥ prativedayasva nṛpate bhavanaṃ praviśya
children.translated_text: With very charming voices they said to the gatekeeper, "Enter the king's palace and announce us."

children.text: dauvāriko vacana śrutva gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ prahvaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo nṛpatiṃ babhāṣe ||
children.translated_text: Having heard their words, the gatekeeper entered the house and, bowing with folded hands, addressed the king:

children.text: jaya deva nityamanupālaya dīrghamāyuḥ dvāre sthitā vipulapuṇyaviśuddhabhāsaḥ
children.translated_text: "Victory, O lord. Ever protect a long life. At the gate stand beings of vast merit, pure in radiance,

children.text: maṇiratnacūḍasuvibhūṣita iryavantaḥ paripūrṇacandravadanā śaśinirmalābhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: adorned and moving gracefully with crests of jewel-gems, their faces like the full moon, their appearance stainless as the moon.

children.text: chāyāṃ na teṣa nṛpate kvacidapyapaśyan śabdaṃ na caiva caraṇotkṣipaṇe śṛṇomi
children.translated_text: I have not seen their shadows anywhere, O king, nor do I hear any sound when they lift their feet.

children.text: na ca medinīṃ vicarato rajamutkṣipanti tṛptiṃ na yānti ca janāḥ samudīkṣatāṃ vai ||
children.translated_text: As they move over the earth, they raise no dust, and people do not become satisfied even while looking at them.

children.text: kāyaprabhā suvipulā ca vibhāti teṣāṃ vācā manojña yatha nāsti ha mānuṣāṇām
children.translated_text: Their bodily radiance shines very widely, and their speech is charming in a way that does not belong to human beings.

children.text: gambhiraślakṣṇasuśilā ca suākarā ca śaṅkā hi me suragaṇā na hi te manuṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their voices are deep, smooth, well-mannered, and beautifully formed. I suspect that they are hosts of gods; they are not humans.

children.text: varapuṣpamālyaanulepanapaṭṭadāmā pāṇī gṛhītvana udīkṣiṣu gauraveṇa
children.translated_text: Holding excellent flowers, garlands, unguents, and silk bands in their hands, they look on with reverence.

children.text: niḥsaṃśayaṃ nṛpati draṣṭu kumāramete devādhideva marutāgata pūjanārtham ||
children.translated_text: Without doubt, O king, these divine overlords, <s>Maruts</s>, have come to see the prince for the purpose of worship."

children.text: rājā niśāmya vacanaṃ paramaṃ udagro gacchā bhaṇāhi praviśantu gṛhaṃ bhavantaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words, the king was supremely delighted: "Go, tell them, 'Let the venerable ones enter the house.'

children.text: na hi mānuṣāṇa iyamīdṛśa ṛddhi kāci yatha bhāṣase ca guṇa teṣa yathā ca iryā ||
children.translated_text: For human beings do not have any such supernormal power as this, as you describe their qualities and their bearing."

children.text: dauvārikaḥ kṛtapuṭo marutaivamāha praviśī bhavanta anujñātu narādhipena
children.translated_text: The gatekeeper, with folded hands, said this to the <s>Maruts</s>: "Enter, venerable ones; you have been permitted by the lord of men."

children.text: te hṛṣṭatuṣṭamanaso varamālyahastā gehaṃ praviṣṭa nṛpateramarālayaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: They, joyful and satisfied in mind, with excellent garlands in their hands, entered the king's house as if it were the abode of the immortals.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ suravarāṃ praviśanta gehaṃ pratyutthito nṛpatirañjali saṃpragṛhya
children.translated_text: Seeing those excellent gods entering the house, the king rose to meet them and respectfully joined his palms.

children.text: saṃvidyayanta ima āsana ratnapādā atrā niṣīdata bhavannanukampya buddhyā ||
children.translated_text: "Here are seats with jeweled feet, arranged for you. Sit here, venerable ones, with a compassionate mind."

children.text: te mānadarpavigatā sthita āsaneṣu yasyārthi āgata ihā nṛpate śṛṇuṣva
children.translated_text: They, free from pride and arrogance, remained on the seats. "Hear, O king, the purpose for which we have come here.

children.text: putrastavātipṛthupuṇyaviśuddhakāyo jātaḥ sujātacaraṇaṃ vaya draṣṭukāmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Your son, whose body is purified by exceedingly vast merit, has been born; we wish to see his well-born feet.

children.text: asmo vidhijña varalakṣaṇalakṣaṇajñā yeṣāṃ tathā bhavati yā gati yaḥ prayogaḥ
children.translated_text: We know the rule and know the marks of excellent marks, the destiny and the application that belong to those for whom they appear.

children.text: tatsādhu pārthivavara prajahasva khedaṃ paśyāma lakṣaṇavicitravibhūṣitāṅgam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, good best of kings, cast off your anxiety. Let us see his limbs adorned with the variegated marks."

children.text: sa strīgaṇaiḥ parivṛto nṛpatiḥ prahṛṣṭo gṛhya kumāramasamaṃ jvalanārcivarṇam
children.translated_text: Then the king, delighted and surrounded by groups of women, took the unequaled prince, whose color was like a blazing flame,

children.text: upanāmayan suravarāṃ suvilambacūḍāṃ dvārāttu niṣkramatu kampita trisahasrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and presented him to the excellent gods with beautifully hanging crests. As he came out through the doorway, the three-thousandfold world shook.

children.text: dṛṣṭvaiva te suravarā krama nāyakasya tāmrā nakhāṃ vimalapatraviśuddhatejā
children.translated_text: As soon as those excellent gods saw the feet of the leader, with copper-colored nails and a stainless radiance pure as petals,

children.text: te utthitā tvarita rūpavilambacūḍā mūrdhnābhivandiṣu kramāṃ vimalaprabhasya ||
children.translated_text: they rose swiftly, their beautiful crests hanging, and bowed with their heads to the feet of the one of stainless radiance.

children.text: yatha lakṣaṇā yatha ca darśita lakṣitā ca yatha puṇyateji śiri mūrdha vilokitaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Judging by the marks, by what was seen and recognized, by the splendor of merit, and by what was observed at his head and crown,

children.text: yatha irya netra vimalāprabha ūrṇakośā niḥsaṃśayaṃ spṛśati bodhi vijitya māram ||
children.translated_text: by his bearing, his eyes, and the stainless shining tuft of hair between his brows, without doubt he will touch awakening after conquering <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: te taṃ stuvanti guṇabhūta yathārthadarśī dhyāyī guṇāṃ vigatakleśatamonudasya
children.translated_text: They praise him, the embodiment of virtues, the one who sees reality, the meditator on the virtues of the dispeller of the darkness of defilements:

children.text: sucireṇa sattvaratanasya hi prādurbhāvo jātījarāmaraṇakleśaraṇaṃjahasya ||
children.translated_text: "After a long time the jewel among beings has appeared, one who abandons the wilderness of birth, old age, death, and affliction.

children.text: ādīpta sarvatribhavaṃ tribhiragnitaptaṃ saṃkalparāgaviṣayāraṇiucchritena
children.translated_text: The whole threefold existence is ablaze, scorched by the three fires, with the fire-drill of conceptual desire and sense-objects raised high;

children.text: tvaṃ dharmamegha trisahasra spharitva dhīrā amṛtodakena praśameṣyasi kleśatāpam ||
children.translated_text: You, steadfast one, having filled the three-thousandfold world with the cloud of <s>dharma</s> (teaching), will calm the burning heat of the afflictions with the water of immortality.

children.text: tvaṃ maitravākya karuṇānvita ślakṣṇavākya brahmasvarāracitaghoṣa manojñavāṇi
children.translated_text: You whose speech is loving, endowed with compassion, smooth in utterance, whose sound is fashioned with a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s, whose words are delightful,

children.text: trisahasra ājñaparivijñapanī jagasya kṣipraṃ pramuñca bhagavan mahabuddhaghoṣam ||
children.translated_text: quickly release, Blessed One, the great voice of the Buddha, which makes known its command to the three-thousandfold world.

children.text: bhagnā kutīrthikagaṇā viparītadṛṣṭiḥ bhavarāgabandhananimagna sthitā bhavāgre
children.translated_text: The hosts of heretical teachers, whose views are perverse, are broken; sunk in the bonds of craving for existence, they stand at the summit of becoming.

children.text: hetu pratītya bhava śūnya śruṇitva dharmā siṃhasya kroṣṭukagaṇaiva palāyināste ||
children.translated_text: When they have heard the teachings that existence arises dependent on causes and is empty, they flee like a pack of jackals before a lion.

children.text: bhittvā avidyapaṭalaṃ mahakleśadhūmaṃ paryutthitā janataye niyataprakāśe
children.translated_text: Having broken through the veil of ignorance and the great smoke of the afflictions that has risen up among the people, in certain illumination,

children.text: jñānārciprajñaprabhavidyuvilokitena sarvaṃ jage vidhamaye mahadandhakāram ||
children.translated_text: with the lightning-flash glance of the flame of knowledge and the radiance of wisdom, dispel the great darkness from the whole world.

children.text: lābhā sulabdha vipulā marumānuṣāṇāṃ yatrodbhavā 'dbhuta ihedṛśi śuddhasattve
children.translated_text: Great and fortunate gains have been obtained by gods and human beings, since such a wondrous pure being has arisen here.

children.text: pithitā apāyapatha sphīta marutpathāni bheṣyanti sattvaratanena vibodhakena ||
children.translated_text: The paths to the bad destinies are closed, and the roads of the gods will become abundant through this jewel among beings, the awakener.

children.text: varṣitva divyakusumāṃ kapilāhvaye 'smin kṛtvā pradakṣiṇa stavitva ca gauraveṇa
children.translated_text: Having showered divine flowers in this city called <s>Kapila</s>, and having circumambulated and praised him with reverence,

children.text: buddha subuddha iti vākyamudīrayantaḥ prakrānta te suragaṇā gagane salīlāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those hosts of gods, saying, 'The Buddha is well awakened,' departed playfully through the sky.

children.text: Chapter 8
iti hi bhikṣavo yāmeva rātriṃ bodhisattvo jātastasyāmeva rātryāṃ viṃśatikanyāsahasrāṇi kṣatriyabrāhmaṇanaigamagṛhapatimahāśālakuleṣu jātāḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed, monks, on the very night on which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was born, twenty thousand maidens were born in the great households of kṣatriyas, brahmins, townsmen, and householders.

children.text: tāśca sarvā mātāpitṛbhirbodhisattvāya dattā upasthānaparicaryāyai
children.translated_text: All of them were given by their mothers and fathers to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> for attendance and service.

children.text: viṃśati ca kanyāsahasrāṇi rājñā śuddhodanena dattāni bodhisattvasyopasthānaparicaryāyai
children.translated_text: And twenty thousand maidens were given by King <s>Śuddhodana</s> for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s attendance and service.

children.text: viṃśati ca kanyāsahasrāṇi mitrāmātyātmajñātisālohitair dattāni bodhisattvasyopasthānaparicaryāyai
children.translated_text: And twenty thousand maidens were given by friends, ministers, kinsmen, and blood-relatives for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s attendance and service.

children.text: viṃśati ca kanyāsahasrāṇi amātyapārṣadyairdattāni bodhisattvasyopasthānaparicaryāyai ||
children.translated_text: And twenty thousand maidens were given by the ministers and courtiers for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s attendance and service.

children.text: tadā ca bhikṣavo mahallakamahallikāḥ śākyāḥ saṃnipatya rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāhur yatkhalu deva jānīyāḥ devakulaṃ kumāra upanīyatāmiti
children.translated_text: Then, monks, the elder Śākyas, men and women, assembled, approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, and said this: 'Your Majesty should know this: let the prince be brought to the shrine.'

children.text: rājā āha sādhu upanīyatāṃ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: The king said, 'Good. Let the prince be brought there.

children.text: tena hi maṇḍyatāṃ nagaram
children.translated_text: In that case, let the city be adorned.

children.text: upaśobhyantāṃ vīthicatvaraśṛṅgāṭakāntarāpaṇarathyāmukhāni
children.translated_text: Let the streets, squares, crossroads, inner markets, and entrances to the roads be beautified.

children.text: apanīyantāmamaṅgalyāḥ kāṇakubjabadhirāndhamūkavisaṃsthitavirūparūpā aparipūrṇendriyāḥ
children.translated_text: Let inauspicious persons be removed: the one-eyed, hunchbacked, deaf, blind, mute, misshapen, ugly, and those with incomplete faculties.

children.text: upanāmyantāṃ maṅgalāni
children.translated_text: Let auspicious things be brought forward.

children.text: ghuṣyantāṃ puṇyabheryaḥ
children.translated_text: Let drums of merit be sounded.

children.text: tāḍyantāṃ maṅgalyaghaṇṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Let auspicious bells be struck.

children.text: samalaṃkriyantāṃ puravaradvārāṇi
children.translated_text: Let the gates of the excellent city be decorated.

children.text: vādyantāṃ sumanojñatūryatālāvacarāṇi
children.translated_text: Let very pleasing musical instruments, rhythms, and accompaniments be played.

children.text: saṃnipātyantāṃ sarvakoṭṭarājānaḥ
children.translated_text: Let all the kings of the forts be assembled.

children.text: ekībhavantu śreṣṭhigṛhapatyamātyadauvārikapāriṣadyāḥ
children.translated_text: Let merchants, householders, ministers, gatekeepers, and courtiers come together.

children.text: yujyantāṃ kanyārathāḥ
children.translated_text: Let the maidens' chariots be yoked.

children.text: upanāmyantāṃ pūrṇakumbhāḥ
children.translated_text: Let full jars be brought forward.

children.text: saṃnipātyantāmadhīyānā brāhmaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Let brahmins engaged in recitation be assembled.

children.text: alaṃkriyantāṃ devakulāni
children.translated_text: Let the shrines be adorned.'

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo yathoktapūrvaṃ sarvaṃ kṛtamabhūt ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, monks, everything was done just as had been said before.

children.text: tato rājā śuddhodanaḥ svagṛhaṃ praviśya mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīmāmantryaivamāha alaṃkriyantāṃ kumāraḥ devakulamupaneṣyata iti
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> entered his own residence, addressed <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>, and said this: 'Let the prince be adorned; he is to be brought to the shrine.'

children.text: sādhviti pratiśrutya mahāprajāpatī gautamī kumāraṃ maṇḍayati sma ||
children.translated_text: Replying, 'Very well,' <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> adorned the prince.

children.text: tataḥ kumāro maṇḍyamānaḥ prahasitavadano vyapagatabhṛkuṭikaḥ paramamadhurayā vācā mātṛsvasāramevamāha amba kutrāhamupaneṣyata iti
children.translated_text: Then, as the prince was being adorned, with a smiling face and without any frown, he said in a supremely sweet voice to his mother's sister, 'Mother, where am I to be taken?'

children.text: āha devakulaṃ putreti
children.translated_text: She said, 'To the shrine, my son.'

children.text: tataḥ kumāraḥ smitamupadarśayan prahasitavadano mātṛsvasāraṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Then the prince, showing a smile and with a laughing face, addressed his mother's sister in verses:

children.text: jātasya mahyamiha kampita trisahasraṃ śakraśca brahma asurāśca mahoragāśca
children.translated_text: At my birth this three-thousandfold world shook, and <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the asuras, and the great serpents,

children.text: candraśca sūrya tatha vaiśravaṇaḥ kumāro mūrdhnā krameṣu nipatitva namasyayanti ||
children.translated_text: the moon and the sun, and likewise <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> and <s>Kumāra</s>, fell with their heads at my feet and paid homage.

children.text: katamo 'nyu deva mama uttari yo viśiṣṭo yasmin mama praṇayase tvamihādya amba
children.translated_text: What other god, superior to me and more distinguished, is there, to whom you would lead me here today, mother?

children.text: devātideva ahu uttamu sarvadevaiḥ devo na me 'sti sadṛśaḥ kuta uttaraṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: I am the god beyond gods, highest among all gods; there is no god equal to me, much less one higher.

children.text: lokānuvartana pratī iti amba yāsye dṛṣtvā vikurvita mamā janatā udagrāḥ
children.translated_text: Still, mother, I shall go in conformity with the world. Seeing my miraculous display, the people will be uplifted.

children.text: adhimātru gaurava kariṣyati citrakāraḥ jñāsyanti devamanujā svaya devadevaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They will show extraordinary reverence and wonder; gods and humans will know that I myself am the god of gods.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ sarvairvarṇaiḥ stutimaṅgalaiḥ pratyupasthitairaparimitālaṃkārālaṃkṛteṣu vīthicatvaraśṛṅgāṭakāntarāpaṇamukheṣvantaḥpure kumārasya rathamalaṃkṛtya rājā śuddhodano brāhmaṇanaigamaśreṣṭhigṛhapatyamātyakoṭṭarājadauvārikapāriṣadyamitrajñātiparivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dhūpanadhūpitena muktapuṣpābhikīrṇena hayagajarathapattikalilenocchritachatradhvajapatākena nānātūryasaṃpravāditena mārgeṇa kumāraṃ gṛhītvā gacchati sma
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, while every kind of praise and auspicious acclaim was present, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> decorated the prince's chariot in the inner palace, amid streets, squares, crossroads, and market-entrances adorned with limitless ornaments; surrounded and preceded by brahmins, townsmen, merchants, householders, ministers, fortress-kings, gatekeepers, courtiers, friends, and kinsmen, he took the prince and proceeded along a road perfumed with incense, strewn with loose flowers, thronged with horses, elephants, chariots, and foot soldiers, with parasols, banners, and flags raised, and with many musical instruments sounding.

children.text: devatāśatasahasrāṇi bodhisattvasya rathaṃ vahanti sma
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of deities carried the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s chariot.

children.text: anekāni ca devaputrāpsaraḥkoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi gaganatalagatāni puṣpavarṣāṇyabhipravarṣanti sma
children.translated_text: And many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of crores of divine youths and apsarases, stationed in the expanse of the sky, rained down showers of flowers.

children.text: tūryāṇi ca pravādayanti sma
children.translated_text: And they played musical instruments.

children.text: iti hi rājā śuddhodano mahatā rājavyūhena mahatā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena kumāraṃ gṛhītvā devakulaṃ praviśati sma
children.translated_text: Thus King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, with a great royal array, great royal splendor, and great royal majesty, took the prince and entered the temple.

children.text: samanantarapratiṣṭhāpitaśca bodhisattvena dakṣiṇaścaraṇayoḥ kramatalastasmin devakule atha tā acetanyo devapratimāḥ tadyathā śivaskandanārāyaṇakuberacandrasūryavaiśravaṇaśakrabrahmalokapālaprabhṛtayaḥ pratimāḥ sarvāḥ svebhyaḥ svebhyaḥ sthānebhyo vyutthāya bodhisattvasya kramatalayornipatanti sma
children.translated_text: And as soon as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had set down the sole of his right foot in that temple, those insentient images of the gods, namely the images of <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Candra</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the guardians of the world, and the rest, all rose from their own places and fell at the soles of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet.

children.text: tatra devamanuṣyaśatasahasrāṇi hīhīkārakilakilāpramukhaiḥ prakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇi prāmuñcan
children.translated_text: There hundreds of thousands of gods and humans let forth hundreds of thousands of shouts, beginning with cries of "hī hī" and jubilant calls.

children.text: cailavikṣepāṇi cākārṣuḥ
children.translated_text: And they waved their garments about.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca kapilavastumahānagaraṃ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prākampitam
children.translated_text: And the entire great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> shook in six ways.

children.text: divyāni ca kusumāni prāvarṣan
children.translated_text: And divine flowers rained down.

children.text: tūryaśatasahasrāṇi cāghaṭṭitāni praṇeduḥ
children.translated_text: And hundreds of thousands of musical instruments, struck together, resounded.

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca devānāṃ tāḥ pratimās te sarve svasvarūpamupadarśyemā gāthā abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: And all the gods whose images those were displayed their own forms and spoke these verses:

children.text: no merū girirāja parvatavaro jātū name sarṣape no vā sāgara nāgarājanilayo jātū name goṣpade
children.translated_text: Mount <s>Meru</s>, the king of mountains, the best of peaks, would never bow to a mustard seed; nor would the ocean, abode of the nāga kings, ever bow to a cow's hoofprint.

children.text: candrāditya prabhaṃkarā prabhakarā khadyotake no name prajñāpuṇyakulodito guṇadharaḥ kasmānname devate ||
children.translated_text: The moon and sun, makers of radiance and light, do not bow to a firefly; why should the bearer of virtues, arisen from the lineage of wisdom and merit, bow to a deity?

children.text: yadvat sarṣapa goṣpade va salilaṃ khadyotakā vā bhavet evaṃ ca trisahasra devamanujā ye keci mānāśritāḥ
children.translated_text: As a mustard seed is, or water in a hoofprint, or fireflies might be, so are all those in the triple-thousand world, gods and humans, whoever are dependent on pride.

children.text: merūsāgaracandrasūryasadṛśo loke svayaṃbhūttamo yaṃ loko hyabhivandya lābha labhate svargaṃ tathā nirvṛtim ||
children.translated_text: He is like <s>Meru</s>, the ocean, the moon, and the sun, the supreme self-arisen one in the world; by worshiping him the world obtains gain, heaven, and also nirvāṇa.

children.text: asmin khalu punarbhikṣavo bodhisattvena mahāsattvena devakule praveśe saṃdarśyamāne dvātriṃśatāṃ devaputraśatasahasrāṇāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpadyante
children.translated_text: Moreover, monks, while this entrance of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being, into the temple was being displayed, the minds of thirty-two hundred thousand divine youths arose toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: ayaṃ bhikṣavo heturayaṃ pratyayo yenopekṣako bodhisattvo bhavati sma devakulamupanīyamāna iti ||
children.translated_text: This, monks, was the cause and this the condition by which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> remained calmly observant when he was being brought to the temple.

children.text: Chapter 9

atha khalu bhikṣava udayano nāma brāhmaṇo rājñaḥ purohita udāyinaḥ pitā sa pañcamātrairbrāhmaṇaśataiḥ parivṛto hastottare citrānakṣatre rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāha yatkhalu devo jānīyādābharaṇāni kumārāya kriyantāmiti
children.translated_text: Then, monks, a brahmin named <s>Udayana</s>, the king's purohita and the father of <s>Udāyin</s>, surrounded by five hundred brahmins, approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> under the <s>Hastottara</s> and <s>Citrā</s> lunar mansions and said this: "Your Majesty should know: ornaments are to be made for the prince."

children.text: taṃ rājā āha bāḍham
children.translated_text: The king said to him, "Very well."

children.text: gāḍhaṃ kriyatāmiti ||
children.translated_text: "Let them be made firmly," he said.

children.text: tatra rājñā śuddhodanena pañcamātraiśca śākyaśataiḥ pañcamātrāṇyābharaṇaśatāni kāritānyabhūvan
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and five hundred <s>Śākyas</s> had five hundred sets of ornaments made.

children.text: tadyathā hastābharaṇāni pādābharaṇāni mūrdhābharaṇāni kaṇṭhābharaṇāni mudrikābharaṇāni karṇikāyākeyūrāṇi mekhalāsuvarṇasūtrāṇi kiṅkiṇījālāni ratnajālāni maṇipratyuptāni pādukā nānāratnasamalaṃkṛtā hārāḥ kaṭakā harṣā mukuṭāni
children.translated_text: They were as follows: hand ornaments, foot ornaments, head ornaments, neck ornaments, rings, earrings, armlets, girdles, golden cords, networks of tinkling bells, jewel nets, sandals inlaid with gems and adorned with various jewels, necklaces, bracelets, ornaments, and crowns.

children.text: kārayitvā ca puṣyanakṣatrayogenānuyuktena te śākyā rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāhur hanta deva maṇḍyatāṃ kumāra iti
children.translated_text: Having had them made at a suitable conjunction with the <s>Puṣya</s> lunar mansion, those <s>Śākyas</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said this: "Come, lord, let the prince be adorned."

children.text: rājā āha alamalaṃkṛtaśca pūjitaśca bhavadbhiḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: The king said, "The prince has already been adorned and honored by you.

children.text: mayāpi kumārasya sarvābharaṇāni kāritāni
children.translated_text: I too have had all the ornaments made for the prince."

children.text: te 'vocan saptasaptarātriṃdivānyapyasmākamābharaṇāni kumāraḥ kāya ābadhnātu
children.translated_text: They said, "For seven days and seven nights at least, let the prince fasten our ornaments upon his body.

children.text: tato 'smākamamogho vyāyāmo bhaviṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Then our effort will not have been fruitless."

children.text: tatra rātrau vinirgatāyāmāditya udite vimalavyūhanāmodyānaṃ tatra bodhisattvo nirgato 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Then, when the night had passed and the sun had risen, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had gone out into the park named <s>Vimalavyūha</s>.

children.text: tatra mahāprajāpatyā gautamyā bodhisattvo 'ṅke gṛhīto 'bhūt
children.translated_text: There the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was taken on the lap of <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>.

children.text: aśītiśca strīsahasrāṇi pratyudgamya bodhisattvasya vadanaṃ prekṣante sma
children.translated_text: And eighty thousand women came forward and looked at the face of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: daśa ca kanyāsahasrāṇi pratyudgamya bodhisattvasya vadanaṃ prekṣante sma
children.translated_text: And ten thousand maidens came forward and looked at the face of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: pañca ca brāhmaṇasahasrāṇi pratyudgamya bodhisattvasya vadanaṃ prekṣante sma
children.translated_text: And five thousand brahmins came forward and looked at the face of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: tatra yāni bhadrikeṇa śākyarājenābharaṇāni kāritānyabhūvan tāni bodhisattvasya kāye ābadhyante sma
children.translated_text: There the ornaments that the <s>Śākya</s> king <s>Bhadrika</s> had caused to be made were fastened upon the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: tāni samanantarābaddhāni bodhisattvasya kāyaprabhayā jihmīkṛtānyabhūvan na bhāsante sma na tapanti sma na virocanti sma
children.translated_text: As soon as they were fastened, they were made dull by the radiance of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body; they did not shine, did not glow, and did not gleam.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma jāmbūnadasya suvarṇasya purato masipiṇḍa upanikṣipto na bhāsati na tapati na virocate evameva tānyābharaṇāni bodhisattvasya kāyaprabhayā spṛṣṭāni na bhāsante na tapanti na virocante sma
children.translated_text: Just as a lump of soot placed before gold from the <s>Jambu</s> river does not shine, does not glow, and does not gleam, so too those ornaments, touched by the radiance of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body, did not shine, did not glow, and did not gleam.

children.text: evaṃ yā yā ābharaṇavikṛtirbodhisattvasya kāya ābadhyate sma sā sā jihmībhavati sma tadyathāpi nāma masipiṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, whatever variety of ornament was fastened upon the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, each became dull, just like a lump of soot.

children.text: tatra vimalā nāmodyānadevatā sā audārikam ātmabhāvam abhisaṃdarśya purataḥ sthitvā rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ taṃ ca mahāntaṃ śākyagaṇaṃ gāthābhirabhibhāṣate sma ||
children.translated_text: There a garden deity named <s>Vimalā</s> displayed a visible, corporeal form, stood before King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and that great assembly of <s>Śākyas</s>, and addressed them in verses.

children.text: sarveyaṃ trisahasra medinī sanagaranigamā pūrṇā kāñcanasaṃcitā bhavet surucira vimalā
children.translated_text: If this whole three-thousandfold earth, together with its cities and market-towns, were filled with heaps of beautiful, pure gold,

children.text: ekā kākiṇi jāmbukāñcane bhavati upahatā nā bhāsī itaraḥ sa kāñcana prabhasirirahitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and if even a single small coin of <s>Jambu</s>-gold were placed there, the other gold would not shine; that gold would be bereft of brilliance.

children.text: jāmbūkāñcanasaṃnibhā punarbhavet sakara iya mahī rome ābha pramukta nāyake hirisiribharite
children.translated_text: Again, if this earth with its mountains became like <s>Jambu</s>-gold, yet when a ray was released from a hair of the leader, filled with glory and splendor,

children.text: nā bhāsī na tapī na śobhate na ca prabhavati ābhāye sugatasya kāyi no bhavati yatha masiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it would not shine, blaze, or appear beautiful; in the radiance of the <s>Sugata</s>'s body it would be like ink.

children.text: sve tejena ayaṃ svalaṃkṛto guṇaśatabharito no tasyābharaṇā virociṣū suvimalavapuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: He is adorned by his own splendor and filled with hundreds of qualities; ornaments do not shine on that body of perfectly pure form.

children.text: candrasūryaprabhāśca jyotiṣā tatha maṇijvalanāḥ śakrabahmaprabhā na bhāsate purata śirighane ||
children.translated_text: The lights of the moon and sun, the flames of jewels, and the radiance of <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> do not shine before that mass of glory.

children.text: yasyā lakṣaṇi kāyu citritaḥ purimaśubhaphalaiḥ kiṃ tasyābharaṇebhiritvaraiḥ parakṛtakaraṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Since his body is adorned with marks produced by former wholesome fruits, what need has he of ornaments, temporary and fashioned by others?

children.text: apanethā bharaṇā ma heṭhatā abudha budhakaraṃ nāyaṃ kṛttimabhūṣaṇārthika paramamatikaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Take away the ornaments; do not dishonor him, foolish ones. This maker of awakening, this supremely wise one, has no need of artificial adornment.

children.text: ceṭasyābharaṇāni dethime surucira vimalā sahajāto ya subhūṣi chandako nṛpatikulaśubhe
children.translated_text: Give these ornaments to the attendants, beautiful and pure. Let <s>Chandaka</s>, his excellently adorned companion born together with him, have them, O auspicious royal house.

children.text: tuṣṭā śākiya vismitāśca abhavanpramuditamanaso vṛddhiḥ śākyakulanandasya cottamā bhaviṣyati vipulā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Śākyas</s> became pleased, amazed, and joyful in mind: 'The increase of the joy of the <s>Śākya</s> family will be supreme and vast.'

children.text: ityuktvā sā devatā bodhisattvaṃ divyaiḥ puṣpairabhyavakīrya tatraivāntaradhāt ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that deity scattered divine flowers over the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and disappeared on the spot.

children.text: Chapter 10
iti hi bhikṣavaḥ saṃvṛddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, the prince grew up.

children.text: tadā māṅgalyaśatasahasraiḥ lipiśālām upanīyate sma daśabhirdārakasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ daśabhiśca rathasahasraiḥ khādanīyabhojanīyasvādanīyaparipūrṇair hiraṇyasuvarṇaparipūrṇaiśca
children.translated_text: Then, with hundreds of thousands of auspicious rites, he was led to the writing school, surrounded and preceded by ten thousand boys and by ten thousand chariots filled with things to eat, foods, delicacies, and with gold and bullion.

children.text: yena kapilavastuni mahānagare vīthicatvararathyāntarāpaṇamukheṣv abhyavakīryate sma abhiviśrāmyante
children.translated_text: These were scattered and distributed in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the streets, squares, lanes, and at the entrances to the shops.

children.text: aṣṭābhiśca tūryaśatasahasraiḥ praghuṣyamāṇairmahatā ca puṣpavarṣeṇābhipravarṣatā vitardiniryūhatoraṇagavākṣaharmyakūṭāgāraprāsādataleṣu kanyāśatasahasrāṇi sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitāḥ sthitā abhūvan
children.translated_text: With eight hundred thousand musical instruments resounding and a great rain of flowers falling, hundreds of thousands of girls, adorned with every ornament, stood on platforms, balconies, gateways, windows, mansions, roof-pavilions, and palace terraces.

children.text: bodhisattvaṃ prekṣamāṇāḥ kusumāni ca kṣipanti sma
children.translated_text: They gazed at the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and threw flowers.

children.text: aṣṭau ca marutkanyāsahasrāṇi vigalitālaṃkārābharaṇālaṃkṛtāni ratnabhadraṃkareṇa gṛhītāni mārgaṃ śodhayantyo bodhisattvasya purato gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: Eight thousand daughters of the <s>Maruts</s>, adorned with loosened ornaments and holding auspicious jewels in their hands, went before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, clearing the road.

children.text: devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāś cārdhakāyikā gaganatalātpuṣpapaṭṭadāmānyabhipralambayanti sma
children.translated_text: Gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, showing half their bodies from the sky, hung down flower-banners and garlands.

children.text: sarve ca śākyagaṇāḥ śuddhodanaṃ rājānaṃ puraskṛtya bodhisattvasya purato gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: And all the <s>Śākya</s> assembly, with King <s>Śuddhodana</s> at their head, went before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: anenaivaṃrūpeṇa vyūhena bodhisattvo lipiśālāmupanīyate sma ||
children.translated_text: With just such an array the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was led to the writing school.

children.text: samanantarapraveśitaśca bodhisattvo lipiśālām
children.translated_text: Immediately after the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had entered the writing school,

children.text: atha viśvāmitro nāma dārakācāryo bodhisattvasya śriyaṃ tejaścāsahamāno dharaṇitale niviṣṭo 'dhomukhaḥ prapatati sma
children.translated_text: the boys' teacher named <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, unable to endure the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s glory and splendor, sank down on the ground and fell face downward.

children.text: taṃ tathā prapatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā śubhāṅgo nāma tuṣitakāyiko devaputro dakṣiṇena karatalena parigṛhyotthāpayati sma
children.translated_text: Seeing him fallen in that way, a divine son of the <s>Tuṣita</s> realm named <s>Śubhāṅga</s> took him by the palm of his right hand and raised him up.

children.text: utthāpya ca gaganatalastho rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ taṃ ca mahāntaṃ janakāyaṃ gāthābhirabhyabhāṣat ||
children.translated_text: After raising him, he stood in the sky and addressed King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and that great multitude in verses.

children.text: śāstrāṇi yāni pracalanti manuṣyaloke saṃkhyā lipiśca gaṇanāpi ca dhātutantram
children.translated_text: The sciences that circulate in the human world, numeration, writing, calculation, and the science of verbal elements,

children.text: ye śilpayoga pṛthu laukika aprameyāḥ teṣveṣu śikṣitu purā bahukalpakoṭyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the many immeasurable worldly arts and disciplines: in all these he was trained long ago, for many crores of kalpas.

children.text: kiṃ tū janasya anuvartanatāṃ karoti lipiśālamāgatu suśikṣitu śiṣyaṇārtham
children.translated_text: But he acts in conformity with people; well trained already, he has come to the writing school for the sake of being a pupil,

children.text: paripācanārtha bahudāraka agrayāne anyāṃśca sattvanayutānamṛte vinetum ||
children.translated_text: in order to ripen many children in the supreme vehicle and to lead many other nayutas of beings to immortality.

children.text: lokottareṣu catusatyapathe vidhijño hetupratītyakuśalo yatha saṃbhavanti
children.translated_text: He is skilled in the path of the four truths, which are supramundane, and skilled in causes and dependent origination, just as they come to be;

children.text: yatha cānirodhakṣayu saṃsthitu śītibhāvaḥ tasminvidhijña kimatho lipiśāstramātre ||
children.translated_text: and he is skilled in cessation, destruction, abiding, and cooling. Since he is skilled in that, what need is there to speak of the mere science of writing?

children.text: netasya ācariya uttari vā triloke sarveṣu devamanujeṣvayameva jeṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: He has no teacher higher than himself in the three worlds; among all gods and humans he himself is the foremost.

children.text: nāmāpi teṣa lipināṃ na hi vittha yūyaṃ yatreṣu śikṣitu purā bahukalpakoṭyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You do not even know the names of those scripts in which he was trained long ago, for many crores of kalpas.

children.text: so cittadhāra jagatāṃ vividhā vicitrā ekakṣaṇena ayu jānati śuddhasattvaḥ
children.translated_text: This pure being knows in a single instant the varied and manifold streams of thought of the world.

children.text: adṛśyarūparahitasya gatiṃ ca vetti kiṃ vā puno 'tha lipino 'kṣaradṛśyarūpām ||
children.translated_text: He knows the course of what is invisible, formless, and without appearance; how much more, then, the visible forms of letters?

children.text: ityuktvā sa devaputro bodhisattvaṃ divyaiḥ kusumairabhyarcya tatraivāntardadhe
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that divine son honored the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with divine flowers and disappeared on the spot.

children.text: tatra dhātryaśca ceṭīvargāśca sthāpitā abhūvan
children.translated_text: There the nurses and groups of maidservants remained stationed.

children.text: pariśeṣāḥ śākyāḥ śuddhodanapramukhāḥ prakrāmantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The remaining <s>Śākyas</s>, with <s>Śuddhodana</s> at their head, departed.

children.text: atha bodhisattva uragasāracandanamayaṃ lipiphalakamādāya divyārṣasuvarṇatirakaṃ samantānmaṇiratnapratyuptaṃ viśvāmitramācāryamevamāha katamāṃ me bho upādhyāya lipiṃ śikṣāpayasi
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, taking up a writing tablet made of uragasāra sandalwood, with a divine golden stylus, inlaid all around with jewel-gems, addressed the teacher <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and said, 'Venerable preceptor, which script will you teach me?'

children.text: brāhmīkharoṣṭīpuṣkarasāriṃ aṅgalipiṃ vaṅgalipiṃ magadhalipiṃ maṅgalyalipiṃ aṅgulīyalipiṃ śakārilipiṃ brahmavalilipiṃ pāruṣyalipiṃ drāviḍalipiṃ kirātalipiṃ dākṣiṇyalipiṃ ugralipiṃ saṃkhyālipiṃ anulomalipiṃ avamūrdhalipiṃ daradalipiṃ khāṣyalipiṃ cīnalipiṃ lūnalipiṃ hūṇalipiṃ madhyākṣaravistaralipiṃ puṣpalipiṃ devalipiṃ nāgalipiṃ yakṣalipiṃ gandharvalipiṃ kinnaralipiṃ mahoragalipiṃ asuralipiṃ garuḍalipiṃ mṛgacakralipiṃ vāyasarutalipiṃ bhaumadevalipiṃ antarīkṣadevalipiṃ uttarakurudvīpalipiṃ aparagoḍānīlipiṃ pūrvavidehalipiṃ utkṣepalipiṃ nikṣepalipiṃ vikṣepalipiṃ prakṣepalipiṃ sāgaralipiṃ vajralipiṃ lekhapratilekhalipiṃ anudrutalipiṃ śāstrāvartāṃ gaṇanāvartalipiṃ utkṣepāvartalipiṃ nikṣepāvartalipiṃ pādalikhitalipiṃ dviruttarapadasaṃdhilipiṃ yāvaddaśottarapadasaṃdhilipiṃ madhyāhāriṇīlipiṃ sarvarutasaṃgrahaṇīlipiṃ vidyānulomāvimiśritalipiṃ ṛṣitapastaptāṃ rocamānāṃ dharaṇīprekṣiṇīlipiṃ gaganaprekṣiṇīlipiṃ sarvauṣadhiniṣyandāṃ sarvasārasaṃgrahaṇīṃ sarvabhūtarutagrahaṇīm
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Kharoṣṭī</s>, and <s>Puṣkarasāri</s> scripts; the Aṅga script, Vaṅga script, Magadha script, Maṅgalya script, Aṅgulīya script, Śakāri script, Brahmavali script, Pāruṣya script, Drāviḍa script, Kirāta script, Dākṣiṇya script, Ugra script, Saṃkhyā script, Anuloma script, Avamūrdha script, Darada script, Khāṣya script, Cīna script, Lūna script, Hūṇa script, the script of expanded middle syllables, the flower script, the deva script, nāga script, yakṣa script, gandharva script, kinnara script, mahoraga script, asura script, garuḍa script, deer-circle script, crow-call script, earth-deva script, sky-deva script, Uttarakuru-continent script, Aparagoḍānī script, Pūrvavideha script, raising script, lowering script, scattering script, projecting script, ocean script, vajra script, writing-and-counterwriting script, swift-running script, śāstra-turning and calculation-turning script, raising-turning script, lowering-turning script, foot-written script, script of twofold and further word-combination, up to the script of tenfold and further word-combination, middle-taking script, script that gathers all sounds, script mixed in accordance with vidyā, the script delighted in by sages who have heated themselves with austerities, earth-gazing script, sky-gazing script, script that pours forth all medicines, script that gathers every essence, and script that grasps the sounds of all beings.

children.text: āsāṃ bho upādhyāya catuṣṣaṣṭīlipīnāṃ katamāṃ tvaṃ śikṣāpayiṣyasi
children.translated_text: Of these sixty-four scripts, venerable preceptor, which one will you teach me?

children.text: atha viśvāmitro dārakācāryo vismitaḥ prahasitavadano nihatamānamadadarpa imāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, the children's teacher, amazed, with a smiling face and with pride, intoxication, and arrogance cast down, spoke these verses:

children.text: āścaryaṃ śuddhasattvasya loke lokānuvartino
children.translated_text: Wonderful is this pure being, who in the world conforms to the ways of the world;

children.text: śikṣitaḥ sarvaśāstreṣu lipiśālāmupāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: trained in all the śāstras (sciences), he has come to the writing school.

children.text: yeṣāmahaṃ nāmadheyaṃ lipīnāṃ na prajānami
children.translated_text: Those scripts whose very names I do not know,

children.text: tatraiṣa śikṣitaḥ santo lipiśālāmupāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: in those this good one is trained, and has come to the writing school.

children.text: vaktraṃ cāsya na paśyāmi mūrdhānaṃ tasya naiva ca
children.translated_text: I do not behold his face, nor indeed his head;

children.text: śiṣyayiṣye kathaṃ hyenaṃ lipiprajñāya pāragam ||
children.translated_text: for how shall I teach him, one who has gone to the far shore of knowledge of scripts?

children.text: devadevo hyatidevaḥ sarvadevottamo vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: For he is the god of gods, beyond the gods, the lord, highest of all gods;

children.text: asamaśca viśiṣṭaśca lokeṣvapratipudgalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is unequaled and distinguished, without counterpart in the worlds.

children.text: asyaiva tvanubhāvena prajñopāye viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Yet through his own power, especially in wisdom and skillful means,

children.text: śikṣitaṃ śiṣyayiṣyāmi sarvalokaparāyaṇam ||
children.translated_text: I shall teach this trained one, the refuge of all the world, as my pupil.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo daśa dārakasahasrāṇi bodhisattvena sārdhaṃ lipiṃ śiṣyante sma
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, ten thousand boys learned writing together with the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: tatra bodhisattvādhisthānena teṣāṃ dārakāṇāṃ mātṛkāṃ vācayatāṃ yadā akāraṃ parikīrtayanti sma tadā anityaḥ sarvasaṃskāraśabdo niścarati sma
children.translated_text: There, through the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s empowerment, when those boys, reciting the alphabet, uttered the letter a, the sound 'all conditioned things are impermanent' came forth.

children.text: ākāre parikīrtyamāne ātmaparahitaśabdo niścarati sma
children.translated_text: When the letter ā was uttered, the sound 'benefit for oneself and others' came forth.

children.text: ikāre indriyavaikalyaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter i, there was the sound 'impairment of the faculties.'

children.text: īkāre ītibahulaṃ jagaditi
children.translated_text: At the letter ī, there was the sound, 'the world is full of calamities.'

children.text: ukāre upadravabahulaṃ jagaditi
children.translated_text: At the letter u, there was the sound, 'the world is full of troubles.'

children.text: ūkāre ūnasattvaṃ jagaditi
children.translated_text: At the letter ū, there was the sound, 'the world is deficient in beings.'

children.text: ekāre eṣaṇāsamutthānadoṣaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter e, there was the sound 'the fault arising from cravings.'

children.text: aikāre airyāpathaḥ śreyāniti
children.translated_text: At the letter ai, there was the sound, 'proper deportment is better.'

children.text: okāre oghottaraśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter o, there was the sound 'crossing beyond the flood.'

children.text: aukāre aupapādukaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter au, there was the sound 'spontaneously born.'

children.text: aṃkāre amoghotpattiśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter aṃ, there was the sound 'birth is not in vain.'

children.text: aḥkāre astaṃgamanaśabdo niścarati sma
children.translated_text: At the letter aḥ, the sound 'setting, passing away' came forth.

children.text: kakāre karmavipākāvatāraśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ka, there was the sound 'entry into the ripening of karma.'

children.text: khakāre khasamasarvadharmaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter kha, there was the sound 'all dharmas are equal to space.'

children.text: gakāre gambhīradharmapratītyasamutpādāvatāraśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ga, there was the sound 'entry into the profound dharma of dependent origination.'

children.text: ghakāre ghanapaṭalāvidyāmohāndhakāravidhamanaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter gha, there was the sound 'dispelling the thick mass of the darkness of ignorance, delusion, and blindness.'

children.text: ṅakāre 'ṅgaviśuddhiśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ṅa, there was the sound 'purification of the limbs.'

children.text: cakāre caturāryasatyaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ca, there was the sound 'the four noble truths.'

children.text: chakāre chandarāgaprahāṇaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter cha, there was the sound 'abandonment of desire and passion.'

children.text: jakāre jarāmaraṇasamatikramaṇaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ja, there was the sound 'passing beyond old age and death.'

children.text: jhakāre jhaṣadhvajabalanigrahaṇaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter jha, there was the sound 'subduing the power of the fish-bannered one.'

children.text: ñakāre jñāpanaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ña, there was the sound 'making known.'

children.text: ṭakāre paṭopacchedanaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ṭa, there was the sound 'cutting off the covering.'

children.text: ṭhakāre ṭhapanīyapraśnaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ṭha, there was the sound 'questions to be set aside.'

children.text: ḍakāre ḍamaramāranigrahaṇaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ḍa, there was the sound 'subduing <s>Ḍamara Māra</s>.'

children.text: ḍhakāre mīḍhaviṣayā iti
children.translated_text: At the letter ḍha, there was the sound, 'the objects are defiled.'

children.text: ṇakāre reṇukleśā iti
children.translated_text: At the letter ṇa, there was the sound, 'the afflictions are dust.'

children.text: takāre tathatāsaṃbhedaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ta, there was the sound 'the non-difference of suchness.'

children.text: thakāre thāmabalavegavaiśāradyaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter tha, there was the sound 'strength, power, force, and fearlessness.'

children.text: dakāre dānadamasaṃyamasaurabhyaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter da, there was the sound 'the fragrance of giving, restraint, and self-control.'

children.text: dhakāre dhanamāryāṇāṃ saptavidhamiti
children.translated_text: At the letter dha, there was the sound, 'the wealth of the noble ones is sevenfold.'

children.text: nakāre nāmarūpaparijñāśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter na, there was the sound 'full knowledge of name-and-form.'

children.text: pakāre paramārthaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter pa, there was the sound 'the ultimate meaning.'

children.text: phakāre phalaprāptisākṣātkriyāśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter pha, there was the sound 'direct realization of the attainment of the fruit.'

children.text: bakāre bandhanamokṣaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ba, there was the sound 'liberation from bondage.'

children.text: bhakāre bhavavibhavaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter bha, there was the sound 'becoming and non-becoming.'

children.text: makāre madamānopaśamanaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ma, there was the sound 'pacification of intoxication and pride.'

children.text: yakāre yathāvaddharmaprativedhaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ya, there was the sound 'realization of dharma just as it is.'

children.text: rakāre ratyaratiparamārtharatiśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ra, there was the sound 'delight, non-delight, and delight in the supreme reality.'

children.text: lakāre latāchedanaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter la, there was the sound 'cutting the creeper.'

children.text: vakāre varayānaśabdaḥ
