children.translated_text: At the letter va, there was the sound 'the excellent vehicle.'

children.text: śakāre śamathavipaśyanāśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter śa, there was the sound 'calm abiding and insight.'

children.text: ṣakāre ṣaḍāyatananigrahaṇābhijñajñānāvāptiśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ṣa, there was the sound 'attainment of higher knowledge and gnosis that restrains the six sense-bases.'

children.text: sakāre sarvajñajñānābhisaṃbodhanaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter sa, there was the sound 'awakening to omniscient knowledge.'

children.text: hakāre hatakleśavirāgaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: At the letter ha, there was the sound 'destruction of the afflictions and dispassion.'

children.text: kṣakāre parikīrtyamāne kṣaṇaparyantābhilāpyasarvadharmaśabdo niścarati sma ||
children.translated_text: When the letter kṣa was uttered, the sound 'all dharmas are expressible only up to the limit of a moment' came forth.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavasteṣāṃ dārakāṇāṃ mātṛkāṃ vācayatāṃ bodhisattvānubhāvenaiva pramukhānyasaṃkhyeyāni dharmamukhaśatasahasrāṇi niścaranti sma ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, while those boys were reciting the alphabet, through the power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone, foremost among them, innumerable hundreds of thousands of gateways to the <s>dharma</s> (teaching) issued forth.

children.text: tadānupūrveṇa bodhisattvena lipiśālāsthitena dvātriṃśaddārakasahasrāṇi paripācitānyabhūvan
children.translated_text: Then, in due order, while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was staying in the writing school, thirty-two thousand boys were brought to maturity.

children.text: anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpāditāni dvātriṃśaddārikāsahasrāṇi
children.translated_text: And thirty-two thousand girls generated thoughts directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: ayaṃ heturayaṃ pratyayo yacchikṣito 'pi bodhisattvo lipiśālāmupāgacchati sma ||
children.translated_text: This was the cause, this the condition, by which the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, although already educated, came to the writing school.

children.text: Chapter 11
iti hi bhikṣavo yāvadvivṛddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, the prince grew older.

children.text: athāpareṇa samayena kumārastadanyaiḥ kumārairamātyaputraiḥ sārdhaṃ kṛṣigrāmam avalokayituṃ gacchati sma
children.translated_text: Then, at another time, the prince went together with other princes, the sons of ministers, to inspect a farming village.

children.text: avalokya ca kṛṣikarmāntamanyata udyānabhūmiṃ praviśati sma
children.translated_text: After seeing the work of farming, he entered a garden ground elsewhere.

children.text: saṃvignamanāstatra bodhisattva ekākī advitīyo 'nucaṅkramyamāṇo 'nuvicaran jambuvṛkṣamapaśyat prāsādikaṃ darśanīyam
children.translated_text: There the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his mind stirred, walking and wandering alone, without a companion, saw a <s>jambu</s> tree, graceful and lovely to see.

children.text: tatra bodhisattvaśchāyāyāṃ paryaṅkena niṣīdati sma
children.translated_text: There the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sat down cross-legged in its shade.

children.text: niṣaṇṇaśca bodhisattvaścittaikāgratām āsādayati sma
children.translated_text: And once seated, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attained one-pointedness of mind.

children.text: āsādya ca viviktaṃ kāmairviviktaṃ pāpakairakuśalairdharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati sma
children.translated_text: Having attained it, secluded from desires and secluded from evil unwholesome factors, with applied thought and sustained thought, with joy and happiness born of seclusion, he entered and remained in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption).

children.text: sa vitarkavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamādadhyātmasaṃprasādāccetasa ekotibhāvād avitarkamavicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati sma
children.translated_text: With the calming of applied and sustained thought, from inner serenity and the unification of mind, without applied thought and without sustained thought, with joy and happiness born of samādhi, he entered and remained in the second <s>dhyāna</s>.

children.text: sa prītervirāgādupekṣako viharati sma smṛtimān samprajānan
children.translated_text: With the fading of joy, he dwelt equanimous, mindful, and clearly aware.

children.text: sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisaṃvedayati sma
children.translated_text: And he experienced happiness with the body.

children.text: yattadāryā ācakṣate upekṣakaḥ smṛtimān sukhavihārī niṣprītikaṃ tṛtīyaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati sma
children.translated_text: He entered and remained in that which the noble ones call the third <s>dhyāna</s>: equanimous, mindful, dwelling happily, and free from joy.

children.text: sa sukhasya ca prahāṇādduḥkhasya ca prahāṇāt pūrvameva ca saumanasyadaurmanasyayor astaṃgamād aduḥkhāsukham upekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati sma ||
children.translated_text: With the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of suffering, and with the earlier passing away of gladness and dejection, he entered and remained in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, neither painful nor pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness.

children.text: tena ca samayena pañca ṛṣayo bāhyāḥ pañcābhijñāḥ ṛddhimanto vihāyasaṃgamā dakṣiṇāyā diśa uttarāṃ diśaṃ gacchanti sma
children.translated_text: At that time five outside seers, possessing the five higher knowledges, endowed with miraculous power and traveling through the sky, were going from the southern direction toward the northern direction.

children.text: te tasya vanakhaṇḍasyopari gacchantaḥ pratyāhatā iva na śaknuvanti sma gantum
children.translated_text: As they were passing above that grove, they were as if struck back, and could not go on.

children.text: te saṃvignaromakūpajātā imāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta ||
children.translated_text: With the pores of their bodies bristling in alarm, they spoke this verse:

children.text: vayamiha maṇivajrakūṭaṃ giriṃ merumabhyudgataṃ tiryagatyarthavaistārikaṃ gaja iva sahakāraśākhākulāṃ vṛkṣavṛndāṃ pradāritva nirdhāvitānekaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Here we have repeatedly rushed on after splitting through Mount <s>Maṇivajrakūṭa</s> and lofty Mount <s>Meru</s>, broad beyond measure across, and through masses of trees dense with mango branches, like an elephant.

children.text: vayamiha marūṇāṃ pure cāpyasaktā gatā yakṣagandharvaveśmani cordhvaṃ nabhe niśritā ima puna vanakhaṇḍamāsādya sīdāma bhoḥ kasya lakṣmī nivarteti ṛddherbalam ||
children.translated_text: Here we have gone unhindered even in the city of the gods and in the abodes of <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Gandharvas</s>, resting high in the sky; but now, having reached this grove, we sink down, sir. Whose majesty turns back the power of our miraculous ability?

children.text: atha yā tatra vanakhaṇḍadevatā sā tānṛṣīn gāthayādhyabhāṣat ||
children.translated_text: Then the deity of that grove addressed those seers with a verse:

children.text: nṛpatipatikuloditaḥ śākyarājātmajo bālasūryaprakāśaprabhaḥ sphuṭitakamalagarbhavarṇaprabhaś cārucandrānano lokajyeṣṭho viduḥ
children.translated_text: Born from the family of a lord among kings, the son of the <s>Śākya</s> king, with a radiance like the light of the young sun, with a color and splendor like the heart of an opened lotus, with a lovely moon-like face, he is known as foremost in the world.

children.text: ayamiha vanamāśrito dhyānacintāparo devagandharvanāgendrayakṣārcito bhavaśataguṇakoṭisaṃvardhitastasya lakṣmī nivarteti ṛddherbalam ||
children.translated_text: He has resorted to this forest, intent on meditative reflection, honored by gods, <s>Gandharvas</s>, lords of <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Yakṣas</s>; strengthened through hundreds of births and koṭis of virtues, his majesty turns back the power of miraculous ability.

children.text: tataste 'dhastādavalokayanto 'drākṣuḥ kumāraṃ śriyā tejasā ca jājvalyamānam
children.translated_text: Then, looking downward, they saw the prince blazing with beauty and majesty.

children.text: teṣāmetadabhūt ko nvayaṃ niṣaṇṇo mā haiva vaiśravaṇo dhanādhipatirbhavet
children.translated_text: This occurred to them: Who is this seated here? Could it be <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, lord of wealth?

children.text: āhosvinmāraḥ kāmādhipatiḥ
children.translated_text: Or perhaps <s>Māra</s>, lord of desire?

children.text: atha mahoragendraḥ
children.translated_text: Or the great lord of serpents?

children.text: athendro vajradharaḥ
children.translated_text: Or <s>Indra</s>, bearer of the thunderbolt?

children.text: atha rudraḥ kumbhāṇḍādhipatiḥ
children.translated_text: Or <s>Rudra</s>, lord of the <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>?

children.text: atha kṛṣṇo mahotsāhaḥ
children.translated_text: Or <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, of great energy?

children.text: uta candro devaputraḥ
children.translated_text: Or <s>Candra</s>, son of the gods?

children.text: uta sūryaḥ sahasraraśmiḥ
children.translated_text: Or <s>Sūrya</s>, the thousand-rayed?

children.text: uta rājā cakravartī bhaviṣyati tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta ||
children.translated_text: Or will he become a wheel-turning king? At that moment they spoke this verse:

children.text: rūpaṃ vaiśravaṇātirekavapuṣaṃ vyaktaṃ kubero hyayaṃ āho vajradharasya caiva pratimā candro 'tha sūryo hyayam
children.translated_text: His form is a body surpassing <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>'s; clearly this is <s>Kubera</s>. Or is he the very likeness of the thunderbolt-bearer, or else the moon or the sun?

children.text: kāmāgrādhipatiśca vā pratikṛtī rudrasya kṛṣṇasya vā śrīmān lakṣaṇacitritāṅgamanagho buddho 'tha vā syādayam ||
children.translated_text: Or is he the supreme lord of desire, or a likeness of <s>Rudra</s> or <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>? Glorious, sinless, with limbs adorned by the auspicious marks, or could this be the Buddha?

children.text: tataḥ sā vanadevatā tānṛṣīn gāthayā pratyabhāṣat ||
children.translated_text: Then that forest deity answered those seers with a verse:

children.text: yā śrī ca vaiśravaṇe ca vai nivasate yā vā sahasrekṣaṇe lokānāṃ paripālakeṣu catuṣū yā cāsurendraśriyā
children.translated_text: Whatever splendor dwells in <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, whatever in the thousand-eyed one, whatever in the four guardians of the worlds, and whatever in the majesty of the lord of the asuras,

children.text: brahme yā ca sahāpatau nivasate kṛṣṇe ca yā ca śriyā sā śrī prāpya imaṃ hi śākyatanayaṃ nopaiti kāṃcitkalām ||
children.translated_text: whatever dwells in <s>Brahmā</s> and in <s>Sahāpati</s>, and whatever splendor is in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: that splendor, on reaching this son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, does not amount to even the least fraction.

children.text: atha khalu te ṛṣayastasyā devatāyā vacanamupaśritya dharaṇītale pratiṣṭhante
children.translated_text: Then those seers, having heard the word of that deity, came to stand upon the surface of the earth.

children.text: te paśyanti sma bodhisattvaṃ dhyāyantam āniñjyamānena kāyena tejorāśimiva jvalantam
children.translated_text: They saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> meditating, his body unmoving, blazing like a mass of light.

children.text: te bodhisattvamupanidhyāya gāthābhirabhituṣṭuvuḥ
children.translated_text: Having approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, they praised him with verses.

children.text: tatraika āha ||
children.translated_text: There one of them said:

children.text: loke kleśāgnisaṃtapte prādurbhūto hyayaṃ hradaḥ
children.translated_text: In a world scorched by the fire of the afflictions, this lake has appeared.

children.text: ayaṃ taṃ prāpsyate dharmaṃ yajjagad hlādayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He will attain that <s>dharma</s> (teaching) which will refresh the world.

children.text: aparo 'pyāha ||
children.translated_text: Another also said:

children.text: ajñānatimire loke prādurbhūtaḥ pradīpakaḥ
children.translated_text: In a world darkened by the gloom of ignorance, a lamp has appeared;

children.text: ayaṃ taṃ prāpsyate dharmaṃ yajjagadbhāsayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: this one will attain that <s>dharma</s> (teaching) by which he will illuminate the world.

children.text: aparo 'pyāha ||
children.translated_text: Another also said:

children.text: śokasāgarakāntāre yānaśreṣṭhamupasthitam
children.translated_text: In the wilderness of the ocean of grief, the best vehicle has appeared;

children.text: ayaṃ taṃ prāpsyate dharmaṃ yajjagattārayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: this one will attain that <s>dharma</s> (teaching) by which he will carry the world across.

children.text: aparo 'pyāha ||
children.translated_text: Another also said:

children.text: kleśabandhanabaddhānāṃ prādurbhūtaḥ pramocakaḥ
children.translated_text: For those bound by the bonds of the afflictions, a liberator has appeared;

children.text: ayaṃ taṃ prāpsyate dharmaṃ yajjaganmocayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: this one will attain that <s>dharma</s> (teaching) by which he will free the world.

children.text: aparo 'pyāha ||
children.translated_text: Another also said:

children.text: jarāvyādhikiliṣṭānāṃ prādurbhūto bhiṣagvaraḥ
children.translated_text: For those tormented by old age and disease, the best of physicians has appeared;

children.text: ayaṃ taṃ prāpsyate dharmaṃ jātimṛtyupramocakam ||
children.translated_text: this one will attain that <s>dharma</s> (teaching) which brings release from birth and death.

children.text: atha khalu te ṛṣayo bodhisattvamābhirgāthābhir abhistutvā tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya vihāyasā prakrāntāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those seers, having praised the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with these verses and circumambulated him three times, departed through the sky.

children.text: rājāpi śuddhodano bodhisattvamapaśyan bodhisattvena vinā na ramate sma
children.translated_text: King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, too, when he did not see the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, took no pleasure without the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: so 'vocat kumāraḥ kva gato nainaṃ paśyāmīti
children.translated_text: He said, "Where has the prince gone? I do not see him."

children.text: tatra mahājanakāyo nirdhāvito 'bhūt kumāraṃ parigaveṣamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the great crowd of people ran out, searching all around for the prince.

children.text: tato 'nyatamo 'mātyo bodhisattvaṃ paśyati sma jambucchāyāyāṃ paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇaṃ dhyāyantam
children.translated_text: Then a certain minister saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seated cross-legged in the shade of a jambu tree, meditating.

children.text: sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ ca tasmin samaye chāyā parivṛttābhūt
children.translated_text: And at that time the shade of all the trees had shifted around,

children.text: jambucchāyā ca bodhisattvasya kāyaṃ na vijahāti sma
children.translated_text: but the shade of the jambu tree did not leave the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body.

children.text: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā āścaryaprāptastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ śīghraṃ śīghraṃ tvaramāṇarūpo rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramya gāthābhyāmadhyabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, amazed, pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness, he quickly and hastily approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and addressed him with two verses:

children.text: paśya deva kumāro 'yaṃ jambucchāyāhi dhyāyati
children.translated_text: "Look, Your Majesty, this prince is meditating in the shade of the jambu tree;

children.text: yathā śakro 'thavā brahmā śriyā tejena śobhate ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Śakra</s> or <s>Brahmā</s>, he shines with splendor and radiance.

children.text: yasya vṛkṣasya chāyāyāṃ niṣaṇṇo varalakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The tree in whose shade the one marked with excellent signs is seated

children.text: sainaṃ na jahate chāyā dhyāyantaṃ puruṣottamam ||
children.translated_text: does not let its shade leave him, that supreme person as he meditates."

children.text: atha rājā śuddhodano yena sa jambuvṛkṣastenopasaṃkrāmat
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> approached that jambu tree.

children.text: so 'drākṣīdbodhisattvaṃ śriyā tejasā ca jvalantam
children.translated_text: He saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> blazing with beauty and radiance.

children.text: dṛṣṭā cemāṃ gāthāmabhāṣat ||
children.translated_text: And, seeing him, he spoke this verse:

children.text: hutāśano vā girimūrdhni saṃsthitaḥ śaśīva nakṣatragaṇānucīrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: "Like a fire standing on a mountain peak, like the moon attended by hosts of stars,

children.text: vepanti gātrāṇi mi paśyato imaṃ dhyāyantu tejo nu pradīpakalpam ||
children.translated_text: my limbs tremble as I behold him meditating, his splendor like a lamp."

children.text: sa bodhisattvasya pādāvabhivandyemāṃ gāthāmabhāṣat ||
children.translated_text: He bowed to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet and spoke this verse:

children.text: yadā cāsi mune jāto yadā dhyāyasi cārciman
children.translated_text: "When you were born, sage, and now when you meditate, radiant one,

children.text: ekadvirapi te nātha pādau vande vināyaka ||
children.translated_text: once and again I bow to your feet, lord, guide."

children.text: tatra triphalavāhakā dārakāḥ śabdaṃ kurvanti sma
children.translated_text: There the boys carrying triphala fruits were making noise.

children.text: tānamātyā evamāhur mā śabdaṃ mā śabdaṃ kārṣṭeti
children.translated_text: The ministers said to them, "Do not make noise, do not make noise."

children.text: te 'vocan kimetaditi
children.translated_text: They said, "What is this?"

children.text: amātyā āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ministers said:

children.text: vyāvṛtte timiranudasya maṇḍale 'pi vyomābhaṃ śubhavaralakṣaṇāgradhārim
children.translated_text: "Though the disk of the dispeller of darkness has moved away, the same tree-shade does not leave

children.text: dhyāyantaṃ girinicalaṃ narendraputraṃ siddhārthaṃ na jahati saiva vṛkṣachāyā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Siddhārtha</s>, the son of the king, who bears the foremost fair and excellent marks, sky-like in radiance, and meditates, motionless as a mountain."

children.text: tatredamucyate ||
children.translated_text: On this point this is said:

children.text: grīṣme vasanta samudāgata jeṣṭhamāse saṃpuṣpite kusumapallavasaṃprakīrṇe
children.translated_text: In summer, when spring had come, in the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, when flowers were in bloom and blossoms and shoots were scattered about,

children.text: kroñcāmayūraśukasārikasaṃpraghuṣṭe bhūyiṣṭha śākiyasutā abhiniṣkramanti ||
children.translated_text: when cranes, peacocks, parrots, and mynahs were calling out, most of the sons of the Śākyas went forth.

children.text: chando 'bhyuvāca parivāritu dārikebhiḥ hantā kumāra vani gacchama locanārtham
children.translated_text: <s>Chanda</s>, surrounded by the children, said, "Come, prince, let us go to the grove to look around.

children.text: kiṃ te gṛhe nivasato hi yathā dvijasya hanta vrajāma vaya codananārisaṃgham ||
children.translated_text: What use is it for you to stay at home like a twice-born? Come, let us go, and we will urge on the company of women."

children.text: madhyāhnakālasamaye suviśuddhasattvaḥ pañcāśataiḥ parivṛtaiḥ saha ceṭakebhiḥ
children.translated_text: At midday, with his being well purified, surrounded by five hundred young attendants,

children.text: na ca mātu naiva ca pituḥ prativedayitvā so 'buddha niṣkrāmiti gacchi kṛṣāṇagrāmam ||
children.translated_text: and without informing either his mother or his father, he, the future <s>Buddha</s>, went out and went to the ploughing village.

children.text: tasmiṃśca pārthivavarasya kṛṣāṇagrāme jambudrumo 'bhavadanekaviśālaśākhaḥ
children.translated_text: And in that ploughing village of the best of kings there was a jambu tree with many broad branches.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā kumāra pratibuddha dukhena cotto dhiksaṃskṛteti bahuduḥkha kṛṣī karoti ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this, the prince awakened to suffering and was moved: "Fie on conditioned existence! Farming brings much suffering."

children.text: so jambuchāyamupagamya vinītacitto tṛṇakāni gṛhya svaya saṃstaru saṃstaritvā
children.translated_text: He approached the shade of the jambu tree with disciplined mind, took some grasses himself, and spread out a seat.

children.text: paryaṅkamābhujiya ujju karitva kāyaṃ catvāri dhyāna śubha dhyāyi sa bodhisattvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Folding his legs crosswise and making his body upright, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> meditated on the four pure meditations.

children.text: pañcā ṛṣī khagapathena hi gacchamānā jambūya mūrdhni na prabhonti parākrametum
children.translated_text: Five seers, traveling through the path of the birds, were unable to pass over the top of the jambu tree.

children.text: te visthitā nihatamānamadāśca bhūtvā sarve samagrasahitā samudīkṣayanto ||
children.translated_text: They stood amazed, their pride and arrogance struck down, and all together, assembled, looked on.

children.text: vaya meruparvatavaraṃ tatha cakravālān nirbhidya gacchama javena asajjamānāḥ
children.translated_text: "We pass swiftly and unobstructed through mighty <s>Mount Meru</s> and the world-rings,

children.text: te jambuvṛkṣa na prabhoma atikrametuṃ ko nvatra heturayamadya bhaviṣyatīha ||
children.translated_text: yet we cannot pass beyond this jambu tree. What cause for this will there be here today?"

children.text: avatīrya medinitale ca pratiṣṭhihitvā paśyanti śākyatanayaṃ tahi jambumūle
children.translated_text: Descending and standing upon the surface of the earth, they saw the son of the Śākyas there at the foot of the jambu tree,

children.text: jambunadārcisadṛśaṃ prabhatejaraśmiṃ paryaṅkabandhu tada dhyāyatu bodhisattvam ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> meditating then in the cross-legged posture, with rays of radiance like <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold.

children.text: te vismitā daśanakhā kariyāna mūrdhni praṇatā kṛtāñjalipuṭā nipatan krameṣu
children.translated_text: Astonished, placing their ten fingernails upon their heads, bowed and with joined palms, they fell at his feet in order.

children.text: sādho sujāta sumukhaṃ karuṇā jagasya śīghraṃ vibuddha amṛte vinayasva sattvān ||
children.translated_text: "Excellent, well-born one, fair-faced compassion of the world; awaken quickly to immortality and discipline beings.

children.text: parivṛtta sūrya na jahī sugatasya chāyā olambate drumavaraṃ yatha padmapatram
children.translated_text: The sun has turned, yet it does not leave the <s>Sugata</s>'s shade; it hangs upon the noble tree like a lotus leaf.

children.text: devā sahasra bahavaḥ sthita añjalībhiḥ vandanti tasya caraṇau kṛtaniścayasya ||
children.translated_text: Many thousands of gods stand with joined palms and bow to the feet of him whose resolve is fixed."

children.text: śuddhodanaśca svagṛhe parimārgamāṇaḥ saṃpṛcchate kva nu gataḥ sa hi me kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Śuddhodana</s>, searching through his own house, asks, "Where indeed has that prince of mine gone?"

children.text: mātṛsvasā avaci mārgata no labhāmi saṃpṛcchatā narapate kva gataḥ kumāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: His maternal aunt said, "I have searched, O lord of men, but I do not find him. Ask where the prince has gone."

children.text: śuddhodanastvaritu pṛcchati kāñcukīyaṃ dauvārikaṃ tathapi cāntajanaṃ samantāt
children.translated_text: <s>Śuddhodana</s>, hurrying, questions the chamberlain, the doorkeeper, and also all the women of the inner apartments:

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ kumāra mama kenaci niṣkramanto śṛṇute varūpagatu deva kṛṣāṇagrāmam ||
children.translated_text: "Has anyone seen my prince going out?" He hears, "The fair one has gone, Your Majesty, to the ploughing village."

children.text: so śīghrameva tvaritaṃ saha śākiyebhiḥ niṣkrāntu prekṣi kṛṣigrāmagiriṃ praviṣṭam
children.translated_text: Then, very quickly and in haste, he went out with the <s>Śākyas</s> and saw him entered into the ploughing village.

children.text: yatha sūryakoṭiniyutāni samudgatāni tatha prekṣate hitakaraṃ śiriyā jvalantam ||
children.translated_text: Just as if ten million suns had risen, so he saw the beneficent one blazing with splendor.

children.text: mukuṭaṃ ca khaṅga tatha pāduka chorayitvā kṛtvā daśāṅguli śire abhivandite tam
children.translated_text: Having cast aside his crown, sword, and sandals, and having placed his ten fingers upon his head, he bowed to him.

children.text: sādhū subhūtavacanā ṛṣayo mahātmā vyaktaṃ kumāra abhiniṣkrami bodhihetoḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Excellent are the words of the great-souled seers, O well-born one; clearly the prince will go forth for the sake of awakening."

children.text: paripūrṇa dvādaśaśatā suprasannadevāḥ paccāśatā upagatā yatha śākiyānām
children.translated_text: A full twelve hundred gods, greatly pleased, and five hundred of the <s>Śākyas</s> had come there.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca ṛddhi sugate guṇasāgarasya saṃbodhicittu janayaṃ dṛḍhaāśayena ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the miraculous power of the <s>Sugata</s>, ocean of virtues, they generated the mind of awakening with firm resolve.

children.text: so kampayitva trisahasra aśeṣabhūmiṃ smṛtu saṃprajānu pratibuddha tataḥ samādheḥ
children.translated_text: Having shaken the entire three-thousandfold world-sphere, mindful and fully aware, he then awoke from that samādhi.

children.text: brahmasvaraḥ pitaramālapate dyutīmān utsṛjya tāta kṛṣigrāmabhato gaveṣa ||
children.translated_text: The radiant one, with a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s, addressed his father: "Give up, father, your search in the ploughing village.

children.text: yadi svarṇakāryu ahu svarṇa pravarṣayiṣye yadi vastrakāryu ahameva pradāsyi vastrāṃ
children.translated_text: If you need gold, I will rain down gold; if you need cloth, I myself will give cloth.

children.text: atha dhānyakāryu ahameva pravarṣayiṣye samyakprayukta bhava sarvajage narendra ||
children.translated_text: And if you need grain, I myself will rain it down. Be rightly engaged for the whole world, O lord of men."

children.text: anuśāsayitva pitaraṃ janapāriṣadyāṃ tasmin kṣaṇe puravaraṃ puna so pravekṣī
children.translated_text: Having instructed his father in the assembly of the people, at that moment he again entered the excellent city.

children.text: anuvartamāna jagataḥ sthihate puresmiṃ naiṣmkramyayuktamanasaḥ suviśuddhasattvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Conforming to the world, he stayed in the city, a being of very pure nature whose mind was yoked to renunciation.

children.text: Chapter 12
iti hi bhikṣavaḥ saṃvṛddhe kumāre rājā śuddhodano 'pareṇa samayena śākyagaṇena sārdhaṃ saṃsthāgāre niṣaṇṇo 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, when the prince had grown up, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> at another time was seated in the assembly hall together with the group of <s>Śākyas</s>.

children.text: tatra te mahallakamahallakāḥ śākyā rājānaṃ śuddhodanamevamāhuḥ yatkhalu devo jānīyāt
children.translated_text: There the elder <s>Śākyas</s> and the very elder <s>Śākyas</s> said this to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: "Your Majesty should know this.

children.text: ayaṃ sarvārthasiddhakumāro naimittikairbrāhmaṇaiḥ kṛtaniścayaiśca devairyadbhūyasaivaṃ nirdiṣṭo yadi kumāro 'bhiniṣkramiṣyati tathāgato bhaviṣyatyarhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: This Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has been foretold mostly in this way by the divining brahmins and by the gods who had reached certainty: if the prince goes forth, he will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: uta nābhiniṣkramiṣyati rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartī caturaṅgo vijitavān dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ
children.translated_text: But if he does not go forth, he will become a king, a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), possessing the fourfold army, victorious, righteous, a king of dharma, endowed with the seven jewels.

children.text: tasyemāni sapta ratnāni bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: These will be his seven jewels:

children.text: tadyathā cakraratnaṃ hastiratnaṃ aśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnam
children.translated_text: namely, the wheel-jewel, the elephant-jewel, the horse-jewel, the jewel-gem, the woman-jewel, the householder-jewel, and the counselor-jewel.

children.text: evaṃ saptaratnam
children.translated_text: Such are the seven jewels.

children.text: sampūrṇaṃ cāsya putrasahasraṃ bhaviṣyati śūrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām
children.translated_text: And he will have a complete thousand sons, heroic, handsome in their limbs, crushers of enemy armies.

children.text: sa imaṃ pṛthivīmaṇḍalamadaṇḍenāśastreṇābhinirjityādhyāvasiṣyati saha dharmeṇeti
children.translated_text: Having conquered this circle of the earth without rod or weapon, he will dwell over it in accordance with dharma.

children.text: tasmānniveśanaṃ kumārasya kriyatāmiti
children.translated_text: Therefore let a residence be made for the prince.

children.text: tatra strīgaṇaparivṛto ratiṃ vetsyati nābhiniṣkramiṣyati
children.translated_text: There, surrounded by a company of women, he will enjoy pleasure and will not go forth.

children.text: evamasmākaṃ cakravartivaṃśasya cānupacchedo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: In this way there will be no interruption of our lineage of <s>cakravartins</s>.

children.text: mānitāśca bhaviṣyāmo 'navadyāśca sarvakoṭarājabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And we will be honored and blameless before all the kings on every side."

children.text: tato rājā śuddhodana evamāha yadyevaṃ tena hi vyavalokayata katamā kanyā kumārasyānurūpā syāt
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said this: "If that is so, then look around: what maiden would be suitable for the prince?"

children.text: tatra pañcamātrāṇi śākyaśatāni
children.translated_text: There were about five hundred <s>Śākyas</s>.

children.text: ekaika evamāha mama duhitā anurūpā syāt kumārasya
children.translated_text: Each one said, "My daughter would be suitable for the prince."

children.text: surūpā mama duhiteti
children.translated_text: "My daughter is beautiful," each said.

children.text: rājā prāha durāsadaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: The king said, "The prince is difficult to approach.

children.text: tat prativedayiṣyāmastāvat kumārasya katamā te kanyā rocata iti
children.translated_text: So first we shall inform the prince: which maiden is pleasing to you?"

children.text: tataśca te sarve saṃnipatya kumārasyaināṃ prakṛtimārocayanti sma
children.translated_text: Then they all gathered together and reported this matter to the prince.

children.text: tān kumāra uvāca saptame divase prativacanaṃ śroṣyatheti ||
children.translated_text: The prince said to them, "You shall hear my answer on the seventh day."

children.text: tato bodhisattvasyaitadabhavat ||
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

children.text: vidita mama ananta kāmadoṣāḥ saraṇasarvairasaśokaduḥkhamūlāḥ
children.translated_text: "Known to me are the endless faults of sensual desires: they are without refuge, without essence, the roots of sorrow and suffering.

children.text: bhayakara viṣapatrasaṃnikāśāḥ jvalananibhā asidhāratulyarūpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are terrifying, like poisoned leaves, like a blazing fire, and like the edge of a sword.

children.text: kāmaguṇi na me 'sti chandarāgo na ca ahu śobhami istrigāramadhye
children.translated_text: I have no desire or passion for the objects of sense pleasure, nor do I shine in the midst of the women's quarters.

children.text: yannu ahu vane vaseya tūṣṇīṃ dhyānasamādhisukhena śāntacittaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Would that I might live silently in the forest, my mind peaceful through the bliss of meditation and samādhi."

children.text: sa punarapi mīmāṃsopāyakauśalyam āmukhīkṛtya sattvaparipākamavekṣamāṇo mahākaruṇāṃ saṃjanayya tasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: But again, bringing skill in means and deliberation before him, considering the maturation of beings, and generating great compassion, he spoke these verses at that time:

children.text: saṃkīrṇi paṅki padumāni vivṛddhimanti ākīrṇa rāja naramadhyi labhāti pūjām
children.translated_text: "Lotuses, though crowded in the mud, grow and flourish; a king, surrounded in the midst of men, receives honor.

children.text: yada bodhisattva parivārabalaṃ labhante tada sattvakoṭinayutānyamṛte vinenti ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Bodhisattvas</s> obtain the strength of a retinue, then they lead many crores and niyutas of beings to immortality.

children.text: ye cāpi pūrvaka abhūdvidu bodhisattvāḥ sarvebhi bhārya suta darśita istrigārāḥ
children.translated_text: And the wise <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who lived in former times all displayed wives, sons, and women's quarters.

children.text: na ca rāgarakta na ca dhyānasukhebhi bhraṣṭāḥ hantānuśikṣayi ahaṃ pi guṇeṣu teṣām ||
children.translated_text: Yet they were not stained by passion, nor did they fall away from the joys of meditation. Come, I too will train in their virtues.

children.text: na ca prākṛtā mama vadhū anukūla yā syād yasyā na iṣyatu guṇā sada satyavākyam
children.translated_text: Nor would an ordinary woman be a suitable bride for me, one whose virtues and constant truthful speech are not desired.

children.text: yā cinti mahyamabhirādhayate 'pramattā rūpeṇa janmakulagotratayā suśuddhā ||
children.translated_text: She who, vigilant, satisfies my thought, pure in beauty, birth, family, and lineage,

children.text: so gāthalekha likhite guṇaarthayuktā yā kanya īdṛśa bhave mama tāṃ varethā
children.translated_text: let a verse-letter be written, endowed with the meaning of these qualities: whichever maiden should be such, choose her for me.

children.text: na mamārthu prākṛtajanena asaṃvṛtena yasyā guṇā kathayamī mama tāṃ varethā ||
children.translated_text: I have no purpose with an ordinary, unrestrained person. The one whose virtues I describe, choose her for me.

children.text: yā rūpayauvanavarā na ca rūpamattā mātā svasā va yatha vartati maitracittā
children.translated_text: She who is excellent in beauty and youth, but is not intoxicated by beauty, and who acts with a friendly mind like a mother or sister,

children.text: tyāge ratā śramaṇabrāhmaṇadānaśīlā tāṃ tādṛśāṃ mama vadhūṃ varayasva tāta ||
children.translated_text: who delights in giving and is accustomed to giving gifts to ascetics and brahmins: choose such a woman as my bride, father.

children.text: yasyā na mānu na khilo na ca doṣamasti na ca śāṭhya īrṣya na ca māya na ujjubhraṣṭā
children.translated_text: She in whom there is no pride, no hardness, and no fault; no deceit, no jealousy, no illusion, and no falling away from uprightness;

children.text: svapnāntare 'pi purūṣe na pare 'bhiraktā tuṣṭā svakena patinā śayate 'pramattā ||
children.translated_text: who is not attached to another man even in a dream, but sleeps content with her own husband, vigilant;

children.text: na ca garvitā na pi ca uddhata na pragalbhā nirmāna mānavigatāpi ca ceṭibhūtā
children.translated_text: who is not proud, not insolent, and not forward; without conceit, devoid of arrogance, and serving like a maid;

children.text: na ca pānagṛddha na raseṣu na śabdagandhe nirlobhabhidhyavigatā svadhanena tuṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: who is not greedy for drink, nor for tastes, sounds, or smells; free from greed and covetousness, content with her own wealth;

children.text: satye sthitā na pi ca cañcala naiva bhrāntā na ca uddhatonnatasthitā hirivastrachannā
children.translated_text: who is established in truth, not fickle and not confused; not standing haughtily or loftily, clothed with modesty as with a garment;

children.text: na ca dṛṣṭimaṅgalaratā sada dharmayuktā kāyena vāca manasā sada śuddhabhāvā ||
children.translated_text: who does not delight in omens from sights, who is always joined to <s>dharma</s> (teaching), and whose disposition is always pure in body, speech, and mind;

children.text: na ca styānamiddhabahulā na ca mānamūḍhā mīmāṃsayukta sukṛtā sada dharmacārī
children.translated_text: who is not much given to sloth and torpor, and is not deluded by pride; who is given to reflection, does good, and always practices <s>dharma</s> (teaching);

children.text: śvaśrau ca tasya śvaśure yatha śāstṛpremā dāsī kalatra jani yādṛśamātmaprema ||
children.translated_text: who has love for her mother-in-law and father-in-law as for a teacher, and love for servant-women, dependents, and people as for herself;

children.text: śāstre vidhijña kuśalā gaṇikā yathaiva paścāt svapet prathamamutthihate ca śayyāta
children.translated_text: who knows the rules of the treatises and is skilled like a courtesan, who sleeps after others and rises first from the bed;

children.text: maitrānuvarti akuhāpi ca mātṛbhūtā etādṛśīṃ mi nṛpate vadhukāṃ vṛṇīṣva ||
children.translated_text: who follows friends, is not deceitful, and is motherly: choose such a bride for me, O king.

children.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo rājā śuddhodana imā gāthā vācayitvā purohitamāmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa kapilavastumahānagare
children.translated_text: Then, monks, King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, after having had these verses read, addressed the chaplain: "Go, great brahmin, into the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>.

children.text: sarvagṛhāṇyanupraviśya kanyā vyavalokaya
children.translated_text: Enter all the houses and inspect the maidens.

children.text: yasyā ete guṇāḥ saṃvidyante kṣatriyakanyāyā vā brāhmaṇakanyāyā vā vaiśyakanyāyā vā śūdrakanyāyā vā tāṃ kanyāmasmākaṃ prativedaya
children.translated_text: Whichever maiden has these qualities, whether she is a kṣatriya girl, a brahmin girl, a vaiśya girl, or a śūdra girl, report that maiden to us.

children.text: tatkasmāddhetor na hi kumāraḥ kulārthiko na gotrārthikaḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? The prince is not seeking family and is not seeking lineage.

children.text: guṇārthika eva kumāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The prince seeks qualities alone."

children.text: tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: At that time he spoke these verses:

children.text: brāhmaṇīṃ kṣatriyāṃ kanyāṃ veśyāṃ śūdrīṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: "A brahmin girl, a kṣatriya girl, a vaiśya girl, and likewise a śūdra girl,

children.text: yasyā ete guṇāḥ santi tāṃ me kanyāṃ pravedaya ||
children.translated_text: whichever has these qualities, announce that maiden to me.

children.text: na kulena na gotreṇa kumāro mama vismitaḥ
children.translated_text: My prince is not impressed by family or lineage;

children.text: guṇe satye ca dharme ca tatrāsya ramate manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his mind delights in qualities, truth, and <s>dharma</s> (teaching)."

children.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sa purohitastaṃ gāthālekhaṃ gṛhītvā kapilavastuni mahānagare gṛhādgṛhaṃ vyavalokayan gatvā hiṇḍan kanyāṃ paryeṣate sma
children.translated_text: Then, monks, that chaplain took the verse-letter and, going from house to house in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, roamed about inspecting and seeking a maiden.

children.text: evaṃguṇayuktām apaśyan na caiva guṇayuktāṃ kanyāṃ
children.translated_text: He did not see a maiden endowed with such qualities, nor indeed a maiden endowed with those qualities.

children.text: so 'nupūrveṇa vicaran yena daṇḍapāṇeḥ śākyasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmat
children.translated_text: Wandering gradually, he approached the residence of <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s>.

children.text: sa taṃ niveśanaṃ praviṣṭo 'drākṣīt kanyāmabhirūpāṃ prāsādikāṃ darśanīyāṃ paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkaratayā samanvāgatāṃ nātidīrghāṃ nātihrasvāṃ nātisthūlāṃ nātikṛśāṃ nātigaurāṃ nātikṛṣṇāṃ prathamayauvanāvasthāṃ strīratnamiva khyāyamānām
children.translated_text: Having entered that residence, he saw a maiden beautiful, pleasing, lovely to behold, endowed with supreme beauty of complexion and figure, not too tall, not too short, not too stout, not too thin, not too fair, not too dark, in the first stage of youth, appearing like a jewel among women.

children.text: atha sā dārikā purohitasya caraṇau gṛhītvā evamāha kena te mahābrāhmaṇa kāryam
children.translated_text: Then that girl took hold of the chaplain's feet and said, "What business have you, great brahmin?"

children.text: purohita āha ||
children.translated_text: The chaplain said:

children.text: śuddhodanasya tanayaḥ paramābhirūpo dvātriṃśalakṣaṇadharo guṇatejayuktaḥ
children.translated_text: "The son of <s>Śuddhodana</s> is supremely handsome, bearer of the thirty-two marks, endowed with virtue and splendor.

children.text: teneti gātha likhitā guṇaye vadhūnāṃ yasyā guṇāsti hi ime sa hi tasya patnī ||
children.translated_text: By him this verse has been written about the qualities of brides; she who has these qualities is his wife."

children.text: sa tasyāstaṃ lekhamupanāmayati sma ||
children.translated_text: He presented that letter to her.

children.text: atha sā dārikā taṃ gāthālekhaṃ vācayitvā smitamupadarśya taṃ purohitaṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣat ||
children.translated_text: Then that girl, after reading the verse-letter, showed a smile and addressed that chaplain in a verse:

children.text: mahyeti brāhmaṇa guṇā anurūpa sarve so me patirbhavatu saumya surūparūpaḥ
children.translated_text: "Brahmin, all these qualities are fitting for me. Let that handsome, fine-formed one be my husband.

children.text: bhaṇahi kumāru yadi kārya ma hū vilamba mā hīnaprākṛtajanena bhaveya vāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell the prince that, if he has business with me, there should be no delay; may I not dwell with a low, ordinary person."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha sa khalu purohito rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaiva tamarthamārocayati sma dṛṣṭā mayā deva kanyā yā kumārasyānurūpā syāt
children.translated_text: Then that chaplain approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and reported that matter: "I have seen, Majesty, a maiden who would be suitable for the prince."

children.text: āha kasyāsau āha daṇḍapāṇerdeva śākyasya duhitā ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Whose is she?" He replied, "Majesty, she is the daughter of <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s>."

children.text: atha rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyaitadabhavad durāsadaḥ kumāraḥ śubhādhimuktaśca
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> thought, "The prince is hard to approach and intent upon what is good.

children.text: prāyeṇa ca mātṛgrāmo 'saṃvidyamānaguṇo 'pi guṇānāmātmani prajānīte
children.translated_text: And generally womankind recognizes virtues in itself even when virtues are not present.

children.text: yannvahamaśokabhāṇḍakāni kārayeyam yāni kumāraḥ sarvadārikābhyo 'nuprayacchet
children.translated_text: Suppose I were to have aśoka ornaments made, which the prince would present to all the girls.

children.text: tatra yasyāṃ dārikāyāṃ kumārasya cakṣur abhiniveśyati tāṃ kumārasya varayiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Then whichever girl the prince fixes his eye upon, I shall choose her for the prince."

children.text: atha khalu rājā śuddhodano 'śokabhāṇḍāni kārayati sma suvarṇamayāni rūpyamayāni nānāratnamayāni
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had aśoka ornaments made, of gold, silver, and various jewels.

children.text: kārayitvā ca kapilavastuni mahānagare ghaṇṭāghoṣaṇāṃ kārayāmāsa saptame divase kumāro darśanaṃ dāsyati aśokabhāṇḍakāni ca dārikābhyo viśrāṇayiṣyati
children.translated_text: And, having caused this to be done, in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> he had a bell-proclamation made: "On the seventh day the prince will give audience and will distribute <s>aśokabhāṇḍakas</s> (aśoka gifts) to the girls."

children.text: tatra sarvadārikābhiḥ saṃsthāgāre saṃnipatitavyamiti ||
children.translated_text: There all the girls are to assemble in the assembly hall.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ saptame divase bodhisattvaḥ saṃsthāgāramupasaṃkramya bhadrāsane nyaṣīdat
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, on the seventh day the <s>Bodhisattva</s> approached the assembly hall and sat down on the fine seat.

children.text: rājāpi śuddhodano 'dṛśyapuruṣān sthāpayati sma yasyāṃ dārikāyāṃ kumārasya cakṣuḥ saṃniviśet tāṃ mamārocayadhvamiti ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Śuddhodana</s> also stationed hidden men, saying, "Tell me which girl the prince's eye rests upon."

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo yāvantyaḥ kapilavastuni mahānagare dārikāstāḥ sarvā yena saṃsthāgāro yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāman bodhisattvasya darśanāya aśokabhāṇḍakāni ca pratigṛhītum ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, all the girls there were in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> approached the assembly hall and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, to see the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and to receive the <s>aśokabhāṇḍakas</s>.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo yathāgatābhyastābhyo dārikābhyo 'śokabhāṇḍakānyanuprayacchati sma
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gave the <s>aśokabhāṇḍakas</s> to the girls as they came forward.

children.text: tāśca dārikā na śaknuvanti sma bodhisattvasya śriyaṃ tejaśca soḍhum
children.translated_text: But those girls could not bear the beauty and radiance of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: tā aśokabhāṇḍakāni gṛhītvā śīghraṃ śīghrameva prakrāmanti sma ||
children.translated_text: Taking the <s>aśokabhāṇḍakas</s>, they departed very quickly indeed.

children.text: atha daṇḍapāṇeḥ śākyasya duhitā gopā nāma śākyakanyā sā dāsīgaṇaparivṛtā puraskṛtā yena saṃsthāgāro yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmat
children.translated_text: Then the daughter of the Śākya <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>, a Śākya maiden named <s>Gopā</s>, surrounded and preceded by a group of female servants, approached the assembly hall and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramyaikānte 'sthāt bodhisattvamanimeṣābhyāṃ nayanābhyāṃ prekṣamāṇā
children.translated_text: Having approached, she stood to one side, gazing at the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with unblinking eyes.

children.text: tadyadā bodhisattvena sarvāṇyaśokabhāṇḍāni dattāni tadā sā bodhisattvamupasaṃkramya prahasitavadanā bodhisattvamevamāha kumāra kiṃ te mayāpanītaṃ yastvaṃ māṃ vimānayasi
children.translated_text: Then, when all the <s>aśokabhāṇḍakas</s> had been given away by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, she approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and, with a smiling face, said this to him: "Prince, what have I taken away from you, that you slight me?"

children.text: āha nāhaṃ tvāṃ vimānayāmi api tu khalu punastvamabhipaścādāgateti
children.translated_text: He said, "I am not slighting you; rather, you have come afterward."

children.text: sa tasyai cānekaśatasahasramūlyamaṅgulīyakaṃ nirmucya prādāt ||
children.translated_text: And he removed a ring worth many hundreds of thousands and gave it to her.

children.text: sā prāha idamahaṃ kumāra tavāntikādarhāmi āha imāni madīyānyābharaṇāni gṛhyatām
children.translated_text: She said, "Prince, am I worthy of this from your presence?" He said, "Take these ornaments of mine."

children.text: sā āha na vayaṃ kumāraṃ vyalaṃkariṣyāmaḥ alaṃkariṣyāmo vayaṃ kumāram
children.translated_text: She said, "We will not strip the prince of ornaments; we will adorn the prince."

children.text: ityuktvā sā kanyā prakrāmat ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, that maiden departed.

children.text: tatastairguhyapuruṣai rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaiṣa vṛttānto nivedito 'bhūd deva daṇḍapāṇeḥ śākyasya duhitā gopā nāma śākyakanyā tasyāṃ kumārasya cakṣurniviṣṭaṃ muhūrtaṃ ca tayoḥ saṃlāpo 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: Then those secret men approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and reported this event: "Your Majesty, the prince's eye rested upon the Śākya maiden named <s>Gopā</s>, the daughter of the Śākya <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>, and there was a moment of conversation between the two."

children.text: ityetatkhalu vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā śuddhodano daṇḍapāṇeḥ śākyasya purohitaṃ dautyena preṣayati sma yā te duhitā sā mama kumārasya pradīyatāmiti ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this speech, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> sent the priest of <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the Śākya as an envoy, saying, "Let your daughter be given to my prince."

children.text: daṇḍapāṇirāha ārya kumāro gṛhe sukhasaṃvṛddhaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> said, "Noble sir, the prince has grown up softly at home.

children.text: asmākaṃ cāyaṃ kuladharmaḥ śilpajñasya kanyā dātavyā nāśilpajñasyeti
children.translated_text: And this is our family custom: a daughter is to be given to one who knows the arts, not to one who does not know the arts.

children.text: kumāraśca na śilpajño nāsidhanuṣkalāpayuddhasālambhavidhijñaḥ
children.translated_text: The prince does not know the arts, nor is he versed in the methods of sword, bow, quiver, battle, and grappling.

children.text: tatkatham aśilpajñāyāhaṃ duhitaraṃ dāsyāmi
children.translated_text: So how shall I give my daughter to one who does not know the arts?"

children.text: ityetacca rājñaḥ prativeditam
children.translated_text: And this was reported to the king.

children.text: tato rājña etadabhavad dvirapīdamahaṃ sahadharmeṇa coditaḥ
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the king: "Now for a second time I have been challenged on this same rule.

children.text: yadāpi mayoktaṃ kasmācchākyakumārāḥ kumārasyopasthānāya nāgacchantīti tadāpyahamabhihitaḥ kiṃ vayaṃ maṇḍakasyopasthānaṃ kariṣyāma iti
children.translated_text: When I asked, 'Why do the Śākya princes not come to attend upon the prince?' then too I was answered, 'Are we to attend upon a dullard?'

children.text: etarhyapyevamiti pradhyāyanniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: Now it is the same." Thinking thus, he sat absorbed in thought.

children.text: bodhisattvaścainaṃ vṛttāntamaśrauṣīt
children.translated_text: And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> heard this event.

children.text: śrutvā ca yena rājā śuddhodanastenopasaṃkrāmat
children.translated_text: Having heard it, he approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramyaivamāha deva kimidaṃ dīnamanāstiṣṭhasi
children.translated_text: Having approached, he said this: "Your Majesty, why do you remain with a downcast mind?"

children.text: rājā āha alaṃ te kumāra anena
children.translated_text: The king said, "Enough, prince; this matter is not for you."

children.text: kumāra āha deva sarvathā tāvadavaśyam evamākhyātavyam
children.translated_text: The prince said, "Your Majesty, in every way it must certainly be told."

children.text: yāvattrirapi bodhisattvo rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ paripṛcchati sma ||
children.translated_text: Up to three times the <s>Bodhisattva</s> questioned King <s>Śuddhodana</s>.

children.text: tato rājā śuddhodano bodhisattvāya tāṃ prakṛtimārocayati sma
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> told the <s>Bodhisattva</s> the facts of the matter.

children.text: tāṃ śrutvā bodhisattva āha deva asti punariha nagare kaścidyo mayā sārdhaṃ samarthaḥ śilpena śilpamupadarśayitum
children.translated_text: Having heard them, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said, "Your Majesty, is there anyone here in the city who is able to display art against art together with me?"

children.text: tato rājā śuddhodanaḥ prahasitavadano bodhisattvamevamāha śakyasi punastvaṃ putra śilpamupadarśayitum sa āha bāḍhaṃ śakyāmi deva
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, with a smiling face, said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: "But are you able, son, to display art?" He said, "Indeed I am able, Your Majesty.

children.text: tena hi saṃnipātyantāṃ sarvaśilpajñā yeṣāṃ purataḥ svaṃ śilpamupadarśayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: Then let all those who know the arts be assembled; before them I will display my own art."

children.text: tato rājā śuddhodanaḥ kapilavastuni mahānagaravare ghaṇṭāghoṣaṇāṃ kārayati sma saptame divase kumāraḥ svaṃ śilpamupadarśayati
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had a bell-proclamation made in the excellent great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>: "On the seventh day the prince will display his own art.

children.text: tatra sarvaśilpajñaiḥ saṃnipatitavyam ||
children.translated_text: There all those who know the arts are to assemble."

children.text: tatra saptame divase pañcamātrāṇi śākyakumāraśatāni saṃnipatitānyabhūvan
children.translated_text: There, on the seventh day, about five hundred Śākya princes assembled.

children.text: daṇḍapāṇeśca śākyasya duhitā gopā nāma śākyakanyā jayapatākā sthāpitābhūd yo vā atra asidhanuṣkalāpayuddhasālambheṣu jeṣyati tasyaiṣā bhaviṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: And the Śākya maiden named <s>Gopā</s>, the daughter of the Śākya <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>, was set up as the victory prize: "Whoever here wins in sword, bow, quiver, battle, and grappling, she will belong to him."

children.text: tatra sarvapurato devadattaḥ kumāro nagarādabhiniṣkrāmati sma
children.translated_text: There, before everyone, Prince <s>Devadatta</s> went out from the city.

children.text: śvetaśca hastī mahāpramāṇo bodhisattvasyārthe nagaraṃ praveśyate sma
children.translated_text: And a white elephant of great size was being led into the city for the sake of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: tatra devadattaḥ kumāra īrṣyayā ca śākyabalamadena ca mattaḥ
children.translated_text: There Prince <s>Devadatta</s>, intoxicated by envy and by pride in the strength of the Śākyas,

children.text: sa taṃ hastināgaṃ vāmena pāṇinā śuṇḍāyāṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇena pāṇinā capeṭayā ekaprahāreṇaiva hato 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: seized that elephant by the trunk with his left hand and, with a slap of his right hand, struck it dead in a single blow.

children.text: tasyānantaraṃ sundaranandakumāro 'bhiniṣkrāmati sma
children.translated_text: Immediately after that Prince <s>Sundarananda</s> came out.

children.text: so 'drākṣīttaṃ hastināgaṃ nagaradvāre hatam
children.translated_text: He saw that elephant lying killed at the city gate.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca paryapṛcchat kenāyaṃ hata iti
children.translated_text: And seeing it, he asked, "By whom was this killed?"

children.text: tatra mahājanakāya āha devadatteneti
children.translated_text: There the great crowd of people said, "By <s>Devadatta</s>."

children.text: sa āha aśobhanamidaṃ devadattasya
children.translated_text: He said, "This is not a fine deed of <s>Devadatta</s>."

children.text: sa taṃ hastināgaṃ lāṅgūle gṛhītvā nagaradvārādapakarṣati sma ||
children.translated_text: Taking that elephant by the tail, he dragged it away from the city gate.

children.text: tadanantaraṃ bodhisattvo rathābhirūḍho 'bhiniṣkrāmati sma
children.translated_text: Immediately after that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, mounted on his chariot, came out.

children.text: adrākṣīdbodhisattvastaṃ hastinaṃ hatam
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> saw that elephant killed.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca paryapṛcchat kenāyaṃ hata iti
children.translated_text: And seeing it, he asked, "By whom was this killed?"

children.text: āhur devadatteneti
children.translated_text: They said, "By <s>Devadatta</s>."

children.text: āha aśobhanaṃ devadattasya
children.translated_text: He said, "This was not a fine deed of <s>Devadatta</s>."

children.text: kena punarasmānnagaradvārādapakarṣita iti
children.translated_text: "But by whom was it dragged away from this city gate?"

children.text: āhuḥ sundaranandeneti
children.translated_text: They said, "By <s>Sundarananda</s>."

children.text: āha śobhanamidaṃ sundaranandasya
children.translated_text: He said, "This was a fine deed of <s>Sundarananda</s>."

children.text: kiṃtu mahākāyo 'yaṃ sattvaḥ
children.translated_text: "Yet this being has a huge body,

children.text: so 'yaṃ klinnaḥ sarvanagaraṃ daurgandhena sphuriṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: and when it rots it will fill the whole city with stench."

children.text: tataḥ kumāro rathasya evaikaṃ pādaṃ bhūmau prasārya pādāṅguṣṭhena taṃ hastināgaṃ lāṅgūle gṛhītvā sapta prākārān sapta ca parikhānatikramya bahirnagarasya krośamātre prakṣipati sma
children.translated_text: Then the prince, from the chariot itself, stretched one foot down to the ground, took that elephant by the tail with his big toe, and hurled it a krośa outside the city, beyond seven ramparts and seven moats.

children.text: yatra ca pradeśe sa hastī patitastasmin pradeśe mahadbilaṃ saṃvṛttaṃ yatsāṃprataṃ hastigartetyabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: And in the place where the elephant fell a great pit came into being, which is now called the Elephant Pit.

children.text: tatra devamanujāḥ śatasahasrāṇi hāhākārakilakilāprakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇi prāmuñcan
children.translated_text: There gods and men released hundreds of thousands of cries of amazement, shouts, and loud exclamations.

children.text: cailavikṣepāṃścākārṣuḥ
children.translated_text: They also waved their garments.

children.text: gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā ime gāthe 'bhāṣanta ||
children.translated_text: And divine youths standing in the expanse of the sky spoke these verses:

children.text: yatha mattagajendragatīnāṃ pādāṅguṣṭhatalena gajendram
children.translated_text: "As he, with the sole of his big toe, has taken the lordly elephant, whose gait was like that of rutting lordly elephants,

children.text: sapta purāparikhā atikramya kṣiptu bahiḥ svapurātu ayaṃ hi ||
children.translated_text: and thrown it beyond seven city walls and moats, outside his own city,

children.text: niḥsaṃśayameṣa sumedhā mānabalena samucchritakāyān
children.translated_text: so without doubt this wise one, by the power of wisdom, will cast out those whose bodies are raised high by pride and strength,

children.text: saṃsārapurātu bahirdhā eka kṣapiṣyati prajñabalena ||
children.translated_text: he alone will throw them outside the city of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence)."

children.text: iti hi pañcamātrāṇi śākyakumāraśatāni nagarānniṣkramya yenānyatamaḥ pṛthivīpradeśo yatra śākyakumārāḥ śilpamupadarśayanti sma tenopasaṃkrāman
children.translated_text: Thus the five hundred Śākya princes went out from the city and approached a certain place on the ground where the Śākya princes were displaying their skills.

children.text: rājāpi śuddhodano mahallakamahallakāśca śākyā mahāṃśca janakāyo yenāsau pṛthivīpradeśastenopasaṃkrāman bodhisattvasya cānyeṣāṃ ca śākyakumārāṇāṃ śilpaviśeṣaṃ draṣṭukāmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Śuddhodana</s> too, along with the elder and younger Śākyas and a great crowd of people, approached that place, wishing to see the special skill of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and of the other Śākya princes.

children.text: tatra ādita eva ye śākyakumārā lipyāṃ paṭuvidhijñāste bodhisattvena sārdhaṃ lipiṃ viśeṣayanti sma
children.translated_text: There, first of all, those Śākya princes who were skilled and expert in writing competed with the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in writing.

children.text: tatra taiḥ śākyairviśvāmitra ācāryaḥ sākṣī sthāpito 'bhūt sa tvaṃ vyavalokaya katamo 'tra kumāro lipijñāne viśiṣyate yadi vā lekhyato yadi vā bahulipiniryāṇataḥ
children.translated_text: There the Śākyas appointed the teacher <s>Viśvāmitra</s> as witness: "You examine which prince here is superior in knowledge of writing, whether in written form or in the production of many scripts."

children.text: atha viśvāmitra ācāryaḥ pratyakṣo bodhisattvasya lipijñāne smitamupadarśayannime gāthe 'bhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Then the teacher <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, directly beholding the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s knowledge of writing and showing a smile, spoke these verses:

children.text: manuṣyaloke 'tha ca devaloke gandharvaloke 'pyasurendraloke
children.translated_text: "In the human world, and also in the divine world, in the world of the <s>Gandharvas</s> and in the world of the lords of the Asuras,

children.text: yāvanti kecillipi sarvaloke tatraiṣa pāraṃgatu śuddhasattvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whatever scripts there are in the whole world, in all of them this pure being has gone to the far shore.

children.text: nāmāpi yūyaṃ ca ahaṃ ca teṣāṃ lipīna jānāma na cākṣarāṇām
children.translated_text: You and I do not even know the names of those scripts, nor their letters,

children.text: yānyeṣa jānāti manuṣyacandro ahamatra pratyakṣu vijeṣyate 'yam ||
children.translated_text: which this moon among men knows. I am a direct witness here that he will be victorious."

children.text: śākyā āhur viśiṣyatāṃ tāvatkumāro lipijñāne
children.translated_text: The Śākyas said, "Let the prince be superior for now in knowledge of writing.

children.text: saṃkhyājñāne kumāro viśeṣayitavyo jijñāsyaśca
children.translated_text: In knowledge of numbers the prince must be tested and investigated."

children.text: tatrārjuno nāma śākyagaṇako mahāmātraḥ saṃkhyāgaṇanāsu pāraṃgataḥ sa sākṣī sthāpito 'bhūt sa tvaṃ vyavalokaya katamo 'tra kumāro viśiṣyate saṃkhyājñānata iti
children.translated_text: There a Śākya accountant named <s>Arjuna</s>, a high official who had mastered calculations and enumeration, was appointed as witness: "You examine which prince here is superior in knowledge of numbers."

children.text: tatra bodhisattvaścoddiśati sma ekaśca śākyakumāro nikṣipati sma na ca pariprāpayati sma
children.translated_text: There the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dictated, and one Śākya prince set it down, but he could not keep pace.

children.text: bodhisattvasyaiko dvau trayaścatvāraḥ pañcadaśa viṃśattriṃśaccatvāriṃśatpañcāśacchataṃ yāvatpañcāpi śākyakumāraśatāni yugapatkāle nikṣipanti sma na ca pariprāpayanti sma
children.translated_text: As the <s>Bodhisattva</s> went on with one, two, three, four, fifteen, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, and a hundred, even as many as five hundred Śākya princes set it down at the same time, but they could not keep pace.

children.text: tato bodhisattva āha uddiśata yūyam ahaṃ nikṣepsyāmīti
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said, "You dictate, and I will set it down."

children.text: tatraikaśākyakumāro bodhisattvasyoddiśati sma na ca pariprāpayati sma
children.translated_text: There one Śākya prince dictated to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, but he could not keep pace.

children.text: dvāvapi trayo 'pi pañcāpi daśāpi viṃśatyapi triṃśadapi catvāriṃśadapi pañcāśadapi yāvatpañcāpi śākyakumāraśatāni yugapaduddiśanti sma
children.translated_text: Two also, three also, five also, ten also, twenty also, thirty also, forty also, fifty also, and finally even five hundred Śākya princes dictated all at once,

children.text: na ca pariprāpayanti sma bodhisattvasya nikṣipataḥ ||
children.translated_text: but they could not keep pace while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was setting it down.

children.text: bodhisattva āha alamalamanena vivādena
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said, "Enough, enough of this dispute.

children.text: sarva idānīmekībhūtvā mamoddiśata ahaṃ nikṣepsyāmīti
children.translated_text: Now all of you, joining together, dictate to me, and I will set it down."

children.text: tatra pañcamātrāṇi śākyakumāraśatāny ekavacanodāhāreṇāpūrvacaritaṃ samuddiśanti sma bodhisattvaścāsaṃmūḍho nikṣipati sma
children.translated_text: There the five hundred Śākya princes, with a single utterance of speech, dictated unprecedented matters together, and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, without confusion, set them down.

children.text: evamaparyantāḥ sarvaśākyakumārāḥ atha paryantaśca bodhisattvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus all the Śākya princes were without limit, and yet the <s>Bodhisattva</s> reached the limit of them all.

children.text: tato 'rjuno gaṇakamahāmātra āścaryaprāpta ime gāthe 'bhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Arjuna</s>, the chief accountant, filled with wonder, spoke these verses:

children.text: jñānasya śīghratā sādhu buddhe saṃparipṛcchatā
children.translated_text: Excellent is the swiftness of knowledge in one who is questioned thoroughly by the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: pañcamātraśatānyete dhiṣṭhitā gaṇanāpathe ||
children.translated_text: these five hundred have been established on the path of calculation.

children.text: īdṛśī ca iyaṃ prajñā buddhirjñānaṃ smṛtirmatiḥ
children.translated_text: Such is this one's wisdom, intelligence, knowledge, memory, and understanding,

children.text: adyāpi śikṣate cāyaṃ gaṇitaṃ jñānasāgaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and still this ocean of knowledge learns arithmetic.

children.text: tataḥ sarvaśākyagaṇa āścaryaprāptaḥ paramavismayāpanno 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Then the whole assembly of the <s>Śākyas</s> was filled with wonder and seized by supreme amazement.

children.text: ekakaṇṭhāścemāṃ vācamabhāṣanta jayati jayati bhoḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ
children.translated_text: With one voice they spoke these words: "Victory, victory, sirs, to Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>!"

children.text: sarve cāsanebhya utthāya kṛtāñjalipuṭā bhūtvā bodhisattvaṃ namaskṛtya rājānaṃ śuddhodanametadavocan lābhāste mahārāja paramasulabdhāḥ yasya te putra evaṃ śīghralaghujavacapalaparipṛcchāpratibhāna iti ||
children.translated_text: And all of them rose from their seats, formed cups with their joined hands, bowed to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and said this to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: "Your gains are great, great king, exceedingly well gained, since your son has such quick, light, swift, agile readiness in answering questions."

children.text: atha sa rājā śuddhodano bodhisattvamevamāha śakyasi putra arjunena gaṇakamahāmātreṇa sārdhaṃ saṃkhyājñānakauśalyagaṇanāgatim anupraveṣṭuṃ tena hi gaṇyatām
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: "Can you, son, enter into the course of calculation and skill in numerical knowledge together with <s>Arjuna</s>, the chief accountant? If so, let the calculation be made."

children.text: athārjuno gaṇakamahāmātro bodhisattvamevamāha jānīṣe tvaṃ kumāra koṭiśatottarāṃ nāma gaṇanāgatiṃ bodhisattva āha śakyāmi deva
children.translated_text: Then <s>Arjuna</s>, the chief accountant, said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: "Do you know, prince, the course of calculation called 'beyond a hundred koṭis'?" The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said, "I can, sir."

children.text: āha jānāmyaham
children.translated_text: He said, "I know it."

children.text: āha kathaṃ punaḥ koṭiśatottarā gaṇanāgatiranupraveṣṭavyā bodhisattva āha śataṃ koṭīnāmayutaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: He said, "How, then, is the course of calculation beyond a hundred koṭis to be entered?" The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said, "A hundred koṭis is called an ayuta."

children.text: śatamayutānāṃ niyuto nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred ayutas is called a niyuta.

children.text: śataṃ niyutānāṃ kaṅkaraṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred niyutas is called a kaṅkara.

children.text: śataṃ kaṅkarāṇāṃ vivaraṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred kaṅkaras is called a vivara.

children.text: śataṃ vivarāṇām akṣobhyaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred vivaras is called an akṣobhya.

children.text: śatamakṣobhyāṇāṃ vivāhaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred akṣobhyas is called a vivāha.

children.text: śataṃ vivāhānāmutsaṅgaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred vivāhas is called an utsaṅga.

children.text: śatamutsaṅgānāṃ bahulaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred utsaṅgas is called a bahula.

children.text: śataṃ bahulānāṃ nāgabalaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred bahulas is called a nāgabala.

children.text: śataṃ nāgabalānāṃ tiṭilambhaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred nāgabalas is called a tiṭilambha.

children.text: śataṃ tiṭilambhānāṃ vyavasthānaprajñaptir nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred tiṭilambhas is called a vyavasthānaprajñapti.

children.text: śataṃ vyavasthānaprajñaptīnāṃ hetuhilaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred vyavasthānaprajñaptis is called a hetuhila.

children.text: śataṃ hetuhilānāṃ karakurnāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred hetuhilas is called a karakuru.

children.text: śataṃ karakūṇāṃ hetvindriyaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred karakurus is called a hetvindriya.

children.text: śataṃ hetvindriyāṇāṃ samāptalambhaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred hetvindriyas is called a samāptalambha.

children.text: śataṃ samāptalambhānāṃ gaṇanāgatirnāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred samāptalambhas is called a gaṇanāgati.

children.text: śataṃ gaṇanāgatīnāṃ niravadyaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred gaṇanāgatis is called a niravadya.

children.text: śataṃ niravadyānāṃ mudrābalaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred niravadyas is called a mudrābala.

children.text: śataṃ mudrābalānāṃ sarvabalaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred mudrābalas is called a sarvabala.

children.text: śataṃ sarvabalānāṃ visaṃjñāgatī nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred sarvabalas is called a visaṃjñāgati.

children.text: śataṃ visaṃjñāgatīnāṃ sarvasaṃjñā nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred visaṃjñāgatis is called a sarvasaṃjñā.

children.text: śataṃ sarvasaṃjñānāṃ vibhūtaṃgamā nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred sarvasaṃjñās is called a vibhūtaṃgamā.

children.text: śataṃ vibhūtaṃgamānāṃ tallakṣaṇaṃ nāmocyate
children.translated_text: A hundred vibhūtaṃgamās is called a tallakṣaṇa.

children.text: iti hi tallakṣaṇagaṇanayā sumeruparvatarājo lakṣanikṣepakriyayā parikṣayaṃ gacchet
children.translated_text: Thus, by the tallakṣaṇa reckoning, <s>Mount Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, would be exhausted by the act of depositing lakṣas.

children.text: ato 'pyuttari dhvajāgravatī nāma gaṇanā yasyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā lakṣanikṣepakriyayā parikṣayaṃ gaccheyuḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond that, too, there is a calculation called dhvajāgravatī, in which sands equal to those of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> would be exhausted by the act of depositing lakṣas.

children.text: ato 'pyuttari dhvajāgraniśāmaṇī nāma gaṇanā
children.translated_text: Beyond that, too, there is a calculation called dhvajāgraniśāmaṇī.

children.text: ato 'pyuttari vāhanaprajñaptirnāma
children.translated_text: Beyond that, too, there is one called vāhanaprajñapti.

children.text: ato 'pyuttari iṅgā nāma
children.translated_text: Beyond that, too, there is one called iṅgā.

children.text: ato 'pyuttari kuruṭu nāma
children.translated_text: Beyond that, too, there is one called kuruṭu.

children.text: ato 'pyuttari kuruṭāvi nāma
children.translated_text: Beyond that, too, there is one called kuruṭāvi.

children.text: ato 'pyuttari sarvanikṣepā nāma gaṇanā yasyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ daśa gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā lakṣanikṣepakriyayā parikṣayaṃ gaccheyuḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond that, too, there is a calculation called sarvanikṣepā, in which sands equal to ten <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers would be exhausted by the act of depositing lakṣas.

children.text: ato 'pyuttari agrasārā nāma gaṇanā yatra koṭīśataṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā lakṣanikṣepāḥ parikṣayaṃ gaccheyuḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond that, too, there is a calculation called agrasārā, where deposits of lakṣas equal to a hundred koṭis of <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river sands would be exhausted.

children.text: ato 'pyuttari paramāṇurajaḥpraveśānugatānāṃ gaṇanā yatra tathāgataṃ sthāpayitvā bodhimaṇḍavarāgragataṃ ca sarvadharmābhiṣekābhimukhaṃ bodhisattvaṃ nānyaḥ kaścitsattvaḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyate ya etāṃ gaṇanāṃ prajānāti anyatrāhaṃ vā yo vā syānmādṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond that, too, there is the calculation of those who have entered into atomic dust, where, apart from the <s>Tathāgata</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has reached the excellent seat of awakening and is facing the consecration into all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), no other being is found among the classes of beings who knows this calculation, except for me or someone who might be like me.

children.text: evaṃ caramabhāviko viniṣkrāntagṛhavāso bodhisattvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Such is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence, one who has gone forth from household life.

children.text: arjuno 'vocat kathaṃ kumāra paramāṇurajaḥpraveśagaṇanānupraveṣṭavyā bodhisattva āha sapta paramāṇurajāṃsyaṇuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s> said, "How, prince, is the calculation of entry into atomic dust to be entered?" The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said, "Seven particles of atomic dust make an aṇu."

children.text: saptāṇavastrutiḥ
children.translated_text: Seven aṇus make a truti.

children.text: saptatruterekaṃ vātāyanarajaḥ
children.translated_text: Seven trutis make one particle of dust in a window beam.

children.text: sapta vātāyanarajāṃsyekaṃ śaśarajaḥ
children.translated_text: Seven particles of dust in a window beam make one hare-dust particle.

children.text: sapta śaśarajāṃsyekameḍakarajaḥ
children.translated_text: Seven hare-dust particles make one ram-dust particle.

children.text: saptaiḍakarajāṃsyekaṃ gorajaḥ
children.translated_text: Seven ram-dust particles make one cow-dust particle.

children.text: sapta gorajāṃsyekaṃ likṣārajaḥ
children.translated_text: Seven cow-dust particles make one louse-dust particle.

children.text: sapta likṣāḥ sarṣapaḥ
children.translated_text: Seven lice make a mustard seed.

children.text: saptasarṣapādyavaḥ
children.translated_text: Seven mustard seeds make a barley grain.

children.text: saptayavādaṅgulīparva
children.translated_text: Seven barley grains make a finger-joint.

children.text: dvādaśāṅgulīparvāṇi vitastiḥ
children.translated_text: Twelve finger-joints make a span.

children.text: dve vitastī hastaḥ
children.translated_text: Two spans make a cubit.

children.text: catvāro hastā dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: Four cubits make a bow-length.

children.text: dhanuḥsahasraṃ mārgadhvajākrośaḥ
children.translated_text: A thousand bow-lengths make a wayside-banner krośa.

children.text: catvāraḥ krośā yojanam
children.translated_text: Four krośas make a yojana.

children.text: tatra ko yuṣmākaṃ yojanapiṇḍaṃ prajānāti kiyanti tāni paramāṇurajāṃsi bhavanti arjuno 'vocad ahameva tāvatkumāra saṃmohamāpannaḥ kimaṅga punarye cānye 'lpabuddhayaḥ
children.translated_text: "Now, who among you knows the mass of a yojana, how many particles of atomic dust there are?" <s>Arjuna</s> said, "Even I, prince, have fallen into confusion, much more those others of little intelligence."

children.text: nirdiśatu kumāro yojanapiṇḍaṃ kiyanti tāni paramāṇurajāṃsi bhavantīti
children.translated_text: "Let the prince explain the mass of a yojana, how many particles of atomic dust there are."

children.text: bodhisattvo 'vocat tatra yojanapiṇḍaḥ paramāṇurajasāṃ paripūrṇamakṣobhyanayutamekaṃ triṃśacca koṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭiśca koṭīśatāni dvātriṃśatiśca koṭyaḥ pañca ca daśaśatasahasrāṇi dvādaśa ca sahasrāṇi etāvān yojanapiṇḍaḥ paramāṇurajonikṣepasya
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: "There, the mass of a yojana, filled with particles of atomic dust, is one akṣobhya-nayuta, thirty-one koṭī-nayuta-hundred-thousands, sixty koṭī-hundreds, thirty-two koṭis, five ten-hundred-thousands, and twelve thousand. So great is the mass of a yojana for the depositing of particles of atomic dust.

children.text: anena praveśenāyaṃ jambudvīpaḥ saptayojanasahasrāṇi
children.translated_text: By this entry, this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> is seven thousand yojanas.

children.text: godānīyo 'ṣṭau yojanasahasrāṇi
children.translated_text: <s>Godānīya</s> is eight thousand yojanas.

children.text: pūrvavideho nava yojanasahasrāṇi
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrvavideha</s> is nine thousand yojanas.

children.text: uttarakurudvīpo daśayojanasahasrāṇi
children.translated_text: The continent of <s>Uttarakuru</s> is ten thousand yojanas.

children.text: anena praveśenemaṃ cāturdvīpakaṃ lokadhātuṃ pramukhaṃ kṛtvā paripūrṇakoṭīśataṃ cāturdvīpakānāṃ lokadhātūnāṃ yatra koṭīśataṃ mahāsamudrāṇām koṭīśataṃ cakravālamahācakravālānām koṭīśataṃ sumerūṇāṃ parvatarajānām koṭīśataṃ caturmahārājikānāṃ devānām koṭīśataṃ trayastriṃśānām koṭīśataṃ yāmānām koṭīśataṃ tuṣitānām koṭīśataṃ nirmāṇaratīnām koṭīśataṃ paranirmitavaśavartīnām koṭīśataṃ brahmakāyikānām koṭīśataṃ brahmapurohitānām koṭīśataṃ brahmapārṣadyānām koṭīśataṃ mahābrahmāṇām koṭīśataṃ parīttābhānām koṭīśataṃ apramāṇābhānām koṭīśataṃ ābhāsvarāṇām koṭīśataṃ parīttaśubhānām koṭīśataṃ apramāṇaśubhānām koṭīśataṃ śubhakṛtsnānām koṭīśataṃ anabhrakāṇām koṭīśataṃ puṇyaprasavānām koṭīśataṃ bṛhatphalānām koṭīśataṃ asaṃjñisattvānām koṭīśataṃ abṛhānām koṭīśataṃ atapānām koṭīśataṃ sudṛśānām koṭīśataṃ sudarśanānām koṭīśataṃ akaniṣṭhānāṃ devānām
children.translated_text: By this entry, taking this four-continent world-system first, there is a full hundred koṭis of four-continent world-systems: where there are a hundred koṭis of great oceans, a hundred koṭis of enclosing and great enclosing mountain-ranges, a hundred koṭis of <s>Sumeru</s> mountains, kings of mountains, a hundred koṭis of the gods of the Four Great Kings, a hundred koṭis of the Thirty-three gods, a hundred koṭis of the <s>Yāma</s> gods, a hundred koṭis of the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, a hundred koṭis of the gods Delighting in Creation, a hundred koṭis of the gods Who Control What Is Created by Others, a hundred koṭis of the Brahma-bodied gods, a hundred koṭis of Brahma's ministers, a hundred koṭis of Brahma's retinue, a hundred koṭis of Great Brahmās, a hundred koṭis of the gods of Limited Radiance, a hundred koṭis of the gods of Measureless Radiance, a hundred koṭis of the Radiant gods, a hundred koṭis of the gods of Limited Beauty, a hundred koṭis of the gods of Measureless Beauty, a hundred koṭis of the gods Complete in Beauty, a hundred koṭis of the Cloudless gods, a hundred koṭis of the Merit-born gods, a hundred koṭis of the Great-fruit gods, a hundred koṭis of non-percipient beings, a hundred koṭis of the <s>Abṛha</s> gods, a hundred koṭis of the <s>Atapa</s> gods, a hundred koṭis of the Fair-seeing gods, a hundred koṭis of the Fair-appearing gods, and a hundred koṭis of the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods.

children.text: ayamucyate trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhāturvipulaśca vistīrṇaśca
children.translated_text: This is called a three-thousand great-thousand world-system, vast and extensive.

children.text: sa yāvanti yojanaśatāni paramāṇurajāṃsi trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau yāvanti yojanasahasrāṇi yāvanti yojanakoṭayaḥ yāvanti yojananayutāni ........ peyālaṃ ............. yāvadyāvanto yojanāgrasārā gaṇanāḥ
children.translated_text: As many hundreds of yojanas of particles of atomic dust as there are in the three-thousand great-thousand world-system, as many thousands of yojanas, as many koṭis of yojanas, as many nayutas of yojanas ... abbreviated passage ... up to as many highest calculations of yojanas as there are,

children.text: kiyantyetāni paramāṇurajāṃsi ityāha
children.translated_text: how many are these particles of atomic dust? he asked.

children.text: saṃkhyāgaṇanā vyativṛttā hyeṣāṃ gaṇanānāṃ taducyate 'saṃkhyeyamiti
children.translated_text: The reckoning by number has passed beyond these calculations; therefore it is called incalculable.

children.text: ato 'saṃkhyeyatamāni paramāṇurajāṃsi yāni trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus the particles of atomic dust that exist in the three-thousand great-thousand world-system are most incalculable."

children.text: asmin khalu punargaṇanāparivarte bodhisattvena nirdiśyamāne arjuno gaṇakamahāmātraḥ sarvaśca śākyagaṇastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramudita āścaryādbhutaprāpto 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Now, while this chapter on calculation was being taught by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, the chief officer of calculators, and the whole assembly of Sakyas became pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with wonder and amazement.

children.text: te sarva ekaikairvastraiḥ sthitā abhūvan
children.translated_text: They all stood there with one garment each.

children.text: pariśiṣṭairvastrābharaṇairbodhisattvam abhicchādayanti sma ||
children.translated_text: With the remaining garments and ornaments they covered the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.
