children.text: atha khalvarjuno gaṇakamahāmātra ime gāthe 'bhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Arjuna</s>, the chief officer of calculators, spoke these verses:

children.text: koṭīśataṃ ca ayutā nayutāstathaiva niyutānu kaṅkaragatī tatha bimbarāśca
children.translated_text: "A hundred koṭis, ayutas and likewise nayutas, niyutas, the range of kaṅkaras, and bimbaras too:

children.text: akṣobhiṇī paramajñānu na me 'styato 'rtha mata uttare gaṇanamapratimasya jñānam ||
children.translated_text: Akṣobhiṇī, supreme knowledge: beyond this I have no command. My knowledge of calculating farther than that is no match for the incomparable one."

children.text: api ca bhoḥ śākyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And furthermore, O Sakyas:

children.text: trisāhasri rajāśrayantakā tṛṇavana oṣadhiyo jalasya bindūn
children.translated_text: "The dust at the end of the three-thousand world-system, the grasses and forests, the herbs, and the drops of water,

children.text: huṃkāreṇa nyaseya ekinaiṣo ko puni vismayu pañcabhiḥ śatebhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he could set down with a single roar. What wonder, then, is there in five hundred?"

children.text: tatra devamanujāḥ śatasahasrāṇi hāhākārakilikilāprakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇi prāmuñcan
children.translated_text: Thereupon gods and humans released hundreds of thousands of cries of astonishment, shouts of joy, and loud exclamations.

children.text: gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā imā gāthā abhāṣanta ||
children.translated_text: And the sons of the gods who were in the sky spoke these verses:

children.text: yāvanta sattva nikhilena triyadhvayuktāḥ cittāni caitasikasaṃjñi vitarkitāni
children.translated_text: "As many beings as are connected with the three times in their entirety, and as many thoughts, mental factors, perceptions, and reasonings as there are,

children.text: hīnāḥ praṇīta tatha saṃkṣipavikṣipā ye ekasmi cittaparivarti prajāni sarvān ||
children.translated_text: whether low or exalted, contracted or distracted, he knows them all in a single turn of thought."

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo 'bhibhūtāḥ sarve śākyakumārā abhūvan
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, all the Sakya princes were overcome.

children.text: bodhisattva eva viśiṣyate
children.translated_text: Only the <s>Bodhisattva</s> surpassed them.

children.text: tadanantaraṃ laṅghite plavite javite sarvatra bodhisattva eva viśiṣyate sma
children.translated_text: After that, in leaping, jumping, and running, everywhere the <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone surpassed them.

children.text: gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā imāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta ||
children.translated_text: And the sons of the gods who were in the sky spoke this verse:

children.text: vratatapasaguṇena saṃyamena kṣamadamamaitrabalena kalpakoṭyaḥ
children.translated_text: "Through the virtue of vows and austerities, through restraint, through the strength of patience, self-control, and loving-kindness for koṭis of kalpas,

children.text: atha kṛtulaghukāyacittanetā tasya javasya viśeṣatāṃ śṛṇotha ||
children.translated_text: his body, mind, and guiding faculty have been made light. Hear of the excellence of his speed.

children.text: iha gṛhagata yuṣme paśyathā sattvasāram api ca daśasu dikṣū gacchate 'yaṃ kṣaṇena
children.translated_text: You see here in the house this essence of beings; yet in a single instant he goes in the ten directions,

children.text: aparimitajinānāṃ pūjanāmeṣa kurvan maṇikanakavicitrairlokadhātuṣvanantā ||
children.translated_text: performing worship of immeasurable <s>Jinas</s> in endless world-systems adorned with jewels and gold.

children.text: na ca puna gati āgatiṃ ca asyā yūyaṃ prajānatha tāvadṛddhiprāpto
children.translated_text: And yet you do not know his going or coming, though he has attained such supernatural power.

children.text: ko 'tra javiti vismayo janeyā asadṛśa eṣa karotha gauravo 'smin ||
children.translated_text: What wonder should anyone feel here about his speed? He is unequalled; show reverence to him."

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā bodhisattva eva viśiṣyate sma ||
children.translated_text: Thus it was that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone surpassed them.

children.text: tatra śākyā āhur yuddheṣu tāvatkumāro viśeṣayitavyo jijñāsyaśca
children.translated_text: Then the Sakyas said, "The prince should indeed be made to excel and be tested in contests."

children.text: tatra bodhisattva ekānte sthito 'bhūt
children.translated_text: There the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stood to one side.

children.text: tāni ca pañcamātrāṇi śākyakumāraśatāni yugapadyudhyanti sma ||
children.translated_text: And those five hundred or so Sakya princes fought all at once.

children.text: iti hi dvātriṃśacchākyakumārāḥ sālambhāya sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus thirty-two Sakya princes stood ready for support.

children.text: tadā nandaścānandaśca bodhisattvamabhigatau sālambhāya
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Ānanda</s> approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in order to take hold of him.

children.text: tau samanantaraṃ spṛṣṭāveva bodhisattvena pāṇinā
children.translated_text: No sooner had they been touched by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s hand

children.text: tau bodhisattvasya balaṃ tejaścāsahamānau dharaṇītale prapatitāvabhūtām
children.translated_text: than, unable to withstand the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s strength and splendor, the two fell down on the surface of the earth.

children.text: tadanantaraṃ devadattaḥ kumāro garvitaśca mānī ca balavāneva tabdhaḥ śākyamānena ca tabdho bodhisattvena sārdhaṃ vispardhamānaḥ sarvāvantaṃ raṅgamaṇḍalaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vikrīḍamāno bodhisattvamabhipatati sma
children.translated_text: After that the prince <s>Devadatta</s>, proud, conceited, and indeed strong, stiff with arrogance and stiff with the pride of the <s>Śākyas</s>, competing with the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, circumambulated the whole arena and, sporting, rushed at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: atha bodhisattvo 'saṃbhrānta evātvaran dakṣiṇena pāṇinā salīlaṃ devadattaṃ kumāraṃ gṛhītvā trirgaganatale parivartya mānanigrahārthamavihiṃsābuddhyā maitreṇa cittena dharaṇītale nikṣipati sma
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, unperturbed and without haste, gracefully took the prince <s>Devadatta</s> with his right hand, whirled him three times in the sky, and, in order to subdue his pride, with no thought of injury and with a mind of friendliness, set him down on the surface of the earth.

children.text: na cāsya kāyaṃ vyābādhate sma ||
children.translated_text: And he did not hurt his body.

children.text: tato bodhisattvo 'pyāha alamalamanena vivādena
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> too said, "Enough, enough of this quarrel.

children.text: sarva eva ekībhūtvā idānīṃ sālambhāyāgacchateti ||
children.translated_text: Now all of you, having become united, come to take hold of me."

children.text: atha te sarve harṣitā bhūtvā bodhisattvamabhinipatitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then all of them, delighted, rushed upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: te samanantaraspṛṣṭā bodhisattvena bodhisattvasya śriyaṃ tejaśca kāyabalaṃ sthāmaṃ cāsahamānāḥ spṛṣṭamātrā eva bodhisattvena dharaṇitale prāpatan
children.translated_text: No sooner had they been touched by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> than, unable to withstand the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s majesty, splendor, bodily strength, and power, at the mere touch of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> they fell upon the surface of the earth.

children.text: tatra marunmanujaśatasahasrāṇi hīhīkārakilakilāprakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇyakārṣuḥ
children.translated_text: There, hundreds of thousands of gods and humans made hundreds of thousands of cries of "hī hī," shouts, and clamorous exclamations.

children.text: gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā mahāntaṃ puṣpavarṣamabhipravṛṣyaikasvareṇemāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta ||
children.translated_text: And the sons of the gods who were in the sky poured down a great rain of flowers and, with one voice, spoke these verses:

children.text: yāvanta sattvanayutā daśasū diśāsu te duṣṭamallamahanagnasamā bhaveyuḥ
children.translated_text: "As many myriads of beings as there are in the ten directions, were they like greatly wicked wrestlers and mighty naked ascetics,

children.text: ekakṣaṇena nipateyu nararṣabhasya saṃspṛṣṭamātra nipateyu kṣitītalesmiṃ ||
children.translated_text: if they were to fall upon the bull among men in a single instant, merely touched by him they would fall here upon the ground.

children.text: merūḥ sumeru tatha vajrakacakravālāḥ ye cānya parvata kvaciddaśasū diśāsu
children.translated_text: Mount <s>Meru</s>, <s>Sumeru</s>, the adamantine mountain-ranges, and whatever other mountains there are anywhere in the ten directions,

children.text: pāṇibhya gṛhya masicūrṇanibhāṃ prakuryāt ko vismayo manujaāśrayake asāre ||
children.translated_text: he could take in his hands and make like powdered soot; what wonder is there with regard to this frail human support?

children.text: eṣo drumendrapravare mahaduṣṭamallaṃ māraṃ sasainyasabalaṃ sahayaṃ dhvajāgre
children.translated_text: At the foot of the best of trees, he will strike down the greatly wicked wrestler <s>Māra</s>, together with his army, his forces, his horses, and his banner-top;

children.text: maitrībalena vinihatya hi kṛṣṇabandhuṃ yāvat spṛśiṣyati anuttarabodhi sāntam ||
children.translated_text: having defeated the dark kinsman by the power of friendliness, he will then touch unsurpassed, peaceful awakening."

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā bodhisattva eva viśiṣyate sma ||
children.translated_text: Having done this, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was indeed distinguished above the rest.

children.text: atha daṇḍapāṇiḥ śākyakumārānetadavocaj jijñāsitamidaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> said this to the <s>Śākya</s> princes: "This has been tested and seen.

children.text: hantedānīmiṣukṣepam upadarśayateti
children.translated_text: Come now, show the shooting of arrows."

children.text: tatra ānandasya dvayoḥ krośayorayasmayī bherī lakṣaṃ sthāpitābhūt
children.translated_text: There, for <s>Ānanda</s>, an iron drum had been set up as a target at a distance of two krośas.

children.text: asyānantaraṃ devadattasya caturṣu krośeṣvayasmayī bherī sthāpitābhūt
children.translated_text: Next to that, for <s>Devadatta</s>, an iron drum had been set up at four krośas.

children.text: daṇḍapāṇeryojanadvaye 'yasmayī bherī sthāpitābhūt
children.translated_text: For <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>, an iron drum had been set up at two yojanas.

children.text: bodhisattvasya daśasu krośeṣvayasmayī bherī sthāpitābhūt
children.translated_text: For the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, an iron drum had been set up at ten krośas.

children.text: tasyānantaraṃ saptatālā ayasmayī varāhapratimā yantrayuktā sthāpitābhūt
children.translated_text: Beyond that, seven iron images of boars, furnished with mechanisms, had been set up in a row like palm trees.

children.text: tatrānandena dvābhyāṃ krośābhyāṃ bheryāhatābhūt tatottari na śaknoti sma
children.translated_text: There <s>Ānanda</s> struck the drum from two krośas away, but he could not do more than that.

children.text: devadattena catuḥkrośasthā bheryāhatābhūt nottari śaknoti sma
children.translated_text: <s>Devadatta</s> struck the drum standing four krośas away, but he could not do more.

children.text: sundaranandena ṣaṭkrośasthā bheryāhatābhūt nottari śaknoti sma
children.translated_text: <s>Sundarananda</s> struck the drum standing six krośas away, but he could not do more.

children.text: daṇḍapāṇinā dviyojanasthā bheryāhatābhūt nirviddhā ca nottari śaknoti sma
children.translated_text: <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> struck the drum standing two yojanas away and pierced it, but he could not do more.

children.text: tatra bodhisattvasya yadyadeva dhanurupānamyate sma tattadeva vicchidyate sma
children.translated_text: Then whatever bow was brought near for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, that very bow broke apart.

children.text: tato bodhisattva āha astīha deva nagare kiṃcidanyaddhanuryanmamāropaṇaṃ saheta kāyabalasthāmaṃ ca rājāhāsti putra
children.translated_text: So the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said, "Is there in this city, lord, any other bow that could withstand my stringing it and the power of my bodily strength?" The king said, "There is, son."

children.text: kumāra āha kva taddeva rājā āha tava putra pitāmahaḥ siṃhahanurnāmābhūt tasya yaddhanustadeva tarhi devakule gandhamālyairmahīyate
children.translated_text: The prince said, "Where is it, lord?" The king said, "Your grandfather, son, was named <s>Siṃhahanu</s>; that bow of his is now honored in the temple of the gods with perfumes and garlands.

children.text: na punastatkaścicchaknoti sma taddhanurāropayituṃ prāgeva pūrayitum
children.translated_text: But no one is able to string that bow, much less to draw it fully."

children.text: bodhisattva āha ānīyatāṃ deva taddhanuḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said, "Let that bow be brought, lord.

children.text: jijñāsiṣyāmahe ||
children.translated_text: We shall test it."

children.text: tāvadyāvattaddhanur upanāmitamabhūt
children.translated_text: Thereupon that bow was brought near.

children.text: tatra sarve śākyakumārāḥ parameṇāpi prayatnena vyāyacchamānā na śaknuvanti sma taddhanurāropayituṃ prāgeva pūrayitum
children.translated_text: Then all the <s>Śākya</s> princes, though exerting themselves with the utmost effort, were unable to string that bow, much less draw it fully.

children.text: tatastaddhanurdaṇḍapāṇeḥ śākyasyopanāmitamabhūt
children.translated_text: Then that bow was brought near to <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s>.

children.text: atha daṇḍapāṇiḥ śākyaḥ sarvaṃ kāyabalasthāma saṃjanayya taddhanurāropayitumārabdho 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s>, summoning all his bodily strength and power, began to string that bow.

children.text: na ca śaknoti sma
children.translated_text: But he could not.

children.text: yāvadbodhisattvasyopanāmitamabhūt
children.translated_text: At last it was brought near to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: tadbodhisattvo gṛhītvā āsanād anuttiṣṭhannevārdhaparyaṅkaṃ kṛtvā vāmena pāṇinā gṛhītvā dakṣiṇena pāṇinā ekāṅgulyagreṇāropitavānabhūt
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> took it and, without even rising from his seat, sitting in a half-cross-legged posture, held it with his left hand and strung it with the tip of one finger of his right hand.

children.text: tasya dhanuṣa āropyamāṇasya sarvaṃ kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ śabdenābhivijñaptamabhūt
children.translated_text: As that bow was being strung, the whole great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was made aware by the sound.

children.text: sarvanagarajanaśca vihvalībhūto 'nyonyamapṛcchat kasyāyamevaṃvidhaḥ śabda iti
children.translated_text: All the people of the city, bewildered, asked one another, "Whose sound is this, of such a kind?"

children.text: anye tadavocan siddhārthena kila kumāreṇa paitāmahadhanurāropitaṃ tasyāyaṃ śabda iti
children.translated_text: Others said to them, "It is said that the prince <s>Siddhārtha</s> has strung his grandfather's bow; this is its sound."

children.text: tatra devamanujaśatasahasrāṇi hāhākārakilikilāprakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇi prāmuñcan
children.translated_text: There, hundreds of thousands of gods and humans released hundreds of thousands of cries of wonder, shouts, and clamorous exclamations.

children.text: gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ taṃ ca mahāntaṃ janakāyaṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣanta ||
children.translated_text: And the sons of the gods, standing in the expanse of the sky, addressed King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and that great crowd of people with a verse:

children.text: yatha pūrita eṣa dhanurmuninā na ca utthitu āsani no ca bhūmī
children.translated_text: "As this bow has been drawn by the sage, while he did not rise from his seat and the earth did not move,

children.text: niḥsaṃśayu pūrṇamabhiprāyu munirlaghu bheṣyati jitva ca māracamūm ||
children.translated_text: the sage's aim is undoubtedly fulfilled; he will soon conquer the army of <s>Māra</s>."

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvastaddhanuḥ pūrayitveṣuṃ gṛhītvā tādṛśena balasthāmnā tamiṣuṃ kṣipati sma yena yā cānandasya bherī yā ca devadattasya yāvatsundaranandasya yāvaddaṇḍapāṇestāḥ sarvā abhinirbhidya tāṃ ca daśakrośasthāṃ svakāmayasmayīṃ bherīṃ saptatālāṃ yantrayuktavarāhapratimāmabhinirbhidya sa iṣurdharaṇītalaṃ praviśya adarśanābhāso 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, after drawing that bow and taking up an arrow, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with such power and strength, shot the arrow so that it pierced all the drums, from <s>Ānanda</s>'s and <s>Devadatta</s>'s as far as <s>Sundarananda</s>'s and <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>'s; and, after piercing that iron drum set ten krośas away, the seven-palmyra-high mechanical boar image, the arrow entered the surface of the earth and disappeared from sight.

children.text: yatra ca pradeśe sa iṣurbhūmitalaṃ bhittvā praviṣṭastasmin pradeśe kūpaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ yadadyatve 'pi śarakūpa ityabhidhīyate
children.translated_text: And in the place where that arrow split the surface of the earth and entered, a well came into being, which even today is called the Arrow Well.

children.text: tatra devamanuṣyaśatasahasrāṇi hīhīkārakilikilāprakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇi prāmuñcan
children.translated_text: There hundreds of thousands of gods and humans released hundreds of thousands of cries of "hī hī," jubilant shouts, and cheers.

children.text: sarvaśca śākyagaṇo vismito 'bhūd āścaryaprāpta āścaryaṃ bhoḥ
children.translated_text: And the whole assembly of the <s>Śākyas</s> was astonished and filled with wonder: "Wonderful, sirs!

children.text: na ca nāma anena yogyā kṛtā idaṃ cedṛśaṃ śilpakauśalam
children.translated_text: He has not even undergone training, and yet there is such skill in the arts."

children.text: gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ taṃ ca mahāntaṃ janakāyamevamāhuḥ ko 'tra vismayo manujāḥ
children.translated_text: And the sons of the gods, standing in the expanse of the sky, said this to King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and that great crowd of people: "What is there to wonder at here, O humans?

children.text: tatkasmāt ||
children.translated_text: Why is that?

children.text: eṣa dharaṇimaṇḍe pūrvabuddhāsanasthaḥ śamathadhanu gṛhītvā śūnyanairātmabāṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Standing on the seat of former Buddhas on the circle of the earth, taking up the bow of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquillity) with arrows of emptiness and selflessness,

children.text: kleśaripu nihatvā dṛṣṭijālaṃ ca bhittvā śivavirajamaśokāṃ prāpsyate bodhimagryām ||
children.translated_text: having struck down the enemy of the afflictions and split apart the net of views, he will attain the highest <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), auspicious, stainless, and free from sorrow."

children.text: evamuktvā te devaputrā bodhisattvaṃ divyaiḥ puṣpairabhyavakīrya prākrāman ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, those sons of the gods scattered divine flowers over the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and departed.

children.text: evaṃ laṅghite prāgval lipimudrāgaṇanāsaṃkhyasālambhadhanurvede javite plavite taraṇe iṣvastre hastigrīvāyāmaśvapṛṣṭhe rathe dhanuṣkalāpe sthairyasthāmni suśaurye bāhuvyāyāme aṅkuśagrahe pāśagrahe udyāne niryāṇe avayāne muṣṭibandhe padabandhe śikhābandhe chedye bhedye dālane sphālane akṣuṇṇavedhitve marmavedhitve śabdavedhitve dṛḍhaprahāritve akṣakrīḍāyāṃ kāvyakaraṇe granthe citre rūpe rūpakarmaṇi dhīte agnikarmaṇi vīṇāyāṃ vādye nṛtye gīte paṭhite ākhyāne hāsye lāsye nāṭye viḍambite mālyagrathane saṃvāhite maṇirāge vastrarāge māyākṛte svapnādhyāye śakunirute strīlakṣaṇe puruṣalakṣaṇe aśvalakṣaṇe hastilakṣaṇe golakṣaṇe ajalakṣaṇe miśralakṣaṇe kauṭubheśvaralakṣaṇe nirghaṇṭe nigame purāṇe itihāse vede vyākaraṇe nirukte śikṣāyāṃ chandasvinyāṃ yajñakalpe jyotiṣe sāṃkhye yoge kriyākalpe vaiśike vaiśeṣike arthavidyāyāṃ bārhaspatye āmbhirye āsurye mṛgapakṣirute hetuvidyāyāṃ jalayantre madhūcchiṣṭakṛte sūcikarmaṇi vidalakarmaṇi patrachede gandhayuktau ityevamādyāsu sarvakarmakalāsu laukikādiṣu divyamānuṣyakātikrāntāsu sarvatra bodhisattva eva viśiṣyate sma ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in leaping and, as before, in writing, seals, calculation, enumeration, archery with supports, running, jumping, swimming, missile-craft, riding on an elephant's neck, on horseback, and in a chariot, in the array of bows, steadiness and strength, fine courage, arm exercise, handling the goad, handling the noose, advancing, setting out, dismounting, fist-locks, foot-locks, topknot-binding, cutting, piercing, splitting, bursting open, hitting what was unbroken, hitting vital points, hitting by sound, striking firmly, dice play, composing poetry, texts, painting, form, image-work, study, fire-work, the vīṇā, instrumental music, dancing, singing, recitation, narration, humor, graceful dance, drama, mimicry, garland-weaving, massage, coloring jewels, dyeing cloth, magic, dream interpretation, bird cries, the marks of women, the marks of men, the marks of horses, the marks of elephants, the marks of cattle, the marks of goats, mixed marks, the marks of Kauṭubheśvara, lexicons, Vedic texts, Purāṇas, Itihāsas, the Veda, grammar, etymology, phonetics, metrics, sacrificial procedure, astrology, Sāṃkhya, Yoga, rites, Vaiśika, Vaiśeṣika, the science of polity and wealth, Bārhaspatya, Āmbhīrya, Āsurya, the cries of beasts and birds, logic, water-machines, work in beeswax, needlework, splitting-work, leaf-cutting, and the art of perfumes, and in all such crafts, whether worldly or beyond divine and human arts, everywhere the <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone excelled.

children.text: atha khalu punastena samayena daṇḍapāṇiḥ śākyaḥ svāṃ duhitaraṃ gopāṃ śākyakanyāṃ bodhisattvāya prādāt
children.translated_text: Then again, at that time, <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s> gave his own daughter <s>Gopā</s>, a <s>Śākya</s> maiden, to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: sā ca rājñā śuddhodanenānupūrveṇa bodhisattvasya vṛtābhūt ||
children.translated_text: And in due order she had been chosen by King <s>Śuddhodana</s> for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: tatra khalvapi bodhisattvaś caturaśītistrīsahasrāṇāṃ madhye prāpto lokānubhavanatayā ramamāṇaṃ krīḍayantaṃ paricārayantamātmānamupadarśayati sma
children.translated_text: There too the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, among eighty-four thousand women, showed himself, in conformity with worldly experience, as enjoying himself, playing, and being attended upon.

children.text: tāsāṃ caturaśīteḥ strīsahasrāṇāṃ gopā śākyakanyā sarvāsāmagramahiṣyabhiṣiktābhūt ||
children.translated_text: Among those eighty-four thousand women, <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden was consecrated as foremost queen over them all.

children.text: tatra khalvapi gopā śākyakanyā na kaṃcid dṛṣṭvā vadanaṃ chādayati sma śvaśrūṃ vā śvaśuraṃ vāntarjanaṃ vā
children.translated_text: There too <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden, on seeing anyone, did not cover her face, whether it was her mother-in-law, her father-in-law, or a member of the inner household.

children.text: te tāmupadhyāyanti sma vicārayanti sma navavadhūkā hi nāma pratilīnā tiṣṭhati iyaṃ punarvivṛtaiva sarvadā iti
children.translated_text: They considered and discussed her, saying, "A new bride normally stays withdrawn, but this one is always unveiled."

children.text: tato gopā śākyakanyā etāṃ prakṛtiṃ śrutvā sarvasyāntarjanasya purataḥ sthitvā imā gāthā abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden, hearing this judgment, stood before the whole inner household and spoke these verses:

children.text: vivṛtaḥ śobhate ārya āsanasthānacaṃkrame
children.translated_text: "A noble person shines unveiled, whether on a seat, in a place, or on a walkway,

children.text: maṇiratnaṃ dhvajāgre vā bhāsamānaṃ prabhāsvaram ||
children.translated_text: like a jewel set on the top of a banner, shining and radiant.

children.text: gacchan vai śobhate ārya āgacchannapi śobhate
children.translated_text: A noble person shines while going, and shines too while coming;

children.text: sthito vātha niṣaṇṇo vā āryaḥ sarvatra śobhate ||
children.translated_text: whether standing or seated, a noble person shines everywhere.

children.text: kathayaṃ śobhate āryastūṣṇībhūto 'pi śobhate
children.translated_text: A noble person shines while speaking, and shines even when silent,

children.text: kalaviṅko yathā pakṣī darśanena svareṇa vā ||
children.translated_text: like a kalaviṅka bird, through its appearance or its voice.

children.text: kuśacīranivasto vā mandacailaḥ kṛśaṃtanuḥ
children.translated_text: Whether dressed in kuśa-grass bark-cloth, poorly clothed, or thin-bodied,

children.text: śobhate 'sau svatejena guṇavān guṇabhūṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: such a person shines by his own radiance, virtuous and adorned with virtues.

children.text: sarveṇa śobhate āryo yasya pāpaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: A noble person in whom no evil is found shines in every way;

children.text: kiyadvibhūṣito bālaḥ pāpacārī na śobhate ||
children.translated_text: however much a foolish evildoer may be adorned, he does not shine."

children.text: ye kilbiṣāḥ svahṛdaye madhurāsu vācaṃ kumbho viṣasmi pariṣiktu yathāmṛtena
children.translated_text: Those who are sinful in their own hearts, though their speech is sweet, are like a pot of poison sprinkled with nectar.

children.text: dusparśa śailaśilavat kaṭhināntarātmā sarpasya vā virasu darśana tādṛśānām ||
children.translated_text: Their inner nature is hard like the stone of a mountain, hard to touch; the sight of such people is tasteless, like that of a snake.

children.text: sarveṣu te namiṣu sarvamupaiti saumyāḥ sarveṣu tirthamiva sarvagopajīvyāḥ
children.translated_text: But the noble and gentle ones are humble toward all, and everything comes well to them among all; they are like a holy ford, to be lived from by all.

children.text: dadhikṣīrapūrṇaghaṭatulya sadaiva āryā śuddhātmadarśanu sumaṅgalu tādṛśānām ||
children.translated_text: Always like jars filled with curds and milk, the sight of such pure-souled noble ones is very auspicious.

children.text: yaiḥ pāpamitra parivarjita dīrgharātraṃ kalyāṇamitraratanaiśca parigṛhītāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who for a long night have avoided evil friends and have been accepted by jewel-like good friends,

children.text: pāpaṃ vivarjayi niveśayi buddhadharme saphalaṃ sumaṅgalu sudarśanu tādṛśānām ||
children.translated_text: who abandon evil and settle themselves in the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>dharma</s> (teaching): the sight of such fruitful, very auspicious people is excellent.

children.text: ye kāyasaṃvṛta susaṃvṛtakāyadoṣāḥ ye vācasaṃvṛta sadānavakīrṇavācaḥ
children.translated_text: Those whose bodies are restrained, whose bodily faults are well restrained, whose speech is restrained and whose words are never scattered,

children.text: guptendriyā sunibhṛtāśca manaḥprasannāḥ kiṃ tādṛśāna vadanaṃ pratichādayitvā ||
children.translated_text: whose senses are guarded, who are very composed and whose minds are serene: why should the faces of such people be covered?

children.text: vastrā sahasra yadi chādayi ātmabhāvaṃ cittaṃ ca yeṣu vivṛtaṃ na hirī na lajjā
children.translated_text: Even if some cover their own bodies with a thousand garments, if their minds are uncovered and there is no modesty or shame in them,

children.text: na ca yeṣu īdṛśa guṇā napi satyavākyaṃ nagne vinagnatara te vicaranti loke ||
children.translated_text: and if such qualities and truthful speech are not in them, they wander in the world naked, more naked than the naked.

children.text: yāścittagupta satatendriyasaṃyatāśca na ca anyasattvamanasā svapatīna tuṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: But those whose minds are guarded, whose senses are constantly restrained, and who are satisfied with their own husbands, not with other beings in thought,

children.text: ādityacandrasadṛśā vivṛtaprakāśā kiṃ tādṛśāna vadanaṃ pratichādayitvā ||
children.translated_text: are open and bright like the sun and moon; why should the faces of such women be covered?

children.text: api ca ||
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: jānanti āśayu mama ṛṣayo mahātmā paracittabuddhikuśalāstatha devasaṃghāḥ
children.translated_text: The great-souled seers, skilled in knowing the minds of others, and likewise the hosts of gods know my intention.

children.text: yatha mahya śīlaguṇasaṃvaru apramādo vadanāvaguṇṭhanamataḥ prakaromi kiṃ me ||
children.translated_text: Since I have moral virtue, qualities, restraint, and heedfulness, what need have I to make a covering for my face?

children.text: aśrauṣīdbhikṣavo rājā śuddhodano nāma gopāyāḥ śākyakanyāyā imāmevaṃrūpāṃ sarvāṃ gāthāṃ pratibhānanirdeśam
children.translated_text: Monks, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> heard this whole verse-speech of just such a kind, this inspired declaration, from <s>Gopā</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> maiden.

children.text: śrutvā ca punastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto 'nekaratnapratyuptena dūṣyayugena koṭīśatasahasramūlyena ca muktāhāreṇābhijātalohitamuktāpratyuptayā ca suvarṇamālayā gopāṃ śākyakanyām abhicchādyainamudānamudānayati sma ||
children.translated_text: And when he had heard it, pleased, uplifted, delighted, glad, and filled with joy and happiness, he covered <s>Gopā</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> maiden, with a pair of garments set with many jewels, with a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand koṭis, and with a golden garland set with fine red pearls, and he uttered this exclamation:

children.text: yathā ca putro mama bhūṣito guṇais tathā ca kanyā svaguṇā prabhāsate
children.translated_text: "Just as my son is adorned with virtues, so this maiden shines by her own virtues.

children.text: viśuddhasattvau tadubhau samāgatau sameti sarpir yatha sarpimaṇḍe ||
children.translated_text: Those two beings of pure nature have come together, as clarified butter joins with the essence of clarified butter."

children.text: Chapter 13

iti hi bhikṣava ātmarutaharṣamudīrayanta āgatā āsan bodhisattvasyāntaḥpuramadhyagatasya anekairdevair nāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśakrabrahmalokapālāḥ ye bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe autsukyamāpatsyante sma ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, while uttering cries of delight arising from their own joy, many gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the world-protectors came to the inner apartments where the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was, eager to perform acts of worship for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: tatra bhikṣavo apareṇa samayena saṃbahulānāṃ devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśakrabrahmalokapālānām etadabhavad aticiraṃ batāyaṃ satpuruṣo 'ntaḥpure vilambitaḥ
children.translated_text: There, monks, at another time this thought occurred to many gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and world-protectors: "Alas, this good man has delayed too long in the inner apartments.

children.text: ye cāsyeme dīrgharātraṃ paripācitāḥ sattvāścaturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhirdānena priyavākyenārthakriyayā samānārthatayā yasya bodhiprāptasya dharmadeśitamājñāsyanti tatsahaiva ca tāni dharmabhājanāni sarvāṇyantarhitāni bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: And these beings of his, matured for a long night by the four means of attraction - giving, pleasant speech, beneficial action, and sharing the same aim - who will understand his teaching of the <s>dharma</s> when he has attained awakening, those very vessels of <s>dharma</s> will all have disappeared.

children.text: bodhisattvaśca paścādabhiniṣkramyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate ||
children.translated_text: And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, going forth only afterward, will awaken to unsurpassed complete and perfect awakening."

children.text: tataste sagauravāḥ sapratīkṣāḥ prāñjalībhūtā bodhisattvaṃ namasyanti sma
children.translated_text: Then, full of reverence and expectation, with joined palms, they paid homage to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: evamabhiprāyāścodīkṣamāṇāḥ sthitā abhūvan kadā ca nāma tadbhaviṣyati yadvayaṃ varapravaraṃ śuddhasattvamabhiniṣkrāmantaṃ paśyema abhiniṣkramya ca tasmin mahādrumarājamūle 'bhiniṣadya sabalaṃ māraṃ dharṣayitvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaṃ daśabhistathāgatabalaiḥ samanvāgataṃ caturbhiśca tathāgatavaiśāradyaiḥ samanvāgatamaṣṭādaśabhiścāveṇikairbuddhadharmaiḥ samanvāgataṃ triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāramanuttaraṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayantaṃ mahatā buddhavikrīḍitena sadevamānuṣāsuralokaṃ yathādhimuktyā subhāṣitena saṃtoṣayantamiti ||
children.translated_text: And they stood watching with this intention: "When indeed will that happen, that we may see the best and foremost pure being going forth, and, after he has gone forth and sat beneath that great king of trees, defeating <s>Māra</s> together with his army, awakened to unsurpassed complete and perfect awakening, endowed with the ten powers of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, endowed with the four fearlessnesses of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, endowed with the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas, setting in motion the unsurpassed wheel of <s>dharma</s> with three turnings and twelve aspects, and, with the great play of a <s>Buddha</s>, satisfying the world with its gods, humans, and asuras according to their inclinations by well-spoken speech?"

children.text: tatra bhikṣavo bodhisattvo dīrgharātramasaṃkhyeyān kalpānupādāya satataṃ samitamaparapraṇeyo 'bhūt
children.translated_text: There, monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, throughout the long night beginning from countless kalpas, had constantly and continually been one who was not led by another.

children.text: sarvalaukikalokottareṣu dharmeṣu svayamevācāryaḥ sarvakuśalamūladharmacaryāsu dīrghakālaṃ ca kālajño velājñaḥ samayajño 'bhūdacyuto 'bhijñaḥ pañcābhijñābhiḥ samanvāgato 'bhūt
children.translated_text: In all worldly and supramundane <s>dharmas</s> he was himself the teacher; in all practices of wholesome roots and <s>dharmas</s>, for a long time, he knew the time, knew the occasion, and knew the proper moment; he was unfailing, possessed of superknowledge, and endowed with the five superknowledges.

children.text: ṛddhipādavikrīḍataḥ sarvendriyakuśalaḥ kālākālajñaḥ kālaveṣī mahāsāgara iva prāptāṃ velāṃ nātikrāmati sma
children.translated_text: Sporting in the bases of miraculous power, skilled in all faculties, knowing the right and wrong time, seeking the proper time, he did not overstep the arrived occasion, like the great ocean.

children.text: so 'bhijñajñānabalena samanvāgataḥ svayameva sarvaṃ jānāti sma
children.translated_text: Endowed with the power of superknowledge and knowledge, he himself knew everything.

children.text: asyāyaṃ kālaḥ pragrahasya ayaṃ kālo nigrahasya ayaṃ kālaḥ saṃgrahasya ayaṃ kālo 'nugrahasya ayaṃ kāla upekṣāyā ayaṃ kālo bhāṣitasya ayaṃ kālastūṣṇīṃbhāvasya ayaṃ kālo niṣkramyasya ayaṃ kālaḥ pravrajyāyā ayaṃ kālaḥ svādhyāyasya ayaṃ kālo yoniśomanaskārasya ayaṃ kālaḥ pravivekasya ayaṃ kālaḥ kṣatriyaparṣadamupasaṃkramituṃ ............. peyālaṃ ............... yāvadayaṃ kālo brāhmaṇagṛhapatiparṣadamupasaṃkramitum ayaṃ kālo devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśakrabrahmalokapālabhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāparṣadam upasaṃkramitum ayaṃ kālo dharmadeśanāyā ayaṃ kālaḥ pratisaṃlayanasya
children.translated_text: For him this was the time for encouragement, this the time for restraint, this the time for gathering in, this the time for favoring, this the time for equanimity, this the time for speaking, this the time for becoming silent, this the time for departure, this the time for going forth, this the time for recitation, this the time for careful attention, this the time for seclusion, this the time to approach an assembly of kṣatriyas ... an abridgement ... up to: this was the time to approach an assembly of brahmins and householders; this the time to approach assemblies of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, world-protectors, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen; this the time for teaching the <s>dharma</s> (teaching), and this the time for withdrawal.

children.text: sarvatra bodhisattvo nityakālaṃ kālajño bhavati sma kālaveṣī ||
children.translated_text: In every situation the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was always one who knew the proper time, one who sought the proper time.

children.text: atha ca punarbhikṣavo dharmatāpratilambha eṣa ca caramabhāvikānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ yadavaśyaṃ daśadiglokadhātusthitairbuddhair bhagavadbhirantaḥpuramadhyagatāḥ saṃgītitūryanirnāditairebhirevaṃrūpairdharmamukhaiḥ saṃcoditavyā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: And furthermore, monks, this is the attainment of the nature of things for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in their final existence: while they are within the inner palace, they must necessarily be urged on by the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> dwelling in the world-realms of the ten directions, with musical instruments sounding together, through such gateways of <s>dharma</s> (teaching) as these.

children.text: tatredamucyate ||
children.translated_text: On this point this is said:

children.text: ye sattvāgrā daśadigloke teṣu viśeṣāttatra ratituriyaiḥ
children.translated_text: Those foremost beings in the worlds of the ten directions, there especially with delightful instruments,

children.text: gāthā gītā ima ratimadhurā saṃcodentī naravarapravaram ||
children.translated_text: with these verses and songs sweet with delight, exhort the best of excellent men.

children.text: pūrvi tubhyaṃ ayu kṛtu praṇidhī dṛṣṭvā sattvān duḥkhaśatabharitān
children.translated_text: Formerly you made this vow, after seeing beings burdened with hundreds of sufferings:

children.text: lenaṃ trāṇaṃ jaganijaśaraṇe bheṣye nāthu hitakaru paramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'I shall be a refuge, a protection, a shelter for the world; I shall be a lord, the supreme benefactor through compassion.'

children.text: sādho vīrā smara cari purimāṃ yā te āsījjagahitapraṇidhiḥ
children.translated_text: Good, hero, remember your former course, the vow for the world's welfare that was yours.

children.text: kālo velā ayu tava samayo niṣkramyāhī ṛṣivarapravarā ||
children.translated_text: The time, the hour, this is your occasion; go forth, best of excellent sages.

children.text: yasyārthe te dhanavara vividhā tyaktā pūrve śirakaracaraṇā
children.translated_text: For the sake of that, various excellent riches were formerly given up by you, as were head, hands, and feet,

children.text: bheṣye buddho naramarudamako lokasyāgro guṇaśatanicitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>, tamer of men and gods, foremost in the world, heaped with hundreds of virtues.'

children.text: tvaṃ śīlena vratatapacaritaḥ tvaṃ kṣāntīye jagahitakaraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: You are accomplished in morality, vow, austerity, and practice; through patience you act for the welfare of the world.

children.text: tvaṃ vīryeṇā śubhaguṇanicito dhyāne prajñe na tu samu tribhave ||
children.translated_text: Through vigor you are heaped with auspicious virtues, and in meditation and wisdom there is no one equal to you in the three worlds.

children.text: krodhāviṣṭā khilamalabahulā te maitrīye tvayi sphuṭa sugatā
children.translated_text: Toward those possessed by anger, barren and full of impurity, your loving-kindness is plainly manifest, O <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: kāruṇyaṃ te bahuvidhamabudhe mithyātveṣū śubhaguṇarahite ||
children.translated_text: Your compassion, in many forms, is for the ignorant, for those in false views and devoid of auspicious qualities.

children.text: puṇyajñāne śubhānicitātmā dhyānābhijño pratapasi virajo
children.translated_text: Your very self is accumulated with merit, knowledge, and wholesome qualities; knowing the meditations and superknowledges, stainless, you shine forth.

children.text: obhāsesī daśa ima diśato meghā muktaḥ śaśiriva vimalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You illumine these ten directions like the spotless moon released from clouds.

children.text: ete cānye bahuvidha rucirā tūryairghoṣāṃ jinarutaravanā
children.translated_text: These and many other lovely sounds, the tones of instruments resounding with the call of the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: ye codentī suranaramahitaṃ niṣkramyāhī ayu tava samayu ||
children.translated_text: exhort the one honored by gods and men: 'Go forth; this is your time.'

children.text: bodhisattvasya khalu punarbhikṣavastasmin gṛhavarapradhāne sarvopakaraṇasamṛddhisamudite yathābhiprāyasukhavihārānukūle amarapurabhavanaprakāśe vitardiniryūhatoraṇagavākṣaharmyakūṭāgāraprāsādavarapravare sarvaratnavicitrālaṃkāravividhabhaktisuvibhakte ucchritachatradhvajapatākānekaratnakiṅkiṇījālasamalaṃkṛte anekapaṭṭadāmaśatasahasrābhipralambite nānāratnapratyupte muktāhārābhipralambite vicitrapaṭṭaratnasaṃkramopaśobhite avasaktapaṭṭamālyadāmakalāpe gandhaghaṭikānirdhūpite avaśyāyapaṭavitatavitāne sarvartukapuṣpaparamasugandhisurucirābhiprakīrṇapuṣkariṇīpuṇḍarīkanavanalinījālasaṃsthānaparibhogabahule patraguptaśukasārikakokilahaṃsamayūracakravākakunālakalaviṅkajīvajīvakādinānāvidhadvijagaṇamadhurasvaranikūjite nīlavaiḍūryamaye dharaṇītalasaṃsthānaparibhoge sarvarūpapratibhāsasaṃdarśane atṛptanayanābhiramye paramaprītiprāmodyasaṃjanane tasmin gṛhavarapradhāne 'dhyāvasato bodhisattvasyodāravaraśaraṇabhavananivāsino 'malavimalanirmalāṅgasyāmuktamālyābharaṇasya pravarasurabhigandhānulepanānuliptagātrasya śuklaśubhavimalaviśuddhanirmalavastraprāvṛtaśarīrasya anekadivyadūṣyasūkṣmasuvinyastamṛdukācilindikasukhasaṃsparśavarāṅgaracitaśayanatalābhirūḍhasya amaravadhūbhiriva sarvato 'navadyāpratikūladarśanaśubhopacāracaritasya abhirūpāntaḥpuramadhyagatasya śaṅkhabherīmṛdaṅgapaṇavatuṇavavīṇāvallakisaṃpatāḍakipalanakulasughoṣakamadhuraveṇunirnāditaghoṣarutanānātūryasaṃgītisaṃprayogapratibodhitasya ye ca nārīgaṇāḥ snigdhamadhuramanojñasvaraveṇunirnāditanirghoṣarutena bodhisattvaṃ pratisaṃbodhayanti sma teṣāṃ daśadigavasthitānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmadhisthānena tebhyo veṇutūryaninādanirghoṣarutebhya imā bodhisattvasya saṃcodanā gāthā niścaranti sma ||
children.translated_text: Now, monks, while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was dwelling in that foremost excellent mansion, endowed with every furnishing and abundance, suited to pleasant living according to his desire, shining like the palace of the city of the immortals, splendid with terraces, gateways, windows, upper rooms, pavilions, and excellent palaces, variously divided by manifold ornamentation with every kind of jewel and variegated decoration, adorned with raised parasols, banners, flags, and nets of many jeweled little bells, hung with many hundreds of thousands of cloth streamers, studded with various jewels, draped with strings of pearls, beautified by varied cloth-and-jewel stairways, covered with clusters of cloth garlands and wreaths, fumigated with jars of fragrance, canopied with dew-cloths spread out, rich with pleasure-ponds strewn with supremely fragrant and lovely flowers of every season and arranged with lotuses, white lotuses, and fresh water-lilies, filled with the sweet calls of many kinds of birds such as sheltered parrots, mynas, cuckoos, geese, peacocks, cakravākas, kuṇālas, kalaviṅkas, and jīvajīvakas, with a floor of blue beryl, showing reflections of every form, delightful to eyes that were never sated, and producing supreme joy and gladness; while the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, residing in that foremost mansion, was living in a noble, excellent refuge-dwelling, his body spotless, stainless, and pure, wearing garlands and ornaments, his limbs anointed with excellent fragrant unguents, his body clothed in white, bright, stainless, pure, and clean garments, mounted upon a couch made with many divine fabrics, fine, well arranged, soft, and pleasant to the touch like kācilindika cloth, surrounded by women of the inner palace who were beautiful and whose lovely conduct and service were in every way blameless, like the women of the immortals, and awakened by the sounds of conches, kettledrums, mṛdaṅgas, paṇavas, tuṇavas, vīṇās, vallakīs, cymbals, palankulas, sweet-voiced flutes, and many instruments joined in concert; those groups of women awakened the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with the sound and tone of flutes, smooth, sweet, and charming, and by the blessing of the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> dwelling in the ten directions, from the sounds and tones of those flutes and instruments these verses of exhortation came forth for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

children.text: yā nāryo muditamanāḥ prasannacittā veṇubhyo madhuramanoramaṃ raṇante
children.translated_text: The women, glad in mind and serene in heart, sounded from the flutes a sweet and charming melody;

children.text: āveśāddaśadiggatāṃ jinottamānāṃ gāthemā vividhavicitracitrarūpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: through the inspiration of the supreme <s>Jinas</s> gone to the ten directions, these verses, diverse, varied, and beautifully formed, arose.

children.text: pūrve te ayu kṛtu praṇidhī abhūṣi vīrā dṛṣṭvemāṃ janata sadā anāthabhūtām
children.translated_text: Formerly, hero, you made this vow, seeing these people always without a protector:

children.text: śociṣye jaramaraṇāttathānyaduḥkhād buddhitvā padamajaraṃ paraṃ aśokam ||
children.translated_text: 'Having awakened to the ageless, supreme, sorrowless state, I shall free them from old age and death and from other suffering.'

children.text: tatsādho puravara ita śīghraṃ niṣkramyā purimaṛṣibhi cīrṇam
children.translated_text: Therefore, good one, quickly depart from this excellent city and follow the course practiced by the former seers;

children.text: ākramyā dharaṇitalapradeśaṃ saṃbuddhyā asadṛśajinajñānam ||
children.translated_text: step upon this region of the earth, and awaken to the unsurpassed knowledge of the unequalled <s>Jina</s>.

children.text: pūrve te dhanaratana vicitrā tyaktābhūt karacaraṇapriyātmā
children.translated_text: Formerly you gave up varied wealth and jewels, as well as hands, feet, and your dear self;

children.text: eṣo 'dyā tava samayu maharṣe dharmaughaṃ jagi vibhaja anantam ||
children.translated_text: today this is your time, great seer: distribute through the world the endless flood of <s>dharma</s> (teaching).

children.text: śīlaṃ te śubha vimalakhaṇḍaṃ pūrvānte vara satatamabhūṣī
children.translated_text: Your morality was auspicious, stainless, unbroken, supreme, and constant in the former time;

children.text: śīlenānatisadṛśu maharṣe śocehī jagu vividhakileśaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: by that incomparable morality, great seer, relieve the world afflicted by manifold defilements.

children.text: kṣāntīye bhava śatacaritastvaṃ kṣāntāste jagi vividha duruktāḥ
children.translated_text: You have practiced patience through hundreds of lives; in the world you endured many kinds of harsh words;

children.text: kṣāntāye kṣamadamaniratātma naiṣkramye mati kuru dvipadendrā ||
children.translated_text: through patience, with a self delighting in forbearance and restraint, set your mind on renunciation, lord of two-footed beings.

children.text: vīryaṃ te dṛḍhamacalamakampyaṃ pūrvānte pṛthu sugata abhūvan
children.translated_text: Your vigor in the past was firm, unmoving, unshaken, and vast, O <s>Sugata</s>;

children.text: dharṣitvā namuci śaṭhaṃ sasainyaṃ śoṣiṣye traya sakalaapāyāt ||
children.translated_text: having defeated the deceitful <s>Namuci</s> with his army, you will dry up the three lower destinies completely.

children.text: yasyārthe vratatapa caritastvaṃ dhyāyitvā kalikaluṣakileśāṃ
children.translated_text: For the sake of which you practiced vows and austerities, meditating on the impurity and defilements of the age,

children.text: tvaṃ varṣā amṛtajalamoghaṃ tarpehī ciratṛṣita anāthāṃ ||
children.translated_text: rain down a flood of nectar-water; satisfy those long-thirsty and without a protector.

children.text: tāṃ pūrvāṃ giravaramanucintyā niṣkramyā puravara ita śīghram
children.translated_text: Reflecting on that former noble utterance, quickly depart from this excellent city;

children.text: buddhitvā padamamṛtamaśokaṃ tarpiṣye amṛtarasi tṛṣārtāṃ ||
children.translated_text: having awakened to the immortal, sorrowless state, satisfy those tormented by thirst with the taste of nectar.

children.text: prajñāyā paricarikuśala tvaṃ jñānaṃ te pṛthu vipulamanantam
children.translated_text: You are skilled in attending upon wisdom; your knowledge is broad, vast, and endless;

children.text: mūḍhānāṃ vimatipathasthitānāṃ prajñābhāṃ śubharucira kuru tvam ||
children.translated_text: for those who are bewildered and standing on the path of doubt, make a beautiful and lovely radiance of wisdom.

children.text: maitrāyāṃ bhava śatacaritastvaṃ kārūṇye vara mudita upekṣe
children.translated_text: You have practiced through hundreds of lives in friendliness, compassion, joy, and equanimity;

children.text: yāmevā varacari caritastvaṃ tāmevā cariṃ vibhaja jagasya ||
children.translated_text: that very supreme conduct which you practiced, distribute that conduct to the world.

children.text: evaṃ daśa diśa jinatejairgāthā vai guṇakusumavicitrāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, through the powers of the <s>Jinas</s> in the ten directions, verses variegated with flowers of virtues

children.text: tūryebhyo vividhamanuravante codentī śayanagatakumāram ||
children.translated_text: resounded in many ways from the instruments, urging on the prince who lay upon his bed.

children.text: yada puna pramudita ratikara pramadā surucira sumadhura prabhaṇiṣu turiyaiḥ
children.translated_text: When again the delighted, pleasure-giving women sounded the instruments with lovely, very sweet notes,

children.text: atha jina daśadiśi suranaradamakāḥ giravaramanuravi tatu ravi turiyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the <s>Jinas</s> in the ten directions, tamers of gods and humans, caused their noble speech to resound in those instruments.

children.text: kṛta tvayi hitakara bahuguṇa janato nijinitu nijaguṇa vicarati gatiṣū
children.translated_text: You have done what brings welfare to beings, rich in many virtues; you have conquered yourself, and by your own qualities you move among the destinies.

children.text: smara smara purimaka bratatapacaraṇa laghu vraja drumavaru spṛśa padamamṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Remember, remember your former practice of vows and austerities; quickly go to the best of trees and touch the immortal state.

children.text: sutṛṣita naramaru jinaguṇarahitā tvayi mati pratibalu amṛtarasadadā
children.translated_text: Humans and gods are very thirsty and bereft of the <s>Jina</s>'s virtues; in you there is the resolve and strength to give the taste of nectar.

children.text: daśabalaguṇadhara budhajanamahitaṃ laghu tvayi narapati vibhajahi amṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Bearer of the qualities of the Ten Powers, honored by the wise: quickly, O lord of men, distribute the nectar among beings.

children.text: tyaji tvayi puri bhavi dhanamaṇikanakā sakhi priya suta mahi sanagaranigamā
children.translated_text: Formerly you gave up wealth, jewels, and gold, friends, beloved sons, and the earth with its cities and market-towns.

children.text: śiramapi tyaji svaku karacaranayanā jagati ya hitakaru jinaguṇaniratā ||
children.translated_text: You even gave up your own head, hands, feet, and eyes, being a benefactor in the world and devoted to the qualities of the <s>Jina</s>.

children.text: puri tuma naravarasutu nṛpu yadabhū naru tava abhimukha ima giramavacī
children.translated_text: Formerly, when you were a prince, a son of the best of men, a man came before you and spoke these words:

children.text: dada mama ima mahi sanagaranigamāṃ tyaji tada pramuditu na ca manu kṣubhito ||
children.translated_text: 'Give me this earth with its cities and market-towns.' Then you gave it gladly, and your mind was not disturbed.

children.text: puri tuma narapati svaku dvija yadabhū gurujani paricari na ca druhi parato
children.translated_text: Formerly, when you were a king and then a brahmin, you served your elders and did no injury to others.

children.text: sthapayisu dvijavara bahujana kuśale cyutu tatu bhavagatu marupuranilayam ||
children.translated_text: Having established the best of brahmins and many people in welfare, you passed from that existence and went to a dwelling of the gods.

children.text: puri tuma nṛpasuta ṛṣivaru yadabhū chini tava tanuruha kalinṛpu ruṣito
children.translated_text: Formerly, when you were a prince and an excellent sage, an angry wicked king cut the hair from your body.

children.text: kṛta tvayi kulakriya na ca manu kṣubhito payu tava sravi tada karatalacaraṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: You performed the duty proper to your lineage, and your mind was not disturbed; then blood streamed from your hands and feet.

children.text: syamu puna ṛṣisuta tvayi puri yadabhū vrataratu gurubharu girivaranilaye
children.translated_text: Again, formerly, when you were a sage's son, devoted to vows, bearing the heavy duty owed to the guru, dwelling on a great mountain,

children.text: hata bhava nṛpatina viṣakṛta īṣuṇā kṛpa tava tahi nṛpa na ca manu kṣubhito ||
children.translated_text: you were struck by a king with a poisoned arrow; compassion for that king arose in you, and your mind was not disturbed.

children.text: puri tuma guṇadhara mṛgapati yadabhū girinadibahujali duyamanu puruṣo
children.translated_text: Formerly, when you were a virtuous lord of beasts in a mountain river full of water, a man was suffering.

children.text: hita bhava tvayi naru sthalapathi sthapito upanayi tava ari na ca manu kṣubhito ||
children.translated_text: For his welfare you set that man on dry land; he brought your enemy to you, yet your mind was not disturbed.

children.text: puri tuma naravara tyaji sutu yadabhū maṇi tava prapatitu jaladhari vipule
children.translated_text: Formerly, when you were the best of men, a son who had renounced, and your jewel had fallen into the broad ocean,

children.text: cyavayitu kṣapayitu tvaya mahaudadhiṃ labhi tada dhanamaṇi dṛḍhabala vaṣabhī ||
children.translated_text: you caused the great ocean to sink and diminish, and then, firm in strength like a bull, you recovered the jewel of wealth.

children.text: puri tuma supuruṣa ṛṣivaru yadabhū dvija tava upagatu bhava mama śaraṇam
children.translated_text: Formerly, O excellent man, when you were a sage, a brahmin came to you saying, 'Be my refuge.'

children.text: bhaṇi ṛṣi dvijavara mama ripuupane tyaji tvaya svaki tanu na ca dvija tyajase ||
children.translated_text: The sage said, 'Best of brahmins, bring my enemy near'; you gave up your own body, but you did not abandon the brahmin.

children.text: syamu ṛṣi upagatu puri drumanilaye ruci bhaṇi taruruha kati ima gaṇaye
children.translated_text: Formerly, when as a sage you came to a dwelling among trees, someone said with interest, 'Count how many leaves are on this tree.'

children.text: suvidita sugaṇita yatha tahi kiśalā tatha tava avitatha samagira racitā ||
children.translated_text: As well known and well counted as the shoots there were, so your words were composed without falsehood.

children.text: sukula suguṇadhara puri drumi vasato kṣayagatu na ca tyaji kṛtu smari purimam
children.translated_text: Formerly, dwelling in a tree, noble and endowed with good qualities, you came to decay but did not abandon what you had undertaken, remembering your former act.

children.text: marupati pramuditu tava guṇa smarato śriyakari drumavari yathariva purimā ||
children.translated_text: The lord of the gods rejoiced as he remembered your quality, and the excellent tree, giver of beauty, became as it had been before.

children.text: iti tava asadṛśa vratatapacaraṇā bahuguṇa guṇadhara guṇapathi carato
children.translated_text: Thus, bearing many qualities and walking the path of virtues, you have practiced incomparable vows, austerities, and conduct.

children.text: tyaji mahi sanagari ayu tava samayo laghu jagu sthapayahi jinaguṇacaraṇe ||
children.translated_text: Give up the earth with its cities; this is your time. Quickly establish the world in the practice of the <s>Jina</s>'s qualities.

children.text: yada pramadaratanā śubhavastrā bhūṣitagātrā varapravaru turiyā sumanojñā saṃprabhaṇīṣu
children.translated_text: When jewel-like women, wearing fine garments and with adorned bodies, made the foremost and excellent instruments sound sweetly,

children.text: atha daśasū diśato jinatejairgātha vicitrā iti raviṣū madhurā rutaghoṣā tūryasvarebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then from the ten directions, through the radiance of the <s>Jinas</s>, there arose varied verses, sweet calls and sounds from the tones of the instruments.

children.text: tava praṇidhī purime bahukalpāṃ lokapradīpā jaramaraṇagrasite ahu loke trāṇu bhaviṣye
children.translated_text: 'Your former vows through many kalpas, O lamp of the world, were these: In a world seized by old age and death I shall become a protector.

children.text: smara purimapraṇidhiṃ narasiṃhā yā ti abhūṣī ayu samayo tvamihā dvipadendrā niṣkramaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: Remember your former vow, lion among men, the one you made. This is the time here, lord of bipeds, for your going forth.

children.text: bhavanayute tvamihā bahudānaṃ dattamanekaṃ dhanakanakā ratanā śubhavastrā ratnavicitrā
children.translated_text: In many hundreds of existences here you gave manifold great gifts: wealth, gold, jewels, fine garments, and many-colored gems.

children.text: karacaraṇā nayanā priyaputrā rājya samṛddhaṃ tvayi tyajitaṃ na ca te khiladoṣā yācanakeṣu ||
children.translated_text: Hands, feet, eyes, beloved sons, and a prosperous kingdom were given up by you, and toward beggars there was no remnant of fault in you.

children.text: śiśunṛpati tvamihā śaśiketo āsi sudaṃṣṭro kṛpa karuṇāmanaso maṇicūḍo candrapradīpaḥ
children.translated_text: As child-kings here you were <s>Śaśiketu</s>, <s>Sudaṃṣṭra</s>, compassionate-minded <s>Maṇicūḍa</s>, and <s>Candrapradīpa</s>.

children.text: iti pramukhā kariyā dṛḍhaśūro rājasunetro bahu nṛpati nayutā rata dāne tvaṃ savikurvan ||
children.translated_text: Making these the foremost examples, along with <s>Dṛḍhaśūra</s>, <s>Rājasunetra</s>, and many tens of thousands of kings, you repeatedly practiced giving.

children.text: tava sugatā carito bahukalpāṃ śīlacarīye maṇiratnā vimalā sadṛśābhūcchīlaviśuddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Your conduct as a <s>Sugata</s> through many kalpas was in the practice of morality; your purity of morality was clear, like spotless jewels and gems.

children.text: tvayi caratā camarī yatha bālaṃ rakṣitu śīlaṃ kṛtu tvamihā jagati vipulārthaṃ śīlaratenā ||
children.translated_text: Practicing here, you protected morality as a yak cow protects her calf, and for the great welfare of the world you acted while delighting in morality.

children.text: gajavaru tvamihā ripulubdhe viddhu iṣūṇā kṛpa karuṇā janiyā atiraudre chāditu śobhe
children.translated_text: When here you were an excellent elephant, pierced with arrows by greedy enemies, compassion arose in you toward those extremely fierce ones, and you covered over your own splendor.

children.text: parityaji te rucirā śubhadantā na ca tyaji śīlaṃ iti pramukhā kariyā bahu tubhyaṃ śīlavikurvī ||
children.translated_text: You gave up your beautiful, fair tusks, but you did not give up morality; making these the foremost examples, you repeatedly practiced morality in many ways.

children.text: tvayi sahitā jagato 'hita anekā duḥkhasahasrā bahukaṭukāvacanaṃ vadhabandhā kṣāntiratenā
children.translated_text: Joined to the welfare of the world, you endured many injuries, thousands of pains, many bitter words, killing, and bondage, because you delighted in patience.

children.text: paricārita purime nara ye te sarvasukhenā puna vadhakāstava teha abhūvan tacca ti kṣāntam ||
children.translated_text: Those men whom you had formerly served with every comfort later became your killers; even that was endured by you.

children.text: giripravarānilaye tuma nāthā ṛkṣu yadāsī himakiraṇā salilā bhayabhītaṃ tvaṃ naru gṛhya
children.translated_text: Lord, when you were a bear dwelling on an excellent mountain, you took in a man frightened by cold, moonlight, and water.

children.text: paricarasi vividhā phalamūlaiḥ sarvasukhenā laghu vadhakāṃ sa tavā upanetrī taṃ ca ti kṣāntam ||
children.translated_text: You tended him with various fruits and roots and every comfort; soon he led your killers to you, and even that was endured by you.

children.text: dṛḍhu saṃsthitamacalamakampyaṃ vīryu tavāsīt vratatapasā vividhā guṇajñānaṃ eṣata bodhim
children.translated_text: Firm, steadfast, unmoving, and unshaken was your vigor, through vows and austerities, while you sought various qualities, knowledge, and awakening.

children.text: kṛtu abalo namucī vaśavartī vīyabalenā ayu samayo tvamihā narasiṃhā niṣkramaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: By the strength of your vigor you made powerless <s>Namucī</s>, who had beings under his sway. This is the time here, lion among men, for your going forth.

children.text: hayapravarū tvamihā puri āsī hemasuvarṇo laghu gagane vajrase kṛpajāto rākṣasidvīpam
children.translated_text: Formerly you were an excellent horse here, golden like refined gold; swiftly through the sky, diamond-like and born of compassion, you went to <s>Rākṣasīdvīpa</s>.

children.text: vyasanagata manujāṃ tada gṛhyā kṣemi thapesī iti pramukhā kariyā bahu tubhyaṃ vīryavikurvā ||
children.translated_text: Then you gathered up the people fallen into calamity and set them in safety; making these the foremost examples, you repeatedly practiced vigor in many ways.

children.text: damaśamatheḥ niyamāhatakleśā dhyāyina agrā laghu capalaṃ viṣayai ratilolaṃ cittu damitvā
children.translated_text: Through self-restraint and tranquility, with the defilements struck down by discipline, O foremost meditator, having tamed the mind that is light, fickle, and pleasure-seeking among sense-objects,

children.text: kṛtu svaguṇo tvamihā jagato 'rthe dhyānaratenā ayu samayo tvamihā varasattvā dhyānavikurvā ||
children.translated_text: manifest your own excellence here for the sake of the world. O you who delight in meditation, this is your time; here, excellent being, display the transformations of meditation.

children.text: tvaṃ purime ṛṣi susthitu āsī dhyānaratīye nṛparahitā manujā tvamu gṛhyā rājyabhiṣiñcī
children.translated_text: In former times you were a well-established seer, delighting in meditation; when human beings were without a king, they took you and consecrated you to kingship.

children.text: daśakuśalī janitā thapitā te brahmapatheṣu cyuta manujā vrajiṣū tada sarve brahmaniketam ||
children.translated_text: You caused the ten wholesome courses to arise and established them on the paths to <s>Brahmā</s>; when those people passed away, they all went to the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: diśividiśi vividhāgatijñāne tvaṃ suvidhijño paracaritā jagati rutajñāne indriyajñāne
children.translated_text: You thoroughly know the various knowledges of destinies in every direction; in the world you know the conduct of others, the knowledge of speech, and the knowledge of faculties.

children.text: nayavinaye vividhāmatidhāre pāragatastvaṃ ayu samayo tvamihā nṛpasūno niṣkramaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: In methods and discipline, bearing manifold insight, you have gone to the far shore. This is your time here, prince, for going forth.

children.text: tvayi purimā janatā ima dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭivipannā jaramaraṇā vividhā bahuduḥkhe kṛchragatā hi
children.translated_text: When the people of former times saw this in you, though ruined by wrong views, afflicted by old age and death, and fallen into many kinds of great suffering and hardship,

children.text: bhavavibhavaṃkaraṇo ṛjumārge svāmanubaddhā hatatamasa tvamihā kṛtu loke arthu mahanto ||
children.translated_text: you became the one who ends becoming and non-becoming; attached to your own straight path, destroyer of darkness, you performed a great benefit here for the world.

children.text: iti vividhā rucirā guṇayuktā gātha vicitrā tatu raviṣu turiyebhī jinatejā codayi vīram
children.translated_text: Thus, with various lovely verses furnished with virtues, and with many-colored music, those radiant ones, possessing the splendor of the <s>Jinas</s>, urged on the hero.

children.text: duḥkhabharitajanate iha dṛṣṭvā mā tvamupekṣā ayu samayo tvamihā varabuddhe niṣkramaṇāya ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the people here filled with suffering, do not be indifferent. This is your time here, excellent <s>Buddha</s>, for going forth.

children.text: vicitravastraratnahāragandhamālyabhūṣitā prasannacitta premajāta nāriyo praharṣitā
children.translated_text: Women adorned with variegated garments, jeweled necklaces, perfumes, garlands, and ornaments, clear in mind, with love arisen and filled with joy,

children.text: prabodhayanti ye 'grasattva tūryasaṃpravāditaiḥ jinānubhāvi ekarūpa gātha tūrya niścarī ||
children.translated_text: awakened the foremost being with the playing of instruments; through the power of the <s>Jinas</s>, a single kind of verse issued from the music.

children.text: yasyārthi tubhya kalpa naika tyaktu tyāga dustyajā sucīrṇa śīlu kṣānti vīrya dhyāna prajña bhāvitā
children.translated_text: For your sake, through many aeons, things hard to relinquish were given up; morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom were long practiced and cultivated.

children.text: jagaddhitārtha so ti kālu sāṃprataṃ upasthito naiṣkramyabuddhi cintayāśu mā vilamba nāyaka ||
children.translated_text: For the welfare of the world, that very time has now arrived: quickly contemplate the thought of renunciation; do not delay, leader.

children.text: tyuktu pūrvi ratnakośa svarṇarūpyabhūṣaṇā yaṣṭā ti yajña naikarūpa tāsu tāsu jātiṣu
children.translated_text: Formerly you gave up treasuries of jewels and ornaments of gold and silver; you offered sacrifices of many kinds in those various births.

children.text: tyakta bhārya putra dhīta kāyu rājyu jīvitaṃ bodhiheturaprameya tyaktuḥdustyajā tvayā ||
children.translated_text: You gave up wife, son, daughter, body, kingdom, and life; for the sake of awakening, immeasurable things hard to give up were given up by you.

children.text: abhūṣi tvaṃ adīnapuṇya rāja viśrutaśriyo nimiṃdharo nimiśca kṛṣṇabandhu brahmadatta kesarī
children.translated_text: You were <s>Adīnapuṇya</s>, a king of renowned splendor, <s>Nimiṃdhara</s>, <s>Nimi</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇabandhu</s>, <s>Brahmadatta</s>, and <s>Kesarī</s>.

children.text: sahasrayajña dharmacinti arcimān dṛḍhadhanu sucintitārtha dīnasattva yeḥti tyakta dustyajā ||
children.translated_text: You were <s>Sahasrayajña</s>, <s>Dharmacinti</s>, <s>Arcimān</s>, <s>Dṛḍhadhanu</s>, and <s>Sucintitārtha</s>; as <s>Dīnasattva</s> and others, things hard to give up were given up by you.

children.text: sutasoma dīptavīrya puṇyaraśmi yo so 'bhū mahatyāgavantu sthāmavantu yaḥ kṛtajña tvaṃ abhūḥ
children.translated_text: You were <s>Sutasoma</s>, <s>Dīptavīrya</s>, and that <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, great in giving, strong, and grateful.

children.text: rājarṣi candrarūpavantu śūra satyavardhano subhāṣitaṃgaveṣi rāji asi sumatiṃ ca sūrato ||
children.translated_text: You were the royal seer <s>Candrarūpavantu</s>, the brave <s>Satyavardhana</s>, the king who searched for good speech, <s>Sumati</s>, and <s>Sūrata</s>.

children.text: candraprabho viśeṣagāmi reṇubhū diśāṃpati pradānaśūra kāśirāju ratnacūḍa śāntagaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Candraprabha</s>, <s>Viśeṣagāmin</s>, <s>Reṇubhū</s>, lord of the directions, the hero in giving, the king of <s>Kāśi</s>, <s>Ratnacūḍa</s>, and <s>Śāntaga</s>:

children.text: eti cānyi pārthivendra yebhi tyakta dustyajā yathā ti vṛṣṭa tyāgavṛṣṭi eṣa dharma varṣahī ||
children.translated_text: these and other lords of earth gave up things hard to abandon. As you rained down a rain of giving, so this is an excellent rain of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭā ti pūrviṃ sattvasāra gaṅgavālukopamā kṛtā ti teṣa buddhapūja aprameyacintiyā
children.translated_text: Formerly, O essence of beings, you saw <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>; for them you performed immeasurable, inconceivable worship of the <s>Buddhas</s>.

children.text: varāgrabodhi eṣamāṇa sattvamokṣakāraṇādū ayaṃ sa kālu prāptu sūru niṣkramā purottamāt ||
children.translated_text: Seeking the highest, foremost awakening for the sake of the liberation of beings, this is the time that has arrived, hero: go forth from the excellent city.

children.text: prathamena te amoghadarśi śālapuṣpapūjito virocanaḥ prasannacitta prekṣitaḥ kṣaṇāntaram
children.translated_text: First, <s>Amoghadarśin</s> was worshiped by you with śāla flowers; <s>Virocana</s> was gazed upon for a moment with a clear mind.

children.text: harītakī ca eka datta dundubhisvarāya te tṛṇottha gṛhya dhāritā ti dṛṣṭa candanaṃ gṛham ||
children.translated_text: A single harītakī fruit was given by you to <s>Dundubhisvara</s>; you took up and held grass, and you saw a house of sandalwood.

children.text: purapraveśi reṇu dṛṣṭa kṣiptu cūrṇamuṣṭikā dharmeśvarāya sādhukāru dattu dharma bhāṣato
children.translated_text: At the city-entry you saw the dust and threw a handful of powder to <s>Dharmeśvara</s>; as he taught the <s>dharma</s>, you offered a cry of approval.

children.text: namo namaḥ samantadarśi dṛṣṭa vāca bhāṣitā mahārciskandhi svarṇamāla kṣipta harṣitena te ||
children.translated_text: You uttered the words, "Homage, homage," on seeing <s>Samantadarśin</s>; with joy you threw a golden garland to <s>Mahārciskandhin</s>.

children.text: dharmadhvajo daśāpradāni rodhu muṅga muṣṭinā aśokapuṣpi jñānaketu yvāgupāna sārathiḥ
children.translated_text: To <s>Dharmadhvaja</s> you gave ten gifts; to <s>Rodha</s>, a fistful of mung beans; to <s>Jñānaketu</s>, aśoka flowers; to <s>Sārathi</s>, a drink of gruel.

children.text: ratnaśikhī ca dīpadāni padmayoni oṣadhī sarvābhibhūśca muktahāri padmadāni sāgaro ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Ratnaśikhin</s> you gave lamps; to <s>Padmayoni</s>, medicine; to <s>Sarvābhibhū</s>, a pearl necklace; to <s>Sāgara</s>, lotus gifts.

children.text: vitānadāni padmagarbhi siṃhu varṣasaṃstare śālendrarāja sarpidāni kṣīratyāgi puṣpitī
children.translated_text: To <s>Padmagarbha</s> you gave a canopy; to <s>Siṃha</s>, a spread for the rains; to <s>Śālendrarāja</s>, ghee; to <s>Puṣpitin</s>, a gift of milk.

children.text: yaśodattu kuruṇṭapuṣpi satyadarśi bhojane kāyu praṇāmi jñānameru nāgadattu cīvare ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Yaśodatta</s> you gave kuruṇṭa flowers; to <s>Satyadarśin</s>, food; to <s>Jñānameru</s>, a bowing down of the body; to <s>Nāgadatta</s>, a robe.

children.text: atyuccagāmi candanāgri tīkṣṇalohamuṣṭinā mahāviyūha padmadāni raśmirāja ratnabhiḥ
children.translated_text: To <s>Atyuccagāmin</s> you gave the best sandalwood; to <s>Tīkṣṇaloha</s>, a fistful of sharp iron; to <s>Mahāviyūha</s>, lotuses; to <s>Raśmirāja</s>, jewels.

children.text: śākyamuni ca suvarṇamuṣṭi indraketu saṃstuto sūryānano vataṃsake hi svarṇapaṭṭi sūmatī ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Śākyamuni</s> you gave a handful of gold; <s>Indraketu</s> was praised by you; to <s>Sūryānana</s>, an ornament; to <s>Sumati</s>, a strip of gold.

children.text: nāgābhibhū maṇipradāni puṣya dūṣyasaṃstare bhaiṣajyarāju ratnachatri siṃhaketu āsane
children.translated_text: To <s>Nāgābhibhū</s> you gave a jewel; to <s>Puṣya</s>, a cloth spread; to <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, a jeweled parasol; to <s>Siṃhaketu</s>, a seat.

children.text: guṇāgradhāri ratnajāli sarvavādi kāśyapo gandhāgri cūrṇi mukta arciketu puṣpacaityake ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Guṇāgradhārin</s> you gave a jeweled net; to <s>Sarvavādin Kāśyapa</s>, the finest powdered perfume; to <s>Arciketu</s>, pearls at a flower shrine.

children.text: akṣobhyarāja kūṭāgāri mālya lokapūjito tagaraśikhi ca rājyatyāgi sarvagandhi durjayo
children.translated_text: To <s>Akṣobhyarāja</s> you gave an upper pavilion; to <s>Lokapūjita</s>, a garland; to <s>Tagaraśikhin</s>, a kingdom; to <s>Durjaya</s>, every perfume.

children.text: mahāpradīpa ātmatyāgi bhūṣaṇe padmottaro vicitrapuṣpi dharmaketu dīpakāri utpalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Mahāpradīpa</s> you gave yourself; to <s>Padmottara</s>, ornaments; to <s>Dharmaketu</s>, varied flowers; to <s>Dīpakārin</s>, lotuses.

children.text: eti cānyi sattvasāra ye ti pūrva pūjitā nānārūpa vicitra pūja anyajanyakurvatā
children.translated_text: These and other essences of beings were worshiped by you in the past; in other births you performed various and manifold worship.

children.text: smarāhi te atīta buddha tā ca pūja śāstunāṃ anāthasattva śokapūrṇa mā upekṣi niṣkramā ||
children.translated_text: Remember those past <s>Buddhas</s> and that worship of the teachers; do not neglect helpless beings filled with sorrow. Go forth.

children.text: dīpaṃkareti dṛṣṭamātri labdha kṣānti uttamā abhijña pañca acyutā ti labdha ānulomikā
children.translated_text: Upon merely seeing <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, you obtained the highest <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance), the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), unfailing, and the <s>ānulomikā</s> (conformity-stage attainment).

children.text: atottareṇa ekameka buddha pūjacintiyā pravartitā asaṃkhyakalpa sarvalokadhātuṣū ||
children.translated_text: Then, with the thought of worshiping each single later <s>Buddha</s>, you proceeded for innumerable kalpas through all world-spheres.

children.text: kṣīṇā ti kalpa aprameya te ca buddha nirvṛtā tavāpi sarva ātmabhāvi te ca nāma kva gatā
children.translated_text: Those immeasurable kalpas have been exhausted, and those <s>Buddhas</s> too have entered nirvāṇa; and all those embodiments of yours, and their names, where have they gone?

children.text: kṣayāntadharmi sarvi bhāvu nāsti nityu saṃskṛte anitya kāma rājyabhoga niṣkramā purottamāt ||
children.translated_text: All existence has destruction as its end; there is nothing eternal among conditioned things. Desires, kingship, and enjoyments are impermanent: go forth from the best of cities.

children.text: jarā ca vyādhi mṛtyu enti dāruṇā mahābhayā hutāśano va ugrateja bhīma kalpasaṃkṣaye
children.translated_text: Old age, sickness, and death come as terrible great fears, like a blazing fire of fierce heat at the destruction of an aeon.

children.text: kṣayāntadharmi sarvi bhāvu nāsti nityu saṃskṛte sukṛcchra prāpta sattva ... niṣkramā guṇaṃdharā ||
children.translated_text: All existence has destruction as its end; there is nothing eternal among conditioned things. Having attained living beings only with great difficulty ... go forth, bearer of virtues.

children.text: yada nārigaṇastuṇaveṇuravaiḥ vividhaisturiyaiḥ pratibodhayiṣu
children.translated_text: When the company of women, with songs, flutes, and various instruments, wished to awaken

children.text: sukhaśayanagataṃ manujādhipatiṃ tada tūryaravo ayu niścarate ||
children.translated_text: the lord of men lying on a pleasant bed, then this sound of instruments issued forth:

children.text: jvalitaṃ tribhavaṃ jaravyādhidukhaiḥ maraṇāgnipradīptamanāthamidam
children.translated_text: The threefold existence is blazing with the sufferings of old age and sickness; this helpless world is kindled by the fire of death.

children.text: bhavani śaraṇe sada mūḍha jagat bhramatī bhramaro yatha kumbhagato ||
children.translated_text: The foolish world, always taking refuge in becoming, wanders like a bee inside a pot.

children.text: adhruvaṃ tribhavaṃ śaradabhranibhaṃ naṭaraṅgasamā jagi rūrmicutī
children.translated_text: The threefold existence is unstable, like an autumn cloud; the world is like an actor's dance, like the breaking of a wave.

children.text: girinadyasamaṃ laghuśīghrajavaṃ vrajatāyu jage yatha vidyu nabhe ||
children.translated_text: The life of the world goes with swift and rapid speed, like a mountain river, like lightning in the sky.

children.text: bhuvi devapure triapāyapathe bhavatṛṣṇaavidyavaśā janatā
children.translated_text: On earth, in the cities of the gods, and on the path to the three bad destinies, people are under the power of craving for existence and ignorance;

children.text: parivartiṣu pañcagatiṣvabudhāḥ yatha kumbhakarasya hi cakrabhramī ||
children.translated_text: ignorant, they turn about in the five destinies, like the turning wheel of a potter.

children.text: priyarūpavaraiḥ saha snigdharutaiḥ śubhagandharasai varasparśasukhaiḥ
children.translated_text: With dear and lovely forms, with soft sounds, with fine smells and tastes, and with excellent pleasures of touch,

children.text: pariṣiktamidaṃ kalipāśa jagat mṛgalubdhakapāśi yathaiva kapi ||
children.translated_text: this world is drenched in the snare of strife, just like a monkey in the snare of a hunter.

children.text: sabhayā saraṇāḥ sada vairakarāḥ bahuśoka upadrava kāmaguṇāḥ
children.translated_text: The qualities of desire are fearful, a constant resort of flight, makers of enmity, full of much sorrow and trouble.

children.text: asidhārasamā viṣapatranibhā jahitāryajanairyatha mīḍhaghaṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are like the edge of a sword, like leaves of poison, abandoned by noble people like jars of filth.

children.text: smṛtiśokakarāstamasīkaraṇāḥ bhayahetukarā dukhamūla sadā
children.translated_text: They produce memory and sorrow, make darkness, cause fear, and are always the root of suffering.

children.text: bhavatṛṣṇalatāya vivṛddhikarāḥ sabhayā saraṇā sada kāmaguṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They make the creeper of craving for existence grow; the qualities of desire are always fearful and a resort of fear.

children.text: yatha agnikhadā jvalitā sabhayā tatha kāma ime viditāryajanaḥ
children.translated_text: As a blazing pit of fire is fearful, so these desires are known by noble people.

children.text: mahapaṅkasamā asisundhusamāḥ madhudigdha iva kṣuradhāra yathā ||
children.translated_text: They are like a great mire, like a river of swords, like the edge of a razor smeared with honey.

children.text: yatha sarpisaro yatha mīḍhaghaṭāḥ tatha kāma ime viditā viduṣām
children.translated_text: As a lake of ghee, as jars of filth, so these desires are known by the wise.

children.text: tatha śūlasamā dvijapeśisamāḥ yatha śvāna karaṅka savairamukhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise they are like stakes, like pieces of meat for birds, like a dog's bone that brings hostile mouths.

children.text: udacandrasamā imi kāmaguṇāḥ pratibimba iva girighoṣa yathā
children.translated_text: These sense pleasures are like the moon in water, like a reflection, like an echo in the mountains.

children.text: pratibhāsasamā naṭaraṅgasamāḥ tatha svapnasamā viditāryajanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are like an apparition, like an actor's dance, and like a dream: so they are known by noble people.

children.text: kṣaṇikā vaśikā imi kāmaguṇāḥ tatha māyamarīcisamā alikāḥ
children.translated_text: These sense pleasures are momentary and overpowering; like magic and a mirage, they are false.

children.text: udabudbudaphenasamā vitathā parikalpasamuchita buddha budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Like bubbles and foam on water, unreal, they are understood by awakened wise people as built up by imagination.

children.text: prathame vayase vararūpadharaḥ priya iṣṭa mato iya bālacarī
children.translated_text: In the first age of life, bearing excellent beauty, dear, desired, and esteemed: such is childish conduct.

children.text: jaravyādhidukhai hatatejavapuṃ vijahanti mṛgā iva śuṣkanadīm ||
children.translated_text: But when one's splendor and body are struck by the sufferings of old age and sickness, they abandon him like deer abandoning a dried-up river.

children.text: dhanadhānyavaro bahudravyabalī priya iṣṭa mato iya bālacarī
