children.translated_text: Rich in wealth and grain, powerful through many possessions, dear, desired, and esteemed: such is childish conduct.

children.text: parihīnadhanaṃ puna kṛcchragataṃ vijahanti narā iva śūnyaṭavīm ||
children.translated_text: But when his wealth is lost and he has fallen into hardship, people abandon him as they would an empty wilderness.

children.text: yatha puṣpadrumo saphaleva drumo naru dānaratastatha prītikaro
children.translated_text: Just as a flowering tree, or a tree with fruit, is pleasing, so a man delighting in giving is pleasing.

children.text: dhanahīna jarārtitu yācanako bhavate tada apriyu gṛdhrasamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when, without wealth and afflicted by old age, he becomes a beggar, then he is disliked, like a vulture.

children.text: prabhu dravyabalī vararūpadharaḥ priyasaṃgamanendriyaprītikaro
children.translated_text: A lord, powerful in possessions, bearing excellent beauty, bringing beloved meetings and pleasure to the senses,

children.text: jaravyādhidukhārditu kṣīṇadhano bhavate tada apriyu mṛtyusamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when afflicted by the sufferings of old age and sickness and with wealth exhausted, then becomes disliked, like death.

children.text: jarayā jaritaḥ samatītavayo druma vidyuhateva yathā bhavati
children.translated_text: Worn by old age, with his lifetime passed by, a man becomes like a tree struck by lightning.

children.text: jarajīrṇa agāru yathā sabhayo jaraniḥsaraṇaṃ laghu brūhi mune ||
children.translated_text: As an old, decayed house is fearful, quickly tell the escape from old age, O sage.

children.text: jara śoṣayate naranārigaṇaṃ yatha mālulatā ghanaśālavanam
children.translated_text: Old age dries up the hosts of men and women as a creeper dries up a dense śāla forest.

children.text: jara vīryaparākramavegaharī jara paṅkanimagna yathā puruṣo ||
children.translated_text: Old age steals vigor, strength, and speed; in old age a person is like one sunk in mud.

children.text: jara rūpasurūpavirūpakarī jara tejaharī balasthāmaharī
children.translated_text: Old age makes what is beautiful and well formed ugly; old age steals splendor, strength, and firmness.

children.text: sada saukhyaharī paribhāvakarī jara mṛtyukarī jara ojaharī ||
children.translated_text: It always steals happiness, brings humiliation, brings death, and steals vital power.

children.text: bahurogaśatai ghanavyādhidukhaiḥ upasṛṣṭa jagajjvalateva mṛgāḥ
children.translated_text: The world, beset by hundreds of many illnesses and by the sufferings of dense disease, burns like frightened creatures.

children.text: jaravyādhigataṃ prasamīkṣva jagat dukhaniḥsaraṇaṃ laghu deśayahī ||
children.translated_text: Look upon the world overcome by old age and sickness; quickly teach the escape from suffering.

children.text: śiśire hi yathā himadhātu mahān tṛṇagulmavanauṣadhiojaharo
children.translated_text: As in winter a great mass of snow steals the sap of grasses, shrubs, forest plants, and herbs,

children.text: tatha ojaharo ahu vyādhijaro parihīyati indriya rūpa balam ||
children.translated_text: so sickness and old age steal vitality here; the senses, beauty, and strength decline.

children.text: dhanadhānyamahārthakṣayāntakaro paritāpakaraḥ sahavyādhijaro
children.translated_text: Bringing the destruction of wealth, grain, and great property, bringing torment, together with sickness and old age,

children.text: pratighātakaraḥ priyu dveṣakaraḥ paridāhakaro yatha sūrya nabhe ||
children.translated_text: bringing injury, making what is loved hated, burning like the sun in the sky.

children.text: maraṇaṃ cavanaṃ cuti kālakriyā priyadravyajanena viyogu sadā
children.translated_text: Death, passing away, falling, and the act of time are always separation from beloved possessions and people.

children.text: apunāgamanaṃ ca asaṃgamanaṃ drumapatraphalā nadisrota yathā ||
children.translated_text: There is no return and no meeting again, like leaves and fruits of a tree in a river's current.

children.text: maraṇaṃ vaśitāmavaśīkurute maraṇaṃ harate nadi dāru yathā
children.translated_text: Death brings the powerful under its power; death carries one away like a river carrying wood.

children.text: asahāyu naro vrajate 'dvitiyo svakakarmaphalānugato vivaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without a companion, a man goes alone, a secondless one, helpless, following the fruits of his own karma.

children.text: maraṇo grasate bahuprāṇiśataṃ makareva jalā hari bhūtagaṇam
children.translated_text: Death swallows many hundreds of living beings, like a makara in the water seizing hosts of creatures.

children.text: garuḍo uragaṃ mṛgarāju gajaṃ jvalaneva tṛṇoṣadhibhūtagaṇam ||
children.translated_text: as a <s>garuḍa</s> overcomes a serpent, a lion a royal elephant, or fire the mass of grasses and medicinal plants.

children.text: ima īdṛśakai bahudoṣaśataiḥ jagu mocayituṃ kṛta yā praṇidhi
children.translated_text: To free the world from many hundreds of such faults, you made that vow.

children.text: smara tāṃ purimāṃ praṇidhānacarīṃ ayu kālu tavā abhiniṣkramitum ||
children.translated_text: Remember that former course of your vow; this is the time for you to go forth.

children.text: yada nārigaṇaḥ praharṣito bodhayatī turiyairmahāmunim
children.translated_text: When the delighted group of women awakened the great sage with instruments,

children.text: tada gātha vicitra niścarī tūryaśabdāt sugatānubhāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then varied verses issued from the sound of the instruments through the power of the <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: laghu tadbhañjati sarvasaṃskṛtaṃ acirasthāyi nabheva vidyataḥ
children.translated_text: Quickly it breaks all that is conditioned; it is short-lived, like lightning in the sky.

children.text: ayu kālu tavā upasthitaḥ samayo niṣkramaṇāya suvrata ||
children.translated_text: This time has come for you, the moment for going forth, O firm-vowed one.

children.text: saṃskāra anitya adhruvāḥ āmakumbhopama bhedanātmakāḥ
children.translated_text: Conditioned formations are impermanent and unstable, like unbaked pots, by nature subject to breaking.

children.text: parakeraka yācitopamāḥ pāṃśunagaropama tāvakālikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are like things borrowed from another, like cities of dust, merely temporary.

children.text: saṃskāra pralopadharmime varṣakāli calitaṃ ca lepanam
children.translated_text: Conditioned formations have the nature of decay, like plaster loosened in the rainy season,

children.text: nadikūla ivā savālukaṃ pratyayādhīna svabhāvadurbalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: like a sandy riverbank, dependent on conditions and weak in their own nature.

children.text: saṃskāra pradīpaacivat kṣiprautpattinirodhadharmikāḥ
children.translated_text: Conditioned formations are like the flame of a lamp, having the nature of swift arising and cessation.

children.text: anavasthita mārutopamāḥ phenapiṇḍave asāra durbalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Unfixed, like the wind, they are like a lump of foam, without essence and weak.

children.text: saṃskāra nirīha śūnyakāḥ kadalīskandhasamā nirīkṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Conditioned formations are inactive and empty, like the trunk of a plantain tree when examined.

children.text: māyopama cittamohanā bālaullāpana ukta muṣṭivat ||
children.translated_text: Like illusion, they bewilder the mind; they are said to be like a closed fist deceiving children.

children.text: hetūbhi ca pratyayebhi cā sarvasaṃskāragataṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: And through causes and through conditions the whole range of conditioned formations proceeds.

children.text: anyonya pratītya hetutaḥ tadidaṃ bālajano na budhyate ||
children.translated_text: Because of mutual dependence on causes, this is so, but childish people do not understand it.

children.text: yatha muñja pratītya balvajaṃ rajju vyāyāmabalena vartitā
children.translated_text: Just as a rope, depending on muñja grass and balvaja grass, is twisted by the force of effort,

children.text: ghaṭiyantra sacakra vartate eṣa ekaikaśa nāsti vartanā ||
children.translated_text: and a wheel-machine with its wheel turns, though no turning exists in each part individually,

children.text: tatha sarvabhavāṅgavartinī anyamanyopacayena niśritā
children.translated_text: so the turning of all the factors of existence is supported by their mutual accumulation.

children.text: ekaikaśa teṣu vartinī pūrvaparāntata nopalabhyate ||
children.translated_text: In each one of them singly that turning is not found, either at the earlier or the later end.

children.text: bījasya sato yathāṅkuro na ca yo bīja sa caiva aṅkuro
children.translated_text: Just as, when there is a seed, there is a sprout, yet what is the seed is not itself the sprout,

children.text: na ca tato na caiva tat evamanuccheda aśāśvata dharmatā ||
children.translated_text: and it is not from something other nor simply the same: thus the nature of things is neither annihilated nor eternal.

children.text: saṃskāra avidyapratyayāḥ te saṃskāre na santi tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: Conditioned formations have ignorance as their condition; those formations do not exist in reality.

children.text: saṃskāra avidya caiva hi śūnya eke prakṛtīnirīhakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Conditioned formations and ignorance itself are empty, one in being naturally inactive.

children.text: mudrātpratimudra dṛśyate mudrasaṃkrānti na copalabhyate
children.translated_text: An impression from a seal is seen, yet no passing over of the seal is found.

children.text: na ca tatra na caiva śāśvato eva saṃskārānucchedaśāśvatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is not there, nor again is it eternal; in just this way conditioned formations are neither annihilated nor eternal.

children.text: cakṣuśca pratītya rūpataḥ cakṣuvijñānamihopajāyate
children.translated_text: Depending on the eye and on form, eye-consciousness arises here.

children.text: na ca cakṣuṣi rūpa niśrita rūpasaṃkrānti na caiva cakṣuṣi ||
children.translated_text: Yet form does not rest in the eye, nor is there a passing over of form into the eye.

children.text: nairātmyaśubhāśca dharmime punarātmeti śubhāśca kalpitāḥ
children.translated_text: Dharmas are selfless and impure, yet again they are imagined as self and as pure.

children.text: viparītamasadvikalpitaṃ cakṣuvijñāna tatopajāyate ||
children.translated_text: From that false imagining of the unreal and inverted, eye-consciousness arises.

children.text: vijñānanirodhasaṃbhavaṃ vijñānotpādavyayaṃ vipaśyati
children.translated_text: He discerns the arising from the cessation of consciousness, the arising and passing away of consciousness.

children.text: akahiṃ ca gataṃ anāgataṃ śūnya māyopama yogi paśyati ||
children.translated_text: The yogin sees it as not having gone anywhere and not having come from anywhere, empty and like illusion.

children.text: araṇiṃ yatha cottarāraṇiṃ hastavyāyāma trayebhi saṃgati
children.translated_text: Just as a lower fire-stick and an upper fire-stick, together with manual effort, come into combination in three ways,

children.text: iti pratyayato 'gni jāyate jātu kṛtārthu laghu nirudhyate ||
children.translated_text: so from conditions fire arises, and once its purpose is accomplished it quickly ceases.

children.text: atha paṇḍitu kaści mārgate kutayaṃ āgatu kutra yāti vā
children.translated_text: Then if some learned person seeks, "From where has this come, and where does it go?"

children.text: vidiśo diśi sarvi mārgato nāgati nāsya gatiśca labhyate ||
children.translated_text: though he searches in the intermediate quarters and in every direction, no coming or going of it is found.

children.text: skandhadhātvāyatanāni dhātavaḥ tṛṣṇa avidyā iti karmapratyayā
children.translated_text: The aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, the elements, craving, ignorance, and karmic conditions:

children.text: sāmagri tu sattvasūcanā sa ca paramārthatu nopalabhyate ||
children.translated_text: their assemblage is a designation of a being, but in ultimate reality that being is not found.

children.text: kaṇṭhoṣṭha pratītya tālukaṃ jihvāparivarti akṣarā
children.translated_text: Depending on the throat, lips, and palate, letters move with the tongue.

children.text: na ca kaṇṭhagatā na tāluke akṣaraikaika tu nopalabhyate ||
children.translated_text: Yet the letters are not in the throat or in the palate, and each single letter is not found.

children.text: sāmagri pratītyataśca sā vācamanabuddhivaśena niścarī
children.translated_text: Depending on that assemblage, speech issues forth under the power of mind and understanding.

children.text: mana vāca adṛśyarūpiṇī bāhyato 'bhyantara nopalabhyate ||
children.translated_text: Mind and speech are invisible in form; they are not found externally or internally.

children.text: utpādavyayaṃ vipaśyato vāca rutaghoṣasvarasya paṇḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: The learned one, discerning the arising and passing away of speech, utterance, sound, and tone,

children.text: kṣaṇikāṃ vaśikāṃ tadā dṛśī sarvā vāca pratiśrutakopamām ||
children.translated_text: then sees all speech as momentary, dependent, and like an echo.

children.text: yatha tantri pratītya dārū ca hastavyāyāma trayebhi saṃgati
children.translated_text: Just as, depending on strings and wood, together with manual effort, a threefold combination occurs,

children.text: tuṇavīṇasughoṣakādibhiḥ śabdo niścarate tadudbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from lutes, vīṇās, pleasant-sounding instruments, and the like a sound issues forth, born from that,

children.text: atha paṇḍitu kaści mārgate kutayaṃ āgatu kutra yāti vā
children.translated_text: then if some learned person seeks, "From where has this come, and where does it go?"

children.text: vidiśo diśi sarvi mārgataḥ śabdagamanāgamanaṃ na labhyate ||
children.translated_text: though he searches in the intermediate quarters and in every direction, the going or coming of sound is not found.

children.text: tatha hetubhi pratyayebhi ca sarvasaṃskāragataṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: So too, through causes and through conditions, the whole range of conditioned formations proceeds.

children.text: yogī puna bhūtadaśanāt śūnya saṃskāra nirīha paśyati ||
children.translated_text: But the yogin, by seeing reality, sees conditioned formations as empty and inactive.

children.text: skandhāyatanāni dhātavaḥ śūnya adhyātmika śūnya bāhyakāḥ
children.translated_text: The aggregates, sense-bases, and elements are empty; what is internal is empty, and what is external is empty.

children.text: sattvātmaviviktamanālayā dharmākāśasvabhāvalakṣaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are separated from being and self, without foundation in the mind; dharmas have the characteristic nature of space.

children.text: iya īdṛśa dharmalakṣaṇā buddha dīpaṃkara darśane tvayā
children.translated_text: Such a characteristic of dharmas, when you saw <s>Buddha Dīpaṃkara</s>,

children.text: anubuddha svayaṃ yathātmanā tatha bodhehi sadevamānuṣāṃ ||
children.translated_text: you yourself awakened to, just as it is. In that same way awaken gods and humans.

children.text: viparītaabhūtakalpitaiḥ rāgadoṣaiḥ paridahyate jagat
children.translated_text: The world is burned by the fires of passion and hatred, imagined from what is inverted and unreal.

children.text: kṛpameghasamāmbuśītalāṃ muñca dhārāmamṛtasya nāyakā ||
children.translated_text: O guide, release a stream of nectar, cool as the water of a cloud of compassion.

children.text: tvayi yasya kṛtena paṇḍitā dattu dānaṃ bahukalpakoṭiṣu
children.translated_text: For whose sake, O wise one, you gave gifts through many koṭis of kalpas,

children.text: saṃprāpya hi bodhimuttamāṃ āryadhanasaṃgraha kariṣya prāṇinām ||
children.translated_text: having attained supreme awakening, you will gather the noble wealth for living beings.

children.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā nārya dhanahīna daridra duḥkhitām
children.translated_text: Remember that former conduct; the noble, bereft of wealth, are poor and afflicted.

children.text: mā upekṣahi sattvasārathe āryadhanasaṃgrahi teṣu kurvahi ||
children.translated_text: Do not neglect them, charioteer of beings; gather the noble wealth for them.

children.text: tvayi śīla sadā surakṣitaṃ pithanārthāya apāyabhūminām
children.translated_text: In you morality has always been well guarded, for the purpose of closing off the realms of bad rebirths.

children.text: svargāmṛtadvāramuttamāṃ darśayiṣye bahusattvakoṭinām ||
children.translated_text: I will show the supreme gateway to heaven and nectar for many koṭis of beings.

children.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā baddhvā dvāra nirayāya bhūminām
children.translated_text: Remember that former practice: after barring the door to hell for the realms,

children.text: svargāmṛtadvāra muñcahī ṛddhyahi śīlavato vicintitam ||
children.translated_text: open the gateway to heaven and nectar; bring to fulfillment the resolve of one endowed with morality.

children.text: tvayi kṣānti sadā surakṣitā pratighakrodhaśamārtha dehinām
children.translated_text: In you patience has always been well guarded, for the sake of pacifying hostility and anger among embodied beings.

children.text: bhāvārṇava sattva tāriyā sthāpayiṣye śivi kṣemi nirjvale ||
children.translated_text: Having ferried beings across the ocean of becoming, I will establish them in the auspicious, secure, flame-free state.

children.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā vairavyāpādavihiṃsaākulām
children.translated_text: Remember that former practice, amid beings confused by enmity, malice, and violence.

children.text: mā upekṣa vihiṃsacāriṇaḥ kṣāntibhūmīya sthape imaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: Do not neglect those who practice violence; establish this world on the ground of patience.

children.text: tvayi vīrya yadartha sevitaṃ dharmanāvaṃ samudānayitvanā
children.translated_text: For the sake of that for which energy was cultivated by you, having raised up the boat of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: uttārya jagadbhavārṇavāt thapayiṣye śivi kṣemi nirjvale ||
children.translated_text: I will carry the world across from the ocean of becoming and establish it in the auspicious, secure, flame-free state.

children.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā caturoghairiva muhyate jagat ||
children.translated_text: Remember that former practice: the world is bewildered as if by the four floods.

children.text: laghu vīryabalaṃ parākramā sattva saṃtārayahī anāyakāṃ ||
children.translated_text: Quickly, with the strength of energy and valor, ferry across the beings who have no guide.

children.text: tvaya dhyānakileśadhyeṣaṇā bhāvitā yasya kṛtena sūratā
children.translated_text: Meditation, the overcoming of afflictions, was cultivated by you, through which gentleness is brought about.

children.text: bhrāntendriya prākṛtendriyāṃ kvapi cittāryapathe sthapeṣyaham ||
children.translated_text: I will establish beings with wandering faculties and ordinary faculties somewhere upon the noble path of mind.

children.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā kleśajālairihamākulaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Remember that former practice: here the world is entangled in the nets of affliction.

children.text: mā upekṣahi kleśupadrutāṃ dhyānaikāgri sthapehimāṃ prajām ||
children.translated_text: Do not neglect the people oppressed by afflictions; establish this folk in meditative one-pointedness.

children.text: tvayi prajña purā subhāvitā mohavidyāndhatamovṛte jage
children.translated_text: Wisdom was formerly well cultivated by you in a world enveloped by the blind darkness of delusion and ignorance.

children.text: bahudharmaśatābhilokane dāsye cakṣuṣi tattvadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: Through the vision of many hundreds of dharmas, I will give the eye that sees reality.

children.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā mohavidyāndhatamovṛte jage
children.translated_text: Remember that former practice in a world enveloped by the blind darkness of delusion and ignorance.

children.text: dadahī varaprajña suprabhā dharmacakṣuṃ vimalaṃ nirañjanam ||
children.translated_text: Give the excellent, brightly shining noble wisdom, the stainless and untainted eye of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: iyamīdṛśa gātha niścarī tūryasaṃgītiravātu nāriṇām
children.translated_text: Such verses issued forth from the women amid the sound of instrumental music,

children.text: yaṃ śrutva middhaṃ vivarjiyā cittu preṣeti varāgrabodhaye ||
children.translated_text: and, having heard them, casting off sleepiness, he directed his mind toward the best, supreme awakening.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo 'ntaḥpuramadhyagato bodhisattvo 'virahito 'bhūddharmaśravaṇena avirahito 'bhūddharmamanasikāreṇa
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, the bodhisattva, while staying in the midst of the inner palace, was not separated from hearing the <s>dharma</s> and was not separated from attention to the <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tatkasmāddhetos tathā hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo dīrgharātraṃ sagauravo 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Why was that? For thus, monks, the bodhisattva had for a long night been reverential

children.text: dharmeṣu dharmabhāṇakeṣu cādhyāśayena dharmārthiko dharmakāmo dharmaratirato 'bhūt
children.translated_text: toward dharmas and toward preachers of <s>dharma</s>; with deep intention he sought <s>dharma</s>, loved <s>dharma</s>, and delighted in taking pleasure in <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: dharmaparyeṣṭyatṛpto yathāśrutadharmasaṃprakāśakaḥ anuttaro mahādharmadānapatiḥ nirāmiṣadharmadeśako dharmadānenāmatsaraḥ ācāryamuṣṭivigato dharmānudharmapratipanno dharmapratipattiśūraḥ dharmalayano dharmatrāṇo dharmaśaraṇo dharmapratiśaraṇo dharmaparāyaṇaḥ dharmanidhyāptiḥ kṣāntiniryātaḥ prajñāpāramitācarita upāyakauśalyagatiṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was never satisfied in searching for <s>dharma</s>; he proclaimed <s>dharma</s> just as he had heard it; he was an unsurpassed great lord of the gift of <s>dharma</s>, a preacher of <s>dharma</s> without material motive, unstingy with the gift of <s>dharma</s>, free from a teacher's closed fist, practicing <s>dharma</s> in accordance with <s>dharma</s>, heroic in the practice of <s>dharma</s>, having <s>dharma</s> as his abode, his protection, his refuge, his final resort, and his supreme goal, absorbed in <s>dharma</s>, directed toward patience, practiced in the perfection of wisdom, and gone into the course of skillful means.

children.text: tatra bhikṣavo bodhisattvo mahopāyakauśalyavikrīḍitena sarvāntaḥpurasya yathādhimuktyā īryāpathamupadarśya paurvikāṇāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ lokaviṣayasamatikrāntānāṃ lokānuvartanakriyādharmatāmanuvartya dīrgharātraṃ suviditakāmadoṣaḥ sattvaparipākavaśād akāmāt kāmopabhogaṃ saṃdarśya aparimitakuśalamūlopacayapuṇyasaṃbhārabalaviśeṣaṇāsadṛśīṃ lokādhipateyatāṃ saṃdarśya devamanuṣyātikrāntaṃ sārodāravividhavicitrarūpaśabdagandharasasparśaparamaratiramaṇīyaṃ kāmaratirasaukhyamupadarśya sarvakāmaratisvaviṣayeṣvaparyantatvāt svacittavaśavartitāṃ saṃdarśya pūrvapraṇidhānabalasahāyakuśalamūlopacitān sattvān samānasaṃvāsatayā paripācya sarvalokasaṃkleśamalāsaṃkliṣṭacittatayāntaḥpuramadhyagato yathābhinimantritasya sattvadhātoḥ paripākakālamavekṣamāṇo bhūyasyā mātrayā bodhisattvastasmin samaye pūrvapratijñāmanusmarati sma buddhadharmāṃścāmukhīkaroti sma praṇidhānabalaṃ cābhinirharati sma
children.translated_text: There, monks, by the play of great skillful means, the bodhisattva showed modes of conduct to the entire inner palace according to their dispositions; following the worldly-conforming practice of former bodhisattvas who had passed beyond the sphere of the world, long aware of the faults of desire, under the power of maturing beings, he displayed the enjoyment of desires though himself without desire. He displayed a lordship over the world unlike any other, through the distinctive power of accumulated immeasurable roots of good and stores of merit; he displayed a pleasure and happiness of desire surpassing gods and humans, supremely delightful through excellent, noble, various, and variegated forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches; since all pleasures of desire are endless within their own domains, he displayed mastery over his own mind. Having matured, by living together with them, beings whose roots of good had been accumulated with the help of the force of his former vow, with a mind unstained by all the stains of worldly defilement, while staying in the midst of the inner palace and observing the time for the maturation of the realm of beings he had undertaken, the bodhisattva at that time, in very great measure, remembered his former vow, brought the dharmas of the Buddha before his mind, and put forth the power of his vow.

children.text: sattveṣu ca mahākaruṇāmavakrāmati sma
children.translated_text: And he entered into great compassion for beings.

children.text: sattvapramokṣaṃ ca cintayati sma
children.translated_text: And he thought about the liberation of beings.

children.text: sarvasaṃpado vipattiparyavasānā iti pratyavekṣate sma
children.translated_text: He reflected, "All attainments end in loss."

children.text: anekopadravabhayabahulaṃ ca saṃsāramupaparīkṣate sma
children.translated_text: And he examined <s>saṃsāra</s> as full of many dangers and fears.

children.text: mārakalipāśāṃśca saṃchinatti sma
children.translated_text: And he cut apart the snares of <s>Māra</s> and conflict.

children.text: saṃsāraprabandhāccātmānamuccārayati sma
children.translated_text: And he lifted himself out from the continuity of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: nirvāṇe ca cittaṃ saṃpreṣayati sma ||
children.translated_text: And he directed his mind toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: tatra bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ pūrvāntata eva suviditasaṃsāradoṣaḥ saṃskṛtenādhyāśayenānarthikaḥ sarvopādānaparigrahairanarthiko buddhadharmanirvāṇābhimukhaḥ saṃsāraparāṅmukhastathāgatagocarābhirataḥ māraviṣayagocarāsaṃsṛṣṭaḥ ādīptabhavadoṣadarśī traidhātukānniḥśaraṇābhiprāyaḥ saṃsāradoṣādīnavaniḥsaraṇakuśalaḥ pravrajyābhilāṣī niṣkramaṇābhiprāyo vivekanimno vivekapravaṇo vivekaprāgbhāraḥ āraṇyaprāraṇyābhimukhaḥ pravivekapraśamābhikāṅkṣī ātmaparahitapratipannaḥ anuttarapratipattiśūro lokasyārthakāmo hitakāmaḥ sukhakāmo yogakṣemakāmo lokānukampako hitaiṣī maitrīvihārī mahākāruṇikaḥ saṃgrahavastukuśalaḥ satatasamitam aparikhinnamānasaḥ sattvaparipākavinayakuśalaḥ sarvasattveṣvekaputrakapremānugatamanasikāraḥ sarvavastunirapekṣaparityāgī dānasaṃvibhāgarataḥ prayuktatyāgaḥ prayatapāṇiḥ tyāgaśūro yaṣṭayajñaḥ susamṛddhapuṇyaḥ susaṃgṛhītapuṇyaḥ pariṣkāravigatamalāmātsaryasunigṛhītacitto 'nuttaro mahādānapatirdattvā ca vipākāpratikāṅkṣī pradānaśūraḥ icchāmahecchālobhadveṣamadamānamohamātsaryapramukhasarvārikleśagaṇapratyarthikanigrahāyābhyutthitaḥ sarvajñatācittotpādaprabandhāccalitaḥ mahātyāgacittasaṃnāhasusaṃnaddhaḥ lokānukampako hitaiṣīva varmitakavacitavīryaḥ sattvapramokṣālambanamahākaruṇābalavikramaparākramaḥ avaivartikasarvasattvasamacittatyāgapraharaṇo yathābhiprāyasattvāśayasaṃtoṣaṇo bodhibhājanībhūtaḥ kālākṣuṇṇadharmavedhī bodhipariṇāmapraṇidhiḥ anavanāmitadhvajas trimaṇḍalapariśodhanadānaparityāgī jñānavaravajradṛḍhapraharaṇaḥ sunigṛhītakleśapratyarthikaḥ śīlaguṇacāritrapratipannaḥ svārakṣitakāyavāṅmanaskarmānto 'ṇumātrāvadyabhayadarśī supariśuddhaśīlaḥ amalavimalanirmalacittaḥ sarvaduruktadurāgatavacanapathākrośaparibhāṣaṇakutsanatāḍanatarjanavadhabandhanāvarodhanaparikleśāluḍitacitto 'kṣubhitacittaḥ kṣāntisaurabhyasampannaḥ akṣato 'nupahato 'vyāpannacittaḥ sarvasattvahitārthāyottaptavīryārambhī dṛḍhasamādānasarvakuśalamūladharmasamudānayanāpratyudāvartyasmṛtimān susaṃprajñāsusamāhito 'vikṣiptacitto dhyānaikāgramanasikāro dharmapravicayakuśalo labdhāloko vigatatamo'ndhakāraḥ anityaduḥkhātmāśubhākāraparibhāvitacetāḥ smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇaṛddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgāryasatyasarvabodhipakṣadharmasuparikarmakṛtamanasikāraḥ śamathavipaśyanāsuparyavadātabuddhiḥ pratītyasamutpādasatyadarśī satyānubodhādaparapratyayastrivimokṣasukhavikrīḍito māyāmarīcisvapnodakacandrapratiśrutkāpratibhāsopamasarvadharmanayāvatīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, monks, from the very beginning the bodhisattva was one who well knew the faults of saṃsāra. In his disposition he had no use for conditioned things, no use for all appropriation and possession; he was turned toward the dharma of the Buddhas and toward nirvāṇa, turned away from saṃsāra, delighted in the range of the Tathāgatas, unmingled with the range that is Māra's domain, seeing the fault of existence as a blazing fire, intending escape from the three realms, skilled in the faults, dangers, and escape from saṃsāra, longing for renunciation, intent on departure, inclined to solitude, bent toward solitude, sloping toward solitude, facing the forest and wilderness, and desiring seclusion and peace. He had set out for the good of himself and others; he was heroic in the unsurpassed practice, wishing for the world's welfare, benefit, happiness, and security, compassionate toward the world, seeking its good, dwelling in loving-kindness, great in compassion, skilled in the means of gathering beings, constantly and continually of unwearied mind, skilled in ripening and disciplining beings, with an attention toward all beings accompanied by love as for an only son, relinquishing all things without regard for them, delighting in gifts and sharing, intent on renunciation, with purified hands, heroic in giving, performing abundant sacrifice, rich in merit, having well gathered merit, with a mind well restrained from the stains of envy over possessions. He was an unsurpassed great lord of gifts and, after giving, did not expect a result; he was heroic in bestowal. He had risen up to subdue every host of enemy-defilements headed by desire, excessive desire, greed, hatred, intoxication, pride, delusion, and envy; he was moved by the continual arising of the thought of omniscience, well armed with the armor of a mind of great renunciation, compassionate toward the world and seeking its good, as if clothed in armor and mail of vigor, with courage and force strengthened by great compassion taking the liberation of beings as its object. He was irreversible, with a mind equal toward all beings, armed with the weapon of generosity and abandonment, satisfying beings according to their intentions and dispositions, made into a vessel for awakening, penetrating the dharma that time had not impaired, resolved to dedicate all to awakening, with an unlowered banner, giving and relinquishing purified in the three spheres, striking with the firm diamond weapon of excellent knowledge, having well subdued the hostile defilements, engaged in the virtues of morality and conduct. His acts of body, speech, and mind were well guarded by himself; he saw fear in the smallest fault, was perfectly pure in morality, with a stainless, spotless, immaculate mind. His mind was not disturbed or shaken by any path of ill-spoken, ill-directed words, abuse, reviling, censure, beating, threats, killing, bondage, confinement, or torment; his mind was uninjured, unharmed, and without malice, endowed with the fragrance of patience. For the welfare and benefit of all beings he undertook heated vigor; mindful and not turning back from the undertaking of firm vows and the accumulation of all roots of wholesome dharmas, he was clearly aware, well concentrated, of undistracted mind, with his attention one-pointed in meditation, skilled in the investigation of dharma, having obtained light and dispelled the darkness of gloom. His mind had been cultivated by the aspects of impermanence, suffering, selflessness, and impurity; his attention had been well trained in all the dharmas on the side of awakening, the establishments of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of miraculous power, faculties, powers, limbs of awakening, path, and noble truths; his intelligence had been well purified in calm and insight. He saw the truth of dependent arising; through awakening to truth he was independent of another's testimony; he played in the happiness of the three liberations, and he had entered into the method that all dharmas are comparable to illusion, mirage, dream, the moon in water, echo, and reflected appearance.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvasyaivaṃ bhavati pratikṛtiḥ evaṃ dharmavihārī evaṃ guṇamāhātmyavihārī evaṃ sattvārthābhiyuktavihārī abhūt
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, monks, such was the bodhisattva's character: in this way he lived in dharma, in this way he lived in the greatness of qualities, and in this way he lived devoted to the welfare of beings.

children.text: bhūyasyā mātrayā ābhirdaśadigbuddhādhiṣṭhānatūryasaṃgītiviniḥsṛtābhirgāthābhiḥ saṃcoditaḥ sa tasyāṃ velāyāṃ pūrveṣāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ caramabhavopagatānām antaḥpuraparipācitāni catvāri dharmamukhānyāmukhīkaroti sma
children.translated_text: Moreover, urged on in great measure by those verses that issued from the music of instruments through the empowering presence of the Buddhas of the ten directions, at that time he brought before his mind the four dharma-gateways by which the inner palaces of former bodhisattvas who had reached their final existence had been matured.

children.text: katamāni catvāri yadidaṃ dānaṃ priyavacanamarthakriyāṃ samānārthatāṃ ca
children.translated_text: What are the four? Namely, giving, pleasant speech, beneficial action, and sharing the same purpose.

children.text: catuḥsaṃgrahavastuprayoganirhāraviśuddhiṃ ca nāma dharmamukhamāmukhīkaroti sma
children.translated_text: He brought before his mind the dharma-gateway called the purification of the successful application of the four means of gathering beings.

children.text: triratnavaṃśasādhāraṇābhiprāyo vipraṇāśasarvajñatācittapraṇidhānabalādhānāvaivartyaviṣayaṃ ca nāma dharmamukhamāmukhīkaroti sma
children.translated_text: He brought before his mind the dharma-gateway called the irreversible sphere of strengthening the power of the vow of the thought of omniscience, whose intention is shared with the lineage of the Three Jewels and is free from ruin.

children.text: sarvasattvāparityāgādhyāśayamahākaruṇāvatāratāṃ ca nāma dharmamukhamāmukhīkaroti sma
children.translated_text: He brought before his mind the dharma-gateway called entry into great compassion, with the disposition not to abandon any being.

children.text: sarvabodhipakṣadharmapade prabhedārthābhiniścayajñānasaṃsārabalaviśeṣasamudānayamahāvyūhaṃ ca nāma dharmamukhamāmukhīkaroti sma
children.translated_text: He brought before his mind the dharma-gateway called the great array for accumulating the distinctive power of knowledge that determines the meanings of the divisions in all the dharmas on the side of awakening and in saṃsāra.

children.text: imāni catvāri dharmamukhānyāmukhīkṛtya bodhisattvaḥ sarvasyāntaḥpurasya paripācanārthaṃ tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpamṛddhyabhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskaroti sma yathārūpeṇa ṛddhyabhisaṃskāreṇābhisaṃskṛtena tebhyaḥ saṃgītirutebhyo bodhisattvānubhāvenemānyevaṃrūpāṇi dharmamukhaśatasahasrāṇi niścaranti sma
children.translated_text: Having brought these four dharma-gateways before his mind, the bodhisattva at that time, for the purpose of maturing the whole inner palace, formed such a miraculous formation that, when that miraculous formation had been formed, by the bodhisattva's power hundreds of thousands of dharma-gateways of this kind issued forth from those musical sounds.

children.text: tadyathā ||
children.translated_text: That is to say:

children.text: udārachandena ca āśayena adhyāśayenā karuṇāya prāṇiṣu
children.translated_text: And with a noble intention, with a deep resolve of compassion for living beings,

children.text: utpadyate cittu varāgrabodhaye śabde ca rūpasturiyebhi niścarī ||
children.translated_text: the mind arises toward the highest and best awakening; and this sound issued from the musical instruments.

children.text: śraddhā prasādo adhimukti gauravaṃ nirmānatā onamanā gurūṇām
children.translated_text: Faith, serenity, conviction, reverence, freedom from pride, humility, honoring of teachers,

children.text: paripṛcchanā kiṃkuśalaṃgaveṣaṇā anusmṛtībhāvanu śabda niścarī ||
children.translated_text: questioning, inquiry into what is wholesome, and cultivation of recollection: this sound issued forth.

children.text: dāne dabhe saṃyamaśīlaśabdaḥ kṣāntīya śabdastatha vīryaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: The sound of giving, generosity, restraint, and morality; likewise the sound of patience and the sound of vigor;

children.text: dhyānābhinirhārasamādhiśabdaḥ prajñā upāyasya ca śabda niścarī ||
children.translated_text: the sound of the production of meditation and samādhi, and the sound of wisdom and skillful means issued forth.

children.text: maitrāya śabdaḥ karuṇāya śabdo muditāupekṣāya abhijñaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: The sound of loving-kindness, the sound of compassion, the sound of sympathetic joy and equanimity, and the sound of superknowledges;

children.text: catusaṃgrahāvastuviniścayena sattvāna paripācanaśabda niścarī ||
children.translated_text: with the ascertainment of the four means of gathering, the sound of bringing beings to maturity issued forth.

children.text: smṛterupasthānaprabhedaśabdaḥ samyakprahāṇāstatha ṛddhipādā
children.translated_text: The sound of the divisions of the establishments of mindfulness; likewise the right efforts and the bases of miraculous power;

children.text: pañcedriyā pañcabalaprabhedā bodhyaṅgaśabdasturiyebhi niścarī ||
children.translated_text: the divisions of the five faculties and the five powers, and the sound of the factors of awakening issued from the instruments.

children.text: aṣṭāṅgiko mārgabalaprabhedaḥ śamathasya śabdo 'tha vipaśyanāyāḥ
children.translated_text: The divisions of the power of the eightfold path, the sound of calm, and then of insight;

children.text: anityaduḥkhārtianātmaśabdaḥ aśubhārtiśabdo turiyebhi niścarī ||
children.translated_text: the sound of impermanence, suffering, affliction, and selflessness, and the sound of the affliction of impurity issued from the instruments.

children.text: virāgaśabdaśca vivekaśabdaḥ kṣayajñānaśabdo anutpādaśabdaḥ
children.translated_text: The sound of dispassion and the sound of seclusion, the sound of knowledge of destruction and the sound of non-arising,

children.text: anirodhaśabdaśca anālayaṃ ca nirvāṇaśabdasturiyebhi niścarī ||
children.translated_text: the sound of non-cessation and of non-clinging, and the sound of <s>nirvāṇa</s> issued from the instruments.

children.text: ima evarūpāsturiyebhi śabdāḥ saṃbodhiśabdaścanubhāva niścarī
children.translated_text: Sounds of just this sort, and the sound of perfect awakening, issued from the instruments by their power.

children.text: yaṃ śrutva sarvā pramadā nu śikṣitā varāgrasattve praṇidhenti bodhaye ||
children.translated_text: Having heard them, all the women, now instructed, made their aspiration for awakening before the highest and best being.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo 'ntaḥpuramadhyagatena bodhisattvena tāni caturaśītistrīsahasrāṇi paripācitānyabhūvan anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bahūni ca devatāśatasahasrāṇi ye tatra samprāptā abhūvan ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, while the bodhisattva was staying within the inner palace, those eighty-four thousand women were brought to maturity for unsurpassed complete awakening, and many hundreds of thousands of deities who had arrived there were also brought to maturity.

children.text: tathā abhiniṣkramaṇakāle tasmin samaye bodhisattvasya hrīdevo nāma tuṣitakāyiko devaputro 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ sa rātrau praśāntāyāṃ dvātriṃśatā devaputrasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bodhisattvasyopasthānaprāsādas tenopasaṃkrāmat
children.translated_text: Then, at the time of the going forth, on that occasion a devaputra named <s>Hrīdeva</s>, belonging to the <s>Tuṣita</s> host, for the sake of unsurpassed complete awakening, in the quiet of night, surrounded and attended by thirty-two thousand devaputras, approached the palace where the bodhisattva was staying.

children.text: upasaṃkramya gaganatalagata eva bodhisattvaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, while remaining in the expanse of the sky, he addressed the bodhisattva with verses:

children.text: cyuti darśitā atiyaśā janma ca saṃdarśitaṃ puruṣasiṃha
children.translated_text: Your passing from heaven has been displayed, O greatly renowned one, and your birth has been displayed, O lion among men.

children.text: antaḥpuraṃ vidarśitu kṛtānuvṛttistvayā loke ||
children.translated_text: You have shown the inner palace; you have acted in conformity with the world.

children.text: paripācitā ti bahavo deva manuja loki dharmamanuprāpya
children.translated_text: Many gods and humans in the world have been brought to maturity by you after attaining the <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: ayamadya kālasamayo niṣkramye mati vicintehi ||
children.translated_text: Now this is the proper time: think on the resolve to go forth.

children.text: na hi baddha mocayātī na cāndhapuruṣena darśiyati mārgaḥ
children.translated_text: One who is bound does not set others free, nor does a blind man show the path.

children.text: muktastu mocayātī sacakṣuṣā darśayati mārgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But one who is free sets others free; one with sight shows the path.

children.text: ye sattva kāmadāsā gṛhe dhane putrabhāryapariśraddhāḥ
children.translated_text: Those beings who are slaves to desire, attached to house, wealth, sons, and wives,

children.text: te tubhya śiṣyamāṇā naiṣkramyamatau spṛhāṃ kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: being taught by you, would develop longing for the resolve of renunciation.

children.text: aiśvarya kāmakrīḍā catudvīpā sapta ratna vijahitvā
children.translated_text: Having abandoned sovereignty, sensual sports, the four continents, and the seven jewels,

children.text: niṣkrānta tvāṃ viditvā spṛhayetsanarāmaro lokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the world with its men and gods knows that you have gone forth, it will long to do the same.

children.text: kiṃ cāpi dhyānasaukhyairviharasi dharmairna cāsi kāmarataḥ
children.translated_text: Although you dwell in the happiness of meditation and in dharmas, and are not attached to desire,

children.text: atha puna ciraprasuptāṃ bodhaya marumānuṣaśatāni ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless awaken the hundreds of gods and humans who have long been asleep.

children.text: atipatita yauvanamidaṃ girinadi yatha cañcalapracalavegā
children.translated_text: This youth passes away; like a mountain river its speed is wavering and unstable.

children.text: gatayauvanasya bhavato naiṣkramyamatirna śobhete ||
children.translated_text: For you, when youth has gone, the resolve for renunciation would not be fitting.

children.text: tatsādhu taruṇarūpe prathame varayāvane 'bhiniṣkramya
children.translated_text: Therefore, while your form is young, in the first and finest youth, go forth.

children.text: uttāraya pratijñāṃ kuruṣva cārthaṃ suragaṇānām ||
children.translated_text: Fulfill your vow, and accomplish the purpose of the hosts of gods.

children.text: na ca kāmaguṇaratībhistṛptirlavaṇodadheryathāmbhobhiḥ
children.translated_text: There is no satisfaction through delight in sensual pleasures, just as the salt ocean is not satisfied by waters.

children.text: te tṛpta yeṣa prajñā āryā lokottarā virajā ||
children.translated_text: Those are satisfied whose wisdom is noble, supramundane, and stainless.

children.text: tvamiha priyo manāpo rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya rāṣṭrasya
children.translated_text: Here you are dear and pleasing to King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and to the kingdom.

children.text: śatapatrasadṛśavadanā naiṣkramyamatiṃ vicintehi ||
children.translated_text: O lotus-faced one, think on the resolve for renunciation.

children.text: ādīpta kleśatāpairaniḥśaraṇairgāḍhabandhanairbaddhāṃ
children.translated_text: Beings are bound by the fires of defilements, without refuge, fastened by tight bonds.

children.text: śīghraṃ pramokṣamārge sthāpaya śānte asamavīrā ||
children.translated_text: Quickly establish them on the peaceful path of release, O hero without equal.

children.text: tvaṃ vaidya dhātukuśalaścirāturāṃ sattvarogasaṃspṛṣṭāṃ
children.translated_text: You are a physician skilled in the elements; beings have long been sick, touched by the disease of existence.

children.text: bhaiṣajyadharmayogairnirvāṇasukhe sthapaya śīghram ||
children.translated_text: By the applications of the medicine of <s>dharma</s>, establish them quickly in the happiness of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: andhātamā anayanā mohākuladṛṣṭijālabaddhāḥ
children.translated_text: They are blind in darkness, without eyes, bound in the net of views confused by delusion.

children.text: prajñāpradīpacakṣuḥ śodhaya śīghraṃ naramarūṇām ||
children.translated_text: With the eye that is the lamp of wisdom, quickly purify the gods and humans.

children.text: samudīkṣante bahavo devāsuranāgayakṣagandharvāḥ
children.translated_text: Many gods, asuras, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas look on,

children.text: drakṣyāma bodhiprāptaṃ niruttaraṃ dharma śroṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'We shall see him attain awakening, and we shall hear the unsurpassed <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: drakṣyati ca bhujagarājo bhavanaṃ avabhāsitaṃ tava śirīye
children.translated_text: And the serpent king will see his palace lit up by your splendor.

children.text: kariyati anantapūjā pūrehi vratāśayastasya ||
children.translated_text: He will perform boundless worship; fulfill the intention of his vow.

children.text: catvāri lokapālāḥ sasainyakāste tava pradīkṣante
children.translated_text: The four world-protectors, together with their armies, are waiting for you.

children.text: dāsyāma caturi pātrāṃ bodhidhvaji pūrṇamanasasya ||
children.translated_text: They think, 'We shall give the four bowls to him whose mind is fulfilled beneath the banner of awakening.'

children.text: brahma praśāntacārī udīkṣate maitravākvaruṇalābhī
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, peaceful in conduct, looks on, having obtained speech imbued with friendliness and boon-granting power.

children.text: adhyoṣiṣye narendraṃ vartenti niruttaraṃ cakram ||
children.translated_text: He thinks, 'I shall entreat the lord of men to turn the unsurpassed wheel.'

children.text: bodhiparipācikāpi ca devata abhivusta bodhimaṇḍesmiṃ
children.translated_text: And the deity who ripens awakening, dwelling at the seat of awakening,

children.text: utpatsye 'yaṃ satya ti drakṣyāmyabhibudhyato bodhim ||
children.translated_text: thinks, 'It is true that this one will arise; I shall see him awakening to enlightenment.'

children.text: satyaṃ hi bodhisattvā antaḥpuriye kriyā vidarśenti
children.translated_text: Truly bodhisattvas display acts within the inner palace.

children.text: pūrvaṃgamo bhava tvaṃ mā bheṣyasi paścimasteṣām ||
children.translated_text: Be the forerunner; you will not be the last among them.

children.text: mañjuruta mañjughoṣā smarāhi dīpaṃkarasya vyākaraṇam
children.translated_text: O sweet-toned one, O gentle-voiced one, remember the prophecy of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>.

children.text: bhūtaṃ tathā avitathā jinaghoṣarutaṃ udīrehi ||
children.translated_text: Utter the real, unmistakable sound of the proclamation of the <s>Jina</s>.

children.text: Chapter 14

iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ saṃcoditaḥ san tena devaputreṇa rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyemaṃ svapnamupadarśayati sma yadrājā śuddhodanaḥ suptaḥ svapnāntaragato 'drākṣīt bodhisattvaṃ rātrau praśāntāyāmabhiniṣkramantaṃ devagaṇaparivṛtam
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, the <s>bodhisattva</s> (awakening-being), having been urged by that devaputra, showed this dream to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, while asleep and within a dream, saw the <s>bodhisattva</s> going forth at night when all was quiet, surrounded by hosts of gods.

children.text: abhiniṣkramya pravrajitaṃ cādrākṣīt kāṣāyavastraprāvṛtam
children.translated_text: And he saw him, after going forth, become ordained, clothed in ochre robes.

children.text: sa pratibuddhaḥ tvaritaṃ tvaritaṃ kāñcukīyaṃ paripṛcchati sma kaccit kumāro 'ntaḥpure 'sti so 'vocat asti deveti ||
children.translated_text: When he awoke, he hastily questioned a chamberlain: 'Is the prince in the inner palace?' He said, 'He is, your Majesty.'

children.text: tato rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyāntaḥpure śokaśalyo hṛdaye 'nupraviṣṭo 'bhūd abhiniṣkramiṣyati avaśyaṃ kumāro 'yam
children.translated_text: Then, in King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s inner palace, a thorn of sorrow entered his heart: 'This prince will certainly go forth.

children.text: yaccemāni pūrvanimittāni saṃdṛśyante sma ||
children.translated_text: For these preliminary signs are being seen.'

children.text: tasyaitadabhavan na khalvavyayaṃ kumāreṇa kadācidudyānabhūmimabhinirgantavyam
children.translated_text: He thought, 'Surely the prince must never be allowed to go out to the park grounds.

children.text: strīgaṇamadhye 'bhirataḥ ihaiva ramyate nābhiniṣkramiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Delighting among a company of women, he will enjoy himself right here and will not go forth.'

children.text: tato rājñā śuddhodanena kumārasya paribhogārthaṃ trayo yathartukāḥ prāsādāḥ kāritā abhūvan graiṣmiko vārṣiko haimantikaśca
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had three seasonal palaces constructed for the prince's enjoyment: one for summer, one for the rains, and one for winter.

children.text: tatra yo graiṣmikaḥ sa ekāntaśītalaḥ
children.translated_text: Of these, the summer palace was entirely cool.

children.text: yo vārṣikaḥ sa sādhāraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The rainy-season palace was temperate.

children.text: yo haimantikaḥ sa svabhāvoṣṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The winter palace was naturally warm.

children.text: ekaikasya ca prāsādasya sopānāni pañca pañca puruṣaśatānyutkṣipanti sma nikṣipanti sma
children.translated_text: And the stairways of each palace were raised and lowered by five hundred men each.

children.text: teṣāṃ tathotkṣipyamāṇānāṃ nikṣipyamāṇānāṃ ca śabdo 'rdhayojane śrūyate sma mā khalu kumāro 'nabhijñāta evābhiniṣkramiṣyatīti
children.translated_text: As they were being raised and lowered, their sound was heard for half a yojana, so that the prince would not go forth unobserved.

children.text: naimittikairvaipañcikaiśca vyākṛtamabhūn maṅgaladvāreṇa kumāro 'bhiniṣkramiṣyatīti
children.translated_text: The omen-readers and diviners had predicted, 'The prince will go forth through the auspicious gate.'

children.text: tato rājā maṅgaladvārasya mahānti kapāṭāni kārayati sma
children.translated_text: Then the king had great doors made for the auspicious gate.

children.text: ekaikaṃ ca kapāṭaṃ pañca pañca puruṣaśatānyudghāṭayanti sma apaghāṭayanti sma
children.translated_text: And each door was opened and shut by five hundred men each.

children.text: teṣāṃ cārdhayojanaṃ śabdo gacchati sma
children.translated_text: And their sound traveled for half a yojana.

children.text: pañca cāsya kāmaguṇān sadṛśānupasaṃharati sma
children.translated_text: And he furnished him with the five qualities of sensual pleasure in fitting form.

children.text: gītavāditanṛtyaiścainaṃ sadaiva yuvataya upatasthuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Young women constantly attended on him with singing, instrumental music, and dancing.

children.text: atha bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ sārathiṃ prāha śīghraṃ sārathe rathaṃ yojaya
children.translated_text: Then, monks, the <s>bodhisattva</s> said to the charioteer, 'Quickly, charioteer, yoke the chariot.

children.text: udyānabhūmiṃ gamiṣyāmīti
children.translated_text: I shall go to the park grounds.'

children.text: tataḥ sārathī rājānaṃ śuddhodanam upasaṃkramyaivamāha deva kumāra udyānabhūmimabhiniryāsyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Then the charioteer approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said, 'Your Majesty, the prince will go out to the park grounds.'

children.text: atha rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyaitadabhavan na kadācinmayā kumāra udyānabhūmimabhiniṣkramitaḥ subhūmidarśanāya
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> thought, 'Never before have I had the prince go out to the park grounds to see the pleasant land.

children.text: yannvahaṃ kumāramudyānabhūmimabhiniṣkrāmayeyam
children.translated_text: What if I were to have the prince go out to the park grounds?

children.text: tataḥ kumāraḥ strīgaṇaparivṛto ratiṃ vetsyate nābhiniṣkramiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Then the prince, surrounded by a company of women, will experience pleasure and will not go forth.'

children.text: tato rājā śuddhodanaḥ snehabahumānābhyāṃ bodhisattvasya nagare ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇāṃ kārayati sma saptame divase kumāra udyānabhūmiṃ niṣkramiṣyatīti subhūmidarśanāya
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, out of affection and high regard for the <s>bodhisattva</s>, had a bell proclamation made in the city: 'On the seventh day the prince will go out to the park grounds to see the pleasant land.

children.text: tatra bhavadbhiḥ sarvāmanāpāni cāpanayitavyāni mā kumāraḥ pratikūlaṃ paśyet
children.translated_text: There all disagreeable things are to be removed by you, so that the prince may not see anything unpleasant.

children.text: sarvamanāpāni copasaṃhartavyāni viṣayābhiramyāṇi ||
children.translated_text: And all agreeable things, delightful objects of the senses, are to be provided.'

children.text: tataḥ saptame divase sarvaṃ nagaramalaṃkṛtamabhūd udyānabhūmimupaśobhitaṃ nānāraṅgadūṣyavitānīkṛtaṃ chatradhvajapatākāsamalaṃkṛtam
children.translated_text: Then, on the seventh day, the whole city was adorned, and the park grounds were beautified, canopied with cloths of many colors and decorated with parasols, banners, and flags.

children.text: yena ca mārgeṇa bodhisattvo 'bhinirgacchati sma sa mārgaḥ siktaḥ saṃmṛṣṭo gandhodakapariṣikto muktakusumāvakīrṇo nānāgandhaghaṭikānirdhūpitaḥ pūrṇakumbhopaśobhitaḥ kadalīvṛkṣocchrito nānāvicitrapaṭavitānavitato ratnakiṅkiṇījālahārārdhahārābhipralambito 'bhūt
children.translated_text: And the road by which the <s>bodhisattva</s> was to go out was sprinkled, swept, sprinkled with scented water, strewn with loose flowers, perfumed by incense vessels of many scents, adorned with full pitchers, set up with banana trees, spread with awnings of many variegated cloths, and hung with jeweled nets of little bells, necklaces, and half-necklaces.

children.text: caturaṅgasainyavyūhitaḥ parivāraścodyukto 'bhūt kumārasyāntaḥpuraṃ pratimaṇḍayitum
children.translated_text: A fourfold army was arrayed, and the retinue was ready to adorn the prince's inner quarters.

children.text: atha śuddhāvāsakāyikā devā nidhyāpayanti sma bodhisattvamāharitum tatra bodhisattvasya pūrveṇa nagaradvāreṇodyānabhūmimabhiniṣkrāmato mahatā vyūhena atha bodhisattvasyānubhāvena śuddhavāsakāyikair devaputraistasmin mārge puruṣo jīrṇo vṛddho mahallako dhamanīsaṃtatagātraḥ khaṇḍadanto valīnicitakāyaḥ palitakeśaḥ kubjo gopānasīvakro vibhagno daṇḍaparāyaṇa āturo gatayauvanaḥ kharakharāvasaktakaṇṭhaḥ prāgbhāreṇa kāyena daṇḍamavaṣṭabhya pravepayamānaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgaiḥ purato mārgasyopadarśito 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: Then the gods belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> realm reflected in order to bring the <s>bodhisattva</s> there, as the <s>bodhisattva</s> was going out to the park grounds through the eastern city gate with a great array. Then, through the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s power, the devaputras belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> realm showed on that road, before him, an aged man: old, advanced in years, his limbs covered with veins, his teeth broken, his body filled with wrinkles, his hair gray, hunchbacked, bent like a roof-ridge, broken down, dependent on a staff, ill, his youth gone, his throat caught in a harsh rasping sound, his body bent forward, leaning on a staff, trembling in all his limbs and members.

children.text: atha bodhisattvo jānanneva sārathimidamavocat ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s>, though he knew, said this to the charioteer:

children.text: kiṃ sārathe puruṣa durbala alpasthāmo ucchuṣkamāṃsarudhiratvacasnāyunaddhaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Who is this man, charioteer, weak, of little strength, bound together by dried-up flesh, blood, skin, and sinews,

children.text: śvetaṃśiro viraladanta kṛśāṅgarūpo ālambya daṇḍa vrajate asukhaṃ skhalantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: white-haired, with sparse teeth, thin-limbed in form, going painfully and stumbling while leaning on a staff?'

children.text: sārathirāha ||
children.translated_text: The charioteer said:

children.text: eṣo hi deva puruṣo jarayābhibhūtaḥ kṣīṇendriyaḥ sudukhito balavīryahīnaḥ
children.translated_text: 'This man, your Highness, is overcome by old age; his faculties are exhausted, he is very miserable, and he lacks strength and vigor.'

children.text: bandhūjanena paribhūta anāthabhūtaḥ kāryāsamartha apaviddhu vaneva dāru ||
children.translated_text: Scorned by his kinsmen, made helpless, unable to act, cast away like a piece of wood in the forest.

children.text: bodhisattva āha ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: kuladharma eṣa ayamasya hitaṃ bhaṇāhi athavāpi sarvajagato 'sya iyaṃ hyavasthā
children.translated_text: Is this the custom of his family? Speak what is beneficial for him. Or else, indeed, is this the condition of this whole world?

children.text: śīghraṃ bhaṇāhi vacanaṃ yathabhūtametat śrutvā tathārthamiha yoniśa cintayiṣye ||
children.translated_text: Quickly speak this matter as it truly is; having heard the truth of it, I will reflect on it properly here.

children.text: sārathirāha ||
children.translated_text: The charioteer said:

children.text: naitasya deva kuladharma na rāṣṭradharmaḥ sarve jagasya jara yauvanu dharṣayāti
children.translated_text: This, O lord, is not a custom of his family, nor a law of the realm; old age assails the youth of the whole world.

children.text: tubhyaṃ pi mātṛpitṛbāndhavajñātisaṃgho jarayā amukta na hi anya gatirjanasya ||
children.translated_text: Your own company of mother, father, relatives, and kin is not freed from old age either; for people there is no other course.

children.text: bodhisattva āha ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: dhiksārathe abudha bālajanasya buddhiḥ yadyauvanena madamatta jarāṃ na paśyet
children.translated_text: Fie, charioteer, on the thought of ignorant, childish people, if, intoxicated and maddened by youth, they do not see old age.

children.text: āvartayāśu mi rathaṃ punarahaṃ pravekṣye kiṃ mahya krīḍaratibhirjarayāśritasya ||
children.translated_text: Turn my chariot back quickly; I will enter again. What have I to do with games and pleasures, when I am subject to old age?

children.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ pratinivartya rathavaraṃ punarapi puraṃ prāviśat ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having turned back the excellent chariot, entered the city again.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo 'pareṇa kālasamayena dakṣiṇena nagaradvāreṇodyānabhūmimabhiniṣkraman mahatā vyūhena so 'drākṣīnmārge puruṣaṃ vyādhispṛṣṭaṃ dagdhodarābhibhūtaṃ durbalakāyaṃ svake mūtrapurīṣe nimagnam atrāṇam apratiśaraṇaṃ kṛcchreṇocchvasantaṃ praśvasantam
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, at another time the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, going out through the southern city gate toward the park with great magnificence, saw on the road a man touched by disease, overcome by burning in the belly, weak in body, sunk in his own urine and feces, without protection and without refuge, breathing in and out with difficulty.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarbodhisattvo jānanneva sārathimidamavocat ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though he knew, said this to the charioteer:

children.text: kiṃ sārathe puruṣa ruṣyavivarṇagātraḥ sarvendriyebhi vikalo guru praśvasantaḥ
children.translated_text: Charioteer, why is this man's body rough and discolored, why is he impaired in all his faculties and breathing heavily?

children.text: sarvāṅgaśuṣka udarākula kṛcchraprāpto mūtre purīṣi svaki tiṣṭhati kutsanīye ||
children.translated_text: His whole body is dried up, his belly distressed, and he has fallen into misery; he remains in his own urine and feces, which are repulsive.

children.text: sārathirāha ||
children.translated_text: The charioteer said:

children.text: eṣo hi deva puruṣo paramaṃ gilāno vyādhībhayaṃ upagato maraṇāntaprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: This man, O lord, is extremely ill; he has come into the danger of disease and has reached the brink of death.

children.text: ārogyatejarahito balaviprahīno atrāṇadvīpaśaraṇo hyaparāyaṇaśca ||
children.translated_text: Bereft of the splendor of health and deprived of strength, he has no protector, island, or refuge, and no further support.

children.text: bodhisattva āha ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: ārogyatā ca bhavate yatha svapnakrīḍā vyādhībhayaṃ ca imamīdṛśu ghorarūpam
children.translated_text: Health, then, is like play in a dream, while the danger of disease has this terrible form.

children.text: ko nāma vijñapuruṣo ima dṛṣṭvavasthāṃ krīḍāratiṃ ca janayecchubhasaṃjñatāṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: What discerning person, seeing such a condition, would produce delight in play and pleasure, or the notion that it is auspicious?

children.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ pratinivartya rathavaraṃ punarapi puravaraṃ prāvikṣat ||
children.translated_text: Then, monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having turned back the excellent chariot, again entered the excellent city.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo 'pareṇa kālasamayena paścimena nagaradvāreṇodyānabhūmimabhiniṣkraman mahatā vyūhena so 'drākṣīt puruṣaṃ mṛtaṃ kālagataṃ mañce samāropitaṃ cailavitānīkṛtaṃ jñātisaṃghaparivṛtaṃ sarvai rudadbhiḥ krandadbhiḥ paridevamānaiḥ prakīrṇakeśaiḥ pāṃśvavakīrṇaśirobhirurāṃsi tāḍayadbhirutkrośadbhiḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nugacchadbhiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, at another time the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, going out through the western city gate toward the park with great magnificence, saw a man dead and departed, placed upon a bier, covered with a cloth canopy, surrounded by his band of kinsmen, while all wept, cried, and lamented, with hair disheveled, heads sprinkled with dust, beating their breasts, wailing, and following behind.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarbodhisattvo jānanneva sārathimidamavocat ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though he knew, said this to the charioteer:

children.text: kiṃ sārathe puruṣa mañcapari gṛhīto uddhūtakeśanakha pāṃśu śire kṣipanti
children.translated_text: Charioteer, why has this man been taken upon a bier? Why do they toss up their hair and nails and throw dust upon their heads?

children.text: paricārayitva viharantyurastāḍayanto nānāvilāpavacanāni udīrayantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why, after attending upon him, do they go along beating their breasts and uttering many words of lamentation?

children.text: sārathirāha ||
children.translated_text: The charioteer said:

children.text: eṣo hi deva puruṣo mṛtu jambudvīpe nahi bhūyu mātṛpitṛ drakṣyati putradārāṃ
children.translated_text: This man, O lord, has died in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; he will not again see mother, father, sons, or wife.

children.text: apahāya bhogagṛha aumātṛpitṛjh mitrajñātisaṃghaṃ paralokaprāptu na hi drakṣyati bhūyu jñātīṃ ||
children.translated_text: Having left behind wealth, home, mother and father, friends, and the company of kinsmen, he has reached the other world and will not see his kinsmen again.

children.text: bodhisattva āha ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: dhigyauvanena jarayā samabhidrutena ārogya dhigvividhavyādhiparāhatena
children.translated_text: Fie on youth, which is overwhelmed by old age; fie on health, struck down by manifold diseases.

children.text: dhigjīvitena viduṣā nacirasthitena dhikpaṇḍitasya puruṣasya ratiprasaṅgaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fie on life, which the wise know does not last long; fie on a learned man's attachment to pleasures.

children.text: yadi jara na bhaveyā naiva vyādhirna mṛtyuḥ tathapi ca mahaduḥkhaṃ pañcaskandhaṃ dharanto
children.translated_text: Even if there were no old age, no disease, and no death, still there would be great suffering for those who bear the five aggregates.

children.text: kiṃ puna jaravyādhirmṛtyu nityānubaddhāḥ sādhu pratinivartyā cintayiṣye pramokṣam ||
children.translated_text: How much more, when old age, disease, and death are constantly bound to one. It is good to turn back; I will reflect on liberation.

children.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ pratinivartya taṃ rathavaraṃ punarapi puraṃ prāvikṣat ||
children.translated_text: Then, monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having turned back that excellent chariot, entered the city again.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvasyāpareṇa kālasamayenottareṇa nagaradvāreṇodyānabhūmim abhiniṣkrāmatastaireva devaputrairbodhisattvasyānubhāvenaiva tasminmārge bhikṣurabhinirmito 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, at another time, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was going out through the northern city gate toward the park, by those very sons of the gods, through the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s own power, a monk was magically created on that road.

children.text: adrākṣīdbodhisattvastaṃ bhikṣuṃ śāntaṃ dāntaṃ saṃyataṃ brahmacāriṇam avikṣiptacakṣuṣaṃ yugamātraprekṣiṇaṃ prāsādikenairyāpathena sampannaṃ prāsādikenābhikramapratikrameṇa sampannaṃ prāsādikenāvalokitavyavalokitena prāsādikena samiñjitaprasāritena prāsādikena saṃghāṭīpātracīvaradhāraṇena mārge sthitam
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> saw that monk, peaceful, disciplined, restrained, practicing celibacy, his eyes not distracted, looking only a yoke's length ahead, endowed with graceful deportment, graceful in going forward and returning, graceful in looking and looking away, graceful in bending and stretching, and graceful in carrying his outer robe, bowl, and robes, standing on the road.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punarbodhisattvo jānanneva sārathimidamavocat ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though he knew, said this to the charioteer:

children.text: kiṃ sārathe puruṣa śāntapraśāntacitto notkṣiptacakṣu vrajate yugamātradarśī
children.translated_text: Charioteer, why does this man go with a calm and very peaceful mind, with eyes not lifted up, seeing only a yoke's length ahead?

children.text: kāṣāyavastravasano supraśāntacārī pātraṃ gṛhītva na ca uddhatu unnato vā ||
children.translated_text: He is clothed in ocher robes, conducts himself very peacefully, and has taken up a bowl; he is neither agitated nor haughty.

children.text: sārathirāha ||
children.translated_text: The charioteer said:

children.text: eṣo hi deva puruṣo iti bhikṣunāmā apahāya kāmaratayaḥ suvinītacārī
children.translated_text: This man, O lord, is called a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk); having abandoned pleasures of desire, his conduct is well disciplined.

children.text: pravajyaprāptu śamamātmana eṣamāṇo saṃrāgadveṣavigato 'nveti piṇḍacaryā ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained going forth, seeking peace for himself, free from passion and hatred, he follows the practice of alms-round.

children.text: bodhisattva āha ||
children.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: sādhū subhāṣitamidaṃ mama rocate ca pravrajya nāma vidubhiḥ satataṃ praśastā
children.translated_text: Good. This is well spoken, and it pleases me. What is called going forth is always praised by the wise,

children.text: hitamātmanaśca parasattvahitaṃ ca yatra sukhajīvitaṃ sumadhuraṃ amṛtaṃ phalaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: where there is benefit for oneself and benefit for other beings, a happy life, very sweet, and immortality as the fruit.

children.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ pratinivartya taṃ rathavaraṃ punarapi puravaraṃ prāvikṣat ||
children.translated_text: Then, monks, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having turned back that excellent chariot, entered the excellent city once more.

children.text: iti hi bhikṣavo rājā śuddhodano bodhisattvasyemāmevaṃrūpāṃ saṃcodanāṃ dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca bhūyasyā mātrayā bodhisattvasya parirakṣaṇārthaṃ prākārān māpayate sma parikhāḥ khānayati sma dvārāṇi ca gāḍhāni kārayati sma
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, when King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had seen and heard this sort of prompting in the <s>bodhisattva</s>, he had walls built in even greater measure for the protection of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, had moats dug, and had the gates made secure.

children.text: ārakṣān sthāpayati sma
children.translated_text: He stationed guards.

children.text: śūrāṃścodayati sma
children.translated_text: He urged on brave men.

children.text: vāhanāni yojayati sma
children.translated_text: He had vehicles yoked.

children.text: varmāṇi grāhayati sma
children.translated_text: He had armor taken up.

children.text: caturṣu nagaradvāraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu caturo mahāsenāvyūhān sthāpayati sma bodhisattvasya parirakṣaṇārtham
children.translated_text: At the four crossroads by the city gates he stationed four great army formations for the protection of the <s>bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: ya enaṃ rātriṃdivaṃ rakṣanti sma mā bodhisattvo 'bhiniṣkramiṣyatīti
children.translated_text: and they guarded him night and day, thinking, 'Let the <s>bodhisattva</s> not go forth.'

children.text: antaḥpure cājñāṃ dadāti sma mā sma kadācitsaṃgītiṃ vicchetsyatha
children.translated_text: And in the inner palace he gave an order: 'Never interrupt the music.

children.text: sarvaratikrīḍāścopasaṃhartavyāḥ strīmāyāścopadarśayata nirbandhata kumāraṃ yathānuraktacitto na nirgacchetpravrajyāyai ||
children.translated_text: All delights and games are to be provided; display the wiles of women; hold the prince fast, so that, with his mind attached, he may not go out for renunciation.'

children.text: tatredamucyate ||
children.translated_text: On this point this is said:

children.text: dvāre sthāpita yuddhaśauṇḍapuruṣāḥ khaḍgāyudhāpāṇayo hastīaśvarathāśca varmitanarā ārūḍha nāgāvalī
children.translated_text: At the gates were posted men eager for battle, with swords and weapons in their hands; elephants, horses, and chariots were there, and armored men had mounted the ranks of elephants.

children.text: parikhā khoṭakatoraṇāśca mahatā prākāra ucchrāpitā dvārā baddha sugāḍhabandhanakṛtāḥ krośasvarāmuñcanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moats, outworks, and gateways were raised along with a great rampart; the gates were fastened, made with firm bonds, and cries rang out for a krośa.

children.text: sarve śākyagaṇā viṣaṇṇamanaso rakṣanti rātriṃdivaṃ nirghoṣaśca balasya tasya mahataḥ śabdo mahā śrūyate
children.translated_text: All the Śākyas, their minds despondent, guarded him night and day, and the roar of that great army, a mighty sound, was heard.

children.text: nagaraṃ vyākulu bhītatrastamanaso mā smād vrajetsūrato mā bhūcchākyakuloditasya gamane chidyeta vaṃśo hyayam ||
children.translated_text: The city was disturbed, its people frightened and terrified in mind: 'Let the lovely one not go away from here; let this lineage, arisen from the Śākya clan, not be cut off by his departure.'

children.text: ājñapto yuvatījanaśca satataṃ saṃgīti mā chetsyathā vasthānaṃ prakarotha krīḍaratibhirnirbandhathā mānasam
children.translated_text: The young women were constantly commanded, 'Do not stop the music. Make alluring poses; with games and pleasures hold his mind fast.

children.text: ye vā istriyamāya nekavividhā darśetha ceṣṭāṃ bahuṃ ārakṣāṃ prakarotha vighna kuruthā mā khu vrajetsūrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever varied wiles of women there are, show many gestures. Set up a guard and make an obstacle, so that the lovely one will not go.'

children.text: tasyā niṣkramikāli sārathivare pūrve nimittā ime haṃsā kroñca mayūra sārika śukā no te ravaṃ muñciṣu
children.translated_text: At the time of his departure these earlier signs appeared before the excellent charioteer: swans, cranes, peacocks, mynah birds, and parrots did not utter their cries.

children.text: prāsādeṣu gavākṣatoraṇavareṣvātālamañceṣu ca jihmājihva sudurmanā asukhitā dhyāyantyadhomūrdhakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the palaces, at the fine windows and gateways, on the watch-platforms and stages, they remained with crooked tongues, deeply dejected and unhappy, brooding with their heads lowered.

children.text: puḍinīpuṣkariṇīṣu padma rucirā mlānāni mlāyanti ca vṛkṣāḥ śuṣkapalāśa puṣparahitāḥ puṣpanti bhūyo na ca
children.translated_text: In the ponds and lotus-pools the beautiful lotuses were withered and fading; the trees, with dry leaves and without blossoms, no longer bloomed.

children.text: vīṇāvallakivaṃśatantriracitā chidyantyakasmāttadā bherīścaiva mṛdaṅga pāṇyabhihatā bhidyanti no vādyiṣu ||
children.translated_text: The strings set on vīṇās, vallakīs, flutes, and lutes suddenly snapped then, and drums and mṛdaṅgas, though struck by the hand, broke and did not sound.

children.text: sarvaṃ vyākulamāsi tacca nagaraṃ nidrābhibhūtaṃ bhṛśaṃ no nṛtte na ca gāyite na ramite bhūyo manaḥ kasyacit
children.translated_text: That whole city became confused and was heavily overcome by sleep; no one's mind turned again to dancing, singing, or pleasure.

children.text: rājāpī paramaṃ sudīnamanasaḥ cintāparo dhyāyate hā dhikśākyakulasya ṛddhi vipulā mā haiva saṃdhakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: The king too, with an utterly wretched mind, absorbed in anxiety, brooded: 'Alas, shame! May the vast prosperity of the Śākya family not be burned away.'

children.text: ekasmiṃ śayane sthite sthitamabhūdgopā tathā pārthivo gopā rātriyi ardharātrasamaye svapnānimāṃ paśyati
children.translated_text: As she lay on one bed, <s>Gopā</s> remained there, and so did the prince; at midnight in the night <s>Gopā</s> saw these dreams:

children.text: sarveyaṃ pṛthivī prakampitamabhūcchailā sakūṭāvaṭī vṛkṣā mārutaeritā kṣiti patī utpāṭya mūloddhṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: This whole earth shook, together with its mountains, peaks, and hollows; trees, driven by the wind, were torn up from the ground, uprooted at the root.

children.text: candrāsūrya nabhātu bhūmipatitau sajyotiṣālaṃkṛtau keśānadṛśi lūna dakṣiṇi bhuje mukuṭaṃ ca vidhvaṃsitam
children.translated_text: The moon and sun fell from the sky to the earth, adorned with the stars; she saw her hair cut off, her right arm severed, and her crown destroyed.

children.text: hastau chinna tathaiva chinna caraṇau nagnā dṛśī ātmanaṃ muktāhāra tathaiva mekhalamaṇī chinnā dṛśī ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Her hands were cut off, and likewise her feet were cut off; she saw herself naked, and she saw her pearl necklace and jeweled girdle cut from herself.

children.text: śayanasyā dṛśi chinna pāda caturo dharaṇītalesmiṃ chayī chatre daṇḍu sucitru śrīma ruciraṃ chinnā dṛśī pārthive
children.translated_text: She saw the four legs of her bed cut off and the bed lying on the surface of the earth; she saw the pole of the royal parasol, splendid, beautiful, and lovely, cut from the prince.

children.text: sarve ābharaṇā vikīrṇa patitā muhyanti te vāriṇā bhartuścābharaṇā savastramukuṭā śayyāgatā vyākulā ||
children.translated_text: All the ornaments were scattered and fallen; they seemed bewildered and wet, while her husband's ornaments, garments, and crown lay disordered on the bed.

children.text: ulkāṃ paśyati niṣkramanta nagarāttamasābhibhūtaṃ puraṃ chinnāṃ jālikamadṛśāti supine ratanāmikāṃ śobhanāṃ
children.translated_text: She saw a meteor going out from the city, and the city overcome by darkness; in her dream she saw a beautiful jeweled net and ring cut apart.

children.text: muktāhāru pralambamānu patitaḥ kṣubhito mahāsāgaraṃ meruṃ parvatarājamadṛśi tadā sthānātu saṃkampitam ||
children.translated_text: She saw a hanging pearl necklace fallen, the great ocean agitated, and <s>Meru</s>, king of mountains, shaken from its place.

children.text: etānīdṛśa śākyakanya supināṃ supināntare adṛśī dṛṣṭvā sā pratibuddha ruṇṇanayanā svaṃ svāminaṃ abravīt
children.translated_text: Such dreams as these the Śākya maiden saw within her dream; having seen them, she awoke with tearful eyes and spoke to her own lord:

children.text: devā kiṃ mi bhaviṣyate khalu bhaṇā supināntarāṇīdṛśā bhrāntā me smṛti no ca paśyami punaḥ śokārditaṃ me manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Lord, tell me, what will happen to me from such dreams as these? My memory is confused; I see no further, and my mind is afflicted with grief.'

children.text: śrutvāsau kalaviṅkadundubhiruto brahmasvaraḥ susvaro gopāmālapate bhava pramuditā pāpaṃ na te vidyate
children.translated_text: Having heard this, he whose voice was melodious like a kalaviṅka and a kettledrum, a lovely voice like Brahmā's, addressed <s>Gopā</s>: 'Be joyful; there is no evil for you.'

children.text: ye sattvā kṛtapuṇyapūrvacaritā teṣeti svapnā ime ko 'nyaḥ paśyati naikaduḥkhavihitaḥ svapnāntarāṇīdṛśā ||
children.translated_text: Those beings whose former conduct has made merit: theirs are such dreams. Who else, afflicted by many sufferings, sees other dreams of this kind?

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭā medinī kampamānā kūṭā śailā medinīye patantā
children.translated_text: That you saw the earth shaking and the peaked mountains falling upon the earth,

children.text: devā nāgā rākṣasā bhūtasaṃghāḥ sarve tubhyaṃ pūjyaśreṣṭhāṃ karonti ||
children.translated_text: means that gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and hosts of spirits all render you the highest worship.

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭā vṛkṣamūloddhṛtāni keśāṃ lūnāṃ dakṣiṇenādṛśāsi
children.translated_text: That you saw trees uprooted from their roots, and saw hair cut off by the right hand,

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope kleśajālaṃ chinitvā dṛṣṭījālaṃ uddharī saṃskṛtātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: means that soon, <s>Gopā</s>, having cut the net of defilements, you will draw out the net of views from conditioned existence.

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭau candrasūryau patantau dṛṣṭā nakṣatrā jyotiṣā nīpatantaḥ
children.translated_text: That you saw the moon and sun falling, and saw the stars, the lights, falling down,

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope kleśaśatrū nihatvā pūjyā loke bhāvinī tvaṃ praśasyā ||
children.translated_text: means that soon, <s>Gopā</s>, having struck down the enemies, the defilements, you will be worshipful and praised in the world.

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭā muktahāraṃ viśīrṇaṃ nagnaṃ bhagnaṃ sarvakāyādṛśāsi
children.translated_text: That you saw a pearl necklace shattered, and saw yourself naked and broken in your whole body,

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope istrikāyaṃ jahitvā puruṣastvaṃ vai bheṣyase nocireṇa ||
children.translated_text: means that soon, <s>Gopā</s>, having abandoned a woman's body, you will indeed become a man before long.

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭaṃ mañcakaṃ chinnapādaṃ chatre daṇḍaṃ ratnacitraṃ prabhagnam
children.translated_text: That you saw a couch with its legs cut off and a jewel-patterned parasol with its staff broken,

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope ogha catvāri tīrtvā māṃ draṣṭāsī ekachatraṃ triloke ||
children.translated_text: means that soon, <s>Gopā</s>, after crossing the four floods, you will see me as the sole parasol over the three worlds.

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭā bhūṣaṇā uhyamānā cūḍā vastrā mahya mañce 'dṛśāsi
children.translated_text: That you saw ornaments carried away, and a crest and garments on my couch,

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope lakṣaṇairbhūṣitāṅgaṃ māṃ saṃpaśyī sarvalokaiḥ stuvantam ||
children.translated_text: means that soon, <s>Gopā</s>, you will behold me, my limbs adorned with the marks, praised by all the worlds.

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭā dīpakoṭīśatāni nagarānniṣkrāntā tatpuraṃ cāndhakāram
children.translated_text: That you saw hundreds of crores of lamps gone out from the city and that city in darkness,
