children.text: kṣipraṃ gope mohavidyāndhakāre prajñāloke kurvamī sarvalokam ||
children.translated_text: means that soon, <s>Gopā</s>, in the darkness of delusion and ignorance I shall make all the world into the light of wisdom.

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭaṃ muktahāraṃ prabhagnaṃ chinnaṃ caiva svarṇasūtraṃ vicitram
children.translated_text: That you saw a pearl necklace broken and a variegated golden thread cut,

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope kleśajālaṃ chinitvā saṃjñā sūtraṃ uddharī saṃskṛtātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: means that soon, <s>Gopā</s>, having cut the net of defilements, I shall draw out the thread of perception from conditioned existence.

children.text: yatte gope cittikāraṃ karoṣī nityaṃ pūjāṃ gauraveṇottamena
children.translated_text: That, <s>Gopā</s>, you show me honor and always perform worship with supreme reverence,

children.text: nāstī tubhyaṃ durgatī naiva śokaḥ kṣipraṃ bhohī prītiprāmodyalabdhā ||
children.translated_text: means that there is no bad destination for you and no sorrow; soon, indeed, you will obtain joy and gladness.

children.text: pūrve mahyaṃ dānu dattaṃ praṇītaṃ śīlaṃ cīrṇaṃ bhāvitā nityakṣānti
children.translated_text: In the past I gave excellent gifts, practiced morality, and always cultivated patience.

children.text: tasmānmahyaṃ ye prasādaṃ labhante sarve bhontī prītiprāmodyalābhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore all who gain faith in me become obtainers of joy and gladness.

children.text: kalpā koṭī saṃskṛtā me anantā bodhīmārgo śodhito me praṇītaḥ
children.translated_text: For countless crores of kalpas my formations have been completed; the excellent path to awakening has been purified by me.

children.text: tasmānmahyaṃ ye prasādaṃ karonti sarve chinnā teṣu trīṇyapyapāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore all who conceive faith in me have the three lower realms cut off for them.

children.text: harṣaṃ vindā mā ca khedaṃ janehi tuṣṭiṃ vindā saṃjanehī ca prītim
children.translated_text: Find joy, and do not produce distress; find contentment, and generate gladness.

children.text: kṣipraṃ bheṣye prītiprāmodyalābhī sehī gope bhadrakā te nimittā ||
children.translated_text: Soon I shall be one who has obtained joy and gladness; these, <s>Gopā</s>, are auspicious omens for you.

children.text: so puṇyatejabharito siritejagarbho pūrve nimittasupine imi adṛśāsi
children.translated_text: Filled with the brilliance of merit and bearing the splendor of fortune, he formerly saw these omens in dreams,

children.text: ye bhonti pūrvaśubhakarmasamuccayānāṃ naiṣkramyakālasamaye narapuṃgavānām ||
children.translated_text: which occur, at the time of renunciation, to bulls among men who have accumulated wholesome actions in the past.

children.text: so adṛśāsi ca karāccaraṇāddhatānā mahasāgarebhi catubhirjala lolayantā
children.translated_text: He saw the waters of the four great oceans lapping at his hands and feet,

children.text: sarvāmimāṃ vasumatīṃ śayanaṃ vicitraṃ meruṃ ca parvatavaraṃ śirasopadhānam ||
children.translated_text: with this whole earth as a variegated bed and the excellent mountain <s>Meru</s> as a pillow beneath his head.

children.text: ābhā pramukta supine tada adṛśāsi loke vilokitu mahātamasāndhakāram
children.translated_text: In the dream he saw a radiance emitted, looking upon the world as a great darkness of blindness;

children.text: chatrodgataṃ dharaṇiye spharate trilokaṃ ābhāya spṛṣṭa vinipātadukhā praśāntā ||
children.translated_text: a parasol risen over the earth spread across the three worlds, and the sufferings of bad destinies, touched by the radiance, were pacified.

children.text: kṛṣṇā śubhā caturi prāṇaka pāda lekhī catuvarṇa etva śakunādbhuta ekavarṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Four birds, black, white, and of four colors, came to his feet and wondrously became one color.

children.text: mīḍhaṃgirī paramahīna jugupsanīyā abhibhūya caṃkramati tatra ca nopalipto ||
children.translated_text: He walked over a mountain of dung, utterly low and disgusting, overcoming it, and there he was not defiled.

children.text: bhūyo 'dṛśī supini nadya jalaprapūrṇā bahusattvakoṭinayutāni ca uhyamānā
children.translated_text: Again in the dream he saw rivers filled with water, and many crores and nayutas of beings being swept away.

children.text: so nāva kṛtva prataritva parāṃ pratārya sthāpeti so sthalavare abhaye aśoke ||
children.translated_text: Having made a boat, he crossed over, ferried others to the far shore, and set them on excellent dry ground, free from fear and sorrow.

children.text: bhūyo 'dṛśāti bahu ātura rogaspṛṣṭāṃ ārogyatejarahitāṃ balaviprahīnāṃ
children.translated_text: Again he saw many sick people touched by disease, lacking the splendor of health and deprived of strength.

children.text: so vaidya bhūtva bahu oṣadha saṃprayacchā moceti sattvanayutāṃ bahurogaspṛṣṭāṃ ||
children.translated_text: Having become a physician, he gave many medicines and freed nayutas of beings touched by many diseases.

children.text: siṃhāsane va hi niṣaṇṇa sumerupṛṣṭhe śiṣyāṃ kṛtāñjalipuṭānamarānnamantāṃ
children.translated_text: And seated on a lion throne on the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, he saw disciples with joined palms and gods bowing down.

children.text: saṃgrāmamadhyi jayu adṛśi ātmanaśca ānandaśabdamamarāṃ gagane bruvantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the midst of battle he saw his own victory, while the immortals in the sky uttered sounds of rejoicing.

children.text: evaṃvidhā supini adṛśi bodhisattvo maṅgalya śobhanavratasya ca pāripūrim
children.translated_text: Such dreams the <s>bodhisattva</s> saw, the auspicious completion of a beautiful vow,

children.text: yāṃ śrutva devamanujā abhavanprahṛṣṭā na cirādbhaviṣyati ayaṃ naradevadevaḥ ||
children.translated_text: hearing which gods and humans became delighted: 'Before long this lord of men and gods will appear.'
